units.la: Uia dicere habeo, quæ peculiariter V.V.A.A. concernunt, nomen vestrum libro huic præscribere volui. Ubi antequam ad rei caput veniam, repeto quod in Secundâ Parte Arcanorum Arminianismi dixi, me quicquid de Arminianis dixi antehac & in futurum dicâ, non dicere nisi de ministris sive Theologis quibusdam, qui se Remonstrantes vocant. De his conquestus sum, atque etiamnum conqueror: non autem de Viris honoratis aut populis quibus illi hactenus turpissimè imposuerunt. Hi enim, cùm existiment se doceri à ministris talibus qui à nobis in Quinque tantùm articulis dissentiant; revera docentur ab iis, qui, cùm orthodoxam doctrinam de Trinitate simulent, more multorum veterum Hæreticorum Antitrinitariorum, ex animo blasphemiis Turcicis Socinianorum contra Sacrosanctam Trinitatem, ac nominatim æternum Filium D E I addicti sunt, & earum publicam atque liberam professionem per dogmata illa quæ à me in primâ Parte Arcanorum expositá sunt, tanquam quam per cuniculos in Belgium invehere conantur: prout luce clariús meridianâ ex Secundâ Parte Arcanorum videre est. Quæ quidem blasphemiæ tales sunt & tàm atroces, ut non dubitem quin omnes honorati & honesti viri quibus illi hactenus imposuerunt eas ex animo detestentur, & Episcopium cum sociis suis detestaturi sint, ubi cognoverint eos blasphemiis illis imbutos esse. Corruit enim per eas totus Christianismus, & non nisi inanis larva illius relinquitur, ac perinde est, illis admissis, sive Turca quis, sive Judæus, sive Christianus sit. Quid enim? ut alia omittam, Jesum Christum non habere naturam divinam sed tantùm humanam; eum non fuisse antequam nasceretur ex Mariâ virgine! Sic igitur nos qui S. Trinitatem colimus, non verum Deum sed idolum colimus; prout Sociniani S. Trinitatem idolum, horrendum dictu, nominant. Cùm contra certum sit, illos, qui veram h. e. æternam Deitatem Filii non credunt, introducere horrendam idololatriam, utpote quâ non colitur unus ille & verus Deus qui se in tribus personis revelavit, ac solus colendus est; & quâ Creator rerum omnium Filius in locum creaturæ detruditur, ut verè Theodoritus ait. Unde patet, si blasphemiis Socinianorum locus detur, actum esse de salute nostrâ & posteritatis nostræ, quandoquidem nullus idololatra regnum Dei hæreditare potest, Scripturâ teste. Et, collapso isto præcipuo fundamento Christianismi, collabuntur alia duo quæ cum illo cohærent. Si enim Christus non est verus & æternus Deus, non potuit utique satisfacere pro nostris peccatis, & sic collabitur doctrina satisfactionis, quâ nititur salus nostra. Pariter si Christus non satisfecit pro peccatis nostris, utique ipsius justitia & meritum nobis imputari non potest ad justitiam, & sic corruit etiam doctrina de justificatione nostri coram Deo, quâ itidem innitur consolatio & salus nostra. Hæc quæ dico vera esse, vel ex eo patet, quòd Sociniani, quia Deitatem Christi negant, simul & satisfactionem Christi & justificationem nostri per Christum negant.
units.tr: Since I have things to say that particularly concern your Honours, I wished to inscribe your names on this book. Before coming to the main matter, I repeat what I said in the Second Part of the Arcana of Arminianism: whatever I have said about the Arminians, and whatever I shall say in future, I say only of certain ministers or theologians who call themselves Remonstrants. I have complained of these men, and I still complain; but not of the honourable men or the peoples whom they have until now shamefully deceived. For these people, thinking they are taught by ministers who differ from us only on the Five Articles, are in fact taught by men who, while pretending to hold the orthodox doctrine of the Trinity, are in their hearts devoted, like many of the old Antitrinitarian heretics, to the Turkish blasphemies of the Socinians against the most holy Trinity, and in particular against the eternal Son of God. They are trying to bring these blasphemies into Belgium openly and freely, as through a tunnel, by means of those doctrines which I set out in the First Part of the Arcana; as is clearer than the midday light from the Second Part of the Arcana. These blasphemies are so monstrous and atrocious that I do not doubt that all the honourable and upright men whom they have until now deceived will utterly detest them, and will detest Episcopius and his companions too, once they learn that these men are steeped in such blasphemies. For by them the whole of Christianity collapses, and nothing remains of it but an empty mask; and once they are admitted, it makes no difference whether someone is a Turk, a Jew or a Christian. For what, to omit other points, is it to say that Jesus Christ has not a divine nature but only a human one, and that he did not exist before he was born of the Virgin Mary? Thus we who worship the holy Trinity do not worship the true God but an idol, as the Socinians, horrible to say, call the holy Trinity an idol. On the contrary, it is certain that those who do not believe in the true, that is, eternal, Deity of the Son introduce a horrible idolatry, since the one true God, who revealed himself in three persons and alone is to be worshipped, is not worshipped by them; and the Creator of all things is thrust down into the place of a creature, as Theodoret rightly says. From this it is plain that if room is given to the blasphemies of the Socinians, our salvation and that of our posterity is undone, since no idolater can inherit the kingdom of God, as Scripture testifies. And when this chief foundation of Christianity has fallen, the two other doctrines that cohere with it fall too. For if Christ is not the true and eternal God, he could not indeed make satisfaction for our sins, and so the doctrine of satisfaction, on which our salvation rests, collapses. Likewise, if Christ did not satisfy for our sins, his righteousness and merit cannot be imputed to us for righteousness, and so the doctrine of our justification before God also falls, on which our comfort and salvation equally rest. That what I say is true is clear from this alone: that the Socinians, because they deny the Deity of Christ, deny at the same time both the satisfaction of Christ and our justification through Christ.

units.la: Ad caput rei venio. Cùm mense Octobri in Hollandiâ essem, incidi in libellum quendam quem isti homines (qui sibi licentiam quidvis audendi sumunt, non sine gemitu omnium bonorum) adversus V. V. A. A. scripserunt idiomate Belgico. In eo Διασυρμα sive traducunt Edictum vestrum superiore æstate adversus conventicula ipsorum promulgatum, & singulas illius partes atque periodos examinant. Scopus autem præcipuus istius Examinis & libelli est ostendere, teneri Vos, Viri Amplissimi, tolerare se & sua quę instituunt conventicula. Multa ibi congerunt argumenta desumta ab officio Magistratus, nec non subditorum piorum, item à suâ innocentiâ, quam in eo præcipuè collocant, quòd non doceant aliam aliquam peculiarem doctrinam quàm eam quæ in quinque articulis ipsorum consistit. Id quàm falsum sit, ipsi manifestum fecere in Vindiciis suis, quibus extra omne dubium posuerunt id cuius hactenus suspecti fuerant, nimirùm se simulare orthodoxam doctrinam de S. S. Trinitate, ex animo autem blasphemiis Socinianorum contra eam addictos esse; &, ut eas blasphemias introducere possint, alia multa horrenda dogmata tenere, quibus Libertinismum in doctrinâ animis hominum ingenerent: Quinque verò ipsorum articulos nihil aliud quàm prætextum suæ impietatis esse. Afferunt in eo libello & alias ratiunculas quibus si opponatur ea quę modò diximus, omnes illæ uno ictu concidunt.
units.tr: I come to the main matter. When I was in Holland in October, I came upon a little book which those men (who take to themselves the licence to dare anything, to the groaning of all good people) have written in the Dutch language against your Honours. In it they produce a Diasyrmos [Διασυρμα], that is, a derisive commentary, on the Edict your Honours issued last summer against their conventicles, and they examine each part and period of it. The chief aim of this examination and of the little book is to show that you, most distinguished Sirs, are bound to tolerate them and their conventicles, which they set up. There they heap up many arguments drawn from the duty of the magistrate, and likewise from the duty of pious subjects, and also from their own innocence, which they chiefly place in this: that they do not teach any peculiar doctrine other than that which consists in their Five Articles. How false this is they themselves made plain in their Vindiciae, in which they placed beyond all doubt what they had until now been suspected of: namely, that they pretend to hold the orthodox doctrine of the holy Trinity, but are in their hearts committed to the blasphemies of the Socinians against it; and that, in order to introduce those blasphemies, they hold many other horrible doctrines, by which they instil into men's minds Libertinism in doctrine; and that their Five Articles are nothing but a pretext for their impiety. In that little book they also offer other petty arguments, which, if we set against them what I have just said, all fall to the ground at one blow.

units.la: Mihi propositum non est examinare libellum istum. Quia tamen in eo hoc agunt, ut evincant ministri illi tolerandos se esse, & permitendum ipsis ut coetus sacros faciant, ac populum doceant; & ex altera parte in eo ipso tractatu nobis novam materiam suppeditant atque argumentum firmissimum quo decidi potest quæstio hæc: An'ne ministri qui se Remonstrantes vocant, tolerandi sunt? seu, An'ne illis permittendum sit ut populum doceant? hinc operæ pretium esse duxi, eam quæstionem perspicuè, breviter, & solidè nova ratione, hoc est, ex proprio ipsorum ore, decidere in hac præfatione.
units.tr: It is not my purpose to examine that little book. Yet because in it they aim to prove that those ministers ought to be tolerated, and that they should be allowed to hold sacred assemblies and teach the people; and because, on the other side, in that very treatise they supply us with new material and a most firm argument by which this question can be decided: Ought the ministers who call themselves Remonstrants to be tolerated? or, Ought it to be permitted to them to teach the people? I have thought it worth while in this preface to settle that question clearly, briefly and soundly, in a new way, that is, out of their own mouths.

units.la: Dicet forte aliquis, opus non esse ut haec decidatur à me, cùm ea dudum & judicio Synodi Dordracenæ & authoritate Illustrissimorum Ordinum, nec non etiam vestrâ, decisa sit. Hîc ego fateor quidem ea ita gesta esse, nec inficias eo opus non fore ut hæc quæstio decideretur, si illi homines quicquam alieno judicio deferrent, & legitimæ auctoritati obtemperarent. Quod quia ab ipsis non fit, videndum igitur est, an aliquid vel proprio suo judicio & decisioni sint delaturi? Quod si ab ipsis impetrari non potest, hoc saltè efficiemus, ut eò magis inexcusabiles sint, non solùm coràm Deo sed etiam hominibus, quando sibi injuriam fieri dicent dum non tolerantur. Accedit quòd non cessant scripta subinde edere, ex quibus illud est quod Edicto vestro oppositum erunt, in quibus ille præcipuus scopus ipsorum est, ut persuadeant hominibus, se tolerandos esse. Quare est è re Ecclesiæ & Reipublicæ, ostendere, quam injustum illorum ministrorum postulatum & molimen sit. Denique, cùm pro vestrâ pietate, ita ut par est, invigiletis prohibendis ipsorum coetibus, & permittere nullâ ratione velitis ut illi populum doceant; scitis, Amplissimi Domini, quàm contraria sint hominum judicia de illo vestro instituto & facto. Alii enim illud omnibus modis probant, alii autem vel sui causâ, vel quòd rem non intelligant, illud improbant. Quòd si igitur jam ex ipsorum ministrorum, qui se Remonstrantes vocant, ore proprio ostendamus ipsis injuriam non fieri; certè eò evidentior & notior erit bonitas causæ vestræ. Hinc enim fiet, ut qui nec nostris nec illorum partibus addicti sunt, sed, ut multi faciunt, neutram partem sequuntur, approbaturi sint (modò hæc legere velint) ea quæ à vobis in hac parte geruntur: contrà verò istorum Theologorum iniquitas eò clariùs elucebit, quandoquidem ἀυτοκατάκριτοι h. e. ex proprio suo ore convicti sunt, se immeritò tolerantiam sui à vobis & aliis Magistratibus postulare, & se nullam conquerendi occasionem de nemine quàm de se & violentis machinationibus suis adversum Reformatos habere.
units.tr: Perhaps someone will say that there is no need for me to settle this, since it has long been settled by the judgement of the Synod of Dort, by the authority of the Most Illustrious Lords States, and also by yours. Here I admit indeed that these things were so done, and I do not deny that there would be no need to decide this question again, if those men deferred to any judgement other than their own and obeyed lawful authority. Since they do not do this, we must see whether they will yield anything even to their own judgement and decision. If that cannot be obtained from them, at least we shall achieve this: that they are the more inexcusable, not only before God but also before men, when they say they are wronged because they are not tolerated. Moreover, they do not cease from time to time to publish writings, among which is the one that is set against your Edict, and in which their chief aim is to persuade men that they ought to be tolerated. Therefore it is in the interest of the Church and the Commonwealth to show how unjust the demand and the contrivance of those ministers is. Finally, since in your piety you watch, as is fitting, to prevent their assemblies, and you are unwilling on any ground to allow them to teach the people, you know, most distinguished Sirs, how contrary men's judgements are concerning that policy and act of yours. For some approve it in every way, while others disapprove of it, either for their own sake or because they do not understand the matter. If, then, we now show from the very mouths of these ministers who call themselves Remonstrants that no wrong is done to them, the goodness of your cause will surely become more evident and better known. For thus it will come about that those who are attached neither to our party nor to theirs, but, as many do, follow neither side, will approve (provided they are willing to read this) what is being done by you in this matter; while on the other hand the iniquity of these theologians will shine out the more clearly, since they are self-condemned [ἀυτοκατάκριτοι], that is, convicted out of their own mouths: that they demand toleration from you and the other magistrates undeservedly, and that they have no ground for complaint against anyone except themselves and their own violent machinations against the Reformed.

units.la: Ut igitur clarum fiat, quid de hac quæstione sentiendum sit, non jam allegabo alia argumenta, inter quæ hoc omnium instar esse potest, quòd Socinianis blasphematoribus & juratis hostibus Filii Dei, quales hos ministros esse, præcipuè autem M. Simonem Episcopium (hominem in quem tanquam in sentinam confluxit quicquid & impietatis, & malitiæ, & petulantiæ in veteribus Hæreticis Antitrinitariis fuit) Parte Secundâ Arcanorum ostendi, permittendum nequaquam est ut populum doceant. Vnicum tantummodò afferam, quod ipsi in libello contra vestram Potestatem scripto nobis suppeditant. In quo, postquam multa sophisticati essent pro Libertate exercitiorum Religionis, tùm in hypothesi tùm in thesi; movent tandem sibi ipsis objectionem, quæ in eo consistit, An ne igitur omnibus omninò sectis permittenda sit libertas exercitii Religionis? Et respondent, se duas sectas excipere à libertate illâ, quibus quidem ea concedenda nequaquam sit. Vna secta, inquiunt, est ea quæ doctrinam habet seditiosam & factiosam, seu quæ causa est seditionum; altera, quæ dependet à capite extraneo. Et addunt: Quæ autem ista duæ sectæ sint, inprasentiarum non necessarium est dicere. Sufficit quòd Remonstrantes tales non sint. Hûc redit summa verborum, quibus in idiomate vulgari utuntur. In quibus quidem verbis celare se profitentur Arcanam mentem suam: quare ea in lucem est protrahenda.
units.tr: So that it becomes clear what ought to be thought about this question, I will not now bring forward other arguments. Among them, this one can stand in for all: these ministers are Socinian blasphemers and sworn enemies of the Son of God, and it must by no means be allowed that they teach the people. This is especially true of M. Simon Episcopius, a man into whom, as into a sewer, everything of impiety, malice and insolence found in the ancient Antitrinitarian heretics has flowed. I showed this in Part Two of the Arcana. I will adduce only one point, which they themselves supply us in a booklet written against your authority. In it, after they have sophisticated a great deal in favour of liberty in the exercise of religion, both in hypothesis and in thesis, they finally raise an objection to themselves, namely: Then should freedom be granted to absolutely all sects? And they answer that they except two sects from that liberty, to which it certainly should not be granted. One sect, they say, is that which holds a seditious and factious doctrine, or which is the cause of seditions; the other is that which depends on a foreign head. And they add: What these two sects are, it is not necessary to say at present. It is enough that the Remonstrants are not such. This is the sum of the words they use in their vernacular. In these words they profess to conceal their secret mind; therefore it must be brought into the light.

units.la: Dicunt igitur duabus illis sectis non esse permittendum exercitium Religionis; nolunt tamen ibi dicere, quænam illæ sectæ sint. Salva res est. Quia enim nolunt earum sectarum nomina exprimere, nostrum est defectum illum supplere. Nam quod ad posteriorem sectam attinet; quamnam intelligant, facile est videre; nimirùm eam, quæ à Pontifice Romano, quem pro Capite Ecclesiæ habent, dependet. Quod cùm adeò per se clarum sit, miretur aliquis cur in eo libello noluerint nominare Pontificios. Causa in eo est posita, quòd Arminiani, circa tolerantiam Pontificiorum, inter se mutuò non conveniunt, aut sententiam suam vel mutant, vel contrarie proferunt, prout putant rerum suarum statum postulare. Nam in aliis tractatibus scribunt, Pontificiis esse permittendos conventus suos; prout fieri debere contendunt in Scripto cui titulum fecerunt Liber cultus Dei, anno 1627. nec non in Responsione ad Excerpta Cll. DD. Professorum vestrorum, in qua urgent par jus & privilegium sectarum omnium; denique in Vindiciis suis anno superiore adversum me editis, in quibus contendunt omnibus omnino sectis parem Libertatem Religionis concedendam esse. Hanc dissensionem aut levitatem suam, adeo turpem in re tanti momenti, non putarunt esse e re sua detegere ac propalare, eo ipso anno, quo scripserant in Vindiciis suis, esse Pontificiis concedendam in Belgio libertatem exercitii sui. Quae igitur posterior illa secta sit, jam manifestum est.
units.tr: They say, then, that the exercise of religion is not to be permitted to those two sects; yet they are unwilling to say there which sects these are. The matter is settled, however. Since they are unwilling to name these sects, it is our task to supply what they leave out. As for the latter sect, it is easy to see whom they mean: namely, the one that depends on the Roman Pontiff, whom they hold as the head of the Church. Since this is so plain in itself, someone may wonder why in that booklet they did not want to name the Papists. The reason is this: the Arminians do not agree among themselves about the toleration of the Papists, but either change their opinion or state it inconsistently, as they think the condition of their affairs demands. For in other treatises they write that the Papists are to be allowed their assemblies, as they contend should be done in the writing entitled Book of the Worship of God, in the year 1627; likewise in their Reply to the Excerpts of your learned professors, where they press the equal right and privilege of all sects; and finally in their Vindications published against me the previous year, in which they contend that absolutely all sects should be granted equal liberty of religion. They did not think it advisable to disclose or proclaim this disagreement, or this levity of theirs, so disgraceful in a matter of such importance, namely that in the very year in which they wrote their Vindications, liberty of exercising their worship should be granted to the Papists in Belgium. Which of these is the latter sect is therefore now clear.

units.la: De priore, quam etiam non tolerandam esse ajunt, major est difficultas, quam tamen ipsi nobis tollunt. Nam quamvis ibi dicere nolint, quaenam illa secta sit, alibi tamen id clarissime & sine ambagibus explicant. Etenim in Vindiciis suis, non contenti sunt dicere; idem quod in libello isto etiam dicunt, nimirum sectam illam tolerandam non esse, sed durioribus remediis coercendam, cuius doctrina factiosa, seditiosa, sive mater & fons seditionum per se sit, noxia Principibus & Rebuspublicis, lib. 2. c. 9. p. 171. sed praeterea etiam expresse nominant sectam illam. Dicunt enim ibi Reformatos esse sectam illam, cuius doctrina talis sit. Nam lib. 2. cap. 2. p. 174. inter alia verba quibus de ea re agunt, inquiunt: Videamus, an non pari imo majore jure horrescere possimus ex doctrina Vedelii (ita vocant doctrinam Reformatorum omnium, quos illi Calvinianos vocant, de praedestinatione & perseverantia Sanctorum) quae non ansam & occasionem sed CAUSAM eiusmodi sceleribus ac flagitiis praebere possunt, non tantum profanis & male perditis hominibus sed iis etiam qui doctrinae & fidei ipsius sunt retinentissimi. Et postquam doctrinam nostram de Praedestinatione & perseverantia Sanctorum ibi rum ibi calumniosissimè pro more suo propositissent, & affin-xissent ea nobis quæ in mentem nulli Reformato Theologo unquam venêre, addunt : Hoc axioma an non genio suo & vi insitâ Regnis, Principibus, Rebuspublicis, periculosissimum, & vitis Principum exitiale sit, cuivis pio &c. dijudicandum relinquo? Nam quæ machina aptior, quis stimulus acrior, qua ratio potentior concipi aut dari potest ad efferandum subditorum animos, qui privatim degeneres, in publicum exitiosi, nihil spei nisi per discordias habent, ad acuendum odia eorum ex quâlibet occasione, ut odio rerum suarum res novas moliantur, & honores, quos quietâ Republicâ desperant, perturbatâ consequantur, atque ita, ex motis facibus Reipublicæ, fortunarum suarum compendia quærant, quàm si credant ac firmiter sibi persuasum habeant nulla peccata ac flagitia sua efficere posse, ut gratiâ ac favore divino excidant? Nulla licet pacatissima imperia tuta sunt à motibus & paroxysmis, in quibus spiritus iste subditorum animos occupavit. Nec commerciorum fides constare potest, nec juramentorum Religio, nec conjugiorum fœdera, nisi vi contineantur. Quâ juvat quisque ibit, securus de futurâ gloriâ. Quis enim fidem fallere cum rerum suarum compendio dubitet, qui se id impunè coram Deo facere posse credit, & salvâ æternæ salutis suæ spe? Potentissimum ad flagitia calcar est impunitatis divinæ fiducia, & certa inter scelera de vitâ æternâ persuasio. Si publica vis & pœna metuitur, arcani licentia quæretur, & clàm fiet quòd palàm non licet. Hinc seditiones, proditiones, & arcana molimina, quæ fieri vix possunt, quin tandem aliquando in nervum erumpant, & Respublicas ac Regna intestinis motibus concutiant ac convellant. Et speciem dabunt mendacia, calumniæ, perjuria, falsa testimonia quæ eâdem impunitatis spe & sine ullo periculo aut detrimento salutis tutò fieri posse credentur, &c. Alia huius generis addunt pag. 75.
units.tr: The former sect, which they also say must not be tolerated, presents a greater difficulty, which nevertheless they themselves remove for us. For although they are unwilling to say there which sect it is, elsewhere they explain it most clearly and without circumlocution. Indeed, in their Vindications they are not content to say, as they say in this booklet too, that that sect must not be tolerated but restrained by harsher remedies, whose factious and seditious doctrine is in itself the mother and fountain of seditions, harmful to princes and commonwealths (book 2, chap. 9, p. 171); they also name that sect expressly. For there they say that the Reformed are that sect, whose doctrine is of such a kind. For in book 2, chap. 2, p. 174, among other words with which they deal with this matter, they say: Let us see whether we cannot shudder with equal or even greater right at the doctrine of Vedel (this is what they call the doctrine of all the Reformed, whom they style Calvinists, concerning predestination and the perseverance of the saints), which can provide not merely an occasion but the CAUSE of such crimes and outrages, not only to profane and thoroughly depraved men but also to those who are most tenacious of that very doctrine and faith. And after they had there most calumniously, as is their custom, set forth our doctrine of predestination and the perseverance of the saints, and attached to it things that never came into the mind of any Reformed theologian, they add: Whether this axiom is not, by its very nature and inborn force, most dangerous to kingdoms, princes and commonwealths, and deadly to the lives of princes, I leave for any pious person to judge, etc. For what machine can be conceived or devised more apt, what goad more sharp, what reasoning more powerful, for inflaming the minds of subjects, who are base in private and harmful in public, who have no hope except through discord, to sharpen their hatreds on any occasion, so that out of hatred of their own affairs they set in motion revolutions and obtain the honours which they despair of under a quiet commonwealth, and thus, by stirring the torches of the commonwealth, seek profit for their own fortunes, than if they believe and firmly persuade themselves that their sins and crimes cannot cause them to fall from the grace and favour of God? No kingdom, however peaceful, is safe from the disturbances and paroxysms into which this spirit has seized the minds of subjects. Neither the good faith of commerce, nor the religion of oaths, nor the bonds of marriage can stand, unless they are held by force. Each will go whither he pleases, secure about future glory. For who would hesitate to betray faith for the sake of his own profit, if he believes he can do so with impunity before God, and with his hope of eternal salvation intact? The most powerful spur to crimes is confidence in divine impunity, and a settled persuasion of eternal life amid wickedness. If public force and punishment are feared, licence in secret will be sought, and what is not allowed openly will be done in private. Hence seditions, treasons and secret machinations, which can hardly happen without at last breaking out into the sinews and shaking and convulsing commonwealths and kingdoms with internal upheavals. Lies, slanders, perjuries and false testimonies will also appear, which will be believed to be safely done with the same hope of impunity and without any danger or loss of salvation, etc. They add other things of this kind on page 75.

units.la: Nunc igitur intelleximus, quosnam Arminiani ministri intelligant per sectam illam priorem, cui negant permittendum esse exercitium Religionis; nimirùm Reformatos coetus, à quibus tamen ipsi tolerari cupiunt. Ubi diligenter expendenda causa
units.tr: Now, then, we have understood which sect the Arminian ministers mean by that former sect, to which they deny that the exercise of religion should be permitted: namely the assemblies of the Reformed, from whom nevertheless they themselves desire to be tolerated. Here the cause must be carefully weighed

units.la: * * causa est illa, propter quam loco allegato Vindiciarum negant, Reformatos tolerandos esse. Non enim ibi causam ponunt in eo, quod Reformati ipsos Remonftrantes tolerare nolint sed coercendos putent: sed eam in doctrinâ nostra ponunt. Verum est, eos in iisdem Vindiciis aliam etiam causam allegare, propter quam Reformati tolerandi non sint, sed durioribus remediis, ita enim ipsi loquuntur, coercendi. Nam lib. 2. cap. 9. pp. 166. 169. 171. nec non cap. 5. p. 108. collato cum eodem cap. 9. p. 171. & Refponf. ad Excerpta &c. p. 126. 127. 136. contendunt, ideò Reformatos coërcendos esse corporaliter, & non permittendum iis exercitium Religionis, quia facta multa admiserint in Belgio & extra Belgium, quibus schisma, seditio, rebellio, factio & alia crimina conjuncta sunt, quemadmodum vidimus Par. II. lib. 1. cap. 7. ubi etiam cap. 6. pluribus de priore causâ, quam in doctrinæ nostræ natura & genio collocant, egimus. Ita igitur quidem etiam illam alteram causam ponunt, sed ista prior causa singulariter consideranda est. Si enim Arminiani Theologi dicerent, Reformatis non esse permittendum exercitium Religionis suæ, ob eam tantùm causam, quòd talia facta, ut isti homines calumniantur, admisissent; speciatim autem quòd ipsos Arminianos ministros tolerare nolunt, videri possent aliquam excusationem habere in lege Talionis, & sensu, seu dolore, quo afficiuntur. Dicere siquidem possent, se ideò Reformatos tolerare non posse, sed durioribus remediis coërcendos putare, quia ipsi Reformati nolint eos tolerare; absque hoc foret, se libenter eos toleraturos esse. Hoc effugio jam uti & palliare se non possunt. Non contenti enim sunt dicere, se ob facta Reformatorum eos non tolerandos judicare; verùm etiam addunt, Reformatos ob doctrinam suam de prædestinatione & perseverantiâ Sanctorum, tolerandos nequaquam esse, sed durioribus remediis coërcendos esse. Adeóque dicunt, se in conscientiâ suâ teneri Reformatis eripere libertatem exercitii & Religionis suæ.
units.tr: * * is that cause for which, in the passage of the Vindications cited, they deny that the Reformed are to be tolerated. For there they do not place the cause in this, that the Reformed are unwilling to tolerate the Remonstrants themselves, but that they think them to be restrained; they place it in our doctrine. It is true that in the same Vindications they also allege another cause, on account of which the Reformed are not to be tolerated but are to be restrained by harsher remedies, for so they themselves speak. For in book 2, chap. 9, pp. 166, 169, 171, and likewise chap. 5, p. 108, compared with the same chap. 9, p. 171, and in the Response to the Excerpts, etc., pp. 126, 127, 136, they contend that the Reformed are therefore to be restrained bodily, and the exercise of religion is not to be permitted them, because they have committed many deeds in Belgium and outside Belgium, to which schism, sedition, rebellion, faction and other crimes are joined, as we saw in Part II, book 1, chap. 7; where also, in chap. 6, we treated at length of the former cause, which they place in the nature and genius of our doctrine. Thus, indeed, they also set down that second cause, but the first cause must be considered on its own. For if the Arminian theologians were to say that the Reformed are not to be permitted the exercise of their religion for this reason alone, that they had committed such deeds as these men slander them with, and specifically that they are unwilling to tolerate the Arminian ministers themselves, they might seem to have some excuse in the law of retaliation and in the feeling or resentment by which they are affected. For they could say that they do not think the Reformed can be tolerated but must be restrained by harsher remedies, because the Reformed themselves are unwilling to tolerate them; apart from this, they would gladly tolerate them. They can no longer use this escape or cover it over. For they are not content to say that they judge the Reformed not to be tolerated on account of the Reformed deeds; they also add that the Reformed, on account of their doctrine of predestination and the perseverance of the saints, are by no means to be tolerated, but must be restrained by harsher remedies. And so they say that they are bound in conscience to snatch from the Reformed the liberty of exercising their religion.

units.la: Cæterum Cæterùm hîc quærat aliquis, quænam duriora illa remedia sint (ita enim loquuntur Vindic. lib. 2. c. 9. p. 171.) quibus censent ministri Arminiani Reformatos, non Doctores solùm & Pastores, sed etiam alios quosvis coërcendos esse. Hoc ipsi etiam nobis aperiunt in Apologiâ, nec non in Vindiciis suis. Utrobique enim hanc maximam tradunt: Quando errantibus (seu revera illi errent seu videantur errare) non permittitur liberum exercitium Religionis, sed per vim extremam qualemcunque coërcitio eorum suscipitur, necessariò tandem ad sanguinem errantium & supplicium extremum veniendum esse, ac impossibile esse ut aliter fiat. Ita enim Apolog. cap. 24. f. 259. a. posteaquam contendissent nullas omninò coërcitiones errantium quę vi externâ qualicunque fit suscipiendas esse, causam inter alias hanc afferunt, quòd non solùm à qualicunque coërcitione facilis progressus ad sanguinem & ultimum supplicium errantium fit, sed etiam quod impossibile sit ut aliter fiat. Ita enim ibi: Quare si coërcitiones ullæ admittuntur, quid erit Christianismus aliud, quàm gladiatorum in se invicem concurrentium arena, ac mutua inque vicem rediens incarceratio, relegatio ac flagellatio? Hic itaque primus obex ponendus est, alioquin facilè ulterius ad sanguinem & cædem ibitur. Facilis ab unâ pœnâ ad aliam progressus est, & ubi semel horror pœnarum animo exemtus est, sanguis etiam tandem vilis haberi incipit. Nec prætextus desunt. Crudelitas dum sibi indulget, facile mantellum reperit, quo se tegit. Titulus novus novam pœnam postulat. Quid verò facilius quàm novum titulum fingere? Principiis obviam eundum est, ne sævitia gradum faciat, & ad culmen enitatur. Non enim consistit, nisi summum attigerit. Pœna pœnæ tegula est ne perpluatur, Nec fieri potest ut non tandem ad sanguinem veniatur, nisi ergastulorum, carcerum, insularum Chiliadas erigere velis, & vastitiem ubique facere. Quid enim? Si errantem pœna prima non coërceat, an non cum Tribuno isto dicetur, Cedo alteram, & alteram, & alteram donec tandem ad ultimum supplicium devenias, & tranquillitatem suam pretio sanguinis redimas? Ista sacra aliter non non constant, dum errantem sua impellit conscientia ut errorem profeminet, & te tranquillitatis carnalis consequenda aut retinenda propositum tenet. Et in eodem capite p.281. a. ubi ad Reges & Principes orationem instituunt, quaeos dehortantur, non solum ab Haereticidio, sed etiam a quacunque etiam moderata coercitione Haereticorum, inter alia sic ajunt. Nec moderata consilia credite quae saevissima quaque praeter solum sanguinem, suadent. Teter & aeternus carcer morte brevi deterior est. Exilium saepe miseriam habet, mors nunquam &c. Nec facile consistit crudelitas. Crudelitas hydrops est, quanto plus bibit tanto plus appetit, nec satiatur nisi sanguinem hauriat, eoque se ubi vult ingurgitet. Enimvero sanguinis odium consilia ista non suggerit, sed offensionis metus, ubi ille desinet sanguis postulabitur. A primo gradu pedem abstinete nisi progredi velitis. Alio pretio non constabit tandem tranquillitas vestra, nisi sanguinis? Et Vindiciarum lib. 2. c. 8. p. 151. adversus medisputant, quod dicam Haereticis resistendum a Magistratu esse. Et quaerunt, Qua coercitione Vedelie? &c. Dic ergo intra quam poenam eos (Magistratus) stare vis aut eos stare posse credis si pertendant Haretici aut Haereticorum Ecclesiae? Nam vel is nolis, ut tandem coercitio desinat in ultimum supplicium necesse erit, nisi carcerum atque ergastulorum numerum augere velis in infinitum usque. Et cap. 9. p. 164.165. multis pariter contendunt tandem necessario ad sanguinem veniendum esse, ac post multa concludunt: Qua vi tandem utemini, Proceres, ne contra regulam hanc generalem Vedelii peccetis & neglecti officii vestri ab eo postulemini? Adure, seca, veniendum vobis erit, & redeundum ad vomitum, totiusque Haeretica inquisitionis Tyrannis restituenda, hoc solum differas ab illa, quod illa Hispanica, haec Reformata Tyrannis vocabitur.
units.tr: Moreover, someone here may ask what those harsher remedies are (for so they put it in the Vindiciae, book 2, chapter 9, p. 171) with which the Arminian ministers think the Reformed should be restrained, not only the teachers and ministers but any others whatever. They themselves disclose this to us in their Apology and also in their Vindiciae. In both places they lay down this maxim: When erring men (whether they really err or only seem to err) are not permitted the free exercise of religion, but some kind of coercion is applied to them by extreme force, it must necessarily come at last to the blood and extreme punishment of those in error, and it is impossible for it to happen otherwise. So in the Apology, chapter 24, p. 259a, after arguing that no coercion of erring men by any external force should be undertaken at all, they give, among other reasons, this one: not only does any coercion at all lead easily to the blood and ultimate punishment of those in error, but it is also impossible for it to happen otherwise. Their words there are: Therefore if any coercion is admitted, what will Christianity be but an arena of gladiators fighting one another, and a mutual back-and-forth of imprisonment, banishment and flogging? Here, then, the first barrier must be set up, or else one will easily go further, to blood and slaughter. The step from one punishment to another is easy, and once the horror of punishments has been taken from the mind, blood too at last begins to be held cheap. Nor are pretexts lacking. While cruelty indulges itself, it easily finds a cloak to cover it. A new title demands a new punishment. And what is easier than to invent a new title? We must meet beginnings head on, so that severity does not take a step and strive for the summit. For it does not stop until it has reached the top. One punishment is a tile to keep out the rain on another. Nor can it happen that one does not at last come to blood, unless you want to erect thousands of workhouses, prisons and islands and make desolation everywhere. For what? If the first punishment does not restrain the erring man, will it not be said, with that Tribune, "Give me another, and another, and another, until at last you come to the ultimate punishment and buy your tranquillity with the price of blood"? Those sacred matters do not otherwise stand, while the erring man's own conscience drives him to spread his error, and holds you to the purpose of securing or keeping carnal tranquillity. And in the same chapter, p. 281a, where they address kings and princes and urge them to abstain not only from killing heretics but from any even moderate coercion of heretics, they say among other things: Do not believe moderate counsels, for the most savage counsels, apart from blood alone, urge you on. A foul and eternal prison is worse than a quick death. Exile often brings misery; death never does, etc. Nor does cruelty easily stop. Cruelty is a dropsy: the more it drinks, the more it craves, and it is not satisfied unless it drinks blood, and so it gorges itself wherever it wishes. Indeed, it is not hatred of blood that suggests these counsels, but fear of offence: wherever that blood ceases, blood will be demanded. Keep your foot back from the first step, unless you wish to go forward. Will your tranquillity at last cost you no price but blood? And in Vindiciae, book 2, chapter 8, p. 151, they argue against Vedelius that the magistrate must resist heretics. And they ask: By what coercion, Vedelius? etc. Say, then, within what penalty you want the magistrates to stand, or do you believe they can stand there if the heretics or the heretical churches press on? For unless you are unwilling, the coercion must in the end come to the ultimate punishment, unless you wish to increase the number of prisons and workhouses to infinity. And in chapter 9, pp. 164–165, they likewise contend at length that it must necessarily come at last to blood, and after much argument they conclude: By what force will you use at last, lords, so that you do not sin against this general rule of Vedelius, and be called to account by him for your neglected duty? Burn, cut: you will have to go back to the vomit and restore the whole tyranny of heretical inquisition. The only difference from that one will be that the Spanish tyranny was so named, but this will be called the Reformed tyranny.

units.la: Sic igitur ministri Arminiani sentiunt ac contendunt: Quando semel coercitio Haereticorum suscipitur, necessario tandem ad sanguinem veniendum esse, & aliter fieri non posse. Qua in re crudelissimum errorem errant. Nam in vetere Ecclesia etiam coercebantur Haeretici ab Imperatoribus, nec tamen ad sanguinem venem veniebant; imò ne quidem ad infinitos (quod impossibile est) carceres, ergastula, proscriptiones, exilia. In eo itaque differt coercitio quâ orthodoxi Magistratus Hæreticis resistendum sciunt, à coercitione quam Arminiani ministri necessariò adhiberi dicunt, ubi semel initium coercendi fit. Quòd scilicet orthodoxi dicunt & sciunt in coercitione errantium non necessario ad sanguinem veniendum esse, imò nunquam ad eum veniendum esse, nisi errantes sint insigniter blasphemi aut revera seditiosi: Arminiani autem ministri dicunt, ubi semel coercitio ulla suscipitur, fieri non posse ut non tandem ad sanguinem & ultimum supplicium deveniatur.
units.tr: So then the Arminian ministers think and contend this: once coercion of heretics is undertaken, it must necessarily come at last to blood, and it cannot happen otherwise. In this they err most cruelly. For in the ancient Church heretics were also coerced by the emperors, and yet they did not come to blood; indeed not even to endless prisons, workhouses, proscriptions and exiles (which is impossible). The coercion by which orthodox magistrates know that heretics must be resisted therefore differs from the coercion which the Arminian ministers say must be applied once a beginning of coercing is made. Orthodox men say and know that in coercing those in error it is not necessary to come to blood, indeed that one should never come to it, unless the erring men are notoriously blasphemous or really seditious. But the Arminian ministers say that once any coercion is undertaken, it cannot fail that one comes at last to blood and the ultimate punishment.

units.la: Atqui dicunt Arminiani, Reformatos coercendos esse & quidem durioribus remediis. Jungatur hoc cum eo quod etiam clamant; ad sanguinem necessariò tandem veniendum esse, ubi semel coercitio alicuius suscipitur. Itaque jam unusquisque videt quid hi homines adversus Reformatos moliantur, quâ doctrinâ animos suorum populorum imbuant, quem affectum in iis adversùm Reformatos ingenerare studeant. Docent enim ex unâ parte, non tolerandos esse Reformatos, non permittendum iis esse exercitium Religionis, sed eos coercendos esse, & quidem durioribus remediis: ex altera parte docent; Quando coercitio errantium suscipitur, & liberum exercitium Religionis ipsis non permittitur, necessariò tandem ad sanguinem & ultimum supplicium deveniendum esse. Videt jam unusquisque quid hi Theologi in animo habeant, quid meditentur, & quàm crudelia consilia agitent adversùm Reformatos? Scio contemni à quibusdam imperitis solere talia, quòd putent Theologos istos parùm virium habere ad exequenda molimina sua. Sed, ut alia jam non allegem, nôrunt rerum periti omnia mala quæ unquam orthodoxi ab errantibus perpessi sunt, persecutiones dico, cædes, incendia, eversiones non familiarum solùm sed & urbium, non urbium solùm sed & Regnorum, initia sua à malis & Hæreticis Theologis h.e. eorum suggestionibus & molitionibus nibus habuisse. Quantum malorum in toto orbe Christiano adversus eos qui Deum in tribus personis adorant, ab uno pres- bytero partibus Arii addicto profectum fuerit olim, nórunt qui veteris Ecclesiæ Historiam vel primis labris degustârunt. Recentiorum exemplorum plena sunt omnia.
units.tr: Yet the Arminians say that the Reformed should be coerced, and indeed with harsher remedies. Join this to what they also cry out: once the coercion of anyone is undertaken, it must necessarily come at last to blood. So now everyone can see what these men are plotting against the Reformed, with what teaching they imbue the minds of their peoples, and what feeling they strive to stir up against the Reformed. For they teach on the one hand that the Reformed are not to be tolerated, that they must not be allowed the exercise of religion, but must be coerced, and indeed with harsher remedies. On the other hand they teach: when coercion of those in error is undertaken, and the free exercise of religion is not permitted them, it must necessarily come at last to blood and the ultimate punishment. Now everyone can see what these theologians have in mind, what they are devising, and how cruel the plans they are shaping against the Reformed are. I know that such things are commonly despised by some unskilled people, who think these theologians have too little strength to carry out their designs. But, not to cite other examples, those who know affairs know that all the evils that orthodox men have ever suffered from those in error, I mean persecutions, slaughters, burnings, and the overthrow not only of families but of cities, not only of cities but of kingdoms, had their beginnings in the evil suggestions and machinations of heretical theologians. How much evil throughout the whole Christian world was once brought about against those who worship God in three persons by a single presbyter devoted to the party of Arius, those know who have tasted the history of the ancient Church even at the surface. Everything is full of more recent examples.

units.la: Jam igitur intelligitis, opinor, Amplissimi Domini, non tàm me quàm ministros Arminianos decidisse hanc quæstionē: an'ne sint tolerandi, seu anne ipsis permitti debeat ut populum doceant? Nam in iis ipsis scriptis quibus hoc agunt ut persuadeant se tolerandos esse à Magistratibus Reformatis, non continere sese possunt (tanta est eorum adversus omnes qui sincerè Reformatam Religionem profitentur acerbitas) quin dicant, etsi nos teneamur tolerare ipsos, sese tamen non teneri nos tolerare, aut nobis licitum exercitium Religionis permittere, sed contrà, non solùm ob facta nostra, verùm etiam ob doctrinam nostram, adeóque ex conscientiâ, teneri nos cocrcere; hanc autem coercitionem nostri non posse fieri sine sanguine, sed necessario in eâ ad ultima supplicia Reformatorum deveniendum esse. An'non igitur jam decidêrunt ipsi contra se quæstionem hanc? & an'non magis ac magis cogunt Reformatos Magistratus, ne ipsis permittant populum docere, seu conventus instituere sacrorum suorum causâ? Ecquî enim fieri possit ut Magistratus orthodoxi tolerent ministros tales, qui in iis ipsis scriptis quibus contendunt (contendunt autem & agunt hoc in omnibus) jus omne postulare ut sibi permittatur libertas Religionis suæ, dicunt simul & palàm profitentur se non teneri Reformatos tolerare, sed contrà ex conscientiâ teneri eos coercere, etsi planè persuasi sint hoc non posse fieri quin in sanguinem Reformatorum sæviant? Annon igitur jam quæstio ista soluta & decîsa ab ipsis est? Quis enim Reformatus tales tolerandos esse putet, qui expressè dicunt se Reformatos tolerare non posse ob doctrinam eorum de prædestinatione &c. nec posse illis libertatem Religionis permittere; quôs scit non solùm carceres & exilia sed etiam cædes adversus se spirare? imò quos scit firmiter credere, fieri non posse ut aliter Reformati quam sanguine suo coerceantur, & tamen eos coercendos esse? Quis serpentem sinu foveat, & non potius eum excutiat?
units.tr: Now, I think, you understand, most distinguished lords, that it is not so much I who have raised this question, but the Arminian ministers themselves: are they to be tolerated, or ought they to be permitted to teach the people? For in those very writings in which they labour to persuade that they must be tolerated by the Reformed magistrates, they cannot restrain themselves (so great is their bitterness against all who sincerely profess the Reformed religion) from saying that, although we are bound to tolerate them, they themselves are not bound to tolerate us or to permit us the lawful exercise of religion; on the contrary, that we are bound, not only on account of our deeds but also on account of our doctrine, and so in conscience, to coerce them; and that this coercion of ours cannot be carried out without blood, but that in it we must necessarily come to the ultimate punishments of the Reformed. Have they not, then, themselves already decided this question against themselves? And do they not more and more compel the Reformed magistrates not to permit them to teach the people, or to hold assemblies for their sacred purposes? For how could it happen that orthodox magistrates tolerate such ministers, who in those very writings in which they contend (and they contend and act on this in all of them) demand every right that the freedom of their religion be permitted them, and at the same time say openly and profess that the Reformed are not bound to be tolerated by them, but on the contrary are bound in conscience to be coerced by them, although they are fully persuaded that this cannot be done without raging against the blood of the Reformed? Has not this question then already been resolved and settled by themselves? For what Reformed man would think that men should be tolerated who expressly say that they cannot tolerate the Reformed on account of their doctrine of predestination, etc., nor can they grant them liberty of religion; whom he knows breathe not only prisons and exile but even slaughter against him; indeed whom he knows to believe firmly that the Reformed cannot be coerced otherwise than with their blood, and yet that they must be coerced? Who would warm a serpent in his bosom, rather than shake it off?

units.la: Quorsum hæc omnia commemoro? Non profecto, Amplissimi Domini, ut vos adversum Arminianos ministros, nedum populos (cum quibus ut dixi, res mihi non est) ipsorum irritem, tantùm abest ut suadeam illos ea ratione coercendos esse quam ministri ipsorum vobis & omnibus ex animo Religioni nostræ addictis præparant; sed ut omnes homines ubivis locorum intelligant, quam justam causam habeatis Vos, Amplissimi Domini, quòd vigilanter & serio resistendum his ministris ducitis; nec permittendum iis ut populum doceant, & funestis illis ac crudelibus maximis eum magis ac magis adversum Reformatas Ecclesias imbuant, & sensim instillent ipsis blasphemias Turcicas Socinianorum. Sed nolite mirari, istos ministros eo crudeli affectu erga Reformatos esse. Hic enim est affectus quem ab Antitrinitariis Hæreticis nunquam separari posse experientia veteris Ecclesiæ docet; nimirum quòd quemadmodum hostes Filii Dei sunt, ita etiam jurati hostes eorum sunt qui eum ut verum atque æternum DEUM honorant, & crudelissimis supplicis in eos sæviunt, ubi potentiam nacti sunt.
units.tr: Why do I recount all this? Certainly not, most distinguished gentlemen, so that you would stir up hostility against the Arminian ministers, let alone their people (with whom, as I have said, I have no business). I am far from advising that they be restrained in the way their ministers prepare for you and for all who are sincerely devoted to our religion. Rather, I want all people everywhere to understand how just a cause you have, most distinguished gentlemen, for resisting these ministers vigilantly and earnestly, and for not allowing them to teach the people and steep them more and more in their deadly and cruel hostility toward the Reformed Churches, and gradually instil into them the Turkish blasphemies of the Socinians. But do not be surprised that these ministers hold such a cruel attitude toward the Reformed. This is the attitude which experience of the early Church teaches can never be separated from the Antitrinitarian heretics: just as they are enemies of the Son of God, so too they are sworn enemies of those who honour him as the true and eternal God, and when they gain power they rage against them with the cruellest punishments.

units.la: Quare omnium piorum est, DEUM ardenter orare & in id pro viribus atque ex officio laborare, ut hæ Provinciæ liberentur istis Theologis Socinianis, quò populos (quibus tam turpiter prætextu quinque Articulorum imponunt) non porrò imbuant tam blasphemis quam crudelibus maximis suis, & adversus Reformatos instigent. Huic enim malo, quòd jam vehementer invaluit, nisi tandem occurratur, impossibile est, quin illi Theologi ad scopum suum perventuri sint, h. e. blasphemiarum Socinianarum contra Filium DEI professionem publicam introducturi, ac simul executuri sint molimina ista sua crudelissima adversum Ecclesias Reformatas. Utrumque clementer menter Deus avertat; quem etiam, ex animo veneror ut oculos aperiat iis quibus hactenus adeo turpiter isti ministri impoposuêre, quò videant quinque articulos non nisi merum prætextum esse, quo illi Theologi blasphemias Turcicas Socinianorum contra Filium Dei introducere conantur; id quod manifestissimum fecerunt in Vindiciis suis, quas prima Parti Arcanorum oppositæ. Eas Vindicias hac Quartâ Parte examino, & tollo prætextus quibus conatus suos nefarios palliare conantur; nec non manifestissimum facio, ministros illos αὐτοχαδακρίτως esse, & contra propriam suam conscientiam defendere pessimam causam suam. Boni igitur consulite, Magnifici & Amplissimi Domini, hunc laborem meum, qui nihil aliud sibi quàm assertionem gloriæ æterni Filii Dei, conservationem pietatis & Religionis Christianæ, pacem Ecclesiæ, & tranquillitatem Reipublicæ propositam habet: & divinâ benedictione quàm diutissimè & prosperrimè fruimini.
units.tr: Therefore it is the duty of all the godly to pray earnestly to God, and to labour to the utmost of their strength and according to their office, that these provinces may be freed from those Socinian theologians, so that they no longer steep the peoples (whom they so shamefully deceive under the pretext of the five Articles) in their blasphemies and in their most cruel designs, and stir them up against the Reformed. For unless this evil, which has already grown very strong, is at last checked, it is impossible that those theologians will not reach their goal, namely, to introduce a public profession of the Socinian blasphemies against the Son of God, and at the same time carry out their most cruel plans against the Reformed Churches. May God mercifully avert both. I also sincerely pray that he will open the eyes of those whom these ministers have hitherto so shamefully deceived, so that they may see that the five Articles are nothing but a mere pretext, under which those theologians try to introduce the Turkish blasphemies of the Socinians against the Son of God. They have made this most plain in their First Part of their Defences, which was set against the Arcana. In this Fourth Part I examine those Defences and remove the pretexts by which they try to cloak their wicked attempts. I also make it most evident that those ministers are self-condemned [αὐτοχαδακρίτως] and that they defend their wretched cause against their own conscience. Therefore, most distinguished and honoured gentlemen, take this labour of mine in good part. Its only aim is the vindication of the glory of the eternal Son of God, the preservation of piety and the Christian religion, the peace of the Church, and the tranquillity of the commonwealth. May you enjoy the divine blessing for as long and as prosperously as possible.

units.la: Scripsi Daventriæ 18. Febr. 1634.
units.tr: Written at Deventer, 18 February 1634.

units.la: V. V. A. A.
units.tr: Your Honours' most devoted servant.

units.la: Observantissimus
units.tr: Your most respectful servant,

units.la: NICOLAUS VEDELIUS.
units.tr: NICOLAUS VEDELIUS.

units.la: PRÆFATIO AD LECTOREM.
units.tr: PREFACE TO THE READER.

units.la: Qua examinantur ea quæ Arminiani præmiserunt primo Capiti Vindiciarum suarum.
units.tr: In which the points the Arminians put forward at the beginning of the first chapter of their Vindiciae are examined.

units.la: BEnevole Lector. Antitrinitarij Hæretici qui se Remonstrantium nomine tegunt & Orthodoxam doctrinam de Trinitate simulant, Titulum fecerunt Responso quod primæ parti Arcanorum opposuere, Vedelius Rhapsodus, seu Vindiciæ adversus calumnias Vedelij, &c. Quod Rhapsodum me vocant, ne faciunt pro solita maledicentia sua & petulantia. Sciunt ipsi me ex Confessione & Apologia sua protulisse dogmata de quibus conquestus in ea prima parte fui. Quod si virus suum in una saltem parte scriptorum illorum duorum sparsissent, eam saltem partem pressissem: Sed quia per totum corpus diffusum habet venenum serpens ille, ideo nunc ex una, nunc ex alia parte venenum exprimendum atque eliciendum fuit. Et hac agendi ratio, qua ego usus sum, non nova est, sed in ipsa vetere Ecclesia usitata & laudata. Sicubi enim aliquis Hæretica dogmata scriptis suis sparserat, illi qui Orthodoxam doctrinam profitebantur Doctores, ut orbi offenderent eum dogmata damnata fovere, non describebant integros libros illius, sed excerpebant ex scriptis ejus loca quæ continebant in se falsa dogmata. Ita sub Adriano Imperatore cum Basilides Hæreticus venenum suum scriptis spargeret, Agrippas Castor librum scripsit, quo Arcana exposuit Hæretici illius, & ostendit quid ille hinc inde in scriptis suis portentosi statueret, ἐκφαίνων τὰ ἀπόρρητα αὐτοῦ, proferens Arcana ipsius &c. ait de eo Eusebius lib. 4. cap. 7. Ob quem modum agendi non ut Rhapsodus traducitur Agrippas Castor etsi e scriptis Basilidæ hinc inde excerpsit et dogmata arcana illius; Sed plurimum ab Eusebio commendatur scriptum illius, tanquam ἱχνευτικὸν καὶ βασιλείδου ἔλεγχον τὴν δεινότητα τῆς τ'ἀνδρὸς ἀπο-καλύψεως γενέσεως, ait Eusebius. b. e. tanquam demonstratio quâ sufficientissimè notatus fuit Basilides, & quâ egregiè præstigiosa illius Hæretici impietas è latebris eruta & detecta fuit.
units.tr: Gentle reader. The heretical Antitrinitarians, who hide behind the name of the Remonstrants and pretend to the orthodox doctrine of the Trinity, have given the title "Vedelius the Rhapsodist, or Vindications against the calumnies of Vedelius, etc." to the answer they have set against the first part of my Arcana. They call me a rhapsodist out of their usual slander and impudence. They know that I have taken the doctrines I complained of in that first part from their Confession and Apology. But if that serpent had spread its poison in only one part of those two writings, I would have pressed only that part. Because the serpent has its venom spread through the whole body, the poison had to be squeezed out and drawn forth now from one part and now from another. This method of proceeding, which I have used, is not new, but was customary and praised in the ancient Church itself. For whenever some heretic had scattered his heretical doctrines in his writings, the teachers who professed orthodox doctrine, so that they might show the world that he was nourishing condemned doctrines, did not copy out his books whole, but excerpted from his writings the passages that contained false doctrines. So under the Emperor Hadrian, when the heretic Basilides was scattering his poison in writings, Agrippa Castor wrote a book in which he set out the secrets of that heretic and showed what that monstrous man taught here and there in his writings, "bringing forth his secrets," as Eusebius says of him in book 4, chapter 7. Agrippa Castor is not reproached as a rhapsodist for this method, even though he excerpted from the writings of Basilides here and there and set out his secret doctrines. Rather, Eusebius greatly commends his writing as a "tracking down and refutation of Basilides," that is, as a demonstration by which Basilides was most fully exposed and by which the monstrous impiety of that heretic was dragged out of its hiding places and detected.

units.la: Similiter cùm Marcellus Ancyra in Galatin Episcopus tempore Constantini Magni librum edidisset quo Photinianarum (quibus Arminiani ministri infecti sunt) blasphemiarum opinionem de se concitarat; Synodus Constantinopoli coacta ad Ecclesias Galatiæ rem perscribit, & ut ea intelligant, quam ob rem ob rem Marcellum Episcopatu depositissent Episcopi, non totum librum illius subjungit Epistola sua ob prolixitatem illius, sed Excerpta quaedam inserie Epistola, ex quibus pateret eum addictum esse haresi Photinianæ, ut Sozomenus refert lib. 2. cap. 31. ἡ δὲ διὰ μὲν τὸ πολύστοιχον, inquit, τῆς γραφῆς μὴ τὸ πᾶν ὑπολάβοι βιβλίον ἐπιλωβῶν. μετὰ δὲ τινα ἐπέδηκαν τῇ αὐτῷ ἐπιστολῇ πρὸς ἔλεγχον τὸ δοξάζειν αὐτὸν τάδε h. e. significarunt porrò Episcopi se non totum librum Marcelli subjunxisse, idque ob prolixitatem illius: interim tamen inseruerunt dicta quaedam seu loca illius, ex quibus manifestum esset eum istis opinionibus imbutum esse. ob hunc modum agendi etiam non reprehenduntur Episcopi illi, aut tanquam Rhapsodi traducuntur: Sed hoc saltem quaerebatur, vere ne an calumniose Marcellus accusatus, & juste ne an injuste condemnatus fuisset. Me autem vere & non per calumniam conquestum esse de his ministris Parte prima Arcanorum, norunt ipsi in conscientia sua prout ex hac parte iv. luce clarius meridiana patebit. Ut adeo mera protervia sit qua imponere Lectori volunt, dum in eodem titulo dicunt me ipsos calumniatum esse.
units.tr: Similarly, when Marcellus, Bishop of Ancyra in Galatia, in the time of Constantine the Great, had published a book by which he drew upon himself the suspicion of the Photinian blasphemies (with which the Arminian ministers are infected), a synod gathered at Constantinople wrote about the matter to the churches of Galatia. So that they might understand why the bishops had deposed Marcellus from his episcopate, they did not append his whole book to their letter, because of its length, but inserted certain excerpts from it, from which it would be plain that he was attached to the Photinian heresy, as Sozomen reports in book 2, chapter 31. "But because of the length of the writing," he says, "they did not take the whole book, but," and afterwards "they appended to the same letter, as proof, the things he taught." That is, the bishops signified that they had not appended the whole of Marcellus' book, and that this was because of its length. Nevertheless, they inserted certain sayings or passages of his, from which it would be evident that he was steeped in those opinions. These bishops are not blamed for this method of proceeding, nor are they reproached as rhapsodists. Rather, the only question was whether Marcellus had been accused truly or by calumny, and whether he had been condemned justly or unjustly. That I have complained truly, and not by calumny, about these ministers in the first part of the Arcana, they know in their own conscience, as will be clearer than the midday light from that part, as it has been seen. So it is sheer shamelessness that they wish to impose upon the reader when, in the same title, they say that they have been calumniated by me.

units.la: Caterum praemittunt capiti primo Vindiciarum suarum nonnulla quae breviter excutienda sunt.
units.tr: Moreover, they prefix to the first chapter of their Vindiciae some points that must be briefly examined.

units.la: PRIMO, ante Epistolam dedicatoriam suam, ex S. Hilario meo seu Antidoto contra tristitiam, odium atque aversationem non tam mei quam doctrinae Reformatae animis suorum & aliorum qui controversiarum imperiti sunt, instillare volunt. Citant ex c. 3. istius libelli mei tria loca. Primus locus est, quo dixi in Inferno multos infantes esse. Quae cantilenam etiam ante hac in Apologia c. 4. p. 57. b. Clarissimis Theologis Proff. Leydd. occinunt. Qua ratione nihil aliud agunt quam ut se Haereticos Pelagianos, me ante Orthodoxum ostendant. Est enim haec constans doctrina veteris & modernae Ecclesiae orthodoxae, quae ita secundum verbum Dei sentit de infantibus iis qui in foedere gratia non constituti sunt, quales sunt infantes Judaeorum, Turcarum, Paganorum. Hi enim infantes infecti sunt non, minus ac infantes Christianorum, Peccato originali, quod, cum vere peccatum sit, certe stipendium illius mors est. Rom. 6. 21. Unde & mors in infantes regnat, teste eodem Apostolo Rom. 5. 14. ubi per mortem intelligit etiam condemnationem, prout ipse se explicat v. 16. 17. Hoc reatu liberantur soli infantes Christianorum. Ad hos enim solos pertinet foedus gratiae & promissio vitae aeternae, nec non signum & sigillum foederis h. e. Baptismus. Quare de Christianorum infantibus non pronunciamus eos damnari. Sed vere fideles & pios parentes suis liberis, non solum post, sed & ante Baptismum, orbatos solamur certa spe vitae aeternae. aterna, qua David solabatur se ob jacturam filioli sui mortui ante circumcisio-nem 2.Sam. 12.23. Imò ne quidem Christianorum idololatrarum & Hære-ticorum, qui fœdus illud quantum in se est annihilarunt, infantes damnamus; sed illos occulto Dei judicio relinquimus, quem non dubitamus Electos suos inter eos quoque habere, qui, quia nobis ignoti sunt, Deo autem notissimi, ma-lumus, ex Charitatis Christiana affectu, bene sperare de singulis, quàm hunc aut illum infantem damnare.
units.tr: FIRST, before their dedicatory letter, they want to instil, out of my St. Hilary, or Antidote against sadness, hatred and aversion, not so much towards me as towards the Reformed doctrine, in the minds of their own people and of others who are inexperienced in controversies. They cite three passages from chapter 3 of that little book of mine. The first passage is where I said that there are many infants in Hell. This is a tune which they have already sung before, in chapter 4, page 57 b of their Apology, to the most distinguished theologians of the Leiden professors. In this they do nothing other than show themselves to be heretical Pelagians and me to be orthodox. For this is the constant doctrine of the old and modern orthodox Church, which judges, according to the word of God, concerning those infants who are not established in the covenant of grace, such as the infants of Jews, Turks, and pagans. For these infants are tainted with original sin no less than the infants of Christians, and since it is truly sin, its wages are certainly death (Rom. 6. 21). Hence death also reigns over infants, as the same Apostle testifies (Rom. 5. 14), where by death he understands also condemnation, as he himself explains (vv. 16, 17). Only the infants of Christians are freed from this guilt. For the covenant of grace and the promise of eternal life, as well as the sign and seal of the covenant, that is, Baptism, belong to these alone. Therefore we do not pronounce that the infants of Christians are damned. But we truly console faithful and pious parents who have been bereaved of their children, not only after but even before Baptism, with the sure hope of eternal life, as David consoled himself over the loss of his little son who died before circumcision (2 Sam. 12. 23). Indeed, we do not even condemn the infants of idolaters and heretics who, as far as they could, have annulled that covenant. Rather we leave them to the hidden judgment of God, whom we do not doubt has his elect among them too, who, since they are unknown to us but most known to God, we prefer, out of Christian charity, to hope well of each of them rather than to condemn this or that infant.

units.la: Alia ratio est infantum qui extra fœdus gratia nati sunt. Hi enim reatu peccati originalis non liberantur, quo liberari nemo potest, nisi per Dei gra-tiam. Iam autem fœdus gratiæ, & promissio vitæ æternæ, nec non signum fœ-deris, quod est Baptismus, ad eos non pertinet, adeòque nec vita æterna; sed sub condemnatione manent. Quamvis non dubitemus cum Augustino En-chirid. c. 92. profiteri, pœnas infantium mitissimas esse, si comparentur cum pœ-nis eorum qui actualibus peccatis condemnationi se obnoxios fecerunt, præser-tim si comparentur cum pœnis eorum qui voluntatem Domini sciverunt & tamen non fecerunt. Quamvis illa quoque pœna non damni tantùm in nescio quo Limbo ut Pontificij fingunt, sed etiam sensus sint Scriptura teste. Hæc est Orthodoxa doctrina de salute & damnatione infantium, quam sententiam non novam sed universa veteris Ecclesia testatur August. l. b. 1. de peccator. merit. & remiss. cap. 28.
units.tr: There is another case, that of infants born outside the covenant of grace. For these are not freed from the guilt of original sin, from which no one can be freed except by the grace of God. Now the covenant of grace, the promise of eternal life, and the sign of the covenant, which is Baptism, do not belong to them, and so neither does eternal life; they remain under condemnation. Yet, with Augustine in the Enchiridion, chapter 92, we do not doubt to profess that the punishments of infants are the mildest, if they are compared with the punishments of those who have made themselves liable to condemnation by actual sins, especially if they are compared with the punishments of those who knew the will of the Lord and yet did not do it. Although that punishment too is not merely loss of God, in some limbo, as the Papists imagine, but is also of the senses, as Scripture testifies. This is the orthodox doctrine on the salvation and damnation of infants, a view which is attested not as something new but by the whole of the ancient Church (Augustine, book 1 On the Merits and Remission of Sins, chapter 28).

units.la: At aliter Arminiani Ministri sentiunt. Quia enim peccatum originale cum Pelagio Hæretico negant; hinc etiam cum eo negant infantes eorum qui extra fœdus gratiæ sunt constituti damnari. Certè si peccatum originale nul-lum est, causa damnationis in nullis infantibus esse potest. Hinc Augusti-nus contra Julian. Pelag. lib. 3. c. 5. egregiè ait: Si nullum esset primi peccati originale contagium, profectò nulli malo parvuli obstricti, nihil mali vel in corpore vel in animâ sub tantâ justi Dei potestate paterentur. Quare manifestissimè patet verum esse quod paulò ante dixi, Arminianos, dum illud mihi & cæteris Reformatis objiciunt, nihil aliud agere quàm ut se Pelagianos & Socinianos, (nam eum errorem Pelagij de Peccato Originali sequitur quoque Socinus, cujus blasphemiis & Hæresibus toti perfusi hi ministri sunt) Hæreticos, nos autem Orthodoxos esse ostendant. Et patet quoque exinde, Arminianos ministros non agnoscere gratiam Christi erga infantes; id quod haud obscurè Augustinus Pelagianus objicit loco alle-gato contra Julian. Pelag. Hæc-si sapias, inquit, simpliciter & veraci-ter gratiam Christi erga parvulos confiteberis. Ita secundùm hos novos Pelagianos, gratia Christi non extendit se ad infantes, sed damnatione illi sine ea eximuntur.
units.tr: But the Arminian ministers think otherwise. For since they deny original sin with the heretic Pelagius, they also deny with him that the infants of those who are outside the covenant of grace are damned. Certainly, if there is no original sin, there can be no cause of damnation in any infant. Hence Augustine, against Julian the Pelagian, book 3, chapter 5, rightly says: "If there were no contagion of the first sin, surely no little ones, bound by no evil, would suffer any evil in body or soul under such power of the just God." Therefore it is most plainly evident that what I said a little earlier is true: when the Arminians object this to me and the other Reformed, they do nothing other than show themselves to be Pelagians and Socinians (for Socinus too follows Pelagius' error on original sin, and these ministers are wholly steeped in his blasphemies and heresies), and show us to be orthodox. It is also evident from this that the Arminian ministers do not acknowledge the grace of Christ towards infants. This Pelagian objection Augustine has not obscurely pointed out in the passage cited against Julian the Pelagian: "If you were wise," he says, "you would confess simply and truly the grace of Christ towards little ones." Thus, according to these new Pelagians, the grace of Christ does not extend to infants, but they are rescued from damnation without it.

units.la: Quare confitemur nos cum Gallicis Ecclesiis (Confess. art. XI.) Credimus hoc vitium (peccatum Originale) esse vere peccatum, quod omnes & singulos homines ne parvulis quidem exceptis adhuc in utero matrum delitescentibus æternæ mortis reos coram Deo peragat. Et cum Ecclesijs Belgicis art. 15. Est autem peccatum Originis corruptio totius naturæ & vitium hæreditarium, quo & ipsi infantes in matris utero polluti sunt &c. essque tam turpe & execrabile coram Deo ut ad universi generis humani condemnationem sufficiat. Hæc paulo uberius de hac re dicenda fuerunt. Cetera percurram brevitatis studio.
units.tr: We therefore confess with the Gallican Churches (Confess. art. XI.) that we believe this vice (original sin) is truly sin, which makes all and each human being, not even infants excepted, still hidden in their mothers' wombs, guilty of eternal death before God. And with the Belgic Churches, art. 15. Original sin is the corruption of the whole nature and a hereditary vice, by which even the infants themselves are polluted in their mother's womb, etc., and it is so foul and detestable before God that it suffices for the condemnation of the whole human race. These things had to be said somewhat more fully on this matter. I will run through the rest briefly.

units.la: Displicet etiam Arminianis ministris, quod in eodem S. Hilarij loco dico: Quot sunt damnati, qui quamvis sine Dei timore in hoc mundo vixerint, crimina tamen forsan tam gravia, aut graviora saltem quam tu patrasti, nunquam commisere? Tandem quot adjudicati sunt atque adjudicabuntur igni æterno, qui probitati studere Deumque sese colere putabant &c. Quid igitur? an non verum est, eos qui sine vero Dei timore vixerunt, ut ut alioquin in speciem honeste egerint, damnari? Monstrent mihi igitur in Scriptura locum, qui salutem assignet iis qui sine vero Dei timore, adeoque sine vera fide sunt. Et an non contra tota Scriptura clamat, multos gravissimos peccatores, qui atrocissima crimina commiserunt, salvari per gratiam Dei in Christo Iesu, ubi resipuerint & vera fide ad ipsum confugerint? An non denique docet Scriptura eos adjudicatos esse igni æterno qui cum colere Deum se putent, eum tamen non colunt, quia vivant sine fide, & pro regula actionum suarum non habuerunt sanctam Dei voluntatem in verbo ejus revelatam? qua ultima verba, in quibus nervus rei consistit, ibi immediate subjeci, qua boni hi viri a cæteris separarunt & truncarunt.
units.tr: These men of the Arminian ministry also take offence at what I say in the same passage of S. Hilary: How many have been condemned who, though they lived in this world without the fear of God, never committed crimes so grave, or at least graver than those you committed? Finally, how many have been and will be adjudged to eternal fire who thought they strove for righteousness and worshipped God, etc.? What then? Is it not true that those who lived without the true fear of God are condemned, even though otherwise they behaved honourably in outward appearance? Let them show me, then, a passage of Scripture that assigns salvation to those who are without the true fear of God, and so without true faith. And does not all Scripture cry out, on the contrary, that many very grave sinners, who have committed the most atrocious crimes, are saved by the grace of God in Christ Jesus, when they have repented and fled to him with true faith? Does Scripture not finally teach that those are adjudged to eternal fire who think they worship God and yet do not worship him, because they live without faith and have not taken the holy will of God revealed in his word as the rule of their actions? I have placed these last words, in which the substance of the matter lies, immediately after, which these good men have separated off and mangled.

units.la: Similiter invidiam mihi ex p. 109. S. Hilarij conflare volunt, quod ibi dixi: Licet in te residuæ sint infirmitates complurimæ, quas caro per opera sua & peccata exserit quotidie, nihilominus tamen illâ fratris tui primogeniti togâ occultantur teguntur-que, justitiâ dico Christi. Quin & peccata ipsa saluti tuæ inserviunt. Hæc quo fine allegent facile videre est, ac si scilicet nos hominibus pulvillos subderemus, & portam aperiremus licentiæ peccandi, quæ quidem solita ipsorum calumnia est. Sed quemadmodum Scriptura docet, Sanctissimos quosque in hac vita carnem circumferre, adeoque peccare quotidie, ea tamen peccata ipsis propter Christum non imputari: ita calumniam illam unusquisque à me retusam videt ibidem. Addidi didi enim immediatè hæc verba quæ pariter dedita opera & malitiâ hi homines truncârunt: Quin & peccata ipsa, dicebam, saluti tuæ inservi-unt, in quantum (exprimo verba mea Gallica quia Latinam versionem Doctissimi Viri Galli Parei ad manus nunc non habeo) experientia turpitudinis ipsorum te excitat ad odium eorum, atque efficit ut magis ea fugias, magis quoque te humilies, & in posterum prudentius vivas.
units.tr: Similarly, they wish to stir up ill will against me from p. 109 of S. Hilary, because I said there: Although many residual weaknesses remain in you, which the flesh puts forth daily through its works and sins, nevertheless they are concealed and covered by the robe of that firstborn brother of yours, I mean the righteousness of Christ. Indeed, even the sins themselves serve your salvation. It is easy to see with what purpose they cite these words, as if, of course, we were placing cushions under men and opening a gate to licence for sinning, which is indeed their customary slander. But just as Scripture teaches that all the holiest people in this life carry the flesh about and so sin daily, yet those sins are not imputed to them for Christ's sake, so every reader sees that this slander was refuted by me in the same place. I added for I immediately added these words, which these men likewise, deliberately and with malice, cut out: Indeed, the sins themselves, I said, serve your salvation, insofar as (I give my French words, since I do not now have at hand the Latin version of the most learned man Gallus Pareus) the experience of their foulness stirs you up to hate them, and makes you flee them more, humble yourself more, and live more prudently in future.

units.la: Ex eodem calumnia fonte citant ex cap. 5. pag. 202. solutionem objectionis, quæ pij nonnunquam tentantur adversus fiduciam in providentia divina collocandam, quæ tentatio ex conscientia peccatorum oritur. Respondera enim, Deum non obstantibus demeritis nostris esse bonum nostrum Patrem cœlestem, quia nos non amat consideratos in nostra persona, sed propter Christum. Et intuleram: Quamobrem certissimus esto amoris ipsius adversum te, non obstantibus tuis iniquitatibus, quibus castigationes ejus tibi quidem attrahis, sed in commodum tuum ac salutem.
units.tr: From the same source of slander they cite, from chapter 5, p. 202, the answer to the objection that the godly are sometimes tempted not to place their trust in divine providence, a temptation arising from the consciousness of sins. For I answered that God, notwithstanding our demerits, is our good heavenly Father, because he does not love us considered in our own person, but for Christ's sake. And I had concluded: Therefore be most certain of his love toward you, notwithstanding your iniquities, by which you indeed draw his chastisements upon yourself, but for your advantage and salvation.

units.la: Quæ ultima verba ipsis displicent, unde ea peculiari charactere expresfære.
