Sed, præterquam quod jam ostendimus quomodo ipsa peccata dixerimus cedere in salutem peccatoris vere resipiscentis: quis non discit ex Scriptura verissimum esse, castigationes quas nobis per peccata attrahimus cedere in commodum ac salutem nostram? Et, siquidem sucum Lectori facere noluissent, debebant addidisse ea verba quibus ibidem judico quomodo id fiat? dum scilicet per castigationes paternas suas testatur curam filiorum suorum quos per correctiones istas à ruina & exitio præservare vult. Si hæc illis displicent, litem moveant Spiritui S. qui pronunciat: ijs qui diligunt Deum omnia simul adjumento esse ad bonum. Rom. 8. 23. ut alia plurima loca omittam. Atque hæc quidem de locis illis, S. Hilarij nostri, quæ, ad invidiam causæ nostræ creandam apud imperitiores, Dedicationi suæ præmiserunt.
units.tr: These last words displease them, and for that reason they have expressed them in a special typeface. But, apart from the fact that we have already shown how I said the sins themselves turn to the salvation of a sinner who truly repents, who does not learn from Scripture that it is most true that the chastisements we draw upon ourselves by sins turn to our advantage and salvation? And if they had not wished to be unfair to the reader, they ought to have added the words in which I go on to explain how this happens, namely that by his paternal chastisements he bears witness to his care for his sons, whom through these corrections he wishes to preserve from ruin and destruction. If these things displease them, let them pick a quarrel with the Holy Spirit, who declares: To those who love God, all things work together for good. Rom. 8. 23. Not to mention many other passages. And these things, concerning those passages of our S. Hilary, which they prefaced to their Dedication to stir up ill will against our cause among the less learned, are enough.

units.la: AD SECVNDVM
units.tr: TO THE SECOND POINT

units.la: venio quod est Epistola Dedicatoria eorum, in quâ se purgare & commendare, me autem & Reformatas Ecclesias accusare atque odiosas reddere nituntur: &, ut rei utriusque veritas scilicet manifesta fiat provocant non semel ad ipsum librum h. e. ad suas Vindicias. Ut igitur illi eo Lectorem remittunt, ita ego ad Secundam, Tertiam, & nunc Quartam Partem Arcanorum, quas ipsorum vindicijs opposui provoco. Ex harum enim lectione manifestum fiet nullum verbum veritatis esse in omnibus illis quæ aut pro se aut contra nos dicunt in ea præfatione. Percurramus eam breviter. Initiò dicit se ea credere & docere quæ non modò non sunt Christianæ Religioni noxia, sed Reformatæ ipsius Religionis quam nobiscum (inquiunt ad Amplissimum Magistratu Daventrienfem) profitemini, principijs apprime sunt consentanea, vestræque Rei-publicæ publicæ & patriæ nostræ salutaria. item: se Religionis Christianæ & quidem Reformatæ amorem quod attinet, in eo nulli cessisse hacte-nus, nec etiamnum cedere. Item, se salutis Reipublicæ studiosissimos esse, maxime pro exteris. Quæ quàm falsa sint, patet præsertim ex secunda parte Arcanorum, qua contrarium luce clarius meridiana ostendimus. Unde etiam patet, hos simulatores Antitrinitarios non leve convitium facere Amplif-simo & Orthodoxo Magistratui Daventriensi, eumque proterve ca-lumniari, dum dicunt eum eidem Religioni cum ipsis addictum esse.
units.tr: I come now to their Dedicatory Epistle, in which they strive to clear and commend themselves, while they try to accuse me and the Reformed Churches and make us hateful. To make the truth of both matters plain, they more than once appeal to the book itself, that is, to their Vindiciae. Just as they send the reader there, so I appeal to our Second, Third, and now Fourth Parts of the Arcana, which I have set against their Vindiciae. For from reading these it will become clear that there is not a word of truth in all the things they say in that preface, whether in their own favour or against us. Let us run through it briefly. First, they say that they believe and teach things which are not only not harmful to the Christian religion, but are very consonant with the principles of the Reformed religion which you profess with us (they say to the most distinguished magistracy of Deventer), and beneficial to your commonwealth and our fatherland. Likewise: as far as love of the Christian religion, and indeed the Reformed one, is concerned, they have yielded to no one up to now, nor do they yield now. Likewise, they are most zealous for the welfare of the commonwealth, especially of foreigners. How false these things are is clear above all from the second part of the Arcana, where we have shown the contrary more clearly than the noonday light. From this it is also plain that these dissembling Antitrinitarians do no small insult to the most distinguished and orthodox magistracy of Deventer, and shamelessly slander it, when they say that it is attached to the same religion as they are.

units.la: Dicunt porro, se in id laborare, ut tueantur primarium fundamentum de perspicuitate Scripturæ contra nos, quos inquiunt Ecclesiæ auctoritate pugnare. Quorum illud falsum esse patebit ex cap.7. lib. 1. §. 1. hoc vero calumniam esse dico, quam in æternum probare non possunt.
units.tr: They further say that they labour to defend the primary foundation of the perspicuity of Scripture against us, whom they say fight against it by the authority of the Church. That the first of these is false will be clear from chapter 7, book 1, §1. The second, however, I call a calumny, which they can never prove.

units.la: Inde post calumniam quà exterorum in his provinciis agentium fideli-tatem impudenter petunt, ut vidimus Par. 11. lib.1. cap.10. §. 5. veni-unt ad Libertinismi crimen quod ipsis objeci, & significationes tres vo-cis illius proponunt. Quarum prima est, qua denotantur Libertini adver-sus quos Calvinus scripsit, & quos ita Bellarminus etiam vocat, quem ibi citant. Ac impingunt nobis per calumniam Libertinismum illum, nisi fun-damentis mendacissimis, ac si sciliet nos venditaremus Spiritum proprium; ac si verbum Dei excluderemus à vera fidei productione; item ac si actionum malarum futuritionem suspenderemus à divina gratia negatione, non autem à Libero arbitrio hominis; ac si satum introduceremus, nec non ex illius fati lege mala omnia ac peccata consequi diceremus; ac si statueremus homines non suâ culpa sed fato perire; qui autem salvantur inter scelera ac flagitia salva-ri posse, denique reprobos per nulla bona opera (quæ professe reprobis verè non conveniunt) salvari posse doceremus. Increpet te Deus calumniator Satana!
units.tr: Then, after the calumny by which they shamelessly seek the good faith of foreigners working in these provinces, as we saw in Part 11, book 1, chapter 10, §5, they come to the charge of Libertinism which I brought against them, and set out three meanings of that word. The first of these is that by which the Libertines are meant, against whom Calvin wrote, and whom Bellarmine also calls by this name, whom they cite there. And they falsely charge us with that Libertinism, on the basis of most lying foundations, as if we were selling off our own spirit; as if we excluded the word of God from the true production of faith; as if we made the future of evil actions depend on the denial of divine grace and not on the free will of man; as if we introduced fate, and said that all evils and sins follow from the law of that fate; as if we held that men perish not through their own fault but through fate; and that those who are saved can be saved amid crimes and wickedness; and finally that the reprobate can be saved through no good works (which in fact do not properly belong to the reprobate). May God the slanderer rebuke you, Satan!

units.la: Sed quid si ego Arminianis ministris objiciam dogma turpissimum quod cum illà Libertinorum specie ipsis commune est? Docebant Libertini, teste inter alios Bellarmino, (quem circa Libertini descriptionem allegant hic Ar-miniani) lib. 2. de amissione gratia cap. 1. licere simulare in negocio Religionis, & cum Pontificijs Pontificiè, cum Lutheranis Lutheranè vivere. At simulare in negocio Religionis non solum docent Arminiani ministri, ut videre est ex Par. 1. lib. 2. cap. 2. & Par. iv. lib. 2. c. 2. (ubi ad effugia, quibus verissimam hanc accusationem sophisticè eludere conantur, respondimus) sed etiam praxi suâ id palàm faciunt, dum simulant ortho-doxam doctrinam de Trinitate, cùm tamen ex animo addicti sint blasphemiis Turcicis Socinianorum contra eam, ac nominatim contra æternum Filium Dei.
units.tr: But what if I were to charge the Arminian ministers with a most shameful doctrine, which they hold in common with that species of Libertines? The Libertines taught, as Bellarmine among others testifies (whom the Arminians cite here in their description of Libertines), in book 2 of On the Loss of Grace, chapter 1, that it is permitted to dissemble in matters of religion, and to live as a Papist among Papists and as a Lutheran among Lutherans. But the Arminian ministers teach dissembling in matters of religion, as is clear from Part 1, book 2, chapter 2, and Part 4, book 2, chapter 2 (where we answered the evasions by which they try to elude this most true accusation with sophistry); and they also do this openly by their practice, when they feign the orthodox doctrine of the Trinity, while in their hearts they are devoted to the Turkish blasphemies of the Socinians against it, and especially against the eternal Son of God.

units.la: Inde veniunt Arminiani ad secundam significationem, quam dicunt in eo consistere ut DIVERSIS sectis libera indulgeat sua Religionis exercitia, & inquiunt se hunc Libertinismum profiteri, & ne quidem nomen detrectant illud. Verum enim vero Arminiani fraudulenter utuntur voce DIVERSIS. Volunt quippe hic videri, ac si tantum diversis, non autem omnibus sectis libertatem illam concederent. Sed revera volunt, quod OMNIBUS sectis, praecipue autem Socinianis Haereticis libertas exercitiorum suorum, & quidem par concedenda sit. Hoc patet ex doctrina Apologia de Libertate prophetandi. Patet etiam ex Vindic. lib. 2. cap. 4. p. 107. ubi dicunt: Hinc est quod Remonstrantes tolerari velint OMNES errantes. Et eodem lib. 2. cap. 9. pag. 167. Quid criminis in eo esse potest, si Remonstrantes in ista libertate patria nati atque educati OMNIBUSQUE subditis vestris PAREM libertatem optantes profiteantur &c. Item quod tum in his Vindiciis tum in Respons. ad Excerp. CLL. DD. Proff. Leydd. Par jus omnium sectarum esse contendunt. Sic in hac ipsa Dedicatione sua dicunt. Fieri ne potest, ut qui eam libertatem, sibi ipsi salvam cupiunt, aliis eam jure ullo invideant? Item post unam paginam dicunt, necessario concedendam esse aut plenam libertatem aut nullam. Itaque imponere hic student Lectori, dum dicunt se tantum diversis sectis libertatem Religionis concedendam urgere. Interim tamen eos inde Reformatos excipere, & illis negare concedendam libertatem conscientiarum, vidimus in praecedente Epistola Dedicatoria nec non Par. II, lib. 1. Unde jam patet eos frustra palliare se velle auctoritate aliorum Theologorum, nec non praxi harum Provinciarum & majorum nostrorum. Nec enim ulli Theologi Reformati, ut de aliis jam nihil dicam, unquam dixerunt omnibus sectis concedendam esse libertatem Religionis sua; nec ha Provincia illud unquam in usu habuerunt in hunc usque diem, praesertim autem Socinianos nunquam ne in solo quidem Provinciarum harum ferre, nedum iis libertatem exercitij permittere voluerunt; nec denique Belgae sub persecutione talem libertatem omnibus sectis concedendam postularunt. Et sic cetera quae ibidem addunt impertinentia sunt. Ineptum vero est, & signum non vulgaris aut insciitiae aut malitiae, quod fingunt nos ad Libertatem conscientiarum relinquere nihil aliud quam ut concedatur cuique libertas intra animum suum sentiendi, quod verum esse judicet, & alimentum quoque ac pabulum conscientiarum necessarium contendunt. Qua re ostendunt ad minimum se Tyrones esse in doctrina de Libertate conscientiarum. Sed de hac re infra suo loco lib. 2. aliquid monebimus, ut & de Lege illa Natura quam hic impertinenter pertinenter detorquent: Quod tibi non vis fieri alteri ne feceris.
units.tr: Next the Arminians come to the second meaning, which they say consists in this: that the DIVERSIS sects be granted the free exercise of their own religion, and they say that they profess this Libertinism and do not even shun the name. But in truth the Arminians use the word DIVERSIS dishonestly. For they want it to appear here as if that liberty were granted to different sects only, and not to all sects. But in fact they want liberty of their own exercises to be granted equally to OMNIBUS sects, and especially to the Socinian heretics. This is clear from the doctrine of the Apologia de Libertate prophetandi. It is also clear from Vindic. book 2, chapter 4, p. 107, where they say: Hence it is that the Remonstrants wish all erring persons to be tolerated. And in the same book, chapter 9, p. 167: What crime can there be in this, if the Remonstrants, born and brought up in this country of liberty, and desiring equal liberty for OMNIBUS your subjects, profess etc. Likewise, in these Vindiciae as well as in the Respons. ad Excerp. of the most learned and distinguished professors of Leiden, they contend that there is an equal right for all sects. So they say in this very Dedication of theirs: Can it be that those who wish that liberty to be safe for themselves should by any right begrudge it to others? Likewise, a page later they say that either full liberty or none must necessarily be conceded. So they try here to deceive the reader, when they say that they urge the granting of religious liberty only to the different sects. Yet meanwhile we have seen in the preceding Dedicatory Epistle, and also in Part 2, book 1, that they exclude the Reformed from this and deny them the liberty of conscience to be granted. From this it is now plain that they try in vain to cloak themselves with the authority of other theologians, and with the practice of these provinces and of our forefathers. For no Reformed theologians, to say nothing yet of others, ever said that liberty of religion should be granted to all sects; nor has this province ever had that custom down to this day, and especially it never wished to tolerate the Socinians, not even in the territory of these provinces, much less to permit them liberty of worship; nor finally did the Belgians, under persecution, ever demand such liberty for all sects. And so the other irrelevant things they add in the same place are beside the point. It is, however, absurd, and a sign of no ordinary ignorance or malice, that they pretend that we leave to liberty of conscience nothing more than that each person be allowed freedom to think within his own mind whatever he judges to be true, and that they also claim this is the necessary nourishment and food of conscience. By this they show that at least they are novices in the doctrine of liberty of conscience. But we shall say something more about this matter below in its proper place, in book 2, and also about that law of nature which they twist here irrelevantly: What you do not wish done to yourself, do not do to another.

units.la: Tandem veniunt ad tertiam significationem Libertinismi, quam dicunt ex mea definitione, esse amorem Religionis miscellæ; & dicunt me sibi hunc Libertinismum tribuere. Quod etsi jure facere possem, tamen falsum est me ipsis attribuisse. Ego enim id non dixi, necejus rei accusavi hactenus vel ullo verbo istos homines, sed conquestus sum eos Ecclesiam miscellam ex omnibus sectis facere velle, relicta unicuique sua Religione, (Religio autem ab Ecclesia differt) integra. Quod verissimum esse patet, tum ex aliis quæ à nobis in quatuor Partibus Arcanorum expositæ sunt, tum speciatim ex Par. I. lib. 2. cap. 5. collato cum hac parte IV. lib. 2. c. 5. ubi effugiys, quibus eludere conantur notitiam criminis in quo deprehensi sunt, obviam imus.
units.tr: Finally they come to the third meaning of Libertinism, which they say is, by my definition, a love of a mixed religion; and they say that I attribute this Libertinism to them. Although I could rightly do so, it is nevertheless false that I have attributed it to them. For I have not said this, nor until now have I accused these men of this thing by any word, but I have complained that they wish to make the Church a mixture of all sects, each person's own religion being left whole (religion, however, differs from the Church). That this is most true is clear both from the other things set out by us in the four Parts of the Arcana, and specifically from Part 1, book 2, chapter 5, compared with this Part 4, book 2, chapter 5, where we meet the evasions by which they try to elude the knowledge of the crime in which they were caught.

units.la: Quod ibidem dicunt Necessariorum dogmatum fidem inviolatam servare apicem esse Religionis suæ, item suum scopum esse tolerantiam mutuam instituere, curare schismata & dissidia Christianitatis: denique quod dicunt de charactere Necessariorum, id omne quàm illusorium sit, patet ex Par. I. lib. 1. capp. 6. 3. & lib. 2. cap. 5. nec non Par. IV. lib. 1. capp. 6. 8. & lib. 2. cap. 5. Quibus adjiciatur, quod ex Par. II. lib. 1. luce clarius meridiana constat, scopum eorum præcipuum esse introductionem Socinianorum blasphematorum in Ecclesiam Dei. Hæc scilicet est præclara illa tolerantia mutua, quam hactenus tantopere venditarunt. Manet itaque firmissimum quod conquestus sum, eos Libertinismum in doctrina invehere velle, quia unicuique permittunt in Confessione & Apologia sua sentire & docere de omnibus {controversis dogmatis quod ipsi rectum videtur esse, & omnes eos qui errant in controversis quibuscunque dogmatis habent pro vera Ecclesia, & salvari posse cum suis erroribus contendunt, modo tolerare velint Socinianos apertos & simulatores. Quam suam mentem & doctrinam etsi palliare conentur, & ad declinandam invidiam negent se ita docere; revera tamen eos ita docere patet tum ex Par. III. Arcan. lib. 2. cap. 1. tum ex hac parte IV. speciatim lib. 1. c. 6. b. & lib. 2. capp. 1. 2. Quare certissimum est hos homines Libertinismum in doctrina invehere, id quod faciunt in hunc præcipuè finem, ut introducere possint blasphemiarum Socinianarum professionem publicam, prout patet ex toto lib. 2. Par. II. nec non ex tota hac Parte quarta. Et sic constat eos falsò dicere in fine præfationis suæ, me calumniari eos, ac non nisi ad invidiam ipsis faciendam Libertinismum impingere. Hæc etiam de præfatione ipsorum Dedicatoria.
units.tr: What they say in the same place, that keeping the faith of the necessary doctrines inviolate is the sum of their religion, and likewise that their aim is to establish mutual tolerance and to take care of the schisms and divisions of Christianity; and finally, what they say about the character of the Necessary doctrines, how entirely illusory all of this is, is clear from Part I, book 1, chapters 6 and 3, and book 2, chapter 5, as well as Part IV, book 1, chapters 6 and 8, and book 2, chapter 5. To these may be added that, as is clearer than the noonday light from Part II, book 1, their chief aim is the introduction of the blasphemous Socinians into the Church of God. This, of course, is that splendid mutual tolerance which they have so greatly puffed up until now. So what I complained of stands firm: they wish to bring Libertinism into doctrine, because they permit each man, in their Confession and Apology, to think and teach about all controverted doctrines whatever he judges to be right, and they regard as the true Church all who err in any controverted doctrine whatever, and contend that these can be saved with their errors, provided only that they are willing to tolerate open and disguised Socinians. Although they try to cloak this their mind and doctrine, and deny that they teach in this way in order to avoid odium, it is nevertheless plain that they do teach so, both from Part III, Arcana, book 2, chapter 1, and from this Part IV, especially book 1, chapter 6 b, and book 2, chapters 1 and 2. Therefore it is most certain that these men bring Libertinism into doctrine, and they do so chiefly for this end: that they may be able to introduce a public profession of Socinian blasphemies, as is plain from the whole of book 2 of Part II and from the whole of this fourth Part. And thus it is established that they speak falsely at the end of their preface, when they say that I slander them and fasten Libertinism on them only to make them odious. These things are also said about their dedicatory preface.

units.la: TERTIUM quod præmittunt Vindiciis suis, consistit in proœmio seu præludio, quod exhibent pag. 1. & seqq. usque ad cap. 1. Quo vel præcipuè puè isti homines manifestum faciunt quo spiritu agantur, nimirum maledi-centia ac petulantia digna Haereticis Antitrinitarijs . Nihil enim continent nisi scommata histrionica & comica, quibus in personam meam scurriliter & inhoneste involant. Quibus examinandis si insisterem, stulte agerem, & stulto secundum stultitiam suam responderem. Res loquatur, & judicet inter me & hos inimicos Sacro Sanctæ Trinitatis. Et sufficiat mihi repetere sententiam quam ipsi adversus se pronunciarunt: Remonstrantes sciunt se propter convitia æternum maledictum iri. Sed de hac re monuimus nonnihil Par. II. lib 1. cap.10. Praetereo igitur omnia illa, & scurrilitatis ac petulantia juvenilis, quam, apud suos praesertim, quaerunt, lauream libenter ipsis concedo. Quo fine autem ista petulantia speciatim in proœmio isto, usi fuerint, ostendi Par. III. Prolegom. cap.6. nimirum hoc praecipue, ut menequitia istius sua partasum piisce mutiorem redderent, quemadmodum M. Episcopum certo futurum praedixerat.
units.tr: THIRDLY, what they put forward in their Vindiciae consists of the prologue or preamble, which they present on page 1 and following, up to chapter 1. In this above all these men make plain what spirit drives them, namely a slanderous and wanton spirit worthy of the Antitrinitarian heretics. For it contains nothing but theatrical and comic jests, with which they scurrilously and dishonourably assail my person. If I were to dwell on examining these, I would be acting foolishly, and would be answering a fool according to his folly. Let the matter speak for itself and judge between me and these enemies of the Most Holy Trinity. And it will suffice for me to repeat the sentence which they themselves have pronounced against themselves: the Remonstrants know that they will be eternally cursed on account of their reproaches. But I have said something about this matter in Part II, book 1, chapter 10. I therefore pass over all those things, and I gladly concede to them the laurel of scurrility and youthful wantonness, which they seek especially among their own people. But I have shown in Part III, Prolegomena, chapter 6, for what end they used this wantonness particularly in this preface, namely chiefly so that they might make the reputation they had won among the godly the more maimed, just as Mr. Episcopius had foretold would surely happen.

units.la: Duo saltem occurrunt, quae tribus, quod ajunt, verbis indicanda aut expendenda sunt. Primo enim pag. 5. fatetur conceptis verbis Episcopius, se ipsum Clarissimum virum (quod solet etiam in Apologia ) appellans, Epistolam quam secunda Editioni Arcanorum addideram, suam esse, adeoque nec à Clarissimis Theol. Proff. Leydd. nec à me ipsis affictam: Denique, inquit, ut Coronidem Prologo dignam imponeret, Epistolam Clarissimi Viri M. Simonis Episcopi ante tredecim annos scriptam, & nunc, quod felix faustumque sit, prisca latinitate donatam, subtexit, in qua, tanquam in Democriti puteo, abdita & arcana Remonstrantium omnia apparent tanquam in suffumigato Speculo. Meminerit autem Lector, de qua re agatur in ea Epistola. Causas inibi exponit Episcopius, propter quas non expediat Remonstrantibus, tum Confessionem fidei edere, tum arctiorem conjunctionem cum Lutheranis inire. Relegat Lector, si ipsi grave non est, Epistolam eam quam subjecimus calci Editionis secundae, Partis primae; maximè autem eam relegat, postquam Episcopius expressè fatetur Epistolam istam suam esse, nec poenitentia judicii sui ducitur de societate arctiore cum Lutheranis non ineunda. Et sic judicandum relinquo Ecclesiis & Doctoribus Lutheranis an non turpissimè ipsis imposuerint Ministri Arminiani, & an non rectè fecerint Ecclesia Reformate quod istos Theologos in suo corpore tolerare noluerint.
units.tr: At least two points occur which must be indicated or weighed in, as they say, three words. For first, on page 5 Episcopius expressly admits that he himself (calling himself, as he is accustomed to do also in the Apology, "a most distinguished man") wrote the letter which I had added to the second edition of the Arcana, and so it was neither fabricated by the most distinguished professors of theology at Leiden nor by me. Finally, he says, in order to place a crown worthy of the Prologue, he appended a letter of the most distinguished man, Mr. Simon Episcopius, written thirteen years ago and now, happily and auspiciously, given a classical Latin dress, in which all the hidden and secret things of the Remonstrants appear as if in a smoked mirror, as in the well of Democritus. Let the reader remember, however, what matter is treated in that letter. Episcopius there sets out the reasons why it is not expedient for the Remonstrants either to publish a Confession of faith or to enter into a closer union with the Lutherans. Let the reader, if it is not troublesome to him, re-read that letter which we subjoined at the end of the second edition, Part I; and let him especially re-read it now, since Episcopius expressly admits that the letter is his, and he is not repentant of his judgement about not entering into closer fellowship with the Lutherans. And so I leave it to the Lutheran churches and teachers to judge whether the Arminian ministers have not most shamefully deceived them, and whether the Reformed Church has not rightly refused to tolerate those theologians in its body.

units.la: Alterum quod in petulanti isto proœmio occurrit est, quod pp. 6.7.8. redeunt ad calumniam qua nobis Libertinismum impingunt illum quem Calvinus
units.tr: The second point that occurs in this wanton preface is that on pages 6, 7 and 8 they return to the calumny by which they fasten on us that Libertinism which Calvin

units.la: *** *, vinus refutavit, de qua calumnia jam ante monuimus. Quare rursus eam diluere superuacaneum nimis foret.
units.tr: *** *, ...vinus refuted, a calumny concerning which we have already warned before. Therefore it would be altogether superfluous to refute it again.

units.la: Tandem inquiunt me, qui ipsis Libertinismum tribuo, eo sensu quem & in prima parte cap. 1. & paulo ante expositum, id facere nova prorsus atque inusitata significatione, & me finxisse illam significationem, atque abusum esse, praeter communem morem, voce Libertinismi. Sed hic ego omnium Christianorum qui Deum in tribus personis adorant judicium appello, annon hi homines ob axiomata & dogmata quibus tantam in Religione licentiam invebunt Libertinorum nomen mereantur? & annon ea significatio recepta sit in tota Christianitate? Verum hi homines libenter mundo persuaderent se non Libertinismum, sed Libertatem conscientiarum docere & tueri. Quod quam falsum sit, vel ex eo patet, quod istis dogmatis eorum, quae in Arcanis protulimus, & in quibus illi libertatem conscientiarum collocant, admissis, necessum omnino est blasphemias Turcicas Socinianorum contra S. Trinitatem plenis velis equisq; admittere. Atq; de his, pie Lector, te monere necessum fuit. Nunc qualiter h. e. quam improbe & contra conscientiam suam oppugnent Primam Partem Arcanorum expende. Videbis quam deplorata & desperata horum simulatorum Antitrinitariorum, & contra quam pia & justa nostra causa sit. Vale.
units.tr: Finally they say that I, who attribute Libertinism to them, do so in the sense which I explained both in Part I, chapter 1, and a little before, namely in a wholly new and unusual meaning, and that I have invented that meaning and have misused the word Libertinism, contrary to common custom. But here I appeal to the judgement of all Christians who adore God in three persons: do not these men, on account of the axioms and doctrines by which they introduce such great licence in religion, deserve the name of Libertines? And has not that meaning been received throughout the whole of Christendom? Indeed these men would gladly persuade the world that they teach and defend not Libertinism but liberty of conscience. How false this is may be seen even from this: if the doctrines of theirs which we have set forth in the Arcana, and in which they locate liberty of conscience, are admitted, it is absolutely necessary to admit with full sails and oars the Turkish blasphemies of the Socinians against the Holy Trinity. And about these things, pious reader, it was necessary to warn you. Now weigh, in the First Part of the Arcana, how wickedly, that is, how contrary to their own conscience, they attack it. You will see how desperate and hopeless these dissembling Antitrinitarians are, and how pious and just our cause is against them. Farewell.

units.la: ARCANORVM ARMINIANISMI Partis Quartæ LIBER PRIMUS.
units.tr: ARCANORUM ARMINIANISMI Pars Quarta, LIBER PRIMUS.

units.la: CAPUT PRIMUM.
units.tr: CHAPTER I.

units.la: Examen Capitis primi lib. 1. Vindiciarum.
units.tr: Examination of the first chapter of the first book of the Vindiciae.

units.la: 1. ARMINIANI fraudulenter eludere conantur receptam significationem vocis Hæreseos sive Hæretici ab autore prolatam. 2. Eorum insignis protervia quâ accusant auctorem falsitatis in re quam conceptis verbis fatentur. Arminiani fatentur se docere, sciri hodiè non posse quis sit Hæreticus in significatione usitatâ Ecclesiæ Christianæ. 3. Fatentur se docere Hæresin quæ sic communiter vocatur non esse peccatum. 4. Nec esse blasphemiam. 5. Non negant se docere Hæresin communiter sic dictam non esse impietatem, sed innocentiam & quidem summam; Hæreticos eos quos Orthodoxi Theologi sic vocant, speciatim Antitrinitarios esse homines pios, piissimos; non esse noxios saluti animarum, nec Ecclesiæ & Regno Christi, nec Reipublicæ; item Eos veniam mereri apud Deum solo bono affectu suo, & sic salvos fieri æternum. 6. Arminiani frustrà eludere conantur significationem receptam vocis Atheismi. Meliores homines qui dicantur Arminianis? 7. Hypocriticè eludere conantur significationem allatam vocis Religionis. Horrenda impietas Arminianorum circa mysterium Trinitatis cultumque veri Dei.
units.tr: 1. The Arminians try by sleight to evade the accepted meaning of the word heresy or heretic as the author has put it forward. 2. Their remarkable obstinacy, by which they accuse the author of falsehood on a point which they admit in plain words. The Arminians admit that they teach that it cannot be known today who is a heretic in the usual sense of the Christian Church. 3. They admit that they teach that heresy, as it is commonly called, is not a sin. 4. Nor is it blasphemy. 5. They do not deny that they teach that heresy, as commonly so named, is not impiety but innocence, and indeed the highest innocence; that those whom orthodox theologians so call heretics, especially the Antitrinitarians, are pious and most devout men; that they do not harm the salvation of souls, nor the Church and kingdom of Christ, nor the commonwealth; likewise that they earn pardon from God by their good disposition alone, and so are saved for eternity. 6. The Arminians try in vain to evade the accepted meaning of the word atheism. Are they the better men who are called Arminians? 7. They hypocritically try to evade the meaning I gave of the word religion. The horrible impiety of the Arminians concerning the mystery of the Trinity and the worship of the true God.

units.la: 1. [woodcut initial] APITE primo suarum Vindiciarum arrodunt Arminiani terminorum Hæreseos, Atheismi, Religionis significationes à me prolatas. Et primò quidem explicationem seu significationem vocis Hæreseos. Dixeram ego: Hareticum tota Ecclesia Christiana inde ab initio in hunc usque diem vocavit eum, qui Hæresiarcham aliquem sequutus negat doctrinam aliquam fundamentalem & ad salutem necessariam inter Christianos controversam. Quales Hæretici verbi gratia sunt Antitrinitarij, h. e. Photiniani, Socinians, Ariani &c. quos tota Ecclesia Christiana qua Deum in tribus personis adorat habet pro Hæreticis. Sumsi autem ibi vocem Hæretici, ut unusquisque ex verbis meis videt, stricte pro Hæretico simplice & qui contradistinctus est Hæresiarchæ. Hic quia istis hominibus tanquam simulatoribus Antitrinitariis summopere displicet judicium Ecclesiæ ex verbo Dei contra Antitrinitarios latum; insurgunt pagg. 9. 10. 11. contra vocis illius significationem à me propositam; eo prætextu quòd ista, inquiunt, DEFINITIO bona non sit, & nemo unquam ita DEFINIERIT Hæreticum. Et afferunt quatuor ratiunculas quibus probare conantur istam DEFINITIONEM quam dicunt me attulisse bonam non esse. Verum enimvero ista mera fraudulentia est. Nam ego nullam proposui definitionem Hæreseos nec Hæretici; nec id mihi propositum fuit. Saltem ostendi in quâ significatione vocem Hæretici sumat Ecclesia tota quæ Deum in tribus personis adorat. Hinc dixi Hæreticum VOCAT Ecclesia &c. Quod quantum distet à definitione, manifestum est. Et sic concidunt omnia illa Sophismata eorum. Quare aliud nihil addam, nisi quòd prætereundum non est, quod dicunt in Sophismate quarto, consistente in eo, quòd ideò definitio ea bona non sit quia deest formale Hæreseos. Vbi inquiunt Clarissimos DD. Professores Leydenses de formali Hæretici statuere etiam malitiam. Sed hoc calumniosissimè dicunt pro more suo Arminiani. Nam in loco illo ad quem Arminiani respiciunt, qui est Cens. Confess. cap.24. §.9. distinguunt modò laudati Viri Clarissimi coercitionem Hæretici simplicis à coercitione Hæretici malitiosum actum voluntatis conjunctum habentis. Ex quo manifestum est eos non ponere malitiosum actum de ratione formali Hæretici, quandoquidem eum non cuivis Hæretico tribuunt.
units.tr: 1. [woodcut initial] AT the very start of their Vindiciae the Arminians gnaw at the meanings I gave of the terms heresy, atheism, religion. And first of all at my explanation or meaning of the word heresy. I had said: The whole Christian Church, from the beginning down to this day, has called a heretic one who, following some heresiarch, denies a doctrine that is fundamental and necessary to salvation and is disputed among Christians. Such heretics, for example, are the Antitrinitarians, that is the Photinians, Socinians, Arians, etc., whom the whole Christian Church, which worships God in three persons, holds to be heretics. I took the word heretic there, as anyone can see from my words, strictly for the simple heretic, and as distinct from the heresiarch. Here, because the judgment of the Church, drawn from the Word of God against the Antitrinitarians, is very displeasing to those men who pose as Antitrinitarians, they rise up on pages 9, 10 and 11 against the meaning of that word which I proposed, on the pretext that, they say, this is not a good DEFINITION, and that no one has ever so defined a heretic. And they offer four little arguments by which they try to prove that the DEFINITION they say I gave is not good. But truly this is pure fraud. For I proposed no definition of heresy or of heretic, nor was that my purpose. I only showed in what sense the whole Church, which worships God in three persons, takes the word heretic. Hence I said that the Church CALLS a heretic, etc. How far this is from a definition is plain. And so all their sophisms collapse. I will add nothing more, except that it must not be passed over that in their fourth sophism they say that the definition is not good because it lacks the formal element of heresy, where they claim that the most distinguished professors of Leiden also place malice in the formal idea of a heretic. But the Arminians say this most calumniously, as is their custom. For in the passage to which the Arminians refer, which is the Censura of the Confession, chap. 24, §9, the said most distinguished men separate the coercion of a simple heretic from the coercion of one who has a malicious act of the will joined to him. From this it is plain that they do not place a malicious act within the formal idea of a heretic, since they do not attribute it to every heretic.

units.la: Post hæc multa sophisticantur Arminiani pagg. 10. 11. contra id quòd dixeram. Totam Ecclesiam & quidem eam quæ Deum in tribus persopersonis adorat sic vocem Hæretici sumsisse; quod verissimum esse patet ex inductione omnium Hæresium, speciatim exemplo à me commemorato Antitrinitariorum. Et quidem sophisticantur eo prætextu, quòd auctoritate Ecclesiæ Pontificium in modum utar. Id quòd salsissimum quoq; est. Nam ego ne quidem auctoritate Ecclesiæ ibi usus sum; sed saltem indicavi quâ in significatione Ecclesia accipiat vocem illam: & contrà in quâ significatione vocem illam non accipiant Arminiani. Vbi profecto non magis dici potest me auctoritate Ecclesiæ Pontificium in morem usum esse, quàm dici potest me usum esse auctoritate Arminianorum. Eadem est ratio omnium aliorum locorum in quibus dico Ecclesiam hoc aut illud credere. Tunc enim nequaquam probo doctrinam meam auctoritate Ecclesiæ, sed tantùm propono doctrinam Ecclesiæ & expono quid ex unâ parte sentiat Ecclesia, quid ex alterâ parte sentiant Arminiani. Quorum prius profecto non minùs mihi licitum est, quàm posterius. Et sic quæstio facti est. An autem Ecclesia recte sentiat, seu an vera sit fides illa Ecclesiæ alia quæstio est, juris scilicet, quam non attingo; aut ubi attingo, ex verbo Dei probo. Patet igitur hos Antitrinitarios simulatores sophisticè & fraudulenter mutare statum quæstionis, & nugis meris quæ ad rem non faciunt chartas suas sexcentics complere, ut me refutâsse videantur. Sed de hac re aliquid etiam Parte II. lib.2. c.1. monuimus.
units.tr: After this the Arminians, on pages 10 and 11, quibble at much of what I had said: that the whole Church, and indeed that which worships God in three persons, has taken the word heretic in this sense. This is most true, as is clear from the induction of all heresies, and especially from the example of the Antitrinitarians that I mentioned. They quibble on the pretext that I use the authority of the Church in the manner of the Papists. This is also most absurd. For I did not use the authority of the Church there at all; I only indicated in what sense the Church takes that word, and, on the contrary, in what sense the Arminians do not take it. Here it can truly be said no more that I have acted in the manner of the Papists by the authority of the Church, than that I have acted by the authority of the Arminians. The same is the case for all the other places where I say that the Church believes this or that. For then I do not at all prove my doctrine by the authority of the Church, but only set out the doctrine of the Church and explain what the Church thinks on the one hand and what the Arminians think on the other. The former is surely no less lawful for me than the latter. And so the question is one of fact. Whether the Church thinks rightly, or whether that faith of the Church is true, is another question, namely one of right, which I do not touch; or where I touch it, I prove it from the Word of God. It is therefore clear that these Antitrinitarian pretenders sophistically and fraudulently change the state of the question, and fill their papers a hundred times over with mere trifles that do not bear on the matter, so that they may seem to have refuted me. But we have also said something about this matter in Part II, book 2, chap. 1.

units.la: 2. Pergunt hi homines, ac quia dixeram Arminianos vocem Hæreseos non accipere in significatione quæ in Ecclesiâ recepta est (quod verissimum est, & ipsi non negant sed fatentur) verùm contrà statuere, Sciri hodiè non posse quis sit Hæreticus: Respondent illi meipsis salsissimè hoc posterius tribuere. Quid enim salsius? inquiunt pag.12. Optime sciri potest quis sit Hæreticus, &c. At tu, pie Lector qui candorem & honestatem amas, judica annon hæc summa protervia sit? Nam cùm ita negàssent, & me falsitatis arguissent, statim fatentur me verum dixisse, ac subjungunt: Sed cùm sciri posse negent Remonstrantes, quid sit Hæresis, aut quis formaliter & proprie sit Hæreticus, ad definitionem Hæreseos & Hæretici respiciunt quam formant Calvinistæ, quæ ad eò lubrica est, &c. Fatentur igitur se dixisse: Sciri hodiè non posse quis sit Hæreticus aut quid sit Hæresis: & tamen audent me falsitatis arguere cum convitio ineptiæ. Si candidè agere voluissent, debebant dixisse: verum esse, se ita docere; sed in eo se respicere ad significationem Hæreseos prout eam vocem nos Reformati accipimus; interim se agnoscere sciri posse quis sit Hæreticus & quid sit HæreHæresis in eâ significatione quam ipsi infrà fingent, ac quæ inusitata & inaudita est in Ecclesiâ, cujus tamen testem Paulum appellare salsissimè audent. Ita egisse debebant. Hûc enim mens arcana redit responsi eorum. Sed de hac re infra ulterius agetur lib.2. cap.4. quod est de Hæresi. Observet igitur Lector ex sectione hac & præcedente, Arminianos non negare se non ferre vocem Hæreseos in significatione à me alata, in quâ, ut dixi, tota Ecclesia eam accipit: cujus rei causa est præcipua quia Hæreticos Antitrinitarios in Ecclesiam introducere volunt, ut ex Arcanorum Partibus tribus præcedentibus est manifestum, & infrà porrò patebit.
units.tr: 2. These men go on, and because I had said that the Arminians do not take the word heresy in the sense that is received in the Church (which is most true, and they do not deny it but admit it), but rather assert that it cannot be known today who is a heretic, they answer that this latter is most absurdly ascribed to me. "For what could be more absurd?" they say on page 12. It can very well be known who is a heretic, etc. But you, kind Reader, who love candour and honesty, judge whether this is not extreme obstinacy. For when they had thus denied it and accused me of falsehood, they immediately admit that I spoke the truth, and add: But since the Remonstrants deny that it can be known what heresy is, or who is formally and properly a heretic, they look to the definition of heresy and of heretic which the Calvinists form, which is so slippery, etc. They therefore admit that they said: It cannot be known today who is a heretic or what heresy is; and yet they dare to accuse me of falsehood, with the reproach of folly. If they had wished to act frankly, they ought to have said: it is true that they teach this; but in this they look to the meaning of heresy as we Reformed take that word; meanwhile they acknowledge that it can be known who is a heretic and what heresy is in that sense which they themselves will invent below, and which is unusual and unheard of in the Church, though they most absurdly dare to call Paul as witness to it. This is how they ought to have acted. For this is where the hidden intention of their answer returns. But this matter will be treated further below, in book 2, chap. 4, which is on heresy. Let the Reader therefore observe from this section and the preceding one that the Arminians do not deny that they refuse the word heresy in the sense I put forward, in which, as I said, the whole Church takes it. The chief reason for this is that they want to introduce Antitrinitarian heretics into the Church, as is plain from the three preceding Parts of the Arcana, and will be made clearer further below.

units.la: 3. Dixeram etiam eos negare Hæresin quæ sic communiter vocatur, esse peccatum. Fatentur, & in eo persistunt: Hujusmodi hæresin, inquiunt p.13. negant Remonstrantes esse peccatum, id est, peccatum vocari, seu pro peccato imputari posse hujusmodi hominibus. Dicunt tamen Hæresin esse peccatum quando pro opere carnis manifesto sumitur: quale opus carnis negant esse Hæresin quam Cll. Proff. Leydd. sic vocant, & de quâ inter eos & Arminianos quæstio est.
units.tr: 3. I had also said that they deny that heresy, as it is commonly so called, is a sin. They admit it and persist in it: Such heresy, they say on p. 13, the Remonstrants deny to be a sin, that is, that it can be called a sin, or imputed as sin, to such men. They say, however, that heresy is a sin when it is taken for a manifest work of the flesh; but this work of the flesh they deny is the heresy which the most distinguished professors of Leiden so call, and about which there is a dispute between them and the Arminians.

units.la: 4. Dixeram etiam eos docere Hæresin non esse blasphemiam. Fatentur; & me, qui id dogma ipsorum jure merito detestor, convitiis proscindunt, insanum vocant, atque Anticyras navigare jubent, & Helleborum mihi propinant. Sed ita solent Vedelium refutare.
units.tr: 4. I had also said that they teach that heresy is not blasphemy. They admit it. And they tear me apart with insults, since I detest their doctrine, which rightly deserves to be detested. They call me mad, bid me sail to Anticyra, and offer me hellebore to drink. But this is how they usually go about refuting Vedelius.

units.la: 5. Dixi etiâ eos docere Hæresin non esse impietatem, sed innocentiâ & quidem innocentiâ summam; Hæreticos qui sic communiter vocantur esse homines pios, imò piissimos, Hæreticos non esse noxios saluti animarum, nec Ecclesiæ & Regno Christi, nec Reip. item, Hæreticos veniam mereri apud Deum solo bono affectu suo, & sic æternum salvos fieri: Speciatim autem Antitrinitarios eos qui negant Christum habere divinam naturam, qui docent Christum non fuisse antequam concieperetur in utero virginis, &c. esse homines pios, imò piissimos, &c. Hæc omnia non negant; sed infrà lib.1. cap.4. Vindiciarum (quò hîc Lectorem remittunt) fatebuntur, ut ibidem videbimus. Ex his igitur patet verum esse quod dixeram, Arminianos non ferre vocem Hæreseos ut tota Ecclesia Christiana eam accipit.
units.tr: 5. I also said that they teach that heresy is not impiety, but innocence, and indeed the highest innocence; that heretics, as they are commonly called, are pious men, indeed most pious; that heretics are not harmful to the salvation of souls, nor to the Church and the Kingdom of Christ, nor to the commonwealth; that heretics earn pardon from God by their good disposition alone, and so are saved for eternity: and specifically that Antitrinitarians, who deny that Christ has a divine nature, who teach that Christ did not exist before he was conceived in the womb of the virgin, etc., are pious men, indeed most pious, etc. They do not deny these things; but in book 1, chapter 4 of the Vindiciae (to which they send the reader here) they will confess them, as we shall see there. From these things, then, it is plain that what I had said is true: that the Arminians do not bear the word "heresy" as the whole Christian Church understands it.

units.la: 6. Post hæc divisionem Atheismi à me propositam aggrediuntur multis nugis pag.13. 14. 15. 16. quæ huc redeunt: Eos quibus indifferens est quamcunque tandem Religionem Christiani nominis profiteantur, non esse dicendos Atheos. Seu, ut ipsi loquuntur, eum non esse dicendum Atheum qui de controversiis in Christiana Religione dogmatis non non statuit quicquam in alteram partem & sectâ alicui nomen suum non dat, atque ita in partes abit. Item paulò post: qui Libertinus est. h. e. qui non accedit aut se dedit in aliquam sectam quæ controversias decidit; talem non esse nominandum Atheum. Quod tamen ego solidè ostenderam ex eo quia Religio Christiana consistit non solùm in illis dogmatis quæ extra controversiam sunt, sed etiam in quibusdam Controversis, quæ absolutè ad salutem necessaria sunt,&c. Talia controversa, in quibus etiam Religio consistit, seu absque quibus ea esse non potest, qui non curat sed floccifacit ac pro indifferenti habet quicquid tandem de iis credatur aut non credatur, dixi merito Atheum vocari solere.
units.tr: 6. After this they take up the division of atheism which I proposed, and in pages 13, 14, 15 and 16 they spend much trifling effort, which comes down to this: that those for whom it is a matter of indifference what religion of the Christian name they profess should not be called atheists. Or, as they put it, one should not call an atheist one who has settled nothing on the controversies in the Christian religion in either direction, and does not give his name to any sect, and so stands apart from the parties. Likewise a little later: one who is a libertine, that is, who does not join or has not given himself to any sect which settles the controversies; such a man should not be named an atheist. Yet I had solidly shown the opposite, because the Christian religion consists not only of those doctrines which are beyond controversy, but also of certain controverted matters which are absolutely necessary to salvation, etc. Regarding such controverted matters, on which religion itself depends, or without which it cannot exist, I said that the man who does not care for them, but makes light of them and regards it as a matter of indifference what is or is not believed about them, is rightly called an atheist, as is customary.

units.la: Probant autem Arminiani suam sententiam ex eo 1 quia Scriptura non patiatur hanc significationem pag.14. utpote quæ nullos vocet Atheos, nisi qui aut Deum negant, aut Deum quem agnoscunt ac profitentur factis abnegant. Quod salsissimum est. Nam scriptura etiam Christianos quosdam Deum non nôsse dicit; speciatim eos qui articulum controversum fundamentalem negant, qualis est articulus de resurrectione olim controversus in Ecclesiâ Corinthiacâ. Unde Apostolus ait ἀγνωσίαν θεοῦ τινὲς ἔχουσι quidam Deum non nôrunt; ad pudo rem vobis incutiendum hoc dico 1. Cor.15.34. Et Gentes vocat Atheos, etsi non negarent Deum esse Eph.2.12.
units.tr: The Arminians, however, prove their view first from this: that Scripture does not allow this meaning, since it calls none atheists except those who either deny God or who deny by their deeds the God whom they acknowledge and profess. This is utterly false. For Scripture also says that some Christians do not know God; especially those who deny a fundamental article under dispute, such as the article on the resurrection, which was once disputed in the Church of Corinth. Hence the Apostle says ἀγνωσίαν θεοῦ τινὲς ἔχουσι [agnosian theou tines echousi], "some have no knowledge of God"; I say this to shame you (1 Cor. 15:34). And he calls the Gentiles atheists, although they did not deny that God exists (Eph. 2:12).

units.la: Deinde rationem afferunt seu potiûs experientiam, dicentes: Neminem unquam concepisse Atheum ut ego eum describo. Sed ego contrà ad experientiam & judicium omnium eorum cœtuum, qui Deum in tribus personis necessariò adorandum credunt, provoco: qui omnes profectò habent pro Atheis tales homines quales ego descripsi, & quorum, proh dolor, non nisi nimia copia est; etsi nunquam iis permissum fuerit in hunc usque diem ut cœtus publicos facerent, prout hodie Arminiani Theologi cœtus tales in Belgio faciunt, & per totum Orbem invehere Libertinismum seu Atheismi illam speciem conantur.
units.tr: Next they offer an argument, or rather an experience, saying: no one has ever conceived of an atheist as I describe him. But I, on the contrary, appeal to the experience and judgment of all those assemblies which believe that God must be worshipped necessarily in three persons: all of whom certainly regard as atheists men such as I have described, and of whom, alas, there is only too great a number; although until this day they have never been permitted to hold public assemblies, as the Arminian theologians today hold such assemblies in Belgium, and try to bring Libertinism, or that kind of atheism, into the whole world.

units.la: Denique ex testimonio ipsorum Ethnicorum probare volunt me immerito Libertinos vocare Atheos. Quod quam egregium argumentum sit, nimirum ad judicium Ethnicorum, qui Deum non noverunt Scripturâ teste, provocare, quò illi decidant qui ἄθεοι dicendi aut non sint, unusquisque videt. Verum tamen ut non absurdè agere videantur; provocant ad auctoritatem non omnium Ethnicorum, sed tantùm MELIORVM. Pari æquitate, inquiunt, censuit melior Gentilitas. Imò ajunt Gentiles neminem vocâsse Atheum, nisi qui vel aperte Deum negabant, vel qui qui sciri posse negabant an Deus esset; cæteros eâdem nomenclaturâ infamare nefas putavit, odio horrendi nominis. Hic ego libenter scirem quid nomine Melioris gentilitatis intelligant. Nam Arminiani Meliores homines mirè æstimant, prout patet ex eo quòd libro 2. Vind. c.9. p.182. meliores Reges & Principes vocant eos qui nullis planè Hæreticis auctoritate suâ resistunt, sed omnibus promiscuè speciatim autem Antitrinitariorum execrandis catervis liberum exercitium Religionis permittunt. Item, quòd Bonos, vocant, & felicissima atque ad Optima quaque nata ingenia, qui Christi doctrinam suspectam falsitatis habent, & in Atheismum delabuntur, ideò quia veram doctrinam percipere non possunt; quemadmodum ostendi Parte Tertiâ lib.1. cap.4. Sed esto; intelligant quos volent. Christiana fides melius nos poterit de divinis instruere quàm Gentilitas. Et verò si tantopere commendant auctoritatem Ethnicorum in eâ re: igitur ipsi Arminiani perperàm faciunt dum paulò ante dixerunt eos etiam Atheos esse qui Deum quem agnoscunt, factis negant. Hos enim Gentilitas pro Atheis non habuit, ut ipsi quidem hic dicunt.
units.tr: Finally, they wish to prove from the testimony of the Gentiles themselves that I wrongly call libertines atheists. How remarkable an argument this is, namely to appeal to the judgment of the Gentiles, who (by Scripture's testimony) did not know God, so that they may decide whether those who are to be called [atheoi] atheists are so or not, anyone can see. Yet, so that they may appear not to act absurdly, they appeal not to the authority of all the Gentiles, but only of the better ones. With equal fairness, they say, the better Gentile world judged so. Indeed they say the Gentiles called no one an atheist except those who either openly denied God, or who denied that it could be known whether God exists; they thought it wrong to brand the rest with the same name, out of hatred for the dreadful word. Here I would gladly know what they understand by the better Gentiles. For the Arminians esteem the better men highly, as is clear from the fact that in book 2 of the Vindiciae, chapter 9, page 182, they call better kings and princes those who do not at all resist any heretics by their authority, but freely permit the exercise of religion to all of them, and especially to the cursed companies of Antitrinitarians. Likewise they call good and most fortunate men, and minds born for the best things, those who hold Christ's doctrine suspect of falsehood and slide into atheism, because they cannot perceive the true doctrine; as I showed in part 3, book 1, chapter 4. But grant it: let them understand whomever they wish. The Christian faith can instruct us about divine things better than the Gentile world. And indeed, if they commend so highly the authority of the Gentiles in this matter, then the Arminians themselves act wrongly when a little earlier they said that those too are atheists who deny by their deeds the God whom they acknowledge. For the Gentile world did not count these as atheists, as they themselves here admit.

units.la: Cæterum argumentum meum convellere conantur, quo probaveram merito tales homines Atheos vocari. Oppugnant autem illud pag. 14. ex eo 1 quia in controversiâ sit, an'ne dogma tale aliquod necessarium sit? Hoc ipsum est, inquiunt, quod quaeritur, & quod ille (Libertinus) pari jure negare poterit necessarium sibi videri, quo Vedelius affirmat illud necessarium esse aut necessarium sibi videri. 2. quia tales homines errant in judicando, igitur non Atheised Hæretici sunt. Denique per retorsionem, quâ eos Atheismi argui posse dicunt, qui decidunt dogmata controversa auctoritate suâ; & sic tandem verba mea in me retorquent, quibus dixeram Arminianos si negare velint se Atheismi hanc speciem introducere, id non ob aliam causam negaturos, quàm quia odiosum nomen Atheismi devitant, & non agnoscunt pro Atheismo id quod revera Atheismus est, ac dicunt: En Vedelium suopte gladio jugulatum & suismet verbis veluti loris constrictum! Sed hæc omnia futilissima sunt, ut unusquisque facile videt. Nam etsi controversum illud sit; tamen alterutra pars contradictionis vera, altera falsa est. De me quod dicunt; ad rem non facit; nec enim quæstio est de Vedelio; sed de quocunque Orthodoxo, quemcunque tandem illi velint Orthodoxum esse. Hic dicere, quod ille affirmat ex verbo Dei verum esse ab Heterodoxo aut Libertino eodem jure negari posse, hoc, inquam, dicere, est planè profanum & impium. Quod ajunt tales homines errare in judicando; verum quidem est; sed hoc non sufficit. ficit. Ita enim errant in judicando, ut simul pro indifferenti habeant dogmata omnia fundamentalia vera, & falsa dogmata: quæ impietas, non Hæreticum sed Atheum constituit. Retorsio ipsorum frivola est & impertinens. Nec enim quisquam propriâ auctoritate suâ decidere dogma ullum controversum debet; nec id à me factum. Debebat igitur eos pudere,quòd dicunt me constrictum propriis verbis meis ut loris esse, & meo gladio jugulatum. Sed his hominibus constitutum est ludere saltem, & illudere Orbi in rebus tanti momenti.
units.tr: Moreover, they try to overturn my argument, by which I had proved that such men are rightly called atheists. They attack it on page 14, first because the question is whether such a doctrine is necessary at all. This very thing, they say, is what is being asked, and what that man (the libertine) could with equal right deny to seem necessary to himself, just as Vedelius affirms that it is necessary, or seems necessary to himself. Second, because such men err in judging, therefore they are not atheists but heretics. Finally, by a counter-argument they say that those who settle controverted doctrines by their own authority can be charged with atheism; and so at last they turn my own words back on me, when I had said that if the Arminians wish to deny that they are introducing this kind of atheism, they will deny it for no other reason than that they avoid the hated name of atheism, and do not acknowledge as atheism what really is atheism. And they say: Behold Vedelius, slain with his own sword and bound with his own words as with thongs! But all these things are most trifling, as anyone can easily see. For even if the matter is disputed, nevertheless one side of the contradiction is true and the other false. What they say about me has nothing to do with the point; for the question is not about Vedelius, but about any orthodox man whomsoever they wish to be orthodox. To say here that what he affirms from the Word of God can equally well be denied by a heterodox man or a libertine, to say this, I say, is plainly profane and impious. That they say such men err in judging is true enough; but this is not sufficient. For they err in judging in such a way that at the same time they regard all the fundamental doctrines, true and false alike, as a matter of indifference; and this impiety makes a man not a heretic but an atheist. Their counter-argument is frivolous and irrelevant. For no one ought to settle any controverted doctrine by his own private authority, and I did not do so. They ought therefore to be ashamed that they say I am bound with my own words as with thongs, and slain with my own sword. But it has been decreed for these men merely to play, and to mock the world in matters of such great moment.

units.la: 7. Denique carpunt quod dixi me usurum voce Religionis in significatione receptâ, quâ aliquis vel à se vel ab alio dicitur Religionis hujus aut illius esse, ut Pontificiæ, Reformatæ, Socinianæ, &c. citra quàm laborare velim vera'ne an falsa Religio sit illa quam hic aut ille profitetur. Dicunt autem me nec piè nec prudenter in hac re facere, p. 16. Non piè, inquiunt, quia Religionis vox augustior & sacrosanctior esse debet, quàm ut ea tribuatur sectæ cuique etiam pessimæ, &c. Nec prudenter, quia acriter aliàs à suis non nescit culpari Pontificios, &c. Sed judica, Candide Lector, an'ne hi homines seriò an verò Hypocriticè pietatis nomen usurpent, & an merito imprudentiæ me taxent; ipsi, inquam, qui in his suis Vindiciis non solùm conventicula quorumcunque Hæreticorum cœtus Religiosos cap.9. p. 166. item Hæreses eorum Religionem sæpius appellant ut ibidem bis p.163. sed etiam blasphemare audent, Eos qui à Christianismo ad Iudaismum deficiunt in cultu veri Dei persistere: Item, eos colere verum Deum qui non colunt Iesum Christum: Denique Christum Iudæorum Religionem modernam ut divinam approbare. Et tamen audent me hi homines impietatis & imprudentiæ arguere. Vides, optime Lector, cum quibus hominibus res nobis sit. Me quod attinet,nec impietatis nec imprudentiæ merito accusari me ab iis unusquisque vir Candidus videt, qui legit verba mea quibus usus eram, ex quibus apparet mihi non fuisse propositum in eo laborare, vera'ne an falsa sit hujus aut illius sectæ Religio; adeòque an proprie an verò ὁμωνύμως Religio dicenda sit: sed me saltem voluisse usum vocis istius communem indicare, & ex hypothesi utentium loqui. Patet itaque Arminianos frustrà allatrasse veritatem à me cap.1. lib.1. partis primæ allatam.
units.tr: 7. Finally, they carp at my saying that I would use the word Religion in its accepted sense, by which someone is said, either by himself or by another, to belong to this or that religion, such as Papist, Reformed, Socinian, etc., without wishing to labour over whether the religion that this or that man professes is true or false. They say that I act neither piously nor prudently in this matter, p. 16. Not piously, they say, because the word religion ought to be more august and more sacred than to be applied to any sect whatever, even the most wicked, etc. Nor prudently, because the Papists are not unaware of being sharply blamed elsewhere by their own people, etc. But judge, candid reader, whether these men use the name of piety seriously or rather hypocritically, and whether they deserve to charge me with imprudence. They themselves, I say, who in these their Vindications not only often call the gatherings of any heretics whatever religious assemblies (chap. 9, p. 166; likewise on p. 163 twice in the same place they call their heresies Religion), but also dare to blaspheme, asserting that those who fall away from Christianity to Judaism persist in the worship of the true God, that those who do not worship Jesus Christ worship the true God, and, finally, that Christ approves the modern religion of the Jews as divine. And yet these men dare to accuse me of impiety and imprudence. You see, excellent reader, with what men we have to deal. As for me, every fair-minded man who reads the words I used will see that I am accused of neither impiety nor imprudence, since it was not my purpose in that passage to labour over whether the religion of this or that sect is true or false, or whether it should properly, or rather equivocally, be called religion. I only wished to indicate the common use of that word and to speak from the hypothesis of those who use it. It is clear, therefore, that the Arminians barked in vain at the truth I had stated in chapter 1 of the first part of the first book.

units.la: CAP. II.
units.tr: CHAPTER II.

units.la: Examen Capitis II. Vindic. lib. 1.
units.tr: Examination of Chapter II of the Vindiciae, Book 1.

units.la: 1. Arminiani fatentur se docere Neminem obligari ab verum sensum verbi divini sequendum contra conscientiam suam licet erroneam. Itam, verbum Dei neminem obligare nisi intellectum prout quis adhibita omni possibili diligentia & prudentia credit esse intelligendum. Ostenditur ea dogmata perperam ab ipsis defendi pratextu axiomatis Theologiae Practicae. 2. Impostura Arminianorum detegitur. 3. Sequi verum sensum verbi divini quid significet, ostenditur ex usu veteris Ecclesiae.
units.tr: 1. The Arminians confess that they teach that no one is bound to follow the true sense of the divine Word against his conscience, even if that conscience is erroneous. Likewise, that the Word of God binds no one except to the sense which someone, using all possible diligence and prudence, believes is to be understood. It is shown that these doctrines are wrongly defended by them under the pretext of an axiom of Practical Theology. 2. The imposture of the Arminians is exposed. 3. That to follow the true sense of the divine Word means what it signifies is shown from the usage of the early Church.

units.la: 1. CApite secundo primae Partis lib.1. attribui Arminianis duo dogmata haec: Neminem obligari ad verum sensum verbi divini sequendum contra conscientiam suam licet erroneam. Item, Verbum Dei neminem obligare nisi intellectum, prout adhibita omni possibili diligentia & prudentia aliquis credit esse intelligendum. Apol.c. 25. f. 289. Fatentur & defendunt. Defendere autem conantur illa axiomate Theologiae Practicae, quod in eo consistit; peccare hominem si agat contra conscientiam suam quamvis erroneam. Quod axioma verum quidem est, sed ad rem non facit. Nam sensus illius est, ut constat: neminem debere quicquam dicere aut facere extrinsecus, cujus contrarium in animo sentiat, credat, foveat. Sic v.g. peccat aliquis qui in conscientia sua putat Religionem aut doctrinam aliquam falsam esse, & tamen contra dictamen suae conscientiae eam doctrinam profitetur, verbis aut factis approbat. Sed hoc, ut dixi, ad rem non facit. Nam hic quaestio non est, an aliquis obligetur extrinseca actione veram doctrinam profiteri, tum cum in conscientia sua eam pro falsa habet. Hoc enim non debere fieri constat; nec est sequi verum sensum verbi divini, sed est fraus & improba simulatio; qualis est Arminianorum simulantium Orthodoxam doctrinam de mysterio Trinitatis quam tamen in animo suo non habent pro vera, ut Parte Secunda ostendi. Sed quaestio est: an ne tanta auctoritas sit verbi divini, ut ab eo homo obligetur sequi verum sensum illius, sive veram doctrinam, tam mente quam Professione, tam corde quam verbis & factis, etiamsi in conscientia sua serio & plane arbitretur illam doctrinam falsam, suam autem opinionem veram esse: ita ut peccet eo ipso quod errat, & veram doctrinam animo suo & professione non sequitur.
units.tr: 1. In the second chapter of the first part of Book 1, I attributed to the Arminians these two doctrines: that no one is bound to follow the true sense of the divine Word against his conscience, even if it is erroneous; likewise, that the Word of God binds no one except to the sense which someone, using all possible diligence and prudence, believes is to be understood. (Apology, ch. 25, p. 289.) They confess and defend them. They try to defend them by an axiom of Practical Theology, which runs: a man sins if he acts against his conscience, however erroneous it may be. This axiom is indeed true, but it has nothing to do with the point. For its meaning, as is plain, is that no one ought to say or do outwardly what he feels, believes, or harbours in his mind to be the contrary. Thus, for example, someone sins who in his conscience thinks a religion or some doctrine is false, and yet against the dictate of his conscience professes that doctrine, or approves it by words or deeds. But this, as I said, has nothing to do with the matter. For the question here is not whether someone is obliged by outward action to profess a true doctrine when in his conscience he holds it to be false. It is agreed that this must not be done; and it is not to follow the true sense of the divine Word, but is deceit and wicked pretence, such as that of the Arminians who pretend to hold the orthodox doctrine of the mystery of the Trinity, which yet they do not hold to be true in their hearts, as I showed in the Second Part. The question is rather this: whether the authority of the divine Word is so great that a man is bound to follow its true sense, that is, the true doctrine, in mind as well as in profession, in heart as well as in words and deeds, even if he seriously and plainly judges in his conscience that this doctrine is false and his own opinion true; so that he sins by the very fact that he errs and does not follow the true doctrine in his mind and in his profession.

units.la: In hoc positum esse statum quæstionis, patet tum ex verbis Cll. DD. Proff. Leydd. quibus Arminiani ista duo dogmata opponunt; tum ex doctrinâ Arminianorum reliquâ. Negant enim Hæresin quæ sic communiter vocatur, speciatim à modò laudatis Theologis, qualis est Hæresis Antitrinitariorum esse peccatum aut culpam. Quòd si verum est, tunc Hæreticus talis non obligatur deponere conscientiam suam erroneam. Quæ consequentia adeò firma est, ut ipsi hic doceant p.18. non obligari Hæreticos tales deponere conscientiam suam erroneam; quâ de re egimus Parte III. Arcan. lib.1. c.2. Hinc etiam docent Hæresin quam illi contra communem sententiam totius veteris & modernæ Ecclesiæ sic vocant, non esse peccatum, quatenus est error, sed quatenus cum pravo affectu conjuncta est ex quo procedit, ut Parte III. vidimus lib.2. c.4. & infrà porrò videbimus. Et sic patet 1 axioma illud Theologiæ Practicæ ac speciatim testimonium Clarissimi Amesii mihi non repugnare, adeoque perperam & impertinenter ab Arminianis illud adduci, frustraque conari eos incrustare dogmata illa duo prætextu illius axiomatis. 2. patet falsò eos & rabularum in modum dicere me statum quæstionis non intelligere. Nam ex dictis apparet me melius eum intelligere quàm ipsi optent. 3. argumentum, quod ex auctoritate verbi divini locoque Pauli 2. Cor.10. 5. à me allatum est, rectè concludere. Etenim si verbi divini auctoritas tanta est, ut ejus vero sensui conscientia contraria esse non debeat, certè tenetur omnis homo errans, animo & opere extrinsecus & intrinsecus sequi verum sensum verbi divini etiam contra conscientiam suam h. e. utut erronea conscientia ei contrarium dictet: Si hoc non facit, peccat non deferendo ei quod deferre debebat, oppugnando & negando quod verbum Dei dicit, mendacii arguendo illud, nomen Dei temere usurpando ac dicendo Dominus dixit, cum tamen Dominus non dixerit, ut est apud Prophetam. Adeoque salsissimum est, quod Arminiani negant Hæresin quæ sic communiter vocatur, speciatim Antitrinitariorum errores circa Mysterium Trinitatis, esse peccatum, aut eos non obligari deponere conscientiam suam erroneam & sequi verum sensum verbi divini: denique Hæresin quam ipsi sic vocant non esse peccatum quatenus error est.
units.tr: That this is the state of the question is clear both from the words of the most distinguished Professors of Leiden, against whom the Arminians set these two doctrines, and from the rest of the Arminian teaching. For they deny that heresy, as it is commonly called, and especially that of the sort the Theologians just praised call it, such as the heresy of the Antitrinitarians, is a sin or a fault. But if this is true, then such a heretic is not bound to lay aside his erroneous conscience. This consequence is so firm that they themselves teach here, on page 18, that such heretics are not bound to lay aside their erroneous conscience; on this matter we treated in Part III, Arcanum, Book 1, ch. 2. Hence they also teach that the heresy which they, against the common opinion of the whole ancient and modern Church, so call, is not a sin insofar as it is error, but insofar as it is joined with a wicked disposition from which it proceeds, as we saw in Part III, Book 2, ch. 4, and as we shall further see below. And so it is plain, first, that that axiom of Practical Theology, and especially the testimony of the most distinguished Amesius, does not oppose me; and therefore the Arminians wrongly and irrelevantly bring it forward, and vainly try to shelter those two doctrines under the pretext of that axiom. Second, it is plain that they falsely and, in the manner of wranglers, say that I do not understand the state of the question. For from what has been said it appears that I understand it better than they would wish. Third, the argument which I drew from the authority of the divine Word and from the passage of Paul, 2 Cor. 10:5, is rightly concluded. For if the authority of the divine Word is so great that conscience ought not to be contrary to its true sense, then surely every erring man is bound, in mind and in outward deed, both outwardly and inwardly, to follow the true sense of the divine Word even against his conscience; that is, however erroneous his conscience may dictate the contrary. If he does not do this, he sins by not yielding what he ought to yield, by opposing and denying what the Word of God says, by charging it with lying, by rashly using the name of God and saying The Lord has spoken, when the Lord has not spoken, as is said in the Prophet. Therefore it is utterly false that the Arminians deny that heresy, as it is commonly called, and especially the errors of the Antitrinitarians about the mystery of the Trinity, is a sin, or that such people are not bound to lay aside their erroneous conscience and follow the true sense of the divine Word; and finally that the heresy which they so call is not a sin insofar as it is error.

units.la: 2. Cæterùm observetur hoc loco impostura horum bonorum virorum. Secundo ipsorum dogmati objeceram inter alia: Si id verum sit, nimirùm verbum Dei neminem obligare nisi intellectum sic prout quis credit, &c. Sequi exinde Arium, Photinum, Samosatenum, Pelagium & reliquos omnes Hæreticos similes non peccâsse aut peccare, &c. Hic illi declinantes versutè Hæresium illarum mentionem & vim argumenti hujus, aliò digrediuntur & formant objectionem hanc: At sic, inquies, sequetur etiam eos qui in rebus scitu ac creditu ad salutem necessariis errant, contra conscientiam erroneam facientes non peccare, &c. Vbi declinant ictum ideò, quia non judicant Antitrinitariorum ut Photini, Pauli Samosateni & Socini hæreses circa mysterium illud, peccata esse; sed contra statuunt verbum Dei circa doctrinam de Trinitate non obligare Socinianos nisi sic prout hi post omnem scilicet adhibitam diligentiam & prudentiam suam id credunt esse intelligendum: nec obligare illos ad deponendam conscientiam suam erroneam; & sic rursus, etiam vi hujus posterioris dogmatis, Arminiani Turcicas & Iudaicas illas blasphemias Socinianorum negant esse peccata. Vos Illustrissimi Proceres audietisne execrandam hanc impietatem istorum hominum & tolerabitis? Porrò quàm turpiter illudant orbi in eo quod de possibili adhibita diligentia dicunt, ostendimus Parte Tertia, lib.1. cap. 9.
units.tr: 2. Moreover, let the imposture of these good men be noted here. Second, among other things I had objected to their doctrine: If this is true, namely that the Word of God binds no one except to the sense which someone believes, etc., it follows that Arius, Photinus, Samosatenus, Pelagius, and all the other similar heretics have not sinned, or do not sin, etc. Here, slyly evading the mention of those heresies and the force of this argument, they wander off elsewhere and frame this objection: But so, you will say, it will follow that those too who err in matters to be known and believed for salvation, acting against an erroneous conscience, do not sin, etc. Here they dodge the blow because they do not judge the heresies of the Antitrinitarians, such as those of Photinus, Paul of Samosata and Socinus about that mystery, to be sins; rather they lay down that the Word of God, as regards the doctrine of the Trinity, does not bind the Socinians except to the sense which these believe, after all possible diligence and prudence, is to be understood; and that it does not bind them to lay aside their erroneous conscience. And so again, even by virtue of this latter doctrine, the Arminians deny that those Turkish and Jewish blasphemies of the Socinians are sins. Most illustrious Lords, will you hear this execrable impiety of these men and tolerate it? Moreover, how shamefully they mock the world in what they say about possible diligence employed, we have shown in Part Three, Book 1, ch. 9.

units.la: 3. Corollarii loco hoc addam. Dixi extrinsecus profiteri veram doctrinam & tamen ejus contrarium animo sentire, non esse sequi verum sensum verbi divini: sed hoc esse sequi verum sensum, quando in eâ re inter mentem & professionem harmonia est. Hoc patet ex usu Phraseos; sequi sententiam seu doctrinam aliquam. Theodoritus loquens de Leontio Episcopo Antiocheno qui, Aëtianus cùm esset, tamen ob metum populi simulabat professione externâ contrarium, non dicit eum sequutum esse Orthodoxam doctrinam, sed opponit ei illos qui sequebantur Orthodoxam doctrinam, h. e. eos qui & Professione & animo erant Orthodoxi: ἔφη, inquit, κρυπτῶν τὸν λαὸν διὰ τὸ τῆς ἀληθείας τὸ δόγμα manifestum erat eum occultare hæresin, tum ob metum populi, &c. manifestum autem animum suum fecit operibus. ὅσοι μὲν γὰρ τοῖς Ἀπostολικοῖς εἵπονλο δόγμα- σιν quotquot enim Apostolicam doctrinam sequebantur non promovebantur ad ullum munus, &c. Similiter Sozomenus ait de Ægyptiis Monachis, quod ob eorum pietatem populus judicarit eorum doctrinam oppositam Arianorum Hæresi veram, Arianorum autem falsam esse, ὡς τῆς δόξης ἡμῶν τὸ ἀληθὲς ἔπεστο ἐκ τῆς μαρτυρίας ἀληθεῖς ὑγιέστερον quorum (Monachorum) sententiam etiam populus sequebatur, & testimonia eorum (de doctrina scilicet an falsa an vera illa esset) vera esse putabat. Idem Sozomenus alibi ait, populos in Syria, Cappadocia & regionibus circumjacentibus ἀπρὶξ mordicus adhæsisse Orthodoxæ doctrinæ & Arianorum hæresin abosin abominatos esse, non secus quàm Αἰγύπτιοι τοῖς παρ' αὐτοῖς μοναχοῖς ἑπόμενοι ἐναντίως εἶχον πρὸς τὰς Ἀρείας. Ægyptii qui Monachorum suorum doctrinam sequuti, (ita enim ipse lib. 4. c. 9. exprimit quod hic dicit τοῖς μοναχοῖς ἑπόμενοι) Arianis sese opponebant. Hoc sibi vult phrasis sequi verum sensum verbi divini. Ex quo ipso etiam melius intelligitur quis verus sit status quæstionis inter nos & Arminianos. Et sic patet etiam ex hoc capite me Arminianos calumniatum non esse, aut falso objecisse ipsis ista duo dogmata; quandoquidem ipsi ea fatentur. Iudica nunc, optime Lector, an'ne Arminiani merito claudant caput suum secundum lib. 1. Vindic. pag. 18. his verbis : Atque hoc primum est, ex quo apparet Vedelii insciitia. Tàm turpis lapsus in ipso limine Arcanorum mali augurii est? an non verò potius omni jure ego hoc caput his verbis claudere debeam:Ex hoc igitur ut & praecedente capite apparet Antitrinitariorum horum simulatorum execranda & non toleranda impietas; atque deplorata causa. Tàm turpis lapsus in ipso limine Vindiciarum, mali augurii est?
units.tr: 3. By way of a corollary I will add this. I said that to profess the true doctrine outwardly while inwardly feeling the contrary is not to follow the true sense of the divine Word; but to follow the true sense is when, in that matter, there is harmony between mind and profession. This is plain from the usage of the phrase to follow an opinion or doctrine. Theodoret, speaking of Leontius, Bishop of Antioch, who though he was an Aëtian, nevertheless for fear of the people pretended outwardly to the contrary, does not say that he followed the orthodox doctrine; rather he sets over against him those who followed the orthodox doctrine, that is, those who were orthodox both in profession and in heart. "He said," he writes, "that he was concealing the heresy" [ἔφη ... κρυπτῶν τὸν λαὸν διὰ τὸ τῆς ἀληθείας τὸ δόγμα] — it was plain that he was hiding his heresy, both for fear of the people, etc. But he revealed his mind plainly by his deeds.
