Quod addunt, se credere multos cœtus Christianos errare in Necessariis; de eo etiam egimus allegato capite 8. præcedentis libri, unde αὐτοκατάκρισις ipsorum etiam in hac parte manifesta est. Igitur quoties negare audent in Vindiciis suis se docuisse & docere Nulla dogmata controversa esse necessaria ad salutem: toties palàm faciunt se αὐτοκαλακρίτως esse, contra propriam conscientiam impudentissimè & improbissimè coram Deo & hominibus agere; Deo & hominibus veteratorie ac fraudulenter imponere velle, nullam fidem amplius in negocio Religionis, nedum alio quodcunque tandem illud sit, mereri; denique detestabiles se Magistratibus & omnibus populis reddere.
units.tr: 2. But the Arminians deny this against their own conscience, by which they are convicted of teaching it in the Apology and in the Answer to the Excerpta, as we have shown at length, solidly and clearly in book 1, chapter 8 of this Fourth Part. Moreover, what is more, in their Vindiciae they repeat the same doctrine, as we made plain in Part III, book 2, chapter 1. As for their addition, that they believe many Christian assemblies err in necessary matters, we have also dealt with that in the cited chapter 8 of the preceding book, whence their own self-condemnation [αὐτοκατάκρισις] in this part is also manifest. Therefore, as often as they dare to deny in their Vindiciae that they have taught, and teach, that no controversial doctrines are necessary to salvation, so often they clearly show themselves self-condemned [αὐτοκατακρίτως], acting most shamelessly and most wickedly against their own conscience before God and men, wishing to deceive God and men by craft and fraud, so that they deserve no further trust in any matter of religion, much less in whatever else it may be; and finally they make themselves detestable to the magistrates and to all peoples.

units.la: Quod addunt p. 62. 63. se verbis illis inter Christianos qui fundamentum salutis tenent; intelligere in Apologia cœtus Christianos, non autem, ut ego dixeram singulos Christianos: id falsum esse patet ex doctrinâ eorum propriâ de Necessariis (ut ex Par. I. Arcan. lib. 2. cap. 1. p. 103. 104. manifestum est, ubi ostendi eos ibi intelligere cœtus Christianos, non autem singulos Christianos) quam hic improbissimè negant. Itaque falsum est quod hic dicunt: nihil fingi posse à MENTE Arminianorum alienum. Et quis credat Arminianis ministris in posterum, quando dicunt MENTEM suam hanc vel illam esse; quandoquidem audent negare verba sua propria quæ scripserunt, quæ scripta etiam nunc exstant, & quorum ab omnibus hominibus convinci possunt, ut ostendi. Certè decipi ac decipere datâ operâ vult, qui ipsos in posterum aliquid asserentes aut negantes fidem mereri putat. Disputant postea p. 63. adversum me, ac si negâssem id quod dixerant; nimirum eos qui necessaria negant non esse Christianos, imò ne Hæreticos quidem. At impertinenter disputant. Nam ego nec affirmavi nec negavi eos recte dixisse; quia id mihi propositum non erat. Sed exinde ostendi eos in Apologia non agnoscere ullos coetus Christianos errare in Necessariis.
units.tr: As for their claim, on pp. 62–63, that by the words among Christians who hold the foundation of salvation they understood in the Apology Christian assemblies, and not, as I had said, individual Christians: this is shown to be false by their own doctrine of necessary matters (as is clear from Part I, Arcanum, book 2, chapter 1, p. 103–104, where I showed that they there understand Christian assemblies and not individual Christians), a point which they most shamelessly deny here. Therefore what they say here is false: that nothing foreign to the MIND of the Arminians can be invented. And who would trust Arminian ministers in future, when they say that their MIND is this or that, since they dare to deny their own words which they wrote, which still survive in writing, and by which they can be convicted by all men, as I have shown. Certainly he who thinks that those who assert or deny anything in future deserve trust wishes to be deceived and to deceive deliberately. Next they dispute against me, on p. 63, as if I had denied what they had said, namely that those who deny necessary matters are not Christians, not even heretics. But they dispute irrelevantly. For I neither affirmed nor denied that they had spoken rightly, because that was not my purpose. Rather, from this I showed that in the Apology they do not acknowledge any Christian assemblies as erring in necessary matters.

units.la: 3. Tertium quod ipsis objeceram, est: Professionem necessariam, sanam, ac salutaris doctrinae h, e. non controversa inter Christianos, esse notam vera Ecclesiae. Ubi monui eos ponere notam, quae saltem INDICET Ecclesiam, seu quae eam veram ac visibilem faciat, non autem quae illam a falsa distinguat ac discernat. Et causam istius turpis dogmatis Arminiani attuleram verissimam, quae in eo consistit, quia illi nullam agnoscunt falsam Ecclesiam Christiani nominis; cum omnes coetus Christiani habeant hanc notam quam illi verae Ecclesiae assignant, nimirum quod agnoscunt dogmata omnia non controversa inter Christianos. Hic illi p. 64. posteaquam solita sua maledicentia & calumniandi libidine rursus me petiissent, credo me ex se metientes; quia post inanes tergiversationes vident se elabi non posse, redeunt ad oppugnandam conscientiam propriam, & illudendum Deo atque hominibus, ac rursus negant contra conscientiam propriam suam se docuisse: Nulla dogmata controversa inter Christianos esse necessaria ad salutem. Et vocant hoc πρῶτον ψεῦδος meum, ac dicunt me illud ipsis non sine fastidio ubivis objicere.
units.tr: 3. The third thing I had objected to them is this: a necessary, sound, and salutary profession of doctrine, that is, one not controverted among Christians, is a mark of the true Church. There I warned that they set up a mark which at least INDICATES the Church, or which makes it true and visible, but not one which distinguishes and separates it from a false one. And I had given the most accurate cause of this shameful Arminian dogma, which consists in this: they acknowledge no false Church of the Christian name, since all Christian assemblies have this mark which they assign to the true Church, namely that they acknowledge all doctrines not controverted among Christians. Here, on p. 64, after they had again attacked me with their customary slander and their lust for calumny (I believe they measure me by themselves), since after vain shifts they see that they cannot slip away, they return to attacking their own conscience and to mocking God and men, and again deny, against their own conscience, that they taught: that no controversial doctrines among Christians are necessary to salvation. And they call this my first lie [πρῶτον ψεῦδος], and say that I object it to them everywhere, not without disgust.

units.la: Addunt p. 64. eadem: Experientia testatur Remonstrantes agnoscere aliquam Ecclesiam falsam. probant: Nam Remonstrantes aperte profitentur ubique se cum Ecclesiis Contra Remonstrantium bona conscientia communionem colere non posse, quamdiu dogmata sua de Praedestinatione, quae Remonstrantes credunt falsa & noxia esse, non modo pro veris, sed & pro Necessariis creditu ad salutem venditabunt, & contraria Remonstrantium vera dogmata non modo ut falsa damnabunt, sed ut intolerabilia in Ecclesia Christi esse afferent. Hoc cum profiteri eos sciat Vedelius, imo cum hoc iis per convitium saepe exprobret, quomodo fieri potest ut credat eos nullam falsam Ecclesiam Christiani nominis agnoscere? Respondeo: 1. exinde non sequi me falsum dixisse, sed Arminianos, quia in Apologia docent: Nulla dogmata controversa inter Christianos esse Necessaria ad salutem; adeoque coetus errantes errare saltem in non necessariis; hic tamen dicunt dari aliquam falsam Ecclesiam, esse αὐτοκαλακρίτως. Haec duo enim simul subsistere non possunt. 2. Argumentum illud etiam ideo me non urget, quia Arminiani profitentur in Apologia se communionem colere non posse cum Reformatis, non ratione dogmatum Praedestinationis & annexorum, aut quasi in Necessariis errent (nam doctrinam non impeditruram quo minus communionem cum iis colant Arminiani ipsi declarant rant in Apologia ) sed ratione praxeos; seu, quia Arminianos & Hæreti- cos quoívis tolerare nolunt h. e. cum iis communionem spiritualem inire. De quâ re ampl̀e egimus Par. I. lib. 2. c. 5. & infrà rursus agemus contra effugia eorum.
units.tr: They add, on p. 64, the same thing: Experience testifies that the Remonstrants acknowledge some false Church. They prove it: For the Remonstrants openly profess everywhere that they cannot, with a good conscience, keep communion with the Churches of the Contra-Remonstrants, as long as they will put forward their dogmas of predestination, which the Remonstrants believe to be false and harmful, not only as true but as necessary to be believed for salvation, and will not only condemn the contrary true doctrines of the Remonstrants as false, but will declare them intolerable in the Church of Christ. Since Vedelius knows that they profess this, indeed often reproaches them with it by way of abuse, how can it be that he believes they acknowledge no false Church of the Christian name? I answer: first, it does not follow from this that I have said something false, but that the Arminians, who teach in the Apology that no controversial doctrines among Christians are necessary to salvation, and so that erring assemblies err at least only in non-necessary matters, here say that there is some false Church; they are self-condemned [αὐτοκαλακρίτως]. For these two things cannot stand together. Second, this argument does not press me because the Arminians profess in the Apology that they cannot keep communion with the Reformed, not on account of the doctrines of predestination and what is attached to them, nor as if they err in necessary matters (for the Arminians themselves declare in the Apology that doctrine would not hinder them from keeping communion with them), but on account of practice; that is, because they will not tolerate the Arminians and heretics in any way, that is, enter into spiritual communion with them. I have dealt with this matter at length in Part I, book 2, chapter 5, and below we shall again deal with their evasions.

units.la: At, inquiet aliquis, Arminiani habent Reformatos (quos illi Calvi- nianos vocant ) pro Hæreticis. Vocant enim sententiam Calvini de prædestinatione Hæreticam, item cum quâ forte nulla Hæresis comparari me- retur Apol. c. 3. f. 53. a b. Igitur habent Reformatos pro Ecclesiâ falsâ seu errante in Necessariis. Ad illud etiam respondi cap. allegato, & ostendi eos nihilominus, h. e. non obstante doctrinâ illâ Hæreticâ, paratos esse nobiscum communionem colere: quod dicere non possunt si judicant nos errare in Necessariis. Nam cum iis qui errant in Necessariis profitentur tàm in Apologia quàm in Vindiciis se communionem colere nolle. Unde patet eos in eo loco aliter sumere vocem Hæreseos quàm in significatione receptâ; & nos in Apologia ob doctrinam de prædestinatione habere pro Hæreticis, etiamsi illius respectu non erremus in Necessariis, adeòque falsa Ecclesia non simus.
units.tr: But, someone will say, the Arminians regard the Reformed (whom they call Calvinists) as heretics. For they call Calvin's opinion on predestination heretical, and also one with which perhaps no heresy deserves to be compared, Apology, chapter 3, p. 53 a–b. Therefore they regard the Reformed as a Church false or erring in necessary matters. To this too I have replied in the chapter cited, and I showed that they nevertheless, that is, notwithstanding that heretical doctrine, are ready to keep communion with us; which they could not say if they judged that we err in necessary matters. For they profess, both in the Apology and in the Vindiciae, that they are unwilling to keep communion with those who err in necessary matters. From this it is clear that in that passage they take the word heresy in a sense other than the accepted one; and that in the Apology they regard us as heretics on account of the doctrine of predestination, even though with respect to that doctrine we do not err in necessary matters, and so we are not a false Church.

units.la: Quod ajunt me ipsis sæpe per convitium exprobrare, quòd nolint nobiscum communionem colere; id quoque falsum est. Nam potius ego cum omnibus Orthodoxis Deo gratias ago, quòd commune nobis nihil est cum talibus hominibus, qui Orthodoxam doctrinam de Trinitate simulant, animo autem toti delibuti sunt & perfusi fæcibus blasphemiarum Socinianarum; & aperte profitentur se communionem colere cum Hæreticis Antitrinitariis. Itaque de hoc quidem conquestus non sum; sed de eo querebar par. I. lib. 2. cap. 5. quòd profitentur se tolerantiâ suâ mutuâ pacem totius Ecclesiæ procurare velle, & schismata omnia ac sectas totius orbis Christiani componere, interim tamen talem conditionem ponunt, quâ ipsi sciunt nec Pontificios, nec Lutheranos, nec Reformatos acceptare posse; & quia illud sciunt, excludunt omnes eos coetus à pace Ecclesiæ, ac profitentur se eos tolerare nolle, sed tantùm Antitrinitarios seu Socinianos, necnon Libertinos, & ex Anabaptistis hos aut illos in eâ fraternitate spirituali & pace Ecclesiæ comprehendunt, exclusò toto reliquo orbe Christiano, quia is non potest acceptare conditionem illam: Unde conquestus fui, eos cum per tot annos istam tolerantiam mutuam & pacem venditârint, nihil aliud egisse quàm ut ejusmodi illusoriâ impiâ & impossibili pacis pollicitatione toti orbi illuderent.
units.tr: As for their saying that I often reproach them to their face for being unwilling to keep communion with us, that too is false. Rather, I thank God with all the Orthodox that nothing is held in common between us and those men who pretend to hold the Orthodox doctrine of the Trinity, yet whose minds are wholly steeped and drenched in the dregs of Socinian blasphemies, and who openly profess that they keep communion with the Antitrinitarian heretics. Accordingly I have not complained about this. What I did complain of, in Part I, book 2, chapter 5, is that they profess that by their mutual tolerance they wish to secure the peace of the whole Church, and to settle all the schisms and sects of the whole Christian world; yet at the same time they lay down a condition which they know neither the Papists, nor the Lutherans, nor the Reformed can accept. And because they know this, they exclude all those assemblies from the peace of the Church, and profess that they are unwilling to tolerate them, but only the Antitrinitarians or Socinians, as well as the Libertines, and some or other of the Anabaptists, whom they include in that spiritual brotherhood and peace of the Church, while the whole rest of the Christian world is shut out, because it cannot accept that condition. Hence I complained that, though for so many years they have been peddling this mutual tolerance and peace, they have done nothing but mock the whole world with this illusory, impious and impossible promise of peace.

units.la: 4. Denique objeceram ipsis, quòd docent Puram prædicationem verbi non non esse illius notam. Item, nullam esse notam proprie sic dictam Ecclesia. Et addideram causam intimam cur ita sentiant: Nimirum, quia, ut ex praecedentibus unicuique manifestum sit; nota proprie sic dicta vera Ecclesia est qua eam discernit a falsa. Quod si igitur puram praedicationem verbi esse notam Ecclesiae aut aliam aliquam proprie sic dictam notam concederent, cogerentur praesupponere esse aliquam Ecclesiam non veram sed falsam &c. Respondent illi p. 65. hanc causam no esse, sed alias. Verum enimvero quis ipsis in posterum credat, ut etiam antea dixi, quando dicunt hanc suam mentem fuisse aut non fuisse; aut se hac aut illa causa motos hoc vel illud dixisse? Nam, ut ostendi, fide indignos se omnino reddiderunt in futurum, qui negare audent se docuisse quod tam luculenter, tam saepe, & conceptis verbis docuerunt in Apologia, atque etiamnum in Vindicis docent. Fuisse a me allegatam causam verissimam patet ex eo, quia docent Nulla dogmata inter Christianos controversa esse Necessaria ad salutem; & , omnes coetus Christianos qui conveniunt in salutari ac necessaria h. e. secundum ipsos non controversa, doctrina esse veram Ecclesiam: Et sic, cum omnes coetus Christiani conveniant in illa salutari doctrina h. e. non controversa, omnes coetus Christianos esse veram Ecclesiam. Possuntne illi qui ita docent assignare notam aliquam verae Ecclesiae, quae eam discernat a falsa? Et an non illi qui ita docent, tenentur omnino vi suae hypothesis cavere sibi ne assignent notam aliquam talem verae Ecclesiae? Nam si notam aliquam proprie sic dictam assignarent Ecclesiae verae per quam discernatur a falsa; cogerentur utique docere dari Ecclesiam falsam quae erret in Necessariis controversis: quo posito corrueret haec doctrina: Nullum dogma controversum esse Necessarium ad salutem; adeoque collapsa praecipua basi ipse Colossus h. e. Libertinismus propemodum concideret. Quod addunt Conclusionis loco, me non distinguere inter veritatem essentialem & puritatem, salsissimum est. Nam me distinguere inter utramque veritatem, patet ex eo quod conqueror, eos docere in Apologia omnes coetus habere veritatem essentialem seu necessariam, & saltem impuritate laborare. Et sic patet etiam ex hoc capite, me nihil per calumniam ipsis imputasse; quandoquidem partem eorum quae ipsis artribui fatentur, partem negant quidem, sed contra propriam conscientiam suam, ut ostensum.
units.tr: 4. Finally, I had objected to them that they teach that the pure preaching of the Word is not a mark of the Church. Likewise, that there is no mark properly so called of the Church. And I had added the inner reason why they think so: namely, because, as is plain to everyone from what has gone before, a mark properly so called is that by which the true Church is distinguished from the false. So if they conceded that the pure preaching of the Word, or some other mark properly so called, is a mark of the Church, they would be forced to presuppose that there is some Church which is not true but false, and so on. They answer on p. 65 that this is not the reason, but another one. But indeed, who will believe them from now on, as I have said before, when they say what their own mind was, or was not; or that they spoke this or that because they were moved by this or that reason? For, as I have shown, they have made themselves wholly unworthy of belief in future, since they dare to deny that they taught what they taught so plainly, so often, and in express words in the Apology, and still teach in the Vindication. That the reason I alleged was most true is clear from the fact that they teach that no doctrines disputed among Christians are necessary to salvation, and that all Christian assemblies which agree in the saving and necessary (that is, according to them, undisputed) doctrine are the true Church. And so, since all Christian assemblies agree in that saving doctrine, that is, in what is undisputed, all Christian assemblies are the true Church. Can those who teach thus assign any mark of the true Church by which it may be distinguished from the false? And are not those who teach thus bound, by the very force of their hypothesis, to take care that they do not assign any such mark of the true Church? For if they assigned to the true Church some mark properly so called by which it is distinguished from the false, they would of necessity be compelled to teach that there is a false Church which errs in disputed necessary matters; and once that is granted, their doctrine that no disputed doctrine is necessary to salvation would collapse, and with its chief support gone, that very Colossus, namely Libertinism, would almost fall down. What they add by way of conclusion, that I do not distinguish between essential truth and purity, is most false. For that I do distinguish between the two kinds of truth is plain from my complaint that they teach, in the Apology, that all assemblies have essential or necessary truth, and suffer at least from impurity. And so it is also clear from this chapter that I have imputed nothing to them by calumny; since they confess that some of what is ascribed to them is true, and deny the rest, but do so against their own conscience, as has been shown.

units.la: CAP. II.
units.tr: CHAPTER II.

units.la: Examen Capitis I I. Vindic. lib. 2.
units.tr: Examination of Chapter II. Vindication, book 2.

units.la: 1. Arminianos contra propriam conscientiam suam negare dogmata sibi in hoc capite objecta ostenditur. Ad effugium & cavillum quoddam eorum circa hanc negationem respondetur. Non negant se duas vias salutis statuere, unam commodiorem, alteram incommodiorem. 2. Calumnia eorum diluitur, quâ Reformatos accusant, ac si aliorum hominum saluti qui Reformatam Religionem non profitentur, non faveant. 3. Novem Corollaria nostra à cavillis Arminianorum vindicantur. 4. Virulentissima & calumniosissima retorsio eorum in doctrinam nostram de Electione diluitur. Eos totam Religionem Christianam, seu totam doctrinam Evangelii ludibrio Atheorum, infidelium, Turcarum, Iudaeorum exponere ista calumniosa suâ retorsione, ostenditur. 5. Arminiani ministri non negant se vi suae doctrinae posse se & alios ingerere in coetus nostros, ut rem secta sua faciant. Defenduntur Respublica & Ecclesia Reformata, quae juramento sibi cavent adversum Antitrinitarios. Exemplum Constantini Magni circa Arium. 6. Arminianorum mala fides circa judicium eorum de Martyribus nostris. Impostura eorum insignis in hac re detegitur. 7. Quaestio, an, & quomodo liceat ad Martyrum sanguinem & auctoritatem provocare, deciditur adversus Arminianos, secundum Scripturam, ex praxi Ecclesiae veteris, ex Theodoreto, Athanasio, Socrate, Sozomeno.
units.tr: 1. The Arminians are shown to deny against their own conscience the doctrines objected to them in this chapter. Their evasion and quibble about this denial is answered. They do not deny that they set up two ways of salvation, one more convenient and the other less convenient. 2. Their calumny is refuted, by which they accuse the Reformed of not favouring the salvation of those men who do not profess the Reformed Religion. 3. Our nine Corollaries are defended against the cavils of the Arminians. 4. Their most virulent and calumnious retorsion against our doctrine of Election is refuted. It is shown that by this calumnious retorsion they expose the whole Christian Religion, or the whole doctrine of the Gospel, to the mockery of atheists, unbelievers, Turks and Jews. 5. The Arminian ministers do not deny that by the force of their doctrine they can thrust themselves and others into our congregations, so as to make the thing serve their sect. The Commonwealth and the Reformed Church are defended, which take precautions by oath against the Antitrinitarians. The example of Constantine the Great concerning Arius. 6. The Arminians' bad faith regarding their judgement of our Martyrs. Their notable imposture in this matter is exposed. 7. The question whether, and how, it is lawful to appeal to the blood and authority of the Martyrs is decided against the Arminians, according to Scripture, from the practice of the ancient Church, from Theodoret, Athanasius, Socrates and Sozomen.

units.la: 1. DOgmata quae ipsis objeci cap. 2. Par. I. lib. 2. haec sunt: Unumquemque Christianum in quocunque coetu impuro salvari posse; seu, ut loquitur Ecclesia Christiana, quamcunque Religionem Christiani nominis profiteatur. Item: Posse & debere aliquem interdum, etsi sciat vel sentiat coetum in quo est impurum esse; tamen manere in eo: hoc est, ut Christiana Ecclesia loquitur, etsi credat aut sciat Religionem aliquam falsam esse, tamen non verum sed falsam profiteri. Item: Licere sententiam suam circa Controversias mutare in horas imo infinities; h. e. ut Christiana Ecclesia loquitur, deficere à Religione gione Christiana una ad aliam quoties lubet. Denique: Duas esse vias salutis, unam commodiorem, nimirum coetum purum, alteram incommodiorem, nimirum coetum impurum.
units.tr: 1. The doctrines which I objected to them in chapter 2, part I, book 2, are these: That every Christian in any impure congregation can be saved; or, as the Christian Church puts it, whatever Religion of the Christian name he professes. Likewise: That someone may and ought sometimes, even if he knows or senses that the congregation in which he is is impure, nevertheless to remain in it; that is, as the Christian Church speaks, even if he believes or knows some Religion to be false, yet to profess it not as true but as false. Likewise: That it is lawful to change one's opinion about the Controversies every hour, indeed infinitely often; that is, as the Christian Church speaks, to fall away from the one Christian Religion to another as often as one pleases. Finally: That there are two ways of salvation, one more convenient, namely the pure congregation, the other less convenient, namely the impure congregation.

units.la: Hic vero Lector facile conjicere poterit, quod effugium Arminiani adversus accusationes has gravissimas captaverint. Negant enim tria priora dogmata. Nam quartum de duplici via salutis non negant, sed illud sicco pede transeunt. Negant autem tria illa ex eo fundamento, quod non docuerint: Nulla dogmata quae Controversa sunt inter Christianos aut controverti in futurum possint, esse necessaria ad salutem. Adeoque rursus impie & proterve contra conscientiae suae dictamen agunt, negantes se docuisse quod in Apologia conceptis verbis docuerunt, atque etiamnum in his Vindiciis docent, ut ostensum libro priore cap. 8. & Par. III. lib. 2. c. 1. quo posteriore loco demonstravi, eos tantum Deo & hominibus illudere conari, quando in Vindiciis suis dicunt se agnoscere dogmata quaedam controversa necessaria ad salutem. Hoc igitur egregio scilicet modo respondent hi boni & honesti viri. Interim tamen, ut me strenue & ample refutatum putent simpliciores & qui ab iis decepti sunt; ac ut causae cognitionem obscurent & praepediant, sedecim integras paginas complent nugis suis. Quas ego omnes transfire possem; quia de re constat. Quoniam tamen inter alia hoc agunt, ut hic mendaciis & calumniis turpissimis doctrinam Reformatam onerent: breviter respondebo.
units.tr: Here the Reader will easily be able to conjecture what evasion the Arminians have seized upon against these most grave accusations. For they deny the three former doctrines. As for the fourth, concerning the twofold way of salvation, they do not deny it, but pass over it with dry feet. They deny those three, however, on the ground that they did not teach: that no doctrines which are controverted among Christians, or may in future be controverted, are necessary to salvation. And so again they act impiously and shamelessly against the dictate of their own conscience, denying that they taught what they expressly taught in the Apology, and what they still teach in this Vindication, as shown in the first book, chapter 8, and part III, book 2, chapter 1, where in the latter place I demonstrated that they only try to mock God and men when, in their Vindication, they say that they acknowledge certain controverted doctrines to be necessary to salvation. Thus these good and honest men answer in this splendid manner. Meanwhile, so that simpler folk, who have been deceived by them, may think I have been vigorously and fully refuted, and so that they may obscure and hinder knowledge of the cause, they fill sixteen whole pages with their trifles. I could pass over all of them, since the matter is settled. Yet since among other things they aim to load our doctrine here with the most shameful lies and calumnies, I will answer briefly.

units.la: Post generalem igitur responsionem illam suam, qua, ut dixi, hi homines palam faciunt se Conscientiae suae nuncium dudum misisse; aliud argumentum addunt, quo volunt probare se illa tria non docere. Argumentum hoc est: Si Remonstrantes ista tria aut saltem duo priora credunt, ut vult Vedelius, tum pro indubitato haberi debet Remonstrantes credere, non tantum Reformatos qui ab Ecclesia pontificia se separarunt, sed & se ipsos stultissime fecisse quod ab Ecclesiis (contra Remonstrantium separari se passi sint, cum honorum, stipendiorum, & libertatis suae jactura, aut quod separati ad eas non redeant &c.
units.tr: After that general answer of theirs, by which, as I said, these men openly show that they long ago sent a messenger to their conscience, they add another argument by which they want to prove that they do not teach those three doctrines. The argument is this: If the Remonstrants believe these three, or at least the first two, as Vedelius wants, then it must be held beyond doubt that the Remonstrants believe not only that the Reformed, who separated themselves from the Papal Church, but also that they themselves, acted most foolishly in allowing themselves to be separated from the Churches (against the Remonstrants), with loss of honours, stipends and liberty, or in not returning to them when separated, etc.

units.la: Respondeo: Quod ad Reformatos attinet, sequitur omnino eos secundum doctrinam Arminianorum, speciatim de Necessariis ac non Necessariis, stultissime fecisse quod ab Ecclesia Pontificia se separarunt. Ad Arminianos quod attinet, non sequitur exinde pro indubitato haberi debere Arminianos credere se stulte fecisse in eo. Sed tunc sequeretur, si Arminiani omnem spem abjecissent conatus suos ad finem perducendi. Atqui nec spem nec animum abjecerunt, prout ipsi fatentur Vindic. lib. 2. c. 9. p. 161 ubi dicunt Religionem suam nunc latiore paululum vultu esse. Sperant igitur etiamnum, fore ut tandem votis suis potiantur h. e. opprimant Orthodoxos Magistratus, Populos, Pastores; & blasphemias Turcicas Socinianorum liberè profiteantur: quem in finem delegerunt medium aptissimum, Libertinismum scilicet; prout omnia haec Illustrissimis Ordinibus Generalibus ostensa sunt Parte II. Arcanorum. Et haec quidem spes ipsos nequaquam fallet, nisi serio & mox ipsis obviam eant Illustrissimi Ordines cum fortissimo Heroe Henrico Friderico Principe Aurasionensi. Itaque non debet, ut hic nobis persuadere volunt Armiiniani, pro indubitato haberi, si verum sit quod ipsis objeci, eos credere se stultissime fecisse quod se ab Ecclesiis Reformatis separari passi sint, ut hic loquuntur. Atque haec quidem de duplice illorum responsione generali dicta sunto.
units.tr: I answer: As far as the Reformed are concerned, it does indeed follow, according to the doctrine of the Arminians, especially concerning Necessary and not Necessary things, that they acted most foolishly in separating themselves from the Papal Church. As far as the Arminians are concerned, it does not follow that it must be held beyond doubt that the Arminians believe they acted foolishly in this. But that would follow only if the Arminians had given up all hope of bringing their endeavours to an end. Yet they have neither given up hope nor courage, as they themselves admit in Vindication, book 2, chapter 9, page 161, where they say that their Religion is now somewhat more broadly spread. They therefore still hope that they will at last attain their wishes, that is, oppress the orthodox magistrates, peoples and ministers, and freely profess the Turkish blasphemies of the Socinians. To this end they have chosen the most suitable means, namely Libertinism; as all these things were shown to the Most Illustrious General Estates in Part II of the Arcana. And this hope will by no means fail them, unless the Most Illustrious Estates, together with the most valiant hero Henry Frederick, Prince of Orange, seriously and soon meet them face to face. Therefore, if what I objected to them is true, it ought not, as the Arminians here want to persuade us, to be held beyond doubt that they believe they acted most foolishly in allowing themselves to be separated from the Reformed Churches, as they here put it. And so much for be said about their twofold general answer.

units.la: 2. Videamus quid in specie ad singula illa tria dogmata sibi objecta respondeant. Primum igitur quod attinet, nimirum Unumquemque Christianum in suâ Religione salvari posse, initio antequam ad rem veniant, calumniantur p. 67. Reformatos, ac si aliorum hominum extra Ecclesias Reformatas constitutorum saluti non faverent, aut extra eas nullos coetus esse putarent in quâ salutis æternæ spes locum habeat, & ideo gravissimis convitiis nos proscindunt, immisericordes, miseros, hostes salutis hominum nos appellant; item dicunt nos putare Deum inclementem esse. Quae merae sunt calumniae. Nam quod ad nos attinet, favemus saluti non eorum solum qui Reformatae Religioni addicti sunt; sed etiam omnium hominum saluti. Verum eum favorem non extendimus ultra charitatis nobis à Deo praescriptae lineam. Videndum quippe est, quomodo faveas saluti aliorum? Favor ille non in eo consistit; ut salutem iis promittas quibus Deus eam non promisit in verbo suo, ac doceas unumquemque Christianum in suâ Religione salvari posse, ut Arminiani in Apologiâ suâ docent: sed ut ad Deum preces fundas pro omnibus hominibus ex praescripto ipsius 1. Tim. 2. 1. Ut in id labores doctrinâ ac vitâ sanctâ, quo proximus tuus convertatur, ac efficias ut luceat lux tua coram hominibus, quo videant bona opera tua, & Patrem Coelestem glorificent. Agnoscimus etiam salutem esse in aliis coetibus Evangelicis, quos nos pro coetibus doctrinae puritate laborantibus habemus, Arminiani autem pro errantibus in fundamento Haereticis habent ob doctrinam de coercendis & non tolerandis Antitrinitariis. Statuimus denique Deum in aliis coetibus, etiam errantibus in fundamento, electos suos habere, quos ante mortem ad agnitionem veritatis salutaris & veram poenitentiam adducat. cat. Itaque non ægrè ferimus, quòd saluti multorum, ut quidem præ se ferunt, faveant Arminiani; sed agrè ferimus, quòd non rectè faveant, id quod nihil aliud est quàm revera non favere; h. e. quòd Libertinismum axiomateisto primo suo in Apologia invehunt, in eum præcipuè finem ut blasphemias Turcicas Socinianorum introducant; & quod, cùm in cœtibus omnibus qui Deum in tribus personis adorant inveniant aut comminis- antur errore fundamentale, tamen in Antitrinitariorum, speciatim Socinianorum sectâ hactenus nullum reperierunt errorem fundamentalem, ac docent illos salvari in suâ Religione posse. Quare ipsos non juvat negare propriam doctrinam suam, ac dicere p. 68. me falso dicere, ipsos statuere Christianum unumquemque in suâ Religione salvari posse. Nam quemadmodum id ibi negant eo prætextu quòd non docuerint Nulla dogmata controversa esse necessaria ad salutem, in quo, ut luce clarius meridianâ ostendi, contra conscientiam suam improbissimè faciunt, ita manet speciale hoc crimen quod ipsis capite meo secundo Part. I. lib. 2. objeci p. 109. nimirum eos statuere Antitrinitarios seu Socinianos in suâ Haresi servari posse, etiamsi sententiam suam non mutent, sed in blasphemiis suis obstinatè persistant. Ad hoc illi, quia id negare nullo colore possunt, ne verbum quidem respondent. Præterea, ex eo quoque apparet eos id primum dogma contra conscientiam suam negare, quod in suis Vindiciis eos non damnant qui in Necessariis controversis dogmatis errant, sed docent illos servari in suo isto errore posse, ut vidimus Par. III. lib. 2. c. 1. & cap. 4. §. 14. Denique, ex inductione sectarum & cœtuum Christianorum illud manifestum fit. Præterquam enim quòd credunt se salvari posse in Arminianismo suo, docent etiam Antitrinitarios, & speciatim Socinianos, salvari posse, ut sæpè vidimus. Docent in hoc ipso capite secundo Pontificios in suâ Religione servari posse p. 80. ut ostendimus Par. III. lib. 2. c. 2. §. 3. Græcos etiam non damnant Arminiani, nec damnare possunt, quia Pontificios, quos tamen pro manifestariis idololatris habent, in suâ Religione salvari posse docent. Non diffitebuntur Lutheranos in suâ Religione servari posse. Expressè etiam dicunt Reformatos salvari posse, etiamsi iis tribuant calumniosissimè hæreses tales quæ ne in atheum quidem cadere queant nisi hominem exuat, ut ostendimus eâdem Par. III. lib. 2. cap. 8. §. 9. Nec denique Anabaptistis in suâ Religione salutem negant. Non autem alii cœtus Christiani nominis hactenus fuerunt quàm modò memorati, nisi fanaticos quosdam seorsim sumere velis. Et sic verissimum est quod dixi, eos statuere unumquemque quemque in suâ Religione salvari posse. Iam, Coronidis loco, concilient mihi haec duo; nimirum quòd docent in his vindiciis suis: Reformatos, Lutheranos, Pontificios errare in Necessariis; & tamen eos salvari posse in suis istis haeresibus & fundamentalibus erroribus.
units.tr: 2. Let us see what they answer, in particular, to each of those three doctrines objected to them. First, then, as far as the first doctrine is concerned, namely that every Christian can be saved in his own Religion, before they come to the matter, they calumniate the Reformed on p. 67, as if they did not favour the salvation of other men who live outside the Reformed Churches, or as if they thought there were no congregations outside them in which the hope of eternal salvation has a place; and so they tear us apart with the gravest abuse, calling us merciless, wretched, enemies of the salvation of men; they also say that we think God to be unmerciful. These are mere calumnies. For as far as we are concerned, we favour the salvation not only of those who are attached to the Reformed Religion, but of all men. Yet we do not extend that favour beyond the line of charity prescribed to us by God. For one must see how you favour the salvation of others. That favour does not consist in this: that you promise salvation to those to whom God has not promised it in his word, and teach that every Christian can be saved in his own Religion, as the Arminians teach in their Apology; but in this: that you pour out prayers to God for all men according to his prescription, 1 Tim. 2.1; that you labour by doctrine and holy life to this end, that your neighbour may be converted, and that you bring it about that your light shines before men, so that they may see your good works and glorify your Heavenly Father. We also acknowledge that there is salvation in other Evangelical congregations, which we regard as congregations labouring under impurity of doctrine, though the Arminians regard them as heretics who err in the foundation, on account of the doctrine concerning the coercing and not tolerating of Antitrinitarians. Finally, we hold that God has his elect in other congregations, even those erring in the foundation, whom before death he brings to the knowledge of the saving truth and to true repentance. Therefore we are not grieved that the Arminians favour the salvation of many, as indeed they profess; but we are grieved that they do not favour it rightly, which is nothing other than in truth not to favour it at all; that is, that in the first axiom of their Apology they introduce Libertinism, chiefly with this end in view, that they may bring in the Turkish blasphemies of the Socinians; and that, although in all congregations which worship God in three persons they find, or invent, a fundamental error, yet in the sect of the Antitrinitarians, especially the Socinians, they have hitherto found no fundamental error, and teach that these can be saved in their Religion. Therefore it does not help them to deny their own doctrine and to say on p. 68 that I falsely say that they hold that every Christian can be saved in his own Religion. For just as they deny this there on the pretext that they did not teach that no controverted doctrines are necessary to salvation, in which, as I have shown as clearly as midday light, they act most shamelessly against their own conscience, so there remains this special charge which I objected to them in my second chapter, Part I, book 2, p. 109, namely that they hold that Antitrinitarians or Socinians can be preserved in their heresy, even if they do not change their opinion, but persist obstinately in their blasphemies. To this, since they can deny it under no pretext, they do not answer even a word. Moreover, from this also it appears that they deny that first doctrine against their own conscience, since in their Vindications they do not condemn those who err in controverted necessary doctrines, but teach that they can be preserved in that error, as we saw in Part III, book 2, chapter 1, and chapter 4, §14. Finally, it becomes manifest from the enumeration of sects and Christian congregations. For besides their believing that they can be saved in their Arminianism, they also teach that Antitrinitarians, and especially Socinians, can be saved, as we have often seen. In this very second chapter they teach that the Papists can be preserved in their Religion, p. 80, as we showed in Part III, book 2, chapter 2, §3. The Arminians also do not condemn the Greeks, nor can they condemn them, because they teach that the Papists, whom nevertheless they regard as manifest idolaters, can be saved in their Religion. They will not deny that the Lutherans can be preserved in their Religion. They also expressly say that the Reformed can be saved, even though they most calumniously attribute to them such heresies as could not fall even into an atheist unless he put off the man, as we showed in the same Part III, book 2, chapter 8, §9. Nor finally do they deny salvation in their Religion to the Anabaptists. Yet apart from those just mentioned there have hitherto been no other Christian sects, unless you wish to take certain fanatics separately. And thus it is most true, what I said, that they hold that every Christian can be saved in his own Religion. Now, by way of a crown, let these two points agree with me: namely that they teach in these their Vindications that the Reformed, the Lutherans and the Papists err in necessary matters, and yet that they can be saved in those their heresies and fundamental errors.

units.la: Atque haec quidem de responsione ipsorum indirectâ ad dogma primum. Directa eorum responsio p. 68. 69. 70. ad istud primum ut & secundum ac tertium dogma sibi à me objectum, continet aliud nihil quàm nugas multas eâ improbitate solitâ nixas, qua negant se docuisse: Nulla dogmata controversaesse necessaria ad salutem. Cui improbitati alia accedit, quod ideò negant se docere: Licere alicui Religionem profiteri quàm in animo suo sentit seu putat falsam esse; quia dicunt hoc non esse profiteri Religionem aliquam, quando quis manet in coetu aliquo & cum eo communicat; quod profectò est facto ipso profiteri Religionem illam; de qua re egimus Par. III. lib. 2. c. 2. §. 1. Quam vere autem objecerim ipsis hoc dogma de simulatione in Religionis negocio; patet etiam ex praxi istorum hominum, qua re ipsa verissimam faciunt accusationem hanc. Simulant enim professione externâ Orthodoxam doctrinam de Trinitate; ex animo autem addicti sunt blasphemiis Socinianorum contra Filium Dei; prout luce clarius meridianâ ostendi Parte II. Arcanorum.
units.tr: And this is what I have to say about their indirect response to the first dogma. Their direct response, at pp. 68, 69 and 70, to that first dogma objected to them by me, and to the second and third, contains nothing but many trifles, resting on that customary impudence by which they deny that they taught No controverted doctrines are necessary to salvation. To this impudence another is added: they deny that they teach It is lawful for anyone to profess a religion which in his mind he judges or thinks to be false, because they say that this is not professing a religion when someone remains in some assembly and communicates with it. Yet by the very deed this is certainly to profess that religion, a matter we treated in Part III, book 2, ch. 2, §1. How truly I objected to them this dogma of dissimulation in religious affairs is also evident from the practice of these men, which in fact makes my accusation most true. For they feign the orthodox doctrine of the Trinity by outward profession, while in their hearts they are devoted to the blasphemies of the Socinians against the Son of God, as I showed as clearly as the noonday light in Part II of the Arcana.

units.la: 3. A dogmatis sibi à me objectis veniunt Arminiani ad Corollaria novem quae ex illis elicueram. Primum Corollarium meum est, quo dijudicandum unicuique reliqui: An non Doctrina Arminianorum qua statuunt aliquem debere interdum aliam Religionem profiteri quàm eam cui in animo suo addictus est, Regnis, Principibus, Rebuspublicis periculosissima sit? Speciatim an non hac egregia machina sit, qua in Principum consuetudinem & consilia Rerumpublicarum introduci possint nebulones, qui extrinsecus Religionem Principis alicujus seu Reipublicae profiteantur, quo à Consiliorum & actionum ipsius cognitione non excludantur, ac ea hostibus prodere possint? Et, ut manifestum fieret, addidi probationem ex experientiâ petitam, quae manifestum facit solere à quibusdam Jesuitas & alios ejus farinae homines qua Ecclesiasticos qua Politicos immitti in aulas principum & in Curias consiliorum prodendorum causâ. Secundo dijudicandum etiam omnibus reliqui, an non ista maxima vitia Regum ac Principum exitialis sit? & an non eo praetextu subornari possint parricidae qui veram Religionem simulantes vitis Principum insidientur. Quod etiam probavi experientia harum provinciarum in persona Magni illius Herois Gulielmi Principis Aurasionensis, in cujus aulam & caput subsidio maxima istius immissus fuit parricida ille, qui laudatissimum Heroem ilum lum trucidavit. Ad primum igitur & secundum istud Corollarium respondent primo p. 71. per negationem consequentiae. Verum consequentia firma est, nixa dogmate Apologiae: Nulla dogmata inter Christianos controversa esse Necessaria ad salutem. Viigitur hujus dogmatis, nec non doctrinae Apologiae de coetibus impuris; aliquis qui hactenus Religionem Reformatam professus est, postea autem à Jesuita aut Arminano seductus illius aut hujus Religionem veram esse credit, non tenetur profiteri novam suam fidem, & sese adjungere publica professione Pontificiis aut Arminianis, sed manere in vetere coetu suo; utpote qui non est falsa Ecclesia, sed coetus tantum impurus, quia non errat nisi in controversis dogmatis, quorum nullum est necessarium ad salutem. Quod an'nō Rebuspublicis & vitis Principum periculosissimum sit, rursus unicuique dijudicandum relinquo! Quid enim? an'non hoc est docere, quòd simulare adeòque facto ipso mentiri in negocio Religionis liceat? Itaque quod hic Arminiani negant consequentiam; faciunt nixi perfidia sua qua contra conscientiam suam se docuisse negant, quod revera docent Apologia sua.
units.tr: 3. From the dogmas objected to them by me the Arminians come to the nine corollaries I drew from them. My first corollary is this, to be judged by everyone else: Is not the doctrine of the Arminians, which holds that someone may sometimes profess a religion other than the one to which he is inwardly attached, most dangerous to kingdoms, princes and commonwealths? Specifically, is this not an excellent contrivance by which scoundrels may be introduced into the company and councils of princes and commonwealths, professing outwardly the religion of some prince or commonwealth, so that they are not excluded from knowledge of its counsels and actions and may betray them to enemies? And, so that this might be made plain, I added a proof drawn from experience, which shows that Jesuits and other men of that stamp, both churchmen and politicians, are commonly sent into the courts of princes and the councils of state for the purpose of betrayal. Second, let everyone also judge whether this most serious vice of kings and princes is not deadly? And whether assassins, pretending to hold the true religion, cannot be suborned under that pretext to lie in wait for the lives of princes? I also proved this from the experience of these provinces in the person of that great hero William, Prince of Orange, into whose court and person that assassin, sent with great assistance, was introduced, who slew that most praiseworthy hero. To the first and second of this corollary they reply, first, at p. 71, by denying the consequence. But the consequence is sound, resting on the dogma of the Apology: No doctrines controverted among Christians are necessary to salvation. Therefore, by this dogma and the Apology's doctrine on impure assemblies, someone who until now has professed the Reformed religion, but who has afterwards been seduced by a Jesuit or an Arminian into believing that this or that religion is true, is not bound to profess his new faith publicly, to join himself to the Papists or the Arminians, but may remain in his old assembly. For that assembly is not a false Church but only an impure assembly, since it errs only in controverted doctrines, none of which is necessary to salvation. Whether this is most dangerous to commonwealths and to the lives of princes, I again leave to everyone to judge! For what? Is this not to teach that it is lawful to dissemble, and thus by the very deed to lie, in matters of religion? So when the Arminians deny the consequence, they do so relying on their perfidy, by which they deny that they taught, against their own conscience, what in truth they teach in their Apology.

units.la: Deinde respondent ibidem & p. 72. 73. quae prolixè ab ipsis & amplè diffusa in pauca redigam. Summa eò redit: Neminem virum bonum abusurum esse ista doctrina Arminianorum, qui quidem credit hac dogmata necessaria & non controversa, sive in quibus omnes (christiani, Pontificiis, inquiunt, exceptis,) convenIunt: ne quis perjurus sit; ne Principi suo fidem fallat; ne Patriam vel Remp. suam in qua est, & cui jurejurando obstrictus est hosti prodat; ne vitae ullius nedum principis insidietur: Et Maximam istam animi aut fiducia nihil addere posse ad fallendum Principem. Ista machina professionis externa opus neminem habere, nisi prius bonam mentem & conscientiam ejeraverit; talem hominem quemcunque praetextum posse adhibere, ut quod illicitum sibi est exequatur; non autem opus habere ut illa maxima Remonstrantium sceleris causam det. At ab iis qui firma fide credunt illa quae modo dicta sunt, & sic bona conscientia rationem praecipue habendam censent, ab iis prodiciones, consilia, cades Principum expectandas non esse. in specie quod ad exemplum parricidii perpetrati a simulatore nebulone illo Balthasare Gerhardi, dicunt maximam illam tanto scelericausam non dedisse. Eum jam antea sceleratum animum habuisse, & alia incitamenta, speciatim eorum qui tam pio, uti credebant, propositio, Martyrii coronam proponebant, & suggerebant licitum esse & gloriosum rebellem Ecclesiae Principem atque Haereticum quovis modo è medio tollere. Eum parricidam simulasse Religionem, quam non habebat pro impura sed Haeretica, in qua fundamentum salutis lutis evertitur. At Remonstrantes loquuntur de dissimulatione, inquiunt, aut professione tolerationis ejusmodi dogmatum quae salutis fundamentum non evertant. Deinde addunt, quibus rationibus vita Principis in tuto esse aut non esse possit; ac denique repetunt maximam illam, etiamsi eam docerent Remonstrantes, nec Rebuffus, nec Principibus noxiam esse posse; neminemque ea abuti posse nisi sceleratos & deplorata malitia homines, qui fas omne & nefas simul[?]que debent, & optima quaeque scelerum suorum remedia vertunt in scelerum suorum nutrimenta ac fomenta; & sic consectarium hoc locum habere non posse nisi in hominibus enormiter & perdite malis &c.
units.tr: Then they reply in the same place and at pp. 72 and 73, and I will reduce to a few words what they have set out at length and in full. The sum comes to this: No good man will abuse this Arminian doctrine, who indeed believes these dogmas to be necessary and not controverted, or those on which all agree (the Papists, they say, excepted), so that he will not be perjured, will not deceive his prince, will not betray his country or commonwealth in which he lives, and to which he is bound by oath, to an enemy, will not plot against the life of any person, much less of a prince. And this greatest of maxims: confidence in one's own mind or courage can add nothing to deceiving a prince. The outward machine of profession needs no one, unless he has first forsworn a good mind and conscience; such a man may use any pretext to carry out what is unlawful for him, but he does not need that greatest maxim to give cause for the crime of the Remonstrants. But from those who firmly believe what has just been said, and who therefore consider a good conscience to be the chief consideration, treacheries, plots and slaughters of princes are not to be expected. In particular, as regards the example of the parricide committed by that dissembling scoundrel Balthasar Gerhard, they say that the greatest maxim did not give cause for so great a crime. He already had a wicked mind, and other incitements, especially from those who, as they believed, held out to him the crown of martyrdom under so pious a proposal, and suggested that it was lawful and glorious to remove by any means a rebel prince and heretic of the Church. That parricide feigned a religion which he did not regard as impure but as heretical, in which the foundation of salvation is overthrown. But the Remonstrants speak, they say, of dissimulation, or of profession of toleration, of dogmas of this kind which do not overthrow the foundation of salvation. Then they add by what reasons the life of a prince can or cannot be safe; and finally they repeat that greatest maxim, even if the Remonstrants taught it, can be harmful neither to the Reformed nor to princes, and no one can abuse it except wicked men of desperate malice, who mix all right and wrong, and turn every best remedy for their crimes into the nourishment and fuel of their crimes; and so this consequence cannot hold except in men enormously and utterly evil, etc.

units.la: His prolixis nugis breviter respondeo, eas esse partim impertinentes, partim ineptas, partim falsas. Impertinens est: quod dicunt neminem abusurum ista maxima, nisi homo sceleratus jam antea sit. Hoc enim adversum me non facit, utpote qui expresse dixeram, hanc maximam idoneam esse, qua NEBULONES ad scelera sua exequenda utantur. Impertinens etiam est, quod dicunt hanc maximam non posse esse aut non fuisse causam sceleris. Nam non dixi maximam eam posse esse causam sceleris, prout hic vocem causa sumunt Arminiani, sed esse machinam qua sceelus executioni detur, seu medium exsequendi impii & nefarii instituti ac consilii. Ineptum est, quod sic argumentantur: Nullus bonus abusurus est ista maxima. Ergo ea non est perniciosa Reip. ac vitis Principum. Nam pernicies ista non a bonis sed a malis est expectanda. Ineptum etiam est, quod inter Necessaria non Controversa ponunt dogmata ista: ne quis perjurus fit &c. & tamen dicunt Pontificios ea negare. Falsum est, eum qui has maximas credit: non licere Principi suo fidem fallere; ne perjurus fit; ne vita Principis insidietur &c. non posse ista maxima uti ad scelus suum exequendum. Nam credet quidem istas maximas, & tamen simulator talis occidere conabitur Principem; quia scilicet eum non habet pro Principe sed Tyranno: item fallere eum conabitur ex eodem fundamento, quia putat licere fallere non Principem sed Tyrannum. Experientia docet me verum dicere. Nam ut alia exempla taceam & longe non eam, patet illud ex conspiratione quam Arminiani Theologi non pauci una cum aliis inire ante annos undecim contra vitam Illustrissimi & laudatissimi Herois Mauritii Principis Aurasionensis; nec non contra statum Reipublicae. In ea conspiratione illi homines praxi sua manifestum fecere quod dico. Nam ex conspiratoribus quidam, ut ex sententia Curiae Hollandicae patet, professus est se in conscientia sua re examinasse ac deprehendisse non esse peccatum occidere Principem illum nunquam satis laudandum. dum. Et ex complicibus Theologis Arminianis Slatium ministrum olim Bleiswicensem (qui M. Episcopio ibi successerat Διάδοχος ἀγαθὸς, φασὶν ἀγαθὸς, Viri boni boni, ut loqui proverbio solent, successor, liceat enim in re dissimili verbis uti Eusebii loquentis de Anatolio successore alterius Eusebii in Episcopatu Laodiceno lib. 2. cap. 26.) introducunt ipsi Arminiani in Epistola quadam Belgica loquente de illustrissimis Ordinibus & de illustrissimo Principe Mauritio, ac dicentem se credere licere fallere Tyrannos. Similiter omnes conspiratores Arminiani Pastores & alii qui eodem anno 1623 & praecedente tunc conspiraverant in subvertendam Rempublicam, norant non licere subvertere Rempublicam, & tamen illud conabantur, ut testantur sententiæ contra ipsos latæ; quia scilicet non judicabant hoc esse subvertere Rempublicam, sed vocabant hoc more loquendi inter ipsos solenni; Regnum Israelis restituere. Ita Balthasar Gerhardus parricida ille norat non licere privato ullum hominem interficere, & tamen id tentavit atque effecit; quia scilicet Principem laudatissimum non considerabat ut hominem simpliciter, aut ut Principem, sed ut rebellem & Haereticum, ut hic ipsi Arminiani dicunt. Itaque etiam ab illis hominibus qui dogmata illa tenent, maxima illa Arminianorum ad exequendum scelus adhiberi potest; credendo scilicet ea dogmata, sed non applicando ad Principem hunc aut ad Rempublicam hanc. Hic, ut hoc obiter dicam, Arminiani concilient hæc duo; nimirum quod hic dicunt Pontificios negare hoc dogma; ne quis perjurus sit, item, non licere vita ullius, etiam vilissimi hominis, nedum Principis insidiari: & tamen Vindic. lib. 1. c. 8. p. 47. dicunt inter alia: Deum prohibere perjurium nemo in dubium vocare potest, neque unquam quisquam negavit aut in dubium vocavit, qui verbum Dei in V. & N. T. expressum pro verbo Dei habet.
units.tr: To these lengthy trifles I briefly reply that they are partly irrelevant, partly absurd, and partly false. It is irrelevant that they say no one will abuse this greatest maxim unless he is already a wicked man. For this does not tell against me, since I had expressly said that this maxim is suited to be used by SCOUNDRELS to carry out their crimes. Also irrelevant is their claim that this maxim cannot be, or was not, the cause of the crime. For I did not say that the maxim could be the cause of the crime, in the sense in which the Arminians take the word cause, but that it is a machine by which a crime is put into effect, or a means of carrying out an impious and wicked plan or design. It is absurd that they argue thus: No good man will abuse this maxim. Therefore it is not pernicious to the commonwealth and the lives of princes. For this harm is to be expected not from good men but from bad. It is also absurd that they place these dogmas among the necessary, non-controverted ones, that no one should become perjured, etc., and yet say that the Papists deny them. It is false that a man who believes these maxims, that it is not lawful to deceive one's prince; that one should not become perjured; that one should not lie in wait for a prince's life, etc., cannot use these maxims to carry out his crime. For such a dissembler will indeed believe these maxims, and yet will try to kill the prince, because he does not regard him as a prince but as a tyrant; likewise he will try to deceive him on the same ground, because he thinks it lawful to deceive not a prince but a tyrant. Experience teaches that I speak the truth. For, to pass over other examples, and not to go far afield, it is shown by the conspiracy which not a few Arminian theologians, together with others, entered into eleven years ago against the life of the most illustrious and most praiseworthy hero, Maurice, Prince of Orange, and also against the state of the commonwealth. In that conspiracy those men made plain by their practice what I say. For one of the conspirators, as appears from the sentence of the Holland court, professed that he had examined the matter in his conscience and found that it is no sin to kill that prince, who is never to be praised enough. And among the Arminian theologian accomplices, Slatius, formerly minister of Bleiswijk (who had succeeded M. Episcopius there), the Arminians themselves introduce in a certain Belgic letter, speaking of the most illustrious Orders and of the most illustrious Prince Maurice, a good successor, as they say, a good successor [Διάδοχος ἀγαθὸς, φασὶν ἀγαθὸς], as good men customarily say in proverb (for words may be used in a dissimilar matter, as Eusebius, speaking of Anatolius, successor to another Eusebius in the bishopric of Laodicea, did in book 2, ch. 26), a man who says that he believes it lawful to deceive tyrants. Likewise all the Arminian pastors and others who conspired in the same year 1623, and before, to subvert the commonwealth, knew that it was not lawful to subvert the commonwealth, and yet tried to do so, as the sentences passed against them attest; because, namely, they did not judge this to be subverting the commonwealth, but called it, in their customary manner of speaking among themselves, restoring the kingdom of Israel. So Balthasar Gerhard, that parricide, knew that it was not lawful for any private man to kill anyone, and yet attempted and accomplished it; because, namely, he did not regard that most praiseworthy prince simply as a man, or as a prince, but as a rebel and heretic, as the Arminians themselves here say. Therefore, even by those men who hold those dogmas, the Arminians' greatest maxim can be applied to carry out a crime; namely, by believing those dogmas, but not applying them to this prince or to this commonwealth. Here, to say this in passing, the Arminians reconcile these two points: that here they say the Papists deny this dogma, that no one should become perjured, likewise that it is not lawful to lie in wait for anyone's life, even the lowliest man, much less a prince; and yet in their Vindication, book 1, ch. 8, p. 47, they say among other things: No one can call in question that God forbids perjury, nor has anyone ever denied or called it in question who holds the word of God as expressed in the Old and New Testament to be the word of God.

units.la: Falsum etiam est, quod dicunt Arminani, eos qui maxima ista utuntur, ea ABUTI ut alis rebus optimis. Nam abusus est rei per se bonæ; at istud dogma Apologiæ per se est salsissimum, pessimum & sua natura pestilentissimum Rebuspublicis ac Principibus. Falsum denique est quod dicunt disparem rationem esse dogmatis sui & Praxeos Gerhardi. Illum enim simulasse Religionem quam Haereticam credebat, at Remonstrantes loqui de dogmatibus iis quæ salutis fundamentum non evertunt. Nam Apologia loquitur de dogmatibus omnibus controversis, quorum nullum esse necessarium ad salutem docent Arminiani: At simulatio parricidæ illius erat etiam circa dogmata controversa.
units.tr: It is also false, what the Arminians say, that those who use those greatest things abuse them as they abuse other excellent things. For abuse belongs to a thing that is good in itself. But that doctrine of the Apology is in itself most unsound, and by its nature most pestilential to commonwealths and princes. Finally, it is false that they say their doctrine differs from the practice of Gerhard. For he pretended a religion that he believed to be heretical, whereas the Remonstrants speak of those doctrines that do not overturn the foundation of salvation. For the Apology speaks of all the disputed doctrines, none of which the Arminians teach to be necessary to salvation. But the pretence of that parricide extended even to disputed doctrines.

units.la: Observetur Coronidis loco Arminianos hic dicere p. 72. Qui necessa-riis riis Scriptura dogmatis, in quibus Christiani omnes, paucis exceptis conveniunt, firma fide adhærent, ii conscientia bona rationem præcipue habendam esse persuasissimi sunt, ii ab omni specie mali abstinendum esse, & mendacium sollicitè fugiendum esse nõrunt. Si hoc verum est, tunc ex proprio suo ore convicti & αὐτοκατάκριτοι sunt Arminiani, atque ostendunt se non credere Necessaria dogmata illa, nimirum non licere fidem fallere, perjurium committere &c. Nam se conscientiæ rationem nullam amplius habere, sed strenuè contra eam mentiri palàm faciunt in Vindiciis suis, toties quoties (ut alia nunc mittamus) negant se docuisse: Nulla dogmata controversa esse necessaria ad salutem. hæc etiam ad secundum responsum Arminianorum.
units.tr: Let it be noted that, by way of a conclusion, the Arminians here say, p. 72: Those who firmly adhere to the necessary doctrines of Scripture, in which all Christians agree apart from a few exceptions, are most firmly persuaded that a good conscience must above all be taken into account, that one must abstain from every appearance of evil, and that one must carefully avoid lying. If this is true, then the Arminians are convicted by their own mouth and are self-condemned [αὐτοκατάκριτοι], and they show that they do not believe those necessary doctrines, namely that one may not break faith, commit perjury, and so on. For by openly lying against conscience in their Vindiciae, as often as they deny (to pass over other things for now) that they have taught that no disputed doctrines are necessary to salvation, they show that they no longer take any account of conscience at all. This applies also to the Arminians' second answer.

units.la: 4. Tertiò respondent per retorsionem virulentissimam & calumniosissimam adversus doctrinam nostram de Electione; quâ retorsione dicunt se pari, imò majore jure hereditscere posse ex nostrâ doctrinâ, quæ non diximus, inquiunt p. 74. ansam & occasionem sed CAUSAM ejusmodi sceleribus præbere possunt, non tantùm profanis & perditè malis hominibus, sed etiam iis qui doctrinæ & fidei ipsius sunt retinentissimi. Item ajunt, doctrinam nostram de Electione & perseverantiâ Sanctorum suo genio & vi insita Regnis Principatibus, Rebusp̄ublicis periculosissimam esse, & vitis Principum exitialem. Et multis sese diffundunt in eam atrocissimam & Diabolicam calumniam p. 74. 75. 76. non sine convitiis in omnes subditos Reformatos cujuscunque dignitatis, conditionis, ordinis sint. Nam addunt inter alia p. 75. Ecquis Princeps securius aut tutus esse poterit inter talium subditorum conscientias &c. Et p.74. dicunt nostram doctrinam tollere fidem commerciorum, juramentorum Religionem, conjugiorum fœdera. Sed primo proponunt calumniosissimè & malitiosissimè doctrinam nostram, dum inter alia nobis tribuunt ac si statueremus, Electum impunè coram Deo scelera committere posse; item, dum dicunt nos docere fiduciam impietatis inter flagitia, & certam inter scelera de vita æterna persuasionem; hominii utut scelerato absque pœnitentia Deum condonare peccata: Electionem stare incolumen & securam inter flagitia; hominem propitio cœlo ac Deo peccare posse; ejus salutem à sanguine & cæde Principum pollui non posse. Et addunt: Vidimus qui hac fiducia pleni sibi ipsis violentas manus conscisscere non dubitarunt. Quod postremum in quo angulo nequitiæ viderint ministri Arminiani ego quidem nescio. Certè fidem nullam amplius merentur in ullâ re nec divinâ nec humanâ. Quod si autem quis infelix & perditus homo id patravit unquam (de quo tamen eo magis dubito quia res talibus testibus nititur) certè non fecit illud ex nostrâ doctrinâ aut vi illius, sed eodem genio ac Spiritu impulsus, quo
units.tr: 4. Thirdly, they reply by a most virulent and most slanderous retort against our doctrine of election. By this retort they say that they can, with equal or even greater right, make the same claim from our doctrine, which we have not said, they say on p. 74, that it can give not merely an occasion but the CAUSE of such crimes, not only to profane and utterly wicked men, but also to those who hold most tenaciously to its teaching and faith. Likewise they say that our doctrine of election and the perseverance of the saints, by its own nature and inherent power, is most dangerous to kingdoms, principalities and commonwealths, and deadly to the lives of princes. And on pp. 74, 75 and 76 they spread themselves over this most atrocious and diabolical calumny, not without abuse of all reformed subjects of whatever rank, condition or order. For they add, among other things, on p. 75: What prince can be safer or more secure among the consciences of such subjects, and so on. And on p. 74 they say that our doctrine destroys the faith of commerce, the religion of oaths, the bonds of marriage. But first, they propose our doctrine most calumniously and maliciously, since among other things they attribute to us that we teach that the elect can commit crimes before God with impunity; likewise when they say that we teach a confidence in wickedness among crimes, and a certain persuasion of eternal life among sins; that God forgives sins to a man, however wicked, without repentance; that election remains intact and secure among crimes; that a man can sin with heaven and God favourably disposed; that his salvation cannot be polluted by the blood and slaughter of princes. And they add: We have seen men who, full of this confidence, did not hesitate to lay violent hands upon themselves. In what corner of wickedness the Arminian ministers saw this last point, I for my part do not know. Certainly they no longer deserve any trust in any matter, divine or human. But if some wretched and lost man ever did such a thing (about which I nonetheless doubt, the more so because the matter rests on such witnesses), certainly he did not do it from our doctrine or its power, but was impelled by the same spirit as

units.la: pessimi & sceleratissimi homines ipsa Scriptura sacra facinora sua tegere ac comprobare nituntur. Nostram doctrinam quae sit, vide adversus calumnias horum hominum libro praecedente c. 10. Hoc unum est. Secundo Arminiani hoc modo ex doctrina nostra calumniose & mendacissime propositâ argumentantes; totam Religionem Christianam Turcis, Iudaeis, Atheis ac quibusvis impiis prostituunt ac ludibrio exponunt. Nam Religionis Christianae summa consistit in Evangelio seu promissione gratiae Dei, condonantis peccata misero peccatori, quae quidem gratia Dei tanta est, ut ubi peccatum abundat, ipsa multo magis abundet, teste Apostolo, & omne peccatum condonari possit excepto peccato in Spiritum Sanctum. Iam igitur praeeuntibus sic mystagogis Arminianis atheus, Turca, Iudaeus omnia illa scelera, quae hi homines ex nostra doctrina tanquam aranea exfugunt, imputabat Evangelio; ac inferet totidem verbis ipsorum quae pag. 74. 75 76. deblatterant, hominem eo praetextu, quod certus sit peccatori poenitenti omnia flagitia ac scelera etiam atrocissima condonatum iri per Christum adeoque salutem ei & vitam aeternam patere, quodcunque scelus contra Principem, Rempublicam, privatos patraturum. Hanc consequentiam negare atheo aut Iudaeo &c. non poterunt Arminiani, qui ita ex doctrina nostra argumentantur. Nec effugient, si dicant, doctrinam nostram de Electione & Perseverantia falsam; Evangelii autem veram esse. Nam primo quod nos de salute miseri peccatoris Electi sed resipiscentis dicimus; id nititur promissione ista Evangelii de gratia Dei in Christo Iesu condonantis peccata serio resipiscenti peccatori: per consequens dum Arminiani blasphemiis istis & calumniosis consequentiis doctrinam nostram de Electione & Perseverantia gravant, doctrinam Evangelii de gratia Dei ob Iesum Christum condonantis peccata misero homini peccatori resipiscenti impetunt: ex qua profecto nequaquam sequitur licentia peccandi, Apostolo teste: Quid igitur dicemus? inquit. Permanebimus in peccato ut gratia auctior fiat? Absit: qui mortui sumus peccato, quomodo adhuc vivemus in eo? Rom. 6. 1. Unde patet Apostolum doctrinam nostram adversus improbitatem horum hominum vindicare. Deinde Turcae, Iudaei, Athei etiam dicunt doctrinam Evangelii falsam esse; & quidem ex eo ipso dicent se eam pro falsa cogi habere & ab ea dissentire, quod non videant per eam peccatum ac sceleribus januam satis arte occludi posse; sed contra ex genio doctrinae Evangelii seu de remissione peccandi licentiam ac commeatum dari ad multarum animarum perniciem, divinae gloriae dedecus, & Religionis opprobrium. Non seeus ac Arminiani, (quorum verbis hic utor) hic fatentur has consequentias, quas falsò calumniosè & protervè ex nostrâ doctrinâ eliciunt, causam principem & præcipuam fuisse cur à nostrâ doctrinâ discesserint: Quin imò, inquiunt hic p. 76. inter alias hac una princeps & præcipua causa fuit, quæ eos à contra Remonstrantium sententia discedere aut dissentire coëgit, quòd non viderent per eam peccatis ac sceleribus januam satis arctè occludi posse, sed contra ex genio doctrinæ de Prædestinatione peccandi licentiam aut commeatum dari ad multarum animarum perniciem, divinæ gloriæ dedecus & Reformationis opprobrium. Patet igitur hos homines istâ suâ argumentandi & calumniandi ratione totam Religionem Christianam prostituere & ludibrio exponere. Et sic manifestum quoque est, eos calumniosissimâ & Diabolicâ retorsione ista suâ eludere frustra conari verissimam accusationem, qua non personas ut mala & consueta fide p. 75. 76. dicunt, sed doctrinam ipsorum ex Apologia & confessione eorum petii capite isto Arcanorum. Cùm igitur hæc lues & labes infamis sit in doctrinâ eorum, quæ Principibus & Rebuspublicis periculosissima & perniciosissima est, quid restat nisi ut ipsos Arminianos judices audiamus, ita adversus semet sententiâ dicentes: Sanè si hæc lues in doctrina Remonstrantium est, digni sunt, inquiunt p. 76. in quos Regum Principumque ira saviat ad extremum usque sine gratia sine venia. Et ut fiducia eorum appareat, culpam non deprecantur, si vel verisimiliter aliquid ex doctrina eorum adduci possit, quòd ulli sceleri aut causa aut ansam præbet. Ego sævitiem quam sibi imprecantur, nunquâ suaserim: sed quia resipiscere nolunt opto non saevitia sed justitia compesci eorum flagitiosam insolentiam in doctrinam & Ecclesiam Reformatam, nec non impietatem horum hominum, qui blasphemias Socinianorum Turcicas contra Filium Dei introducere in Belgium conantur sub prætextu fraudulentissimo quinque articulorum notoriorum. Hoc opto, id quod multarum myriadum in Orbe Christiano votum erit ubi rem hanc comperennt.
units.tr: the most wicked and criminal men, who strive to cover and justify their crimes by Holy Scripture itself. What our doctrine is, see against the calumnies of these men in the preceding book, chapter 10. This is one point. Secondly, the Arminians, reasoning in this way from our doctrine, calumniously and most falsely proposed, expose the whole Christian religion to Turks, Jews, atheists and all kinds of impious men, and make it a laughing-stock. For the sum of the Christian religion consists in the Gospel, or the promise of God's grace, which forgives sins to the wretched sinner; and this grace of God is so great that where sin abounds, grace itself abounds much more, as the Apostle witnesses, and every sin can be forgiven except the sin against the Holy Spirit. Now, therefore, with the Arminian mystagogues going before in this way, the atheist, the Turk and the Jew would impute all those crimes, which these men escape from our doctrine as if from a spider's web, to the Gospel; and he will infer, in the very words of theirs which they babble on pp. 74, 75 and 76, that a man, on the pretext that he is sure that for the penitent sinner all crimes and wickedness, even the most atrocious, will be forgiven through Christ, and that therefore salvation and eternal life lie open to him, may commit whatever crime against prince or commonwealth. The Arminians will not be able to deny this consequence to the atheist or the Jew, etc., since they reason in this way from our doctrine. Nor will they escape if they say that our doctrine of election and perseverance is false, but the doctrine of the Gospel true. For first, what we say of the salvation of the wretched sinner who is elect but penitent, rests on that promise of the Gospel of God's grace in Jesus Christ, forgiving sins to the sinner who truly repents. Consequently, when the Arminians burden our doctrine of election and perseverance with these blasphemies and calumnious consequences, they attack the doctrine of the Gospel of God's grace forgiving sins for Jesus Christ's sake to the wretched, repentant sinner; and from this certainly no licence to sin follows, as the Apostle witnesses: What then shall we say? Shall we continue in sin that grace may abound? God forbid. How shall we, who are dead to sin, live any longer in it? Rom. 6.1. Whence it is plain that the Apostle vindicates our doctrine against the wickedness of these men. Next, the Turks, Jews and atheists also say that the doctrine of the Gospel is false; and indeed from this very fact they will say that they are compelled to hold it false and to dissent from it, because they do not see that sin and crimes can be sufficiently closed off by it; but on the contrary, from the spirit of the doctrine of the Gospel, or of the remission of sins, a licence and passage to sin is given, to the ruin of many souls, the disgrace of divine glory and the reproach of religion. Just as the Arminians (whose words I use here) also confess in this place that these consequences, which they falsely, calumniously and insolently draw from our doctrine, were the chief and principal cause why they departed from our doctrine: Indeed, they say here on p. 76, among other reasons this one was the chief and principal cause which forced them to depart from or dissent from the opinion of the Remonstrants, namely that they did not see that by it the door to sins and crimes could be shut tightly enough, but on the contrary, from the spirit of the doctrine of predestination, a licence or passage to sin is given, to the ruin of many souls, the disgrace of divine glory and the reproach of the Reformation. It is plain, therefore, that by this manner of reasoning and calumny these men expose the whole Christian religion and make it a laughing-stock. And thus it is also manifest that by this most calumnious and diabolical retort they vainly try to evade the most true accusation, in which we charge not their persons, as they say on pp. 75 and 76 with their usual good faith, but their doctrine, which we have drawn from their Apology and confession in this chapter of the Arcana. Since, therefore, this plague and infamous blot is in their doctrine, which is most dangerous and most destructive to princes and commonwealths, what remains but that we hear the Arminians themselves as judges, pronouncing sentence against themselves in this way: Certainly, if this plague is in the doctrine of the Remonstrants, they say on p. 76, they deserve that the anger of kings and princes should rage against them to the utmost, without grace and without pardon. And so that their confidence may appear, they do not deprecate blame if anything at all can be brought from their doctrine which provides cause or occasion for any crime. I would never advise the savagery which they invoke upon themselves; but since they are unwilling to repent, I wish that their shameful insolence against the doctrine and the Reformed Church, and likewise the impiety of those men who try to introduce into the Netherlands the Socinian and Turkish blasphemies against the Son of God under the most fraudulent pretext of the five notorious articles, be checked not by savagery but by justice. This I wish, as will be the prayer of many myriads in the Christian world when they learn of this matter.

units.la: 5. Tertium corollarium meum erat, quo dijudicandum unicuique reliqui, an'non Arminiani Theologi per illam maximam de simulanda Religione se & alios sectæ suæ homines ingerere possint in eos coetus, quos pro impuris habent, in eum finem ut simulantes Religionem coetus alicujus, res sectæ suæ faciant & promoveant.
