Et probavi id experientia seu Praxi simili Ioh: Wilhelmi Reguli Anabaptistici, qui eandem maximam sicarios, exploratores & latrunculos suos docuit, ejusque subsidio in Ducatu Clivensi caedibus & latrociniis omnia replevit, ob quæ anno 1580 combustus fuit. Circa hoc corollarium mihi tribuunt primò inscitiam, secundò malitiam. Inscitia, inquiunt, p. 77. Nam contradictio manifesta hic est, Remonstrantes se ingerere in coetus impuros, ut quos in iis esse nórunt, lucrentur & ab aeterna damnationis periculo avertant. Periculum enim damnationis in coetibus impuris qua talibus esse negant Remonstrantes, quia coetus illos impuros fundamentum salutis tenere asserunt. Respondeo: Contradictio illa & inscitia, ut hic loquuntur, non mea est, sed ipsorum, ex quorum hypothesi ea dixi. Ita enim in praefatione Confessionis suae, postquam dixissent Christianos teneri ad eligendum coetum quem credunt omnium esse purissimum &c. nisi forte justius majoris alicuius periculi aut scandali metus obstet: addunt paulò post rationem: Multò maioris momenti apud nos esse debet aeterna proximi nostri salus, quàm nostra maior ad salutem perveniendi commoditas. Quare si salutis aeternae periculum ex transitione nostra à coetu impuro ad puriorem redundaturum videtur ad Proximum nostrum, ratio ipsa vetat nos transfire. Praestat enim nos incommodiore via ire ad salutem, ut aeternum nobiscum salvetur proximus noster, quàm commodiore, unde verisimiliter futurum est ut proximus aeternum pereat. Vides, Lector, eos statuere manere aliquem debere in coetu impuro in eum finem ut lucretur proximum & ab aeternae damnationis periculo avertat, quod in eo coetu incurrit.
units.tr: 5. My third corollary was meant to let each reader judge whether the Arminian theologians, by that great maxim of simulating religion, can thrust themselves and their party's people into those congregations they regard as impure, with the aim that these men, pretending to belong to a congregation, may advance and promote the cause of their sect. I proved this by experience, and by a similar practice of Johann Wilhelm, the Anabaptist chieftain, who taught the same maxim to his assassins, spies and bandits, and by its help filled the Duchy of Cleves with murders and robberies, for which he was burned in 1580. Regarding this corollary they charge me first with ignorance and second with malice. Ignorance, they say, p. 77. For here the contradiction is plain: the Remonstrants thrust themselves into impure congregations so that they may win over those whom they know to be in them and turn them away from the danger of eternal damnation. For the Remonstrants deny that there is danger of damnation in impure congregations as such, because they assert that those impure congregations hold the foundation of salvation. I answer: that contradiction and ignorance, as they call it here, is not mine but theirs, since I drew the point from their own hypothesis. For in the preface to their Confession, after saying that Christians are bound to choose the congregation they believe to be the purest of all etc., unless perhaps the fear of some greater danger or scandal stands in the way, more justly, they add the reasoning a little later: The eternal salvation of our neighbour must weigh far more with us than our greater convenience in attaining salvation. Therefore, if it seems that the danger to eternal salvation would arise for our neighbour from our passing from an impure congregation to a purer one, reason itself forbids us to cross over. For it is better for us to go by a less convenient road to salvation, so that our neighbour may be saved eternally along with us, than by a more convenient one, whence it will probably follow that the neighbour perishes eternally. You see, reader, that they hold that someone ought to remain in an impure congregation, with the aim of winning his neighbour and turning him away from the danger of eternal damnation which he incurs in that congregation.

units.la: Malitiam mihi tribuunt ex eo: Quia non ignorat, inquiunt, Remonstrantes urgere ut necessaria dogmata firma semper fide retineantur. At inter necessaria dogmata etiam hoc est, nequis profiteatur se credere verum esse quod in conscientia sua credit falsum esse, &c. item: Nemini Christiano licet profiteri Confessionem suam cum coetu in iis, in quibus ab eo dissentit & dissidet &c. Verùm enimvero
units.tr: They charge me with malice on this ground: Because, they say, he is not unaware that the Remonstrants urge that the necessary doctrines be always retained with firm faith. But among the necessary doctrines is also this: that no one should profess that he believes true what in his conscience he believes to be false, etc. Likewise: It is not lawful for any Christian to profess his Confession with a congregation in those matters in which he dissents and disagrees from it, etc. But in truth

units.la: 1. Sophisticantur hic phrasi, aliquem profiteri se credere verum esse quod in conscientia sua credit esse falsum: item profiteri confessionem suam in dogmatis &c. Non enim ego dixi Arminianos vi suae istius maximae posse profiteri se credere verum esse quod in conscientia sua credunt esse falsum &c. Sed dixi eos per illam maximam se & alios ingerere posse in eos coetus quos pro impuris habent. Ad hoc illi ne verbulum quidem respondent; sed aliud fingunt ad quod respondent. Observetur igitur diligenter, Arminianos non negare, nec posse negare, se posse vi istius doctrinae suae se & alios ingerere in eos coetus quos pro impuris habent, id quod mihi sufficit. Et certè experientia hoc in Belgio testatur. Deinde dixi eos per istam maximam suasuros alicui, ut publicè & externè non profiteatur Religionem Remonstrantium, sed eam qua in coetu quem pro impuro habet, obtinet. Ubi sumsi phrasin profiteri Religionem pro esse aut manere in coetu aliquo, seu communiomunionem externam cum eo colere. Hoc enim Phrasi usitata in tota Ecclesia est Religionem profiteri coetus illius: At illi hic respondent de Professione hujus vel illius dogmatis necessarii aut non necessarii qua ore fit. Hoc dicunt non licere; prius autem non negant se docere, aut illud non licere; quia nimirum illud egregii hi homines non habent pro professione Religionis ut Par. III. lib. 2. cap. 2. ostendi, quò scilicet impunè coetus quibus se ingerunt decipere possint. Ex quibus patet firmum manere hoc Corollarium, adeóque unumquemque debere sibi cavere ab hac arte horum simulatorum Socinianorum, qua se aut alios ingerunt in coetus quos pro impuris habent, ut res suae sectae faciant & augeant, id quod ipsi hic non negant nec negare audent: sed versutè & impudenter ictum declinant, &,ut res Lectorem lateat,inscitiæ me accusant ob contradictionem quæ non mea sed ipsorum est,& malitiæ ob umbram quam sibi fingunt & quam impugnant relicto corpore & vero crimine cuius convicti sunt.
units.tr: 1. Here they play sophistically with the wording: that someone professes that he believes true what in his conscience he believes to be false; likewise to profess his Confession in doctrines, etc. For I did not say that the Arminians, by virtue of that maxim of theirs, could profess that they believe true what in their conscience they believe to be false, etc. What I said was that by that maxim they could thrust themselves and others into those congregations which they regard as impure. To this they do not answer even a word, but they invent something else to answer. Let it therefore be carefully observed that the Arminians do not deny, nor can they deny, that by virtue of this doctrine of theirs they can thrust themselves and others into those congregations which they regard as impure. That is enough for me, and indeed experience in Belgium bears witness to it. Next I said that by that maxim they would persuade someone not to profess publicly and outwardly the religion of the Remonstrants, but the one that he holds in the congregation he regards as impure. Here I took the phrase to profess a religion to mean to belong to some congregation, or to keep external communion with it. For in the usage of the whole Church, to profess the religion of a given congregation has this sense. But they answer here about the profession of this or that necessary or unnecessary doctrine, which takes place by the mouth. This they say is not permitted; but they do not deny that they teach the former, or that the latter is not permitted, because, of course, these distinguished men do not regard that as the profession of religion, as I showed in Part III, book 2, chapter 2, namely so that they may deceive the congregations into which they thrust themselves with impunity. From these things it is plain that this corollary stands firm, and therefore everyone ought to beware of this art of these dissembling Socinians, by which they thrust themselves or others into congregations they regard as impure, so as to advance and increase the cause of their sect. This they do not deny here, nor dare they deny it; but they cunningly and shamelessly sidestep the blow, and, so that the matter may be hidden from the reader, they accuse me of ignorance on account of a contradiction which is not mine but theirs, and of malice on account of a shadow which they invent for themselves and attack, leaving aside the body and the true charge of which they have been convicted.

units.la: Quod dicunt inter Necessaria dogmata etiam hoc esse, ut ne quis profiteatur se credere verum esse, quod in conscientia sua credit falsum esse; hoc enim, est, inquiunt, conscientiam bonam violare ac vastare: id verò primò ostendit eos αυτοκατακριτυς esse. Si enim hoc inter Necessaria dogmata est, item si hoc est bonam conscientiam violare ac vastare:cur igitur in his Vindiciis profitentur, quod in conscientia sua sciunt falsum esse ? dum v. g. negant se docuisse Nulla dogmata Controversa esse necessaria ad salutem. Quod magis est,cur igitur profitentur Orthodoxā doctrinam de mysterio Trinitatis, quam tamen in animo suo pro falsa habent,ut ostendimus Parte II. Arcanorum. Pronunciarunt igitur jam hic adversus se sententiam æternæ condemnationis,adeóque etiam hac in parte αυτοκατακριτοι sunt. Secundò falsum est ex doctrina quidem & hypothesi Apologiæ, illud dogma esse Necessarium ad salutem. Est enim controversum & controverti in futurum potest; ut patet ex eo,quòd Priscillianistæ, qui etiam in coetus Catholicorum se ingerebant quò res suae sectae facere possent, affirmabant licere profiteri se credere verum esse quod tamen in conscientia sua credunt falsum esse; id quod Augustinus prolixè & ex professo confutat libro 2. contra mendacium ad Consentium. Et hodie Jesuitæ idem docent. Atque ex his etiam manifestum est, verum esse quod dixi capite isto 2. lib. 2. Par. I. p. 116. mirum non esse Arminianos tantis cum convitiis iracti Reformatis Ecclesiis & Rebuspublicis aliquibus, eò quod juramento sibi caveri velint ab illis, quos ad Ecclesiæ ministerium admittunt, quò certi fiant eos Arminianorum norum secta aut Religioni addictos non esse. Hoc factum ægrè etiam hic fe-runt boni hi Viri & p. 77. vocant enorme ac detestabile factum: quod ta-men si unquam, in posterum profecto magis etiam fieri ab omnibus Re-buspublicis & Ecclesiis, quæ sibi ab Arminiana factione cavere volunt, necessarium est; postquàm illi etiam reprehensi ideò quòd vi suæ doctri-næ ingerere sese possint in cœtus impuros, ut res suæ sectæ faciant, illud non negant, sed aliorsum dilabuntur, diverticula quærunt ut Lectorem fallant & in aliis occupent quàm in cognitione veritatis h.e. criminis sibi à me objecti. Itaque necessum est tùm aliis modis, tùm etiam ea ratione Principes Respublicas & Ecclesias cavere sibi à moliminibus Arminia-norum, exemplo Constantini Magni qui antequam Ario ignosceret & eum in integrum restituere vellet, exegit ab eo juramentum quo testaretur Arius se doctrinæ Concilii Nicéni ex animo assentiri. Nam cùm Arium ad Palatium vocasset, & ex eo quæsiisset, an'ne Concilii Nicéni decretis astipularetur; ille verò sine morâ promtè & alacriter coràm Imperatore subscripsisset illis; Constantinus M. ὅρκον ἐτέρῳ. ὁ δὲ ἐν τούτῳ σοφιστὴς ὀμνύειν ... ἀποίει ad juramentum quoque illum adegit; ille simulatè & fallaciter id quoque præstitit, ait Socrates lib. 1. c. 26.
units.tr: As to their saying that among the necessary doctrines is also this, that no one should profess that he believes true what in his conscience he believes to be false; for this, they say, is to violate and lay waste a good conscience: this, in the first place, shows them to be self-condemned [αὐτοκατάκριτοι]. For if this is among the necessary doctrines, and if this is to violate and lay waste a good conscience, why then do they profess in these Vindiciae what they know in their conscience to be false, when, for example, they deny that they taught that no controverted doctrines are necessary to salvation? What is more, why then do they profess the Orthodox doctrine of the mystery of the Trinity, which nevertheless they hold in their mind to be false, as we showed in Part II of the Arcana? They have therefore already pronounced against themselves the sentence of eternal condemnation, and so in this part too they are self-condemned [αὐτοκατάκριτοι]. In the second place, it is false that, on the teaching and hypothesis of the Apologia, that doctrine is necessary to salvation. For it is controverted, and may be controverted in future, as is plain from the fact that the Priscillianists, who also thrust themselves into the congregations of the Catholics so that they might advance the cause of their sect, affirmed that it is lawful to profess that they believe true what nevertheless in their conscience they believe to be false; a view which Augustine refutes at length and expressly in book 2 Against Lying, to Consentius. And today the Jesuits teach the same. From these things it is also manifest that what I said in chapter 2 of book 2, Part I, p. 116, is true, that it is no wonder the Arminians are so enraged with such reproaches against the Reformed Churches and some commonwealths, because they wish to be guarded by oath against those whom they admit to the ministry of the Church, so that they may be assured that these men are not devoted to the Arminian sect or religion. This deed the good men here also take ill, and at p. 77 they call it an enormous and detestable deed. Yet if ever it was necessary, it certainly is necessary in future, and even more so, for all commonwealths and Churches which wish to guard themselves against the Arminian faction; since these men, when they were rebuked because by virtue of their doctrine they can thrust themselves into impure congregations so as to advance the cause of their sect, do not deny it, but slip away in another direction, seeking detours so that they may deceive the reader and occupy themselves with other things than the knowledge of the truth, that is, the charge laid against them by me. Therefore it is necessary for princes, commonwealths and Churches to guard themselves against the machinations of the Arminians both by other means and also by this method, after the example of Constantine the Great, who, before he pardoned Arius and wished to restore him fully, required of him an oath by which he would testify that he assented from his heart to the doctrine of the Council of Nicaea. For when he had summoned Arius to the palace and asked him whether he would subscribe to the decrees of the Council of Nicaea, Arius indeed subscribed to them at once, readily and cheerfully, in the presence of the Emperor; yet Constantine the Great required him to swear another oath [ὅρκον ἕτερον]; but the sophist, in swearing this ... [ὁ δὲ ἐν τούτῳ σοφιστὴς ὀμνύειν ... ἀποίει], he also compelled to take the oath; and he swore it deceitfully and insincerely, as Socrates says in book 1, chapter 26.

units.la: Ad experientiam quâ confirmaveram veritatem tertii mei Corollarii respondent per convitia adversus me, & relabuntur ad istam præceden-tem calumniam quâ Reformatam Ecclesiam & doctrinam de Electione modò petierant. Dicunt inter alia. Reguli istius astutæ ac præcipuos forte in-centores fuisse duos Ordinis nostri Concionatores Stapredam & Rotmannum, addi-ctos, inquiunt, sententia Reformatorum de prædestinatione & Lutheri de Servo arbitrio, p. 78. Quasi verò qui Anabaptisticæ sectæ se jungunt ordinis nostri h. e. Reformatæ aut Lutheranæ Religioni addicti sint, & non potius Apostatæ. Et ipsi hic ajunt eos quoad sententiam de Pædobaptismo seductos fuisse à Regulo illo: sed constat ipsos etiam in aliis cum eo sensisse. Et sufficit ad professionem Anabaptisticæ Religionis communio cum eâ & conjunctio cum cœtibus eorum. Addunt: Si Regulus ille ista maximâ usus est, non novâ sed vetere & omnibus retrò seculis usitatâ machina usus est. Eam ut Nebulones & sicarii à Remonstrantibus discant, metuendum non est: sua sponte illa sese ingerit animus eorum, quibus privata stimulatio & vile decus publicum est. Pium animum non intrat tàm prava cogitatio. Et cùm pietatem ante omnia alia requirant Remonstrantes, quomodo fieri potest, ut pestem illam suadeant quæ pietatis & sinceritatis Christianæ venenum est. Verùm enim verò ego non dixi Arminianos novum scelus docere. Hoc saltem dixi, atque etiamñum dico eos docere homines simulare in negocio Religionis, dum docent: Posse imo debere aliquem interdum non solùm scandali sed etiam periculi evitandi causâ manere in coetu quem pro impuro habet (quales impuri coetus secundùm doctrinam Apologiæ sunt omnes coetus Christiani) quod nihil aliud est, quàm profiteri Religionem illius coetus. Hanc simulationem, etiamsi ea vetus crimen sit à Diabolo Patre mendacii profectum, tamen docere non debent Arminiani. Confirmantur enim per eam mali in malitiâ h. e. arte simulandi; & multi qui antea ignorabant eam, jam ex doctrinâ Arminianorum eam discunt. Nec docendum est malum, quod ultrò sese ingerit. Satis per se ad improbitatem prona est mens humana.
units.tr: To the evidence by which I had confirmed the truth of my third Corollary, they answer with insults against me, and they fall back on that earlier slander by which they had lately attacked the Reformed Church and the doctrine of Election. They say, among other things: That crafty little king, and perhaps the chief instigators, were two preachers of our own order, Stapredas and Rotmann, who, they say, were devoted to the Reformed view of predestination and to Luther's view of the Bondage of the Will, p. 78. As if those who join the Anabaptist sect were not of our order, that is, adherents of the Reformed or Lutheran religion, but apostates instead. Here they also say that these men were seduced by that little king in regard to infant baptism; but it is clear that they agreed with him on other matters as well. Communion with that sect and association with its assemblies are enough to count as a profession of the Anabaptist religion. They add: If that little king used this great device, he used not a new but an old machine, one used in every age past. Nebulones and assassins need not fear that the Remonstrants will learn it: their own minds throw it up unbidden, in men for whom private gain and vile public esteem are everything. Such a corrupt thought does not enter a pious mind. And since the Remonstrants require piety above all else, how can they recommend that plague which is the poison of Christian piety and sincerity? But in truth I did not say that the Arminians teach a new crime. I said only, and I still say, that they teach men to dissimulate in matters of religion, when they teach that a person may, and sometimes must, remain, for the sake of avoiding not only scandal but also danger, in an assembly which he regards as impure (and according to the doctrine of the Apology all Christian assemblies are such impure assemblies), which is nothing other than professing the religion of that assembly. Even though this dissimulation is an ancient crime, originating with the Devil, the father of lies, the Arminians ought not to teach it. For through it the wicked are confirmed in their wickedness, that is, in the art of pretence; and many who previously did not know it now learn it from the doctrine of the Arminians. Nor should an evil be taught which forces itself forward of its own accord. The human mind is inclined enough to wickedness by itself.

units.la: Quod de pietate suâ dicunt Arminiani; mera est hypocrisis. Quæ enim pietas in Socinianis blasphematoribus, esse possit? Hæc duo simul subsistere nequeunt. Et docet hoc maledicentia eorum quâ promiscuè Reges principes Respublicas, Ecclesias Reformatas, Doctoresque earum vivos & mortuos petunt. Docet hoc fraudulentia eorum, quâ in vindiciis suis utuntur & defendêda pessimâ causâ. Docet improbitas, quâ contra conscientiam sæpissimè negant se docuisse, quod sciunt se docere. Docet simulatio eorum in negocio Religionis. Docent denique reliqua eorum dogmata de quibus in Arcanis nostris agimus.
units.tr: What the Arminians say about their own piety is sheer hypocrisy. For what piety could there be in the Socinian blasphemers? These two cannot subsist together. Their slander, by which they indiscriminately attack kings, princes, commonwealths, the Reformed Churches and their teachers, living and dead, teaches this. Their fraudulence, which they use in their defences and in defending a very bad cause, teaches this. The wickedness by which they very often deny, against their conscience, that they have taught what they know they teach, teaches this. Their dissimulation in matters of religion teaches this. Finally, the remaining doctrines of theirs with which we deal in our Arcana teach the rest.

units.la: Quartum Corollarium est, quo dijudicandum unicuique reliqui, an non ista doctrina de variatione sententiæ circa controversias evertant constantiam in Confessione veritatis & homines ad Apostasiam ac falsam Religionem impellant? Quintum, an non veternus & sopor lethalis injiciatur per eam Apostatis, ita ut judicia Dei non apprehendant, & ad veram Religionem redire non curent? Sextò, an non consolationem illam insignem tollant Ecclesiæ veræ persecutionem patienti à falsa, nimirum Deum Ecclesiæ suæ auxiliaturum & falsam puniturum. Septimò, an non stimulus pietatis eripiatur fidelibus, nimirum Deum peculiariter invigilare castigandæ Ecclesiæ veræ. Octavò, an non etiam illa consolatio in persecutione eripiatur Ecclesiæ, quæ novit se non ideò castigari à Deo quod Deus sibi inimicus factus sit, sed quia Ecclesia vera est domus Dei ex filiis ipsius constans, quos quia Pater cœlestis amat, castigat. Ad hæc Corollaria respondet uno ictu: nimirum se constantiam urgere in veritatis necessaria professione: at constantia, inquiunt, in non Necessariis dogmatis, si meliores rationes occurrant, non constantia sed pertinacia est. Atqui primò nulla dogmata controversa Necessaria sunt ad salutem secundùm doctrinam Apologiæ; secundùm doctrinam autem Vindiciarum controversa Necessaria ad salutem talia sunt ut homo qui mo qui ea negat absque illis salvari possit ; h. e. non sunt necessaria. Deinde non agitur de dogmatis falsis, sed veris quæ per consequens everti non possunt per rationes meliores. Circa hæc vera ipsa variationem docent Arminiani ut ostendimus libro præcedente cap. 8.
units.tr: The fourth Corollary is that each reader should judge for himself whether this doctrine of changing opinion on controversies does not overthrow constancy in confessing the truth and drive men into apostasy and false religion. Fifth, whether a deadly lethargy and drowsiness is not cast over apostates through it, so that they do not perceive the judgments of God and take no care to return to the true religion. Sixth, whether it does not take away that remarkable consolation of the true Church suffering persecution from the false, namely that God will help his Church and punish the false. Seventh, whether the spur of piety is not snatched from the faithful, namely that God watches over the chastisement of the true Church in a special way. Eighth, whether that consolation too is not taken away from the Church in persecution, which knows that it is not chastised by God because God has become its enemy, but because the true Church is the house of God, made up of his sons, whom the heavenly Father loves and therefore chastises. To these Corollaries they reply with a single blow: namely, that they urge constancy in the necessary profession of the truth; but constancy in non-necessary doctrines, if better reasons present themselves, is not constancy but obstinacy. But first, according to the doctrine of the Apology, no controverted doctrines are necessary to salvation; according to the doctrine of the Vindications, however, the controverted doctrines that are necessary to salvation are of such a kind that a man who denies them can be saved without them, that is, they are not necessary. Next, the question is not about false doctrines but about true ones, which consequently cannot be overthrown by better reasons. Concerning these very truths the Arminians teach variation, as we showed in the preceding book, chapter 8.

units.la: 6. Nonum Corollarium est, quo ostendi Arminianos secundum istam doctrinam suam non habere eos qui præsertim postremis seculis propter confessionem Evangelii variis suppliciis è medio sublati sunt, quā quidem pertulerunt non nisi pro dogmatis controversis, non habere, inquam, eos pro Martyribus. Ac ut dubitandi locus eò minus Lectori relinqueretur, ostendi Arminianos quando in Apologia loquuntur de Martyribus Evangelicis, qui pro dogmatis inter Christianos controversis oppositis doctrinæ Antichristi mortui sunt, non appellare eos simpliciter Martyres sed Martyres quos vocant; non secus ac quando de Hæreticis quos ita vocat tota Ecclesia Christiana, quia ipsi pro Hæreticis eos non habent, in eadem Apologia dicunt, Hæreticos quos vocant, Hæretici qui vocantur. Ad hoc Corollarium respondent pag. 79. 80. 81. 82. se nihil detrahere velle gloriæ Martyrum: item se statuere eos qui à Pontificiis ob doctrinam ipsis oppositam è medio sublati sunt, ob necessaria dogmata è medio sublatos esse, &, sic in verorum Martyrum numero censendos esse. Nam etsi mortui sint pro controversis dogmatis, esse tamen etiam dogmata quædam controversa, in specie illa ob quæ illi passi sunt, necessaria ad salutem. Et ut videas, Lector, quàm egregiè me refutent, addunt: Ipse Vedelius asserit ea dogmata esse Necessaria ad salutem, cùm ea dogmata vocat dogmata opposita doctrinæ Antichristi, & quod amplius est, ipsam Evangelii professionem; doctrina enim Antichristi qua talis non puritati doctrinæ Christi sed ipsi veritati essentiali doctrinæ Christi adversa est. Hic verò quis unquam vidit improbiorem & proteriorem agendi rationem, quàm eam quâ hi homines utuntur; dum videri volunt adversus me probare & quidem ex meâ propriâ Confessione dogmata quædam controversa esse necessaria ad salutem; adversus me, inquam, qui de iis eo nomine gravissimè conquestus sum atque etiamnum conqueror quòd statuunt in Apologiâ suâ, Nulla dogmata Controversa esse necessaria ad salutem! Quis unquam vidit majorem impudentiam. Certè vel ex hoc apparet, homines hos nec veritatis, nec honestatis, nec conscientiæ ullam rationem habere, sed tantùm rabulas agere pessimæ fidei ac perfrictæ frontis; & hoc quærere ut hominibus imponant.
units.tr: 6. The ninth Corollary, by which I showed that the Arminians, according to this doctrine of theirs, do not count as martyrs those who, especially in recent ages, were put to death in various ways for the confession of the Gospel, which they endured only for controverted doctrines; I say they do not count them as martyrs. And so that the reader would have less room for doubt, I showed that when the Arminians speak in the Apology of the Evangelical martyrs, who died for controverted doctrines among Christians opposed to the doctrine of Antichrist, they do not call them simply martyrs but "martyrs, as they are called"; just as, when speaking of heretics, whom the whole Christian Church so calls, they say in the same Apology "heretics, as they are called", because they do not themselves regard them as heretics. To this Corollary they reply on pages 79, 80, 81 and 82: that they wish to take nothing away from the glory of the martyrs; likewise that they hold that those who were put to death by the Papists for doctrines opposed to them were put to death for necessary doctrines, and so are to be counted among the number of true martyrs. For although they died for controverted doctrines, there are nevertheless some controverted doctrines, namely those for which they suffered, that are necessary to salvation. And so that you may see, Reader, how splendidly they refute me, they add: Vedelius himself asserts that those doctrines are necessary to salvation, when he calls them doctrines opposed to the doctrine of Antichrist, and what is more, the very profession of the Gospel; for the doctrine of Antichrist, as such, is opposed not to the purity of Christ's doctrine but to its essential truth. But who has ever seen a more shameless and impudent way of acting than that which these men use, while they wish to appear to prove against me, and indeed from my own Confession, that certain controverted doctrines are necessary to salvation? Against me, I say, who on that very account have most gravely complained, and still complain, that they state in their Apology: No controverted doctrines are necessary to salvation! Who has ever seen greater impudence? Certainly from this alone it appears that these men have regard neither for truth, nor honesty, nor conscience, but only play the mountebank of the worst faith and hardened brow; and they seek this, to impose upon men.

units.la: Sed venio ad caput rei. Dicunt igitur se habere eos pro Martyribus, utpote mortuos pro controversis dogmatis necessariis. Sunt igitur rursus αυτονατακρίτοι & nostræ causæ bonitas etiam in hac parte vicit. Nam cùm in Apologia suâ docent Nulla controversa dogmata esse Necessaria ad salutem: eò ipsos compuli ut sibi jam contradicant, se ipsos mendacii arguant, doctrinam suam de controversis falsitatis hoc loco damnent, denique se injuriam fecisse sanctis animabus illis & doctrinæ eorum pro quâ passi sunt, hoc ipso palàm faciunt. Adeò ut nihil ipsis defit ad plenam confessionem bonitatis causæ nostræ & victoriæ illius; nisi candor, honestas, & probitas quæ si ad esset non negarent se docere in Apologiâ: Nulla dogmata controversa esse necessaria ad salutem. Ex quâ ipsorum doctrinâ manifestum est, verum me dixisse in loco allegato Arcanorum Par. I. lib. 2. cap. 2. stante istâ doctrinâ de Necessariis, non posse verè Martyres vocari eos qui ob professionem Evangelii à Pontificiis è medio sublati sunt. Atque hæc causa est, cur Arminiani in Apologia eos non vocent simpliciter Martyres, sed quando de iis loquuntur, dicunt Martyres quos vocant.
units.tr: But I come to the heart of the matter. They say, then, that they count those men as martyrs, since they died for controverted necessary doctrines. So they are once more self-condemned, and the goodness of our cause has conquered in this part too. For when in their Apology they teach that no controverted doctrines are necessary to salvation, I have compelled them to contradict themselves, to convict themselves of falsehood, to condemn at this point their doctrine of controverted matters as false, and finally, by this very act, to show that they have done wrong to those holy souls and to the doctrine for which they suffered. So that nothing is lacking to them for a full confession of the goodness of our cause and of its victory, except candour, honesty and uprightness; if these were present, they would not deny that they teach in the Apology: No controverted doctrines are necessary to salvation. From their own doctrine it is plain that I spoke the truth in the passage cited from our Arcana, Part I, book 2, chapter 2: while this doctrine about necessary matters stands, those who were put to death by the Papists for their profession of the Gospel cannot truly be called martyrs. And this is the reason why the Arminians in the Apology do not call them simply martyrs, but when they speak of them say "martyrs, as they are called".

units.la: Ad hoc postremum de ipsorum loquendi isto modo, quia rursus constricti tenentur, dici non potest quomodo serpentum instar sese contorqueant ut exitum inveniant. At distinguenda sunt tempora, inquiunt, & occasiones inspiciendæ quas Remonstrantes ita aliquando loqui coegerunt &c. Summa responsi ipsorum eò redit: Cùm natæ in Belgio controversiæ de prædestinatione excandescerent, Reformatos Theologos nullum crebrius argumentum adhibuisse quàm argumentum à sanguine Martyrum defuit. Se autem contrà contendisse eos sanguinem non fudisse ad confirmandum dogma Calvini, ut hic pag. 81. loquuntur, de prædestinatione. Itaque Remonstrantes utuntur, inquiunt, restrictiva illa formulâ Qui Vocantur; id est, qui pro tota illa formula aut pro parte ejus hac vel illa Martyrium perpessi esse, vel falsò vel immeritò dicuntur aut creduntur, uti ex allegato à Vedelio loco manifestum est. Bone Deus! quo nomine satis digno appellem hanc insignem & improbissimam impostauram! Putant'ne Reformatos Magistratus, Doctores, populos fungos esse, quibus quidvis persuadere possint? Aut putant'ne animas suorum quos seducunt adeò viles esse, ut eas ita decipere debeant? Impossibile est quin in conscientiâ suâ convicti sint se hic sine fronte ullâ mentiri, dum dicunt se isto sensu usos restrictiva formula istâ. Cui homini qui quidè sanum sinciput habet, & qui nō libenter ab ipsis decipi gaudet, persuadere possunt horum verborum; Martyres qui vocantur sensum hunc esse: qui pro tota illa formula aut pro parte eius hac vel illa Martyrium perpessi esse vel falsò vel inmeritò dicuntur aut creduntur? Aut contrà quis non videt potius, eorum verborum sensum hunc esse; qui putantur & dicuntur à quibusdam esse Martyres. Et ut clarius appareat pareat fraudulentia ac protervia horum hominum, ac quàm studiosè contra propriam conscientiam luctentur; inspiciamus locum Apologiæ & videbimus, an'ne verba ipsorum ferre possint istam expositionem?Ita enim Apol. Exam. Cens. Præfat. f. 6. a. Per hunc gradum ( nimirum per formulas fidei quibus decìduntur Controversiæ more recepto in Ecclesiâ vetere & modernâ ) non est difficile Satana ascendere ad supremum Tyrannidis culmen, in primis ubi formula ista ætatem aliquam nacta est, & inter persecutiones aliquandiu stetit infracta, contra adversarios acriter propugnata & MARTYRUM QUI VOCANTUR Sanguine veluti auctoramento aliquo sancita ac stabilita est. Vides, optime Lector, nullo modo excsculpi posse istum sensum ex his verbis Martyres qui vocantur. Sed istam expositionem & sensum quem hic Arminiani proponunt pertinere ad sequentia verba quibus dicunt : formula sanguine eorum veluti auctoramento aliquo sancita ac stabilita est. Etenim quando dicitur formula sanguine Martyrum veluti auctoramento aliquo sancita ac stabilita esse, sensus est : Martyres pro totâ illa formula aut pro parte eius hac velillâ Martyrium perpessos dici aut credi. En igitur novum & luculentissimum specimen candoris, honestatis & conscientiæ horum hominum !
units.tr: As for this last point, their way of speaking, they are again driven into a corner and cannot escape it, however much they twist like serpents to find a way out. "But the times must be distinguished," they say, "and the occasions considered which compelled the Remonstrants to speak in this way from time to time," and so on. The sum of their answer comes to this: when the controversies about predestination, which had arisen in Belgium, grew heated, the Reformed theologians used no argument more often than the argument from the blood of the Martyrs. On the contrary, they contend, the Reformed did not shed blood to confirm the doctrine of Calvin on predestination, as they put it here on page 81. "Therefore the Remonstrants," they say, "use that restrictive formula, Who are called; that is, those who are said or believed, either falsely or undeservedly, to have suffered martyrdom for the whole of that formula or for some part of it, in this or that way, as is clear from the passage cited by Vedel. Good God! By what name worthy enough shall I call this remarkable and most wicked imposture? Do they think the Reformed magistrates, teachers and peoples are so many mushrooms, whom they can persuade of anything? Or do they think the souls of those whom they lead astray are so worthless that they may deceive them in this way? It is impossible that they are not convicted in their own conscience of lying here without shame, when they say they have used that restrictive formula in this sense. Can they persuade any man of sound mind, and one who does not gladly allow himself to be deceived by them, that the meaning of these words, Martyrs who are called, is this: those who are said or believed, either falsely or undeservedly, to have suffered martyrdom for the whole of that formula or for some part of it, in this or that way? Or on the contrary, who does not rather see that the meaning of those words is this: those who are thought and said by some to be Martyrs? And so that the trickery and shamelessness of these men may appear more clearly, and how eagerly they struggle against their own conscience, let us look at the passage of the Apology, and we shall see whether their words can bear that interpretation. For thus the Apology, Examen of the Censure, Preface, f. 6 a: By this step (namely, through the formulas of faith by which controversies are decided, in the manner received in the ancient and modern Church) it is not difficult for Satan to climb to the highest summit of tyranny, especially where that formula has gained some age and has stood unbroken for some time amid persecutions, has been fiercely defended against its opponents, and has been sanctioned and established, as it were by some pledge, with the blood of the MARTYRS WHO ARE CALLED. You see, most careful reader, that this sense cannot in any way be squeezed out of the words Martyrs who are called. But that interpretation and the sense which the Arminians propose here belong to the following words, in which they say: the formula was sanctioned and established, as it were by some pledge, with their blood. For when it is said that the formula was sanctioned and established, as it were by some pledge, with the blood of the Martyrs, the sense is: that the Martyrs are said or believed to have suffered for the whole of that formula or for some part of it, in this or that way. Behold, then, a new and most striking specimen of the candour, honesty and conscience of these men!

units.la: 7. Sub finem concludunt, etsi Martyres Evangelici revera sanguine fuderint pro dogmate aliquo aut integris eorum formulis; tamen nihil minus decere Reformatos Theologos, quàm argumento à sanguine isto Martyrum desumto pugnare ac contendere. Nam causam facere Martyrē. Deinde sic causam præberi à nobis non levem reliquis sectis sua dogmata eâ ratione afferendi, nimirum Pontificiis, Anabaptistis, Arianis, qui multas myriadas martyrum suorum allegant. Respondeo : Hoc omne ad rem non facit, ut ex dictis patet. Deinde nostri argumento illo usi non sunt primò & per se, sed saltem secundario & per accidens ; eo scilicet modo quo Orthodoxorum Patrum testimoniis utuntur, in quantum scilicet verbo Dei consentanea sunt. Et ideò quidem eo usi sunt in concionibus ad populum ut ostenderent Arminianorum sententiam antehac in Reformatis Ecclesiis nunquam traditam fuisse sed nostram, quam etiam Martyres professi sunt, & in quâ piè in Domino obierunt. Itaque diligenter dispiciendum esse populis, ne temerè sibi patiantur obtrudi novam doctrinam : sed contenti sint doctrinâ illâ priore in verbo Dei revelatâ. Adeòque semper Pastores Ecclesiàrum Belgicarum ita de sanguine Martyrum loquuti sunt, ut ostenderent eorum fidem etiam in hoc articulo in verbo Dei fundatam esse. Eò magis autem necessum fuit ut sanguinem Martyrum allegarent; quod Arminiani mature adeo impudentes fuissent, ut dicere, concionari, scribere auderent doctrinam suam de quinque articulorum praetextu esse doctrinam Ecclesiarum Reformatarum, non autem nostram. Cujus mendacii inanitatem retuderunt Orthodoxi testimonio sanguinis Martyrum, qui non istum Socinianismi ab his hominibus introducendi & evertendae Reipublicae praetextum sed nostram doctrinam noverant & in ea salvi facti sunt. Unde factum ut isti homines tandem non aliter mendacium suum & impudentiam palliare potuerint nec etiamnum possint, quam negando nostras Ecclesias Reformatas esse, prout in Vindiciis suis faciunt, in qua tamen re sibi non constant: (solet enim mendacium vertiginosum esse) nam in iisdem Vindiciis quando id judicant e re sua esse dicunt se Reformatae Religioni nobiscum addictos esse. Pudeat tandem hos homines deploratae causae suae.
units.tr: 7. At the end they conclude that, even if the Evangelical Martyrs really shed their blood for some doctrine or for the whole of its formulas, nothing would be less fitting for the Reformed theologians than to fight and contend with the argument drawn from the blood of those Martyrs. For this would give no small occasion to the other sects to advance their own doctrines in that way, namely the Papists, the Anabaptists and the Arians, who cite many myriads of their martyrs. I reply: all this has nothing to do with the matter, as is clear from what has been said. Moreover, our people did not use that argument first and of itself, but only secondarily and incidentally, in the way in which they use the testimonies of the orthodox Fathers, namely so far as those are consistent with the Word of God. And therefore they did indeed use it in sermons to the people, to show that the opinion of the Arminians had never before been taught in the Reformed Churches, but ours, which the Martyrs also professed, and in which they died devoutly in the Lord. Thus the people must carefully be watched, lest they allow a new doctrine to be thrust upon them rashly, but should be content with that former doctrine revealed in the Word of God. And so the ministers of the Belgian Churches have always spoken of the blood of the Martyrs in such a way as to show that their faith is founded in the Word of God even on this article. It was all the more necessary that they should cite the blood of the Martyrs, because the Arminians had early on become so shameless that they dared to say, to preach and to write that their doctrine, under the pretext of the Five Articles, was the doctrine of the Reformed Churches and not ours. The emptiness of this lie was refuted by the orthodox with the testimony of the blood of the Martyrs, who knew not this pretext of introducing Socinianism and overthrowing the Commonwealth by these men, but our doctrine, and were saved in it. Hence it came about that these men could not, and still cannot, cover their lie and shamelessness otherwise than by denying that our Churches are Reformed, as they do in their Vindications, though in this they are not consistent with themselves (for a lie is wont to be giddy): for in the same Vindications, when they judge it to be to their advantage, they say that they are attached to the Reformed Religion together with us. May these men at last be ashamed of their desperate cause.

units.la: Caeterum hic modus agendi quo sanguis Martyrum in testimonium adducitur, novus non est, sed usitatus in veteri Ecclesia Ita enim Athanasius & tota Synodus Alexandrina in Epistola Synodica ad Iovinianum Imperatorem. Ubi de doctrina Orthodoxa opposita Arianis & formula Nicena in qua illa doctrina exposita est, inquiunt: ἐν πάντῃ ᾧ ἡμεῖς οἱ ἀπόστολοι πεπληρωθέντες ἐμαρτύρησαν, ᾧ νῦν ἀναλελυκότες εἰσὶν ἐν κυρίῳ: in ista fide enim Sancti Martyres mortem oppetiere, & nunc in Domino quiescunt. Theodor. lib. 4. c. 3. Item Athanasius in Epistola ad suos amicos cujus etiam Socrates meminit lib. 2. c. 29. τί ποιήσωσι οἱ πατέρες καὶ οἱ μακάριοι Μάρτυρες quid de Patribus & beatis Martyribus fiet? Similiter Orthodoxi Patres Synodi Ariminensis dicunt Arianos τοσούτους ἀγίους ὁμολογητὰς ἐν Μάρτυσιν ὑπερ-ειδεῖν tot Sanctos Confessores & Martyres contemnere, in Epist. Synodica ad Constantium Imperatorem ibidem. Et postulant in Concilio ipso ut nemo in posterum Concilii Niceni decreta argueret; ἄτοπον γὰρ εἶναι &c. absurdum enim esse doctrinam quam non modo ipsi observassent, verum etiam ii tenuissent qui ante se Ecclesiis praefuerant, ὧν οἱ πλεῖστοι ἐν ὁμολογίαις ἐν Μάρτυσι τὸν βίον μετῆλθαν quorum plerique per fidei in tormentis confessionem & per Martyrium e vita migrarant. Sozomen. lib. 4. c. 17. Ex dictis etiam patet duo argumenta illa Arminianorum nulla esse. Nam testimonium Martyrum nunquam est accersitum ab Orthodoxis nisi conjunctum cum testimonio Scripturae & eo revera nixum, nec non ad retundendum mendacium horum hominum qui dicebant doctrinam nostram novam esse, in Ecclesia Reformata, suam autem esse receptam doctrinam Ecclesiae Reformatae. Nunc Lector videt me etiam capite isto Partis primae candide egisse, & eos calumniatum non esse.
units.tr: Moreover, this manner of acting, by which the blood of the Martyrs is brought forward as testimony, is not new, but was customary in the ancient Church. For thus Athanasius and the whole Alexandrian Synod in their Synodal Epistle to the Emperor Jovian, where, speaking of the orthodox doctrine opposed to the Arians and of the Nicene formula in which that doctrine is set forth, they say: ἐν πάντῃ ᾧ ἡμεῖς οἱ ἀπόστολοι πεπληρωθέντες ἐμαρτύρησαν, ᾧ νῦν ἀναλελυκότες εἰσὶν ἐν κυρίῳ [in that faith to which we the Apostles bore witness, having been filled with it, and in which they have now departed in the Lord]: for in that faith the holy Martyrs met death, and now rest in the Lord. Theodoret, book 4, chapter 3. Likewise Athanasius, in a letter to his friends, which Socrates also mentions, book 2, chapter 29: τί ποιήσωσι οἱ πατέρες καὶ οἱ μακάριοι Μάρτυρες [what will the Fathers and the blessed Martyrs do?] What will become of the Fathers and the blessed Martyrs? Similarly the orthodox Fathers of the Synod of Ariminum say that the Arians τοσούτους ἀγίους ὁμολογητὰς ἐν Μάρτυσιν ὑπερ-ειδεῖν [despised so many holy Confessors and Martyrs], in their Synodal Epistle to the Emperor Constantius, in the same place. And in the Council itself they ask that no one in future should dispute the decrees of the Council of Nicaea: ἄτοπον γὰρ εἶναι &c. [for it is absurd &c.] for it is absurd that a doctrine should be held not only by themselves, but also by those who presided over the Churches before them, ὧν οἱ πλεῖστοι ἐν ὁμολογίαις ἐν Μάρτυσι τὸν βίον μετῆλθαν [most of whom by confessing the faith under torments and by martyrdom departed this life]. Sozomen, book 4, chapter 17. From what has been said it is also clear that those two arguments of the Arminians are nothing. For the testimony of the Martyrs was never summoned by the orthodox except when joined with the testimony of Scripture and resting on it, and also to refute the lie of those men who said that our doctrine was new in the Reformed Church, while theirs was the received doctrine of the Reformed Church. Now the reader sees that I have dealt candidly in this chapter of the first Part too, and that I have not calumniated them.

units.la: CAP. III.
units.tr: CHAP. III.

units.la: Examen Capitis Tertii Vindiciarum lib. 2.
units.tr: Examination of the Third Chapter of the Vindiciae, Book 2.

units.la: 1. Diluuntur varia Arminianorum cavillationes & sophisticationes adversus id quod Auctor de pura Antiquitatis Ecclesiasticae suffragio contra Haereticos speciatim Antitrinitarios dixerat, 2. Arminiani fatentur & frustra tueri conantur quod docent: Puriorem & impuriorem Antiquitatem non nisi inanes voces esse. 3. Fatentur se docere: Regnum Christi esse posse, etiamsi omnes ejus subditi seducerentur ab hostibus ejus. Eorum cavillationes circa id dogma diluuntur. Locus Ephes. 1. 23. vindicatur adversus corruptelam ipsorum.
units.tr: 1. Various cavils and sophistries of the Arminians against what the Author said about the pure suffrage of Antiquity against the heretics, especially the Antitrinitarians, are refuted. 2. The Arminians confess, and vainly try to defend, what they teach: that the purer and the less pure Antiquity are nothing but empty words. 3. They confess that they teach that the kingdom of Christ can exist even if all its subjects were led astray by its enemies. Their cavils on that doctrine are refuted. Eph. 1. 23 is vindicated against their corruption.

units.la: 1. DOgmata ipsis cap 3. par. I. lib. 2. à me objecta duo sunt. Prius est quo docent; Puriorem & impuriorem antiquitatem non nisi inanes voces esse. Antequam Arminiani ad hoc respondeant, eludere conantur quod dixeram initio capitis illius: Pura antiquitatis suffragium contra Haereticos & in specie Antitrinitarios ex verbo Dei latum, unanimi consensu inde ab initio pro repagulo habitum fuisse, quo illi ab Ecclesia Dei abarcerentur, ne eam invaderent. Et fuisse illud in hunc usque diem in magna auctoritate apud omnes qui unum Deum in tribus personis colunt: adeo ut nunquam pro membris Ecclesiae habiti fuerint Antitrinitarii (quales hodie sunt Socinianii) primario quidem propter auctoritatem verbi Dei; secundario propter hoc testimonium & judicium ministeriale Ecclesiae universalis ex illo verbo recte institutum ac pronunciatum &c.
units.tr: 1. The two doctrines I objected to them in Book 2, chapter 3, part I, are these. The first is what they teach: the purer and the less pure antiquity are nothing but empty words. Before the Arminians answer this, they try to evade what I had said at the beginning of that chapter: The pure suffrage of antiquity, given from the Word of God against the heretics and in particular the Antitrinitarians, has by unanimous consent from the beginning been held as a barrier by which they were kept out of the Church of God, lest they invade it. And that suffrage has remained to this day of great authority among all who worship one God in three persons; so that the Antitrinitarians (such as the Socinians today) were never regarded as members of the Church, chiefly indeed because of the authority of the Word of God, and secondarily because of this testimony and ministerial judgment of the universal Church, rightly drawn from that Word and pronounced, etc.

units.la: Hic illi per convitia exorsi dubitari merito dicunt, an ego Papista sim an bene sanae mentis, & dicunt me sine cerebro scripsisse. Causam dubitandi in eo ponunt; quia Antiquitatis Ecclesiasticae auctoritate pugnare non sit Reformatorum sed Pontificiorum. Antiquitatis autem pura Ecclesiastica suffragium ex verbo Dei contra Haereticos latum a quoquam negari, inquiunt, non est sanorum credere. Quis enim suffragium purum nisi impurus respuat? quis suffragium ex ipso verbo Dei contra Haereticos latum non admittat libens?
units.tr: Here, having begun with insults, they say it may rightly be doubted whether I am a Papist or of sound mind, and they say I wrote without a brain. They place the ground of doubt in this: that to fight with the authority of ecclesiastical antiquity is the mark not of Reformers but of Papists. Yet, they say, to deny that the pure ecclesiastical suffrage given from the Word of God against the heretics is held by anyone is not the belief of sane men. For who would reject a pure suffrage unless he were impure? Who would not gladly admit a suffrage given from the very Word of God against the heretics?

units.la: Respondeo me non pugnare Ecclesiae auctoritate. Antiquitatis autem Ecclesiasticae purae suffragium ex verbo Dei contra Haereticos latum respui ab Arminianis, praeterquam quod probavi ipsorum propriis verbis ex Apol. c. 11. f. 126. b. de quibus hoc loco quaestio est, & in quibus illi persistunt, ut mox videbimus; etiam exinde constat, quod contemnunt nunt totius Ecclesiæ veteris suffragium contra Antitrinitarios latum, quos non habent pro Hæreticis, nec illis anathema dicunt, sed habent pro hominibus piis, piissimis, sanctissimis, & non habent dogmata illa Orthodoxa pro Necessariis ad salutem; imò simulantes doctrinam Orthodoxam, habent eam revera pro falsâ, & ex animo blasphemiis Socinianorum addicti sunt. Post egregium hoc dilemma suum, aggrediuntur singula membra Orationis meæ; & ludos sibi faciunt divellendo verba mea, quærendo Emphasin modò in voce antiquitatis modò in voce puritatis, modò in vocibus ex verbo Dei: Quæ sophisticatio, ut in sesquitissima est & improbissima, quâ omnis omninò veritas, imò ipsa Scriptura sacra derideri à scelestis hominibus & atheis potest, concidit propriâ ipsorum confessione quâ ipsi fatentur me verum dixisse dum ajunt, ut modò vidimus: Antiquitatis puræ suffragium ex verbo Dei latum contra Hæreticos à nemine respuendum esse. Quæstio saltem restat, an'ne Arminiani id respuant? Hoc enim negant se facere, dum hïc ajunt: Suffragium illud à quoquam negari non est sanorum credere. At ego solidè probavi, & res clamat eos respuere id judicium contra Hæreticos, speciatim Antitrinitarios latum.
units.tr: I reply that I do not fight with the authority of the Church. That the Arminians reject the pure suffrage of ancient antiquity given from the Word of God against the heretics is shown, apart from what I have proved from their own words in Apol. c. 11, f. 126 b, which is the matter in question here and which they maintain, as we shall presently see; it is also clear from this, that they despise the suffrage of the whole ancient Church given against the Antitrinitarians. They do not regard these as heretics, nor do they pronounce anathema on them; they regard them as pious, most pious, most holy men, and they do not hold those Orthodox doctrines to be necessary to salvation. Indeed, while pretending to teach the Orthodox doctrine, they in fact hold it to be false, and they are devoted in heart to the blasphemies of the Socinians. After this outstanding dilemma of theirs, they attack the individual parts of my speech and make sport of themselves by tearing my words apart, seeking emphasis now in the word antiquity, now in the word purity, now in the words from the Word of God. This sophistry, which is most shameless and wicked, by which every truth, indeed Holy Scripture itself, can be mocked by wicked men and atheists, collapses by their own confession, by which they admit that I spoke the truth when they say, as we have just seen: that the suffrage of pure antiquity given from the Word of God against the heretics is not to be rejected by anyone. The only question left is whether the Arminians reject it. For they deny that they do so, when they here say: To deny that suffrage is not the belief of sane men. But I have solidly proved, and the matter itself cries out, that they reject that judgment given against the heretics, especially the Antitrinitarians.

units.la: Tertiò ad id quod dixeram id suffragium contra Hæreticos latum ex verbo Dei habitum fuisse pro repagulo adversus Hæreticos; respondent. 1. illud suffragium non posse haberi à Reformatis pro repagulo, quia Dn. Beza scribat: Optimis temporibus etiam eam fuisse nonnullorum Episcoporum partim futilitatem & ignorantiam, ac multorum etiam apertissimam improbitatem ut Satanam plane cœtibus eorum præfuisse vel ipsi cæci facile perspiciant. Hæc verba D. Bezæ subinde crepant Arminiani ministri & sermonibus & scriptis suis, quod faciunt, ut patet ex Responsi. ad Exc. D.D.Proff. Leydd. p. 43. in eum finem ut elevent Conciliorum Orthodoxorum Veterum speciatim Nicenæ Synodi decreta contra Antitrinitarios. Verùm enimverò quis non videt nullam esse hanc consequentiam: Beza conqueritur de Nonnullorum Episcoporum, qui optimis etiam temporibus vixerunt, ambitione &c. Ergò antiquitatis purae suffragium contra Hæreticos ex verbo Dei latum non habetur aut haberi potest à Reformatis, pro repagulo quo illi ab Ecclesiâ Dei arceantur ne eam invadant: aut prout in Resp. ad Exc. argumentantur: Ergò Antitrinitarii non leves causas habent propter quas error eorum ab hæreseos culpa immunis censeri debet. Quid enim Nonnullorum Episcoporum & cœtuum improborum quibus Satanas præsedit vitia ad purae antiquitatis suffragium ex verbo Dei ab orthodoxis Synodis, piis Doctoribus, sanctis Confessoribus latum, quibus Spiritus S. praesedit ? Et ne quis existimet Dn. Bezam illiberalius locutum; sciat hanc querelam vetustissimam esse, ut videre est inter alios apud Eusebium lib. 8. cap. 1. 2. qui longè etiam vehementius conqueritur de improbitate & impietate Episcoporum nonnullorum qui seculo etiam tertio vixerunt à Christo nato.
units.tr: Thirdly, to what I had said, that this suffrage given against the heretics from the Word of God was held as a barrier against the heretics, they reply: (1) that this suffrage cannot be held by the Reformed as a barrier, because Mr. Beza wrote: In the best times too there was, in some bishops, partly foolishness and ignorance, and in many also the most open wickedness, so that even the blind can easily see that Satan presided over their assemblies. The Arminian ministers keep harping on these words of Beza in their sermons and writings, as they do, as is plain from the Response to the Examination of the Leiden Professors, p. 43, with the aim of disparaging the decrees of the Orthodox ancient Councils, especially the Synod of Nicaea, against the Antitrinitarians. But truly, who does not see that this inference is no good? Beza complains of the ambition of some bishops who lived even in the best times, etc. Therefore the pure suffrage of antiquity given against the heretics from the Word of God is not, or cannot be, held by the Reformed as a barrier by which they are kept out of the Church of God, lest they invade it; or, as they argue in the Response to the Examination: Therefore the Antitrinitarians have no slight causes on account of which their error ought to be regarded as free from the guilt of heresy. For what do the faults of some bishops and wicked assemblies, over which Satan presided, have to do with the pure suffrage of antiquity given from the Word of God by orthodox Synods, pious teachers and holy confessors, over whom the Holy Spirit presided? And lest anyone think that Mr. Beza spoke too harshly, let him know that this complaint is very ancient, as may be seen among others in Eusebius, Book 8, chapters 1 and 2, who complains even more vehemently of the wickedness and impiety of some bishops who lived in the third century after Christ's birth.

units.la: Deinde respondent: Haereticos eodem repagulo contra Reformatos uti cum maxima specie veri, & non raro cum felicissimo successu; & multa in eam rem nugantur, fingentes me excepturum, quaestionem esse de pura antiquitate, non Haeretica &c. Quae omnia impertinentia sunt; & tum demum locum haberent si ego dixissem repagulo illo utendum in disputando adversum Antitrinitarios seu in confutandis illis; quod mihi in mentem non venit: sed conceptis verbis indicavi quo modo id judicium pro repagulo habitum fuerit, nimirum dum primario propter judicium supremum verbi divini, secundatio propter testimonium illud seu judicium ministeriale Ecclesiae, non admissi fuerunt ad communionem Ecclesiae seu pro membris illius habiti. Confutandis autem Haereticis non adhibemus judicium Ecclesiae, nisi ubi illi adeo impudentes sunt ut dicant judicium Ecclesiae pro se facere, seu suam doctrinam esse doctrinam Ecclesiae veteris, Orthodoxorum autem dogmata nova esse; prout cum Socinianis apertis Arminiani hoc in capite dicere audent, ut jam videbimus.
units.tr: Next they reply: that the heretics use the same barrier against the Reformed with the greatest show of truth, and not rarely with the most happy success; and they trifle at length on this, imagining that I will object that the question is about pure antiquity, not heretical antiquity, etc. All of this is irrelevant, and it would have force only if I had said that this barrier must be used in disputing against the Antitrinitarians, or in refuting them; which did not come into my mind. Rather, I stated in plain words how that judgment was held as a barrier: namely, that they were chiefly, because of the supreme judgment of the divine Word, and secondarily, because of that testimony or ministerial judgment of the Church, not admitted to communion with the Church, nor regarded as its members. But in refuting heretics we do not apply the judgment of the Church, except where they are so shameless as to say that the judgment of the Church favours them, or that their doctrine is the doctrine of the ancient Church and that the Orthodox doctrines are new; as the Arminians now dare to say in this chapter along with the open Socinians, as we shall presently see.

units.la: Quarto convellere volunt, quod dixi Antitrinitarios nunquam pro membris Ecclesiae habitos fuisse. Et dicunt se contrarium solidis argumentis ex Justino ostendisse. Hoc quam falsum sit, ex propria ipsorum Confessione ostendimus lib. 1. cap. 7. Addunt magno judicio opus esse, ut quis antiquissimorum Scriptorum inprimis qui Concilium Nicenum praecesserunt mentem ac sententiam de Trinitate pervideat. Non pauca nec obscura indicia reperiri passim est, inquiunt, quae eos vel Arii, vel Platonis, vel nescio quam peculiarem de divinis personis opinionem habuisse testatum faciunt. Ex Justino sole clarius est, eum fateri Ecclesias Christianas suo tempore agnovisse Jesum quidem verum esse Deum, sed tamen alium a Creatore universi, praeter & supra quem alius non esset Deus. Id ita esse vel hoc unum arguit, quod neget Deum auctorem & Parentem universi, supercoelestia omnia reliquisse & in pusilla parte terra sese exhibuisse, in Dialogo cum Tryphone Judaeo, & quod Filium voluntate Dei genitum esse passim asserat. Ex Ignatii Epistolis non levia Arianismi indicia colligere est.
units.tr: Fourthly, they wish to overturn what I said, that the Antitrinitarians were never regarded as members of the Church. They say that they have shown the contrary by solid arguments from Justin. How false this is, we have shown from their own confession in Book 1, chapter 7. They add that great judgment is needed, so that one may clearly perceive the mind and opinion of the most ancient writers, especially those who preceded the Council of Nicaea, concerning the Trinity. Not a few and not obscure indications are found everywhere, they say, which make it attested that they held the opinion of Arius, or of Plato, or I know not what peculiar opinion about the divine persons. From Justin it is clearer than the sun that he admits that the Christian Churches in his time acknowledged Jesus indeed to be true God, but yet another than the Creator of the universe, beside and above whom there is no other God. That this is so is shown by this one thing alone: that in the Dialogue with Trypho the Jew he denies that God, the author and parent of the universe, left all the things above heaven and showed himself in a small part of the earth, and he asserts everywhere that the Son was begotten by the will of God. From the Epistles of Ignatius one may gather no slight indications of Arianism.

units.la: Respondeo: Haec omnia salsissima sunt, ex Antitrinitariorum Scholiis lis repetita & fœpius abOrthodoxæ sententiæ Doctoribus refutata. Quæ sit Patrum sententia, qui præcesserunt concilium Nicenum ; planissi-mum est & notissimum omnibus, exceptis Antitrinitariis, speciatim So-cinianis apertis & his simulatoribus. Ostenderunt id sæpe Orthodoxi adversum Antitrinitarios. Et ii ipsi qui tempore Concilii Niceni vixe-runt, ostenderunt prædecessores suos eandem cum ipsis doctrinam circa illud mysterium tradidisse ; & ipse Arius id fatebatur, ut vidimus Par. III. lib. 2. c. 3. Itaque calumnia est, quod hic dicunt Sociniani hi simu-latores ; Patres ante Concilium Nicenum, Arii aut aliam erroneam opi-nionem de Trinitate habuisse. Iustinus nullibi Christum alterius essentiæ à Patre dicit, sed tantum agit contra eos Hæreticos qui personas con-fundebant, & ipsum Patrem incarnatum somniabant ; plane quemad-modum ante eum S. Ignatius, ut libro præcedente vidimus, contra eos-dem Hæreticos agens, eodem loquendi modo utitur. Filium voluntate Patris genitum dicit quidem Iustinus, sed non opponit voluntatem na-turæ, ut Antitrinitarii faciunt, h. e. non negat eum natura genitum esse: verum opponit eam coactioni & mere naturali agendi modo qui sine in-tellectu & voluntate est, ut in brutis. Quod dicunt ex Ignatii Epistolis non levia Arianismi signa apparere, salsissimum esse supra ostendimus.
units.tr: I reply: all of this is utterly silly, a worn-out repetition of the Antitrinitarians' scholia, and it has been refuted again and again by the teachers of the Orthodox view. What the Fathers who preceded the Council of Nicaea believed is perfectly plain and well known to everyone, except the Antitrinitarians, especially the open Socinians and these dissemblers. The Orthodox have often shown this against the Antitrinitarians. And those who lived at the time of the Council of Nicaea showed that their predecessors had handed down the same doctrine as themselves concerning that mystery; Arius himself admitted it, as we saw in Part III, book 2, ch. 3. So it is a slander when these Socinian dissemblers say that the Fathers before the Council of Nicaea held the opinion of Arius, or some other erroneous view of the Trinity. Justin nowhere says that Christ is of a different essence from the Father. He is arguing only against those heretics who confused the persons and dreamed that the Father himself was incarnate, just as Ignatius before him, as we saw in the preceding book, arguing against the same heretics, uses the same way of speaking. Justin does indeed say that the Son was begotten by the will of the Father, but he does not set will against nature, as the Antitrinitarians do; that is, he does not deny that the Son was begotten by nature. Rather, he sets it against compulsion and against a merely natural mode of acting, which lacks intellect and will, as in brute beasts. That they say the Epistles of Ignatius show no slight signs of Arianism, we have shown above to be utterly silly.

units.la: Quintò, ad id quod dixeram : Arminianos id repagulum velle ablatum, quia nolunt agnoscere dogmata illa Orthodoxa de Trinitate esse necessaria ad salutem, Respondent ; Si ex antiquitatis Ecclesiasticæ testimonio evinci possit ea dogmata esse necessaria ad salutem ; se libenter ea agnituros pro necessariis. Sed hæc mera hypocrisis est. Nam 1. ego solidissimo argumento ostenderam Par. I. lib. 1. c. 7. p. 53. illa esse Necessaria ad salutem, ex eo quòd Arminiani dicunt alicubi Mysterium illud prout extra controversiam est necessarium esse ad salutem : quod subsistere non potest nisi etiam statuatur esse necessarium in suo vero sensu qui illis dogmatis Orthodoxis (quæ Antitrinitarii negant) continetur. Ad hoc argumentum illi ne quidem respondent, nec respondere possunt; adeoque convicti sunt in animo suo. Attamen tantum abest, ut velint agnoscere ea pro Necessariis ad salutem, ut quia respondere mihi non possunt, præ rabie convitiis me insolentissimis petant & contumeliose habeant. Multò minus ergò gloriam Sacrosanctæ Trinitati daturi sunt, si testimonio & auctoritate Ecclesiæ contra eos pugnarem. 2. Patet esse meram hypo-crisin etiam ex eo, quòd nolunt, ut Lector videt, in hoc ipso capite an-tiquitatis puræ auctoritate quemquam pugnare in Controversiis his aut aliis. Et cap. 4. p. 90. invitant me ut probem Socinianos esse Hæreticos sed hac conditione ut auctoritate Ecclesiæ non pugnem: Si aliter credit Vedelius, inquiunt, age experiatur vires suas, & si Papista esse nolit, id est, si auctoritate Ecclesiæ pugnare non velit &c. 3. Ex tota historia Ecclesiastica & ex Patribus patet anathema perpetuo dictum fuisse iis qui negant Christum habere divinam naturam. Sed hoc homines hi nescīunt, adeoque ostendunt quam parum periti sint antiquitatis Ecclesiasticæ. Hoc unum est quod respondent. Deinde dicunt: antiquam Ecclesiam non habuisse ea pro necessariis ad salutem; quod ajunt se ex Iustino probâsse. Hoc falsum esse supra ostendimus. Tertiò dicunt se mysterium Trinitatis, prout Scriptura de eo loquitur, (h. e. prout extra controversiam est) habere pro Necessario. De hoc quid sit sentiendum vidimus Par. I. lib. 1. c. 7. & libro præcedente Partis hujus cap. 7. Ubi ostendimus quàm turpiter se dent isti homines in hac re. Hoc prætereundum non est, quòd ibidem causam reddentes cur non possint dogmata illa controversa Trinitatis habere pro necessariis; dicunt p. 85. se id facere ne ex una parte leviter damnent infinitas hominum myriadas &c. ) de cujus prætextus futilitate egimus lib. præcedente cap. 7. ) ex altera parte, ne prafratè refragari velle videantur unanimi & diuturno multorum LICET NON ANTIQUISSIMORUM SECULORUM consensui. His junge, quòd p. 84. dicunt, ut paulò ante vidimus, non pauca nec obscura indicia passim reperiri, quæ testatum faciant Patres ante Concilium Nicenum non sensisse in doctrinâ Trinitatis ut Nicenum Concilium sed vel Arii, vel Platonis, vel nescio quam peculiarem de divinis personis opinionem habuisse. Quibus verbis repetunt quod dixerant lib. 1. Vindic. c. 7. p. 73. 38. ubi itidem dicunt doctrinam Orthodoxam de Trinitate controversam cum Antitrinitariis coepisse demum cum Concilio Niceno, ut ostendimus Par. III. lib. 1. c. 7. §. 1. Unde rursus luce clarius meridianâ est, hos homiens simulare tantùm Orthodoxam doctrinam de Trinitate; & ex animo blasphemiis Socinianorum addictos esse.
units.tr: Fifthly, to what I had said, that the Arminians want that barrier removed because they are unwilling to acknowledge that those Orthodox doctrines of the Trinity are necessary to salvation, they reply: If it can be proved from the testimony of ancient Church antiquity that those doctrines are necessary to salvation, we will gladly acknowledge them as necessary. But this is mere hypocrisy. For first, I had shown by a most solid argument, in Part I, book 1, ch. 7, p. 53, that those doctrines are necessary to salvation, from the fact that the Arminians say somewhere that that mystery, as it is beyond controversy, is necessary to salvation. This cannot stand unless it is also held to be necessary in its true sense, which is contained in those Orthodox doctrines that the Antitrinitarians deny. To this argument they do not even reply, nor can they reply; and so they are convicted in their own minds. Yet they are so far from wishing to acknowledge these doctrines as necessary to salvation that, because they cannot answer me, they attack me in their rage with the most insolent insults and treat me with contumely. Much less, therefore, will they give glory to the most holy Trinity if I contend against them by the testimony and authority of the Church. 2. It is also plain that this is mere hypocrisy from the fact that, as the reader sees, in this very chapter they do not want anyone to contend in these or other controversies by the authority of pure antiquity. And in ch. 4, p. 90, they invite me to prove that the Socinians are heretics, but on this condition: that I do not contend by the authority of the Church. If Vedelius believes otherwise, they say, let him try his strength, and if he does not wish to be a Papist, that is, if he does not wish to contend by the authority of the Church, etc. 3. From the whole ecclesiastical history and from the Fathers it is plain that anathema was constantly pronounced against those who deny that Christ has a divine nature. But these men do not know this, and so they show how little skilled they are in ecclesiastical antiquity. This is the only thing they answer. Then they say that the ancient Church did not hold these doctrines as necessary to salvation, which they say they proved from Justin. That this is false we have shown above. Thirdly, they say they hold the mystery of the Trinity, as Scripture speaks of it (that is, as it is beyond controversy), to be necessary. What is to be thought of this we saw in Part I, book 1, ch. 7, and in the preceding book of this part, ch. 7, where we showed how shamefully these men act in this matter. It must not be passed over that, in the same place, giving the reason why they cannot hold those controversial doctrines of the Trinity to be necessary, they say at p. 85 that they do so lest on the one hand they lightly condemn infinite myriads of men, etc. (the flimsiness of this pretext we discussed in the preceding book, ch. 7), and on the other hand lest they seem to be rashly opposing the unanimous and long-standing consensus of many, though not of the most ancient centuries. Add to this that at p. 84 they say, as we saw a little above, that not a few and not obscure indications are found everywhere which make it evident that the Fathers before the Council of Nicaea did not think about the doctrine of the Trinity as the Council of Nicaea did, but held either the opinion of Arius, or of Plato, or I know not what peculiar opinion about the divine persons. In these words they repeat what they had said in book 1 of their Vindications, ch. 7, p. 73, 38, where likewise they say that the Orthodox doctrine of the Trinity, contested with the Antitrinitarians, began only with the Council of Nicaea, as we showed in Part III, book 1, ch. 7, §1. Whence it is again clearer than midday light that these men only pretend to hold the Orthodox doctrine of the Trinity, and are in their hearts devoted to the blasphemies of the Socinians.

units.la: 2. His omnibus subjiciunt p.85.86. Confessionem dogmatis sibi objecti; ita ut primò causam exponant quæ ipsos moverit ut ita in Apologiâ clarissimis D. D. Proff. Leydd. responderent: nimirum studium tuendi auctoritatem verbi divini &c. Quasi scilicet auctoritas verbi divini non aliter possit conservari quàm dicendo puram & impuram antiquitatem non nisi inanes voces esse. Et constat, quæ vera causa sit cur Socviniani Hæretici (quales Arminiani ministri se esse in Vindiciis suis manifemanifestissimum faciunt) contemnant puram antiquitatem; quia scilicet anathema dicit blasphemiis eorum.
units.tr: 2. To all these things they add, at p. 85–86, a confession of the doctrine laid to their charge. They first explain the cause that moved them to answer in this way in their Apology to the most distinguished professors of Leiden: namely, zeal for defending the authority of the divine Word, etc. As if, forsooth, the authority of the divine Word could not be preserved except by saying that pure and impure antiquity are nothing but empty words. And it is plain what the true cause is why the Socinian heretics (such as the Arminian ministers show themselves to be in their Vindications, most manifestly) despise pure antiquity: namely, because it pronounces anathema on their blasphemies.

units.la: Deinde defendunt illud dogma suum pag. 86. eo praeclaro praetextu, quòd puritas antiquitatis non possit æstimari ex verbo Dei, quia de verbi Dei interpretatione quæstio est. Item p. 87. quia Arius pari jure puritatem antiquitatis pro se allegabit; & quia, si definitio puritatis in verbo Dei quæritur; ineptè illud fiat. Nam Arius, inquiunt, idem dicet, & verbum Dei inepte à se citari ex purae antiquitatis sensu probabit. De quibus Novis Arcanis eorum vide Par. III. lib. 1. c. 4. & lib. 2. c. 3. §. 1. 2.
units.tr: Then they defend their doctrine at p. 86 under that splendid pretext, that the purity of antiquity cannot be judged from the Word of God, because the question concerns the interpretation of the Word of God. Likewise at p. 87, because Arius will claim with equal right the purity of antiquity for himself, and because, if the definition of purity is sought in the Word of God, that is done foolishly. For Arius, they say, will say the same, and will prove by the sense of pure antiquity that the Word of God is wrongly cited by him. On these points see their New Mysteries, Part III, book 1, ch. 4, and book 2, ch. 3, §§1, 2.

units.la: Tandem ex me p. 87. Pontificium facere volunt, ideò quia dixi: Sitota Ecclesia vera inde ab initio usque ad hæc tempora non potuit decidere hanc quaestionem An hoc vel illud dogma Photini, Samosateni &c. de Trinitate sit Haereticum; neminem hominem igitur aut solum aut cum aliis eam decidere posse. Ubi dum me ideò Pontificium esse volunt, quis non videt hos homines sophisticari in eâ etiam parte contra conscientiam suam? Quomodo enim vocem decisionis sumam, nôrunt ipsi ex cap. 6. Par. I. lib. 2. p. 184. 185. Ubi ostendi quomodo Ecclesia possit dici decidere controversias fidei; nimirum non proprie sed improprie, non per se sed per accidens, respectu scilicet verbi Dei, cuius norma qua Deus solus & supremus judex utitur, judicium decisionis competit. Est'ne hoc Pontificium esse? Sed de eâ re h. e. de judicio humano circa res fidei copiosè etiam & ex professo egimus in Rationali Theologico. Addunt, nec Ecclesiae nec ulli homini talem decisionem Pontificiam competere; quod adversum me non facit; qui Deum in verbo suo loquentem supremum judicem constituo; cui verbo si conforme est judicium Ecclesiae, illud non est rejiciendum; si autem ei repugnat omninò est repudiandum. Et sic concidunt etiam ea quae de controversiâ Liberi arbitrii p. 88. impertinenter & extra oleas vagabundi nugantur.
units.tr: At last, at p. 87, they want to make me a Papist, because I said: If the whole true Church from the beginning until these times could not decide this question, whether this or that doctrine of Photinus, Samosatenus, etc. about the Trinity is heretical, then no man, either alone or with others, can decide it. When they want me to be a Papist on this ground, who does not see that these men here sophisticate, even in this part, against their own conscience? For how I take the word decision they themselves know from ch. 6, Part I, book 2, pp. 184–185, where I showed how the Church can be said to decide controversies of faith: not properly but improperly, not per se but per accidens, namely with respect to the Word of God, whose norm God alone, the supreme and judge, uses; the judgment of decision belongs to it. Is this being Papist? But that matter, that is, human judgment concerning matters of faith, we have also discussed at length and expressly in the Rational Theology. They add that neither the Church nor any man has such a Papist decision; which does not tell against me, since I set up God speaking in his word as the supreme judge. If the judgment of the Church agrees with that word, it is not to be rejected; but if it is contrary to it, it must be utterly repudiated. And so also fall those things which they babble, wandering impertinently and out of the furrow, about the controversy of free will at p. 88.

units.la: 3. Alterum dogma quod ipsis objeceram est: Regnum Christi subsistere posse, etiamsi omnes subditi ejus seducerentur ab hostibus ejus, quales sunt Haeretici. Fatentur hoc p. 88. cum consuetis scommatis, & initiò exagitant quod dixi Ecclesiam à Deo collectam esse propter regnum Christi non tantum propter salutem suam. Quibus verbis indicavi Deum, qui decreverat ab aeterno Christo Mediatori Regnum, etiam populum seu subditos ei decrevisse, quos ipse collegit. Quâ re verius nihil est. Hoc illi sophisticè exagitant 1. ex eo quòd absurdum sit, Ecclesiam Christo regnum colligere. Atqui ego illud non dixi, nec verba mea eò tendunt; sed potiùs contracontrarium expresse dixi; nimirum Ecclesiam à Deo colligi; & sic quod Christus regnat non Ecclesiae sed Deo Patri adscribo. II. Sic dicendum erit, inquiunt, Ecclesiam etiam propter Christum esse, & non Christum tantum propter Ecclesiam: id quod absurdum esse dicunt 1. quia sic Christus & Ecclesia sibi invicem vicem rependunt, & alter alteri reciprocam gratitudinem debet. 2. quia Regem non faciunt subditi: jus Regium à voluntate subditorum non dependet. 3. quia populus non est propter Regem, sed Rex propter populum. 4. quia Majestas Regia constat etiamsi subditi omnes rebellent. probant.
