Non negant Arminiani se ita docere: & ne verbulo quidem ad hæc quæ profectò enormia & detestanda dogmata sunt respondent, sed sicco pede transeunt: saltem tacitè ob eam causam haud dubiè convitia aliquot meditantes & volventes, quibus mox me proscindent in pœnam veritatis quâ ipsis ista duo etiam dogmata objeci. Porrò quia docent ideò seductores nō peccare quia suos errores nobis proponunt tanquam perditionis æternæ remedium: ostenderam ego p. 135. illam falsam causam esse. Nam non omnes Hæreticos in specie Antitrinitarios eum scopum habere, imò secundùm Augustinum lib. de util. cred. cap. 1. nullum Hæreticum eum scopum sibi propositum habere. Ad hoc etiam Arminiani ne γῆ quidem respondent.
units.tr: 11, 12. The eleventh doctrine is: not only do simple heretics, or those led astray by others, not sin, but the seducers themselves are without fault. The twelfth is: and therefore seducers are not worthy of hatred. The Arminians do not deny that they teach this, and they answer not a word to these doctrines, which are truly monstrous and detestable, but pass over them with dry feet. Doubtless they are silently composing and turning over some insults with which they will soon tear me apart in punishment for the truth I have set against them in these two doctrines. Moreover, since they teach that seducers do not sin because they offer their errors to us as a remedy for eternal perdition, I had shown on p. 135 that this is a false reason. Not all heretics, and certainly not the Antitrinitarians, have that aim. Indeed, according to Augustine, De utilitate credendi, ch. 1, no heretic sets that aim before himself. To this the Arminians do not reply even a syllable [γῆ].

units.la: 13. Aliud est: Hæreticos non esse impios. Hoc etiam non negant sed fatentur, contenti iis quæ antea dixerant circa dogma quod Hæresis non sit peccatum.
units.tr: 13. The next doctrine is: heretics are not impious. This too they do not deny but admit, content with what they had said before about the doctrine that heresy is not sin.

units.la: 14. Aliud: Nullum Hæreticum esse blasphemum proprie sic dictum. Hoc etiam non negant, sed cùm convitio inscitiæ in pœnam veritatis à me prolatæ fatentur & defendere conantur sed impertinentibus nugis quibus contendunt Hæreticum quâ talem non esse blasphemum: Et cùm has nænias quæ ad rem non faciunt deblatterâssent; fatentur me loqui de quibusdam Hæreticis tantùm ut Serveto & similibus monstris, quemadmodum modum expresse dixeram; & illud etiam negant, duabus ineptis ratiun-culis allatis, quæ corruunt prout vox blasphemiæ sumitur vel late vel stricte. Late sumta voce blasphemiæ, omnis hæresis blasphemia est; quia vias Domini evertit, & idolum mentis suæ loco veri Dei colit, & eâ ratione gloriæ Dei detrahit. Stricte sumta vox blasphemiæ denotat crimen speciale illud, quod corporaliter, & pro ratione delicti etiam morte puniendum docet Scriptura, ut quando Sacrosancta & adoranda Trinitas benedicta in seculum vocatur ab Antitrinitariis Cerberus, triforme monstrum &c. In posteriore significatione sumsi vocem blasphemiæ ibi. Hæc est uno verbo orthodoxa doctrina de blasphemiis Hæreticorum. Et sic concidunt etiam quæ lib. 1. c. 1. p. 13. tot convitiis quot verbis respondent ad id quod conquestus fueram de eodem dogmate cap. 1. Arc. lib. 1. Par. I. ubi me Anticyras & ad Helleborum ablegant, alioquin, inquiunt, brevi pra insani à faciet Hæreticũ incestuosum perduellem, veneficum &c.
units.tr: 14. Another doctrine is: no heretic is blasphemous, properly so called. This too they do not deny. But when I charged them with the insult of ignorance, in punishment for the truth I had brought forward, they admit it and try to defend it with irrelevant trifles, contending that a heretic as such is not blasphemous. After babbling these trifles, which have nothing to do with the matter, they admit that I speak only of certain heretics, such as Servetus and similar monsters, as I had expressly said. They also deny it, citing two silly little arguments which collapse according as the word blasphemy is taken broadly or narrowly. Taken broadly, every heresy is blasphemy, since it overturns the ways of the Lord, worships the idol of its own mind in place of the true God, and by that reasoning detracts from the glory of God. Taken narrowly, the word blasphemy denotes that special crime which Scripture teaches must be punished bodily, and even by death in proportion to the offence, as when the most holy and adorable blessed Trinity is called by the Antitrinitarians "Cerberus, the three-formed monster," and so on. In that latter sense I took the word blasphemy there. In a word, this is the orthodox doctrine about the blasphemies of heretics. And so also fall those things in book 1, ch. 1, p. 13, where, with as many insults as words, they answer what I had complained of on the same doctrine in Arcana, book 1, Part I, ch. 1. There they send me off to Anticyra and to hellebore: "otherwise," they say, "you will soon go so mad as to make a heretic an incestuous man, a traitor, a poisoner, etc."

units.la: 15. Hæresin esse innocentiam proprie sic dictam; imò nullam esse majorem innocentiam quàm Hæreticorum. Item; Nullos minus peccare quàm eos quà tales sunt. Denique Hæresin esse perfectam innocentiam, quando eam comitetur par in dissentientes benevolentia. 16. Hæreticos esse legum Christi retinentissimos. 17. Hæreticos proscribere esse Christum crucifigere, & contra profanos, avaros, ebriosos, invidos non pellere esse Barrabam dimittere. 18. Hæreticos esse homines innocentissimos, optimos, carnis & mundi osores. Esse homines pios, vita plane inculpata, aliosque ad pietatem exemplo & sensu suo provocare. 19. Eos esse animas piissimas, sanctissimas, Christum, & Religionem ejus ex animo ompletti. Hæc omnia non negant, sed cum rursus in poenam veritatis mihi fermentum insciitiæ objecissent: fatentur ac defendunt. Summa autem defensionis redit: Hæresin de quâ Paulus loquitur, quatenus est opus carnis, non esse innocentiam: sed esse innocentiam, primò, quia Hæreticus animo suo innocens est. Secundò, quia suæ & aliorum salutem per errorem suum consulere vult. Tertiò, quia media quæ usurpat h. e. argumenta non nocere possunt nisi volenti &c. Quartò, quia sæpè sunt vitæ adeò emendatæ ut aliis exemplo sint & pænè miraculo p. 99. 100. Bonum factum! Ecce inscitiam Vedelii strenuè repulsam. Commemorare ista est refutare. Et falsitas eorum partim ex dictis patet; partim manifesta est ex iis quæ Par. III. lib. 2. c. 4. de Arcanis novis quæ ibi latent diximus. Unum addam. Quod dicunt hic de Christo crucifixo & Barraba dimissio; aliter longè Scripturam nos docere; quæ indicat Christum crucifigi quando profani & impii ita tolerantur, ut Christus in membris suis h. e. Orthodoxis perfequutionem patiatur. Hinc Christus de coelo clamat Act. 9. 4. Saul, Saul quid me persequeris! Hinc Eusebius dicit cum praesente Diocletiano Imperatore Agapius Martyr una cum quodam malefico & scelesto homine in theatrum productus & bestiis objectus, maleficus autem dimissus esset, id esse μονογυχὶ κατ' αὐτὸν ἐκεῖνον τὸν ὂπὶ τῆς σωτηρίας Βασιλέα propè ad similitudinem Barrabae Latronis cum Christo captivi. lib. 8. c. 16. Quod dicunt Haereticos provocare alios ad pietatem exemplo suo; eo quid sibi velint facile intelligi potest, tum ex eo quòd Haereticos aliis h. e. Orthodoxis opponunt; tùm quod Vindic. lib. 2. c. 9. p. 184. dicunt Haereticos obsequio, fide & vita probitate inter subditos excellere. Uno verbo mens eorum est, eos verae pietatis exemplo esse Orthodoxis.
units.tr: 15. That heresy is innocence, properly so called; indeed that there is no greater innocence than that of heretics. Likewise, that none sin less than those who are heretics as such. Finally, that heresy is perfect innocence when it is accompanied by a like benevolence towards dissenters. 16. That heretics are the most tenacious keepers of Christ's laws. 17. That to proscribe heretics is to crucify Christ, and that not to drive away profane, avaricious, drunken and envious men is to release Barabbas. 18. That heretics are the most innocent and best of men, haters of the flesh and the world; that they are pious men of altogether blameless life, who by their example and their feeling stir others to piety. 19. That they are the most pious and holy souls, who embrace Christ and his religion from the heart. They do not deny all this, but when I again objected to them the leaven of ignorance, in punishment for the truth, they affirm and defend it. The sum of their defence comes to this. The heresy of which Paul speaks, insofar as it is a work of the flesh, is not innocence; but it is innocence, first, because the heretic is innocent in his own mind; second, because he wishes to secure his own and others' salvation through his error; third, because the means he uses, that is, arguments, cannot harm anyone except one who is willing; and fourth, because often their lives are so reformed that they are examples to others and almost a miracle (pp. 99, 100). "Well done!" Behold, Vedel's ignorance vigorously repulsed. To recount these things is to refute them. Their falsity is partly evident from what has been said, and partly manifest from what we said in Part III, book 2, ch. 4 about the new Arcana that lie hidden there. I will add one thing. As to what they say here about Christ crucified and Barabbas released, Scripture teaches us quite otherwise: it shows that Christ is crucified when the profane and impious are so tolerated that Christ suffers persecution in his members, that is, in the orthodox. Hence Christ cries from heaven, Acts 9:4, "Saul, Saul, why do you persecute me?" Hence Eusebius says that, when the Emperor Diocletian was present, Agapius, a martyr, was led into the theatre together with a certain wicked and criminal man and thrown to the beasts, but the wicked man was released; and that this was almost like Barabbas the robber, released while Christ was taken captive [μονονουχὶ κατ' αὐτὸν ἐκεῖνον τὸν ὑπὲρ τῆς σωτηρίας Βασιλέα], Church History 8, ch. 16. As to what they say, that heretics provoke others to piety by their example, what they mean can easily be understood, both from the fact that they set heretics over against others, that is, the orthodox, and because in Vindication, book 2, ch. 9, p. 184, they say that heretics excel among subjects in obedience, faith and uprightness of life. In a word, their intention is that heretics, by the example of true piety, are superior to the orthodox.

units.la: 20. Haereticos non esse noxios salutì animarum. Hoc etiam non negant sed defendunt cavillo suo contra doctrinam nostram de Electione & reprobatione p. 101. 102, quo cavillo etiam volunt eludere quod dixeram de pennis Aquilinis quas veritati tribuunt Arminiani, & quas ego Arminianos ei eripere, ac Solem illum convertere in tenebras ostenderam. Cui cavillo uno verbo respondeo: velle quidem Deum Electos ad salutem perducere, sed per media, quae non sunt negligenda aut violanda. Ex his mediis est cognitio veritatis divinae. Perducit enim Deus nos ad salutem per sanctificationem Spiritus & fidem habitam veritati, ait Apoft. 2. Theff. 2. 13. Reprobi autem pereunt, sed sua culpa pereunt: propterea quod amorem veritatis non receperunt, ut salvi fierent, & damnantur quia non crediunt veritati ait ibid v. 10. 11. 12. Unde haereses a veteribus secundum Scripturam φρενοπλαγέαι vocabantur non tam ob insaniam quam ob noxam quam animarum saluti inferunt prout Theodor. lib. 5. cap 8. Apollinarii haeresin φρενοπλαγέαν vocat.
units.tr: 20. That heretics are not harmful to the salvation of souls. This too they do not deny but defend, with their quibble against our doctrine of election and reprobation (pp. 101, 102). By this quibble they also wish to evade what I had said about the Eagle's feathers, which the Arminians attribute to the truth, and which I had shown they snatch from it, turning that Sun into darkness. To that quibble I answer in one word: God indeed wills to bring the elect to salvation, but by means that are not to be neglected or violated. Among these means is the knowledge of divine truth. For God brings us to salvation through the sanctification of the Spirit and faith in the truth, says the Apostle, 2 Thess. 2:13. But the reprobate perish, and they perish by their own fault, because they did not receive the love of the truth, that they might be saved, and they are condemned because they do not believe the truth, says the same at vv. 10, 11, 12. Hence the ancients, following Scripture, called heresies phrenoplagiai [φρενοπλαγέαι], not so much for their madness as for the harm they do to the salvation of souls; so Theodoret, book 5, ch. 8, calls the heresy of Apollinaris phrenoplangeai [φρενοπλαγέαν].

units.la: Postulant etiam absurditatis ea quaedixerã de Arminianorum conatu, nimirum eos veritatis Solem convertere in tenebras, dum naturam fidei Christianae & media quibus Deus illam conservari vult evertunt. Dicunt impossibile esse, ut veritatis Sol convertatur in tenebras ab ipsis, idque ob vim veritatis. Sed hoc ad rem non facit. Constat veritatem opprimi aut exstingui non posse; sed tamen ex altera parte etiam constat Haereticos spectatim simulatores Antitrinitarios Solem veritatis in tenebras convertere quantum in ipsis est, hoc est, eos conari illam oppimere praetextu eo, quòd veritas non veritas sed error sit. Quia igitur conantur Solem in tenebras convertere, adeòque quantum in se est eum in tenebras convertunt, hinc dicuntur Solem in tenebras convertere, caliginem injicere veritati prout Severus Sulpitius de Arianis loquitur 1.2. an.357.ubi dicit Arianos caliginem injecisse veritati: Ariani, inquit, non occultè, ut antea, sed palàm ac publicè haresis piacula praedicabant; quin etiam Synodum Nicenam pro se interpretantes, quam unius literula adjectione corruperant, caliginem quandam injecerant veritati.
units.tr: They also demand absurdity for what I said about the Arminians' attempt, namely that they turn the Sun of truth into darkness while they overturn the nature of the Christian faith and the means by which God wills it to be preserved. They say it is impossible for the Sun of truth to be turned into darkness by them, and that on account of the power of truth. But this does not bear on the matter. It is certain that truth cannot be overwhelmed or extinguished; but on the other hand it is also certain that heretics, and especially the Antitrinitarian dissemblers, turn the Sun of truth into darkness as far as in them lies, that is, they try to suppress it under the pretext that truth is not truth but error. Since, therefore, they try to turn the Sun into darkness, and as far as they are concerned do turn it into darkness, they are said to turn the Sun into darkness and to cast a mist over the truth. So Severus Sulpicius speaks of the Arians, in book 2, year 357, where he says that the Arians had cast a mist over the truth: "The Arians, he says, did not hide as they had before, but openly and publicly proclaimed the abominations of heresy; moreover, interpreting the Nicene Synod in their own favour, which they had corrupted by adding a single letter, they had cast a certain mist over the truth."

units.la: 21. Haereticos non esse noxios Ecclesiae. Etiam fatentur, & tuentur his verbis p. 102. Ecclesiae eadem ratio est. Si enim nullius individui in Ecclesiâ salus laborat ab haeresium turbâ ac turmâ, quod periculum ab haeresibus metuere aut potest aut habet Ecclesia quae ex individuis illis constat? Ad quod sophisma modò respondimus, sectione praecedente.
units.tr: 21. Heretics are not harmful to the Church. They even admit this and defend it in these words, p. 102: "The Church is in the same position. For if the salvation of no individual in the Church is endangered by the crowd and host of heresies, what danger can the Church, which is made up of those individuals, fear or face from heresies?" I have already answered this sophism in the preceding section.

units.la: 22. Haeresibus & Schismatis januam optimè claudi, quando liberum exercitium Religionis permittitur Haereticis & Schismaticis. Hoc Arminiani non negant, sed sicco pede transeunt, ac planè tacent, silentio vindictam prementes quam per convitia exserent, quae mox mihi in poenam veritatis dicturi sunt. Ita nunquam inulti discedunt. Interim pius Lector & eruditus observet singularem istam proterviam, quâ hi homines audent hoc etiam dogma spargere; id quod proficiscitur tùm ex aliis tùm ex inexperientiâ & inscitiâ rerum quae in Ecclesiâ veteri contigerunt, quae inscitia multorum errorum & malorum causa esse solet, ut in Nestorio vidit Ecclesia, qui non solùm ob superbiam, sed etiam ὑπὸ ἀμαθείας πολλῆς, ut Socrates loquitur, ex multâ inscitiâ & inexperientiâ rerum antiquioris Ecclesiae in haeresin prolapsus est. Si Arminiani (qui, cùm solidae eruditionis nihilum quidem habeant, omnes tamen homines, speciatim, ut antè dixi, Orthodoxos Doctores vivos & mortuos prae se contemnunt, & eos qui se ipsorum partibus opponunt, pro stupidis & ineruditissimis atque ineptissimis hominibus habent,) legissent veterum scripta, didicissent utique eâ ratione Haeresibus & Schismatis januam nequaquam claudi quando ipsis liberum exercitium permittitur. Contrarium enim testatur experientia veteris Ecclesiae. Constantinus M. libertatem eam negârat Arianis, & tunc haeresis alas trahebat: succedit Constantius, qui liberum exercitium iis reddidit, & tunc totus penè orbis Arianum se esse vidit & ingemuit. Et, ne quis dicat, tùm demum haereses solere crescere per liberum exercitium, quando Princeps Haereticus est, sciat idem contingere, tum quando Princeps Orthodoxus liberum exercitium Haereticis permittit. Macedoniani, cùm ipsis ereptum esset exercitium à Constantio, rejecerant Arianismum, & amplexi erant Orthodoxam doctrinam, ut videre est apud Socratem lib. 4. c. 11. p. 650. At cùm Gratianus & Valentinianus Iunior postea permisissent omnibus sectis liberum exercitium, ad vomitum redeunt Macedoniani, ut videre est apud eundem lib. 5. c. 3. & apud Sozomenum lib. 7. c. 2. Itaque janua non clauditur hæresibus, quando liberum exercitium Hæreticis permittitur; sed tunc iis aperitur. Ratio evidens in Scriptura proponitur: quia doctrina eorum ut gangrena serpit 2. Tim. 2. 17. Contrà vero claditur iis janua quando non permittitur ipsis libertas seu potius licentia illa: prout patet ex allatis exemplis Arianorum & Macedonianorum; nec non etiam Aëtianorum seu Eunomianorum, quorum hæresin tempore Constantii exortam, eodem tempore pene extinctam refert Sozomenus, non quòd liberum exercitium ipsis permissum fuerit, sed quòd ademtum fuerit: ἢ δὲ ὑπ' αὐτῶν σφίσιν αἰτεῖσθαι τροπόν τινα τὸν ἐν μέρει διδοῦσθαι γενόντων, ἀλλ' ἐν λόγῳ, ἐπεὶ δὲ ὑπομείνειν εἰς τὸ φανερὸν ἐπὶ τῶν τὴν παρρησίαν ἀφαιρεῖσθαι τολμώντων: Hæresis autem excogitata ab Aëtio interea temporis quodammodo extincta fuit, propterea quòd neque Eunomius neq; alius quisquam qui loco aliquo inter Hæreticos illos esset eam publicè docere ausus fuit. Sozom. l. 6. c. 26. Eodem modo postea, ubi hæresis illa caput extollere rursus coepisset, à Theodosio M. ei janua clausa fuit, ut ibidem refert. In summâ hoc modo corrigere & reprimere velle Hæreticos est idem, ac si quis castigare mulierem adulteram vellet, permittendo ei promiscuam fornicationem. Qualiter turpem in modum olim adulteræ puniebantur Romæ, ut videre est apud Socratem lib. 5. c. 18. Hoc certè non est coërcere & januam claudere ἐπιφωνήσαι ἀλλὰ προσθήκῃ τῶν ἁμαρτιῶν correctione sed additione sive augmentatione peccati, ut Socrates de eo puniendi modo ibi loquitur. Quæ non dicuntur à me eo fine, ut taxem Principes & Magistratus eos qui quibusdam sectis hæreticis liberum exercitium coguntur permittere; sed contra hanc portentosam Arminianorum doctrinam ago, qui statuunt Hæresibus januam optimè claudi, quando liberum exercitium Hæreticis permittitur.
units.tr: 22. The gate is best closed to heresies and schism when free exercise of religion is permitted to heretics and schismatics. The Arminians do not deny this, but pass over it with dry feet and keep quite silent, storing up a vengeance which they will vent through insults, which they are about to hurl at me as punishment for the truth. So they never leave unpunished. Meanwhile let the pious and learned reader note this remarkable impudence, by which these men dare to spread this doctrine too. It arises partly from other causes, and partly from inexperience and ignorance of what happened in the ancient Church. Such ignorance is often the cause of many errors and evils, as the Church saw in Nestorius, who fell into heresy not only through pride but also through great ignorance [ὑπὸ ἀμαθείας πολλῆς], as Socrates says, through much ignorance and inexperience of the affairs of the more ancient Church. If the Arminians (who, though they have no solid learning at all, nevertheless despise all men, especially, as I said before, the living and dead Orthodox teachers, and regard as stupid, most unlearned and most inept men all who oppose their side) had read the writings of the ancients, they would surely have learned that by this reasoning the gate is by no means closed to heresies and schism when free exercise is granted to them. For the experience of the ancient Church testifies to the contrary. Constantine the Great had denied that liberty to the Arians, and then the heresy was spreading its wings. Constantius succeeded him, restored free exercise to them, and then almost the whole world saw itself become Arian and groaned. And lest anyone say that heresies grow through free exercise only when the prince is a heretic, let him know that the same happens when an orthodox prince permits free exercise to heretics. The Macedonians, when Constantius had taken the exercise away from them, had rejected Arianism and embraced orthodox doctrine, as can be seen in Socrates, book 4, ch. 11, p. 650. But when Gratian and Valentinian the Younger afterwards granted free exercise to all sects, the Macedonians returned to their vomit, as can be seen in the same author, book 5, ch. 3, and in Sozomen, book 7, ch. 2. Therefore the gate is not closed to heresies when free exercise is permitted to heretics; rather it is opened to them. The clear reason is set out in Scripture: their teaching spreads like gangrene [doctrina eorum ut gangrena serpit], 2 Tim. 2.17. On the contrary, the gate is closed to them when that liberty, or rather licence, is not granted to them, as is plain from the examples already cited of the Arians and Macedonians, and also of the Aëtians or Eunomians. Sozomen reports that their heresy arose in the time of Constantius and was almost extinguished at the same time, not because free exercise was granted to them, but because it was taken away: "The heresy devised by Aëtius was in the meantime somewhat extinguished, because neither Eunomius nor anyone else who held some position among those heretics dared to teach it publicly." [ἢ δὲ ὑπ' αὐτῶν σφίσιν αἰτεῖσθαι τροπόν τινα τὸν ἐν μέρει διδοῦσθαι γενόντων, ἀλλ' ἐν λόγῳ, ἐπεὶ δὲ ὑπομείνειν εἰς τὸ φανερὸν ἐπὶ τῶν τὴν παρρησίαν ἀφαιρεῖσθαι τολμώντων] Sozomen, book 6, ch. 26. In the same way later, when that heresy began to raise its head again, the gate was closed against it by Theodosius the Great, as Sozomen relates in the same place. In sum, to wish to correct and restrain heretics in this way is the same as if someone wanted to punish an adulterous woman by allowing her promiscuous fornication. The shameful manner in which adulteresses were once punished at Rome can be seen in Socrates, book 5, ch. 18. This is certainly not restraining, nor closing the gate: not correction but addition or augmentation of sin [οὐ διορθώσει ἀλλὰ προσθήκῃ τῶν ἁμαρτιῶν], as Socrates there says of that mode of punishment. I do not say these things with the aim of censuring princes and magistrates who are forced to permit free exercise to certain heretical sects. I am contending against this monstrous doctrine of the Arminians, who lay down that the gate is best closed to heresies when free exercise is permitted to heretics.

units.la: 23. Objeci etiam quod docent: Gravissima pericula imminere Ecclesiæ, speciatim Lutherana; quando liberum exercitium Hæreticis non permittitur. Hoc etiam non negant, sed sicco & tacito pede transeunt, & ne verbum quidem respondent.
units.tr: 23. I also objected to what they teach: Very grave dangers threaten the Church, especially the Lutheran, when free exercise is not permitted to heretics. This too they do not deny, but pass over with dry and silent feet, and do not answer even a word.

units.la: 24. Item: Hæreticos non esse noxios Reipublicæ, si in Ecclesiam Dei introducantur, imò esse salutares Reipublicæ. Respondent p. 102. 103. hanc orationem incoëtam esse, quasi scilicet Remonstrantes credant ac doceant, hæreses in Ecclesiam introduci posse, & quod multò est ineptius, tuto & sine periculo introduci posse. posse denique quod ineptissimum est omnium, hoc Reip. salutare esse, si introducantur. Et cum convitio dicunt, verba quae ego cito nec volam habere nec vestigium tam inepta orationis. Hoc tantum dicunt Remonstrantes, Reipublicae nullum periculum creari posse, si dissentientes ferant ac tolerent &c. Ita illi. Negant igitur uno verbo, se ita docere. Verum enim vero contra conscientiam suam id negant: nam Arminiani non solum doctrina sua Haereticos in Ecclesia introducunt, ut ex omnibus praecedentibus & sequentibus, imo ex omnibus Quatuor Partibus Arcanorum luce clarius meridiana patet; nec solum docent, ut modo vidimus, nihil periculi inde imminere nec saluti animarum nec Ecclesiae; item, ut ipsi hic fatentur, nihil periculi imminere ab Haereticis Reipublicae; sed etiam asserunt salutarem Reipublicae esse eorum tolerantiam, prout patet ex verbis, quae in Arcanis Par. I. lib. 2. c. 4. p. 142, 143. citavimus. Aiunt enim: Pacem & tranquillitatem si vultis vestris regnis, innocentia (ita vocant liberi exercitii potestatem Haereticis factam sine ulla corporali coercitione) praestabit &c. Docent id Regna & Respublicae, quae inter infinita sententiarum divortia incolumes durant solius innocentia beneficio. Apol. c. 24. f. 280. b. item sol. 281. 1. (olumen Rerump. & Regnorum est dissentientium tolerantia. Imo, quod clarius etiam est in Respons. ad Excerp. p. 125. ajunt: Ita profecto est, & ut hoc non notum tantum sed notissimum & persuasissimum sit D. D. Magistratibus, ex animo optant ac cupiunt Remonstrantes. NIHIL AEQUE PRODESSE POSSE AD SALUTEM Rectorum, pacem & concordiam subditorum, totiusque Reip. tranquillitatem atque incolumitatem. Et tamen audent hi homines negare se docere tolerantiam Haereticorum esse Reip. salutarem, & dicere; se hoc tantum statuere, nimirum nihil periculi Reipublicae exinde creari posse. Huc pertinet quod Vindiciarum lib. 2. c. 2. p. 73. dicunt Rerumpublicarum tranquillitati ac securitati tum maxime consuli, cum non turbatur propter ea quae in controversiam vocantur a viris doctis & pius idcirco, quod nec expresse in Scripturis eorum veritas aut necessitas decisa sit, nec per consequentiam evidentem & exceptione omni majorem ex iis deducatur: Contra tum maxime nutare regna ac Respublicas cum propter ea turbae dantur & motus existunt. Atqui secundum Arminianos Socíniani sunt homines pii & docti, qui in controversiam vocant dogmata de Trinitate quae (secundum Arminianos) nec γυμνῶς nec per evidentem consequentiam in Scriptura exstant. Sic igitur secundum Arminianos tum maxime tranquillitati ac securitati Regnorum & Rerumpublicarum, speciatim Belgio consuletur, cum Socinianismi aperta professio introducetur. Unde vides, pie & prudens Lector, ētor, quò tendant Arminiani cùm has maximas seu axiomata ista spar- gunt : nimirum eò, ut ubi maximæ illæ generales fidem apud proceres invenerint, postea eas applicare Socinianis possint, utpote quos habent pro hominibus doctis & piis, & quos dicunt in controversiam vocare dogmata quæ nec φιλῶς nec per evidentem consequentiam in Scripturâ reperiuntur. An'ne diutius oculos claudemus? Certè qui hæc non videt, manifestum facit se videre nolle, & Arminianorum blasphemæ & Socinianæ factioni aut palàm aut clanculùm favere.
units.tr: 24. Likewise: Heretics are not harmful to the commonwealth if they are introduced into the Church of God; indeed they are salutary to the commonwealth. They reply on pp. 102 and 103 that this statement is absurd, as if the Remonstrants believed and taught that heresies can be introduced into the Church, and, what is far more inept, can be introduced safely and without danger; and, what is most inept of all, that this would be salutary to the commonwealth if they were introduced. And they add with abuse words which I quickly neither want to have nor a trace of so inept a statement. The Remonstrants say only this: that no danger can be created for the commonwealth if they bear with and tolerate dissenters, etc. Thus they. They therefore deny in a word that they teach this. But they deny it against their own conscience. For the Arminians not only introduce heretics into the Church by their doctrine, as is clearer than the noonday light from all that precedes and follows, indeed from all the Four Parts of the Arcana. Nor do they only teach, as we have just seen, that no danger thence threatens either the salvation of souls or the Church. Likewise, as they themselves admit here, no danger threatens the commonwealth from heretics. They also assert that tolerance of heretics is salutary to the commonwealth, as is clear from the words which I cited in Arcana, Part I, book 2, ch. 4, pp. 142, 143. For they say: If you want peace and tranquillity in your kingdoms, innocence (so they call the power of free exercise granted to heretics without any bodily coercion) will provide it, etc. Kingdoms and commonwealths which endure unharmed amid infinite divergences of opinion do so by the benefit of innocence alone. Apology, ch. 24, f. 280 b; likewise p. 281, col. 1: The safeguard of commonwealths and kingdoms is the tolerance of dissenters. More clearly still, in the Response to the Excerpts, p. 125, they say: It is truly so, and that this is not only known but most well known and firmly believed by the lords magistrates, the Remonstrants sincerely wish and desire. NOTHING CAN CONTRIBUTE EQUALLY TO THE SALVATION of rulers, the peace and concord of subjects, and the tranquillity and safety of the whole commonwealth. And yet these men dare to deny that they teach that tolerance of heretics is salutary to the commonwealth, and to say that they only lay down that no danger can thence be created for the commonwealth. To this pertains what they say in the Vindiciae, book 2, ch. 2, p. 73: The tranquillity and security of commonwealths are then especially consulted when they are not disturbed on account of those matters which are called into controversy by learned men, and which are pious on this account, because their truth or necessity is not expressly settled in the Scriptures, nor deduced from them by evident consequence beyond all exception. On the contrary, kingdoms and commonwealths then especially totter when disputes arise and tumults are stirred up on account of these things. Yet according to the Arminians the Socinians are pious and learned men, who call into controversy doctrines of the Trinity which (according to the Arminians) are found in Scripture neither plainly [γυμνῶς] nor by evident consequence. So according to the Arminians, the tranquillity and security of kingdoms and commonwealths, and especially of Belgium, will be best served when an open profession of Socinianism is introduced. Here you see, pious and prudent reader, where the Arminians are heading when they spread these maxims or axioms: namely, that once those general maxims have found credence among the nobles, they can afterwards apply them to the Socinians, whom they regard as learned and pious men, and who, they say, call into controversy doctrines which are not found in Scripture plainly or by evident consequence. Shall we close our eyes any longer? Certainly whoever does not see this makes it plain that he is unwilling to see, and either openly or secretly favours the blasphemous and Socinian faction of the Arminians.

units.la: Cæterùm, quia dixeram falsum & impium esse, quòd docent Regna & Resp. subsistere SOLO BENEFICIO istius tolerantiæ : hoc verò nugatores hi valdè verbosè p. 103. 104. exagitant. Et in contrarium allegant sensum communem totius Belgii, quod, inquiunt, se subsistere semper credidit & adhuc credit SOLO hujus innocentiæ beneficio : Speciatim Illustrissimorum Ordinum & Procerum testimonium in id allegant, quos dicunt arma initio sumsisse contra Hispanum ob communem istam libertatem & adhuc ferre. Addunt, si hoc diceret in Italiâ Vedelius, seipsum exilio aut vivicomburio DIGNUM redderet : inde ad coccysmum suum de judicio Hæreseos & pari jure omnium sectarum relabuntur : tandem cum convitio & calumniâ indicant se saturos mei esse, & optant ac volunt ut non amplius in Belgio vivam, sed ut Genevam redeam : Hæreticidam hujusmodi Gebenna habeat atque alat, non Daventria &c. p. 104. Paucis respondeo ; Falsissimum est Orthodoxos Magistratus aut populos aut Theologos in Belgio unquam sensisse se beneficio, nedum solo tolerantiæ mutuæ, & licentiæ talis qualem Arminiani volunt subsistere aut substitisse. Nam primò tolerantia illa quam Arminiani volunt est introductio Antitrinitariorum Hæreticorum in Ecclesiam DEI. Secundò Illustrissimi Ordines arma contra Hispanum initiò nequaquam sumserunt, nec etiam num ferunt, pro libertate ac tolerantiâ omnis generis sectarum. Etenim nunquam arma tulerunt pro libertate & tolerantiâ Socinianorum. Deinde etiam non sumserunt ea pro libertate omnium sectarum quæ in futurum orituræ essent. Speciatim autem ea non sumserunt initiò neque in hunc usque diem tulerunt pro libertate sectæ Arminianæ. Non initiò ; nam Arminianorum secta tùm nondum in rerum natura erat. Quod enim Illustrissimi Ordines initiò sumserunt arma pro Religione Reformatâ id ipsos non juvat. Ipsi enim Arminiani eos Reformatos Magistratus, & populos qui tunc in Belgio arma gerebant, non semel negant fuisse suæ Religionis, & quando de Reformatis loquuntur qui sub jugo Pontificio & inquisitione Hispanicâ gemebant, ajunt, cur boc agrè ferant Doctores qui cum suis ὁμοιψύχοις hactenus, inprimis cùm sub jugo Pontificio gemerent &c. Item: videte ergò etiam atque etiam, an'non hac ratione Hispanam sive Albanam savitiam olim contra segreges ac non raro armatos cœtus VESTROS jure exercitam esse &c. In Resp. ad Excer. p. 125. 126. Unde dicunt se fuisse olim fidei nostrae confortes: Hoc unum sufficeret, inquiunt, quod in Remonstrantes fidei QUONDAM vestrae consortes &c. ib.p. 127. Ita igitur initio arma non tulerunt Ordines Illustrissimi pro Religione Arminianâ, contra Hispanum. Ex eo etiam tempore nunquam id factum. Nam tempore induciarum secta haec prodiit; ex eo tempore h. e. postquam exspirāssent induciae, Edictis publicis sublata Religio illa fuit, quae nondum sunt abrogata. Fateor Illustrissimos Ordines adversus Hispanum defendere omnes subditos suos seu incolas bonos harum Provinciarum; interim certum quoque est, eos non omnium Religionem adversus Hispanum defendere.
units.tr: Since I had said that it is false and impious to teach that kingdoms and commonwealths subsist ONLY by the benefit of that toleration, these trifling fellows rail against this at length, on pp. 103–104. To the contrary, they cite the common opinion of all Belgium, which, they say, has always believed and still believes that it subsists ONLY by the benefit of this innocence. They cite, in particular, the testimony of the most illustrious Orders and nobles, who, they say, took up arms at the start against the Spaniard for this common liberty and still bear them. They add: if Vedelius said this in Italy, he would render himself WORTHY of exile or of being burned alive. From there they slide back into their chatter about the judgment of heresy and the equal right of all sects, and at last, with insult and slander, they declare that they are sick of me, and they wish and desire that I no longer live in Belgium but return to Geneva: Gehenna may keep and nourish such a heretic-burner, not Deventer, and so on, p. 104. I answer briefly. It is most false that the orthodox magistrates, peoples or theologians in Belgium ever thought that they subsist by benefit, much less by mutual toleration and by a licence such as the Arminians want, or that they ever subsisted so. For, first, that toleration which the Arminians want is the introduction of anti-Trinitarian heretics into the Church of God. Second, the most illustrious Orders did not at the start take up arms against the Spaniard, nor do they bear them even now, for the liberty and toleration of every kind of sect. Indeed they never took up arms for the liberty and toleration of the Socinians. Moreover, they did not take them up for the liberty of all the sects that were to arise in the future. Specifically, they did not take them up at the start, nor have they borne them to this day, for the liberty of the Arminian sect. Not at the start, for the Arminian sect did not yet exist in the nature of things. That the most illustrious Orders at the start took up arms for the Reformed religion does not help them. For the Arminians themselves deny more than once that those Reformed magistrates and peoples who then bore arms in Belgium belonged to their religion; and when they speak of the Reformed who groaned under the Papist yoke and the Spanish Inquisition, they say: why do the teachers take it so hard, who with their like-minded [ὁμοιψύχοις] until now, especially when they groaned under the Papist yoke, etc. Likewise: see then, again and again, whether it was not by this reasoning that the Spanish or Alban cruelty was once rightly exercised against your separate and not seldom armed assemblies, etc., in the reply to the Excerpts, pp. 125–126. Whence they say they were once companions of our faith: this one thing would suffice, they say, that the Remonstrants were once companions of your faith, etc., ibid., p. 127. So, then, at the start the most illustrious Orders did not take up arms against the Spaniard for the Arminian religion. Nor has it been done since that time. For this sect emerged during the truce; from the time, that is, after the truce had expired, that religion was suppressed by public edicts, and those edicts have not yet been repealed. I grant that the most illustrious Orders defend against the Spaniard all their subjects, or the good inhabitants of these Provinces; yet it is also certain that they do not defend the religion of all against the Spaniard.

units.la: Quod ajunt ME DIGNUM me redditurum vivicomburio si id in Italiâ dicerem; observet Lector hanc sententiam à mitissimo illo Spiritu Arminiano, de quo tantopere gloriantur, & propter quem nolunt Hereticos ullo modo à Magistratu coërceri. Iam unusquisque judicet primò an'ne Arminiani Theologi in posterum occasionem conquerendi habeant, si in futurum aut exterae nationes aut incolae harum Provinciarum dixerint, impietatem horum Theologorum, qui ex animo blasphemiis Turcicis Socinianorum addicti sunt, dignam esse quae à Magistratu castigetur, &, si alibi ea docerent quae in Belgio docent, eos non solùm dignos judicatum iri sed etiam revera se dignos reddituros, adversum quos Magistratus etiam atque etiam vindicent gloriam filii Dei & totius Sacrosanctae Trinitatis. Quid enim dicent, exteri praesertim, si ille qui dicit quod impium sit docere, Regna & Resp. subsistere solo beneficio tolerantiae omnis generis haereticorum & sectariorum vivicomburio dignum se reddit secundùm Arminianos; item, si dignus est experiri Tyrannidem Pontificiam magno suo malo ut loquuntur Vindic. p. 130. quo igitur supplicio digni erunt ministri hi Arminiani qui non credunt Iesum Christum & Spiritum S. esse verum æternùmque Deum cum Patre, qui non credunt Iesum Christum fuisse antequam homo fieret; qui Turcicas illas blasphemias praetextu quinque articulorum introducere conantur? Non mihi sed sibi imputent violentissimi illi homines hanc consequentiam. Claudam hanc sectionē, ubi prius dixero, Arminianos, quemadmodum in Apologiā Apologia docent Hæreticos non esse noxios Ecclesiæ, nec Reip, nec salu-ti animarum, ita in genere dicere in Vindiciis nullum plane periculum esse si Hæreticis quibuscunque liberum exercitium permittatur sine ullâ plane coercitione Magistratus: Ex altera vero parte, inquiunt cap. 9. p. 183. periculum nullum est. Qui seduci vult, sibi imputet. Suo malo seducitur. Nemo invitus aut nolens seducitur.
units.tr: As to their saying that I would render MYSELF WORTHY of being burned alive if I said this in Italy: let the reader note this sentence, which comes from that most gentle Arminian spirit in which they so greatly boast, and on account of which they will not have heretics restrained in any way by the magistrate. Let everyone then judge, first, whether the Arminian theologians will not in future have occasion to complain if foreigners or inhabitants of these Provinces say that the impiety of these theologians, who from the heart are devoted to the Turkish blasphemies of the Socinians, is worthy of being punished by the magistrate, and that if they taught elsewhere what they teach in Belgium, they would not only be judged worthy but would in fact render themselves worthy; against whom the magistrate should again and again vindicate the glory of the Son of God and of the whole most holy Trinity. For what will they say, especially foreigners, if he who says that it is impious to teach that kingdoms and commonwealths subsist solely by the benefit of toleration of every kind of heretic and sectary renders himself worthy of being burned alive, according to the Arminians; likewise, if he is worthy to experience the Papist tyranny to his great harm, as they put it in the Vindiciae, p. 130? With what punishment, then, will those Arminian ministers be worthy, who do not believe that Jesus Christ and the Holy Spirit are the true and eternal God together with the Father, who do not believe that Jesus Christ existed before he became man, and who try to introduce those Turkish blasphemies under the pretext of the five articles? Let those most violent men impute this consequence not to me but to themselves. I will close this section, after first saying that the Arminians, just as in their Apology they teach that heretics are not harmful to the Church, to the Commonwealth, or to the salvation of souls, so in the Vindiciae they say in general that there is no danger at all if free exercise is permitted to any heretics whatever, without any coercion at all by the magistrate: On the other hand, they say in chapter 9, p. 183, there is no danger. Whoever wishes to be seduced, let him impute it to himself. He is seduced to his own harm. No one is seduced against his will or unwillingly.

units.la: 25. Objeceram etiam ipsis quod docent: Hæresès non solùm non noxias esse Reipublicæ, sed etiam contrà noxium & periculosum esse, eas non admittere. Item Arminianos in eum finem metum subditorum incutere Regibus & Principibus qui eas non tolerant. Et ostendi eos impiè vocare hoc columen Rerumpublicarum & Regnorum ; nec non conquestus eram de eorum Theologiâ, quæ etiam ex Turcarum Scholis & Iapanorum hausta est in hæreticorum subsidium p.143.144. Ad hæc Arminiani ne hilum quidem.
units.tr: 25. I had also objected to them what they teach: heresies are not only not harmful to the commonwealth, but on the contrary it is harmful and dangerous not to admit them. Also, that the Arminians, to that end, instil fear in subjects against kings and princes who do not tolerate them. And I showed that they impiously call this the pillar of commonwealths and kingdoms; and I also complained of their theology, which was drawn even from the schools of the Turks and the Japanese, to the aid of heretics, pp. 143–144. To these things the Arminians reply not a whit.

units.la: 26. Aliud dogma est: Si Respublica turbetur ab Hæreticis, id illis crimini dandum non esse. Hoc etiam non negant sed fatentur, & culpam omnium turbarum rejiciunt in Orthodoxos qui se Hæreticis opponunt. Ac multas nugas texunt p.105.106. contra consequentiam quam ex eo elicueram, quòd Arminiani dicunt: Hæreticis ideo crimini dandum id non esse, quando Remp. turbant, quia hoc faciunt bono & commodo eorum quos convertere volunt non secus ac medici quando corpus turbant ægri. Hinc inferebam: si hoc verum est, sequi exinde Hæreticos tanquam medicos animarum non solùm non impedendios esse ullâ coercitione seu potius ullâ resistentiâ, sed etiam laudem mereri & salaria. Hic sophisticantur illi scoprice & contumeliosè contra consequentiam illam meam quam negant & contra meam personam, & retorquent totum hoc in Vedelium si Romæ aut Mediolani esset atque in vivicomburium ipsius, denique redeunt ad coccysmum suum de pari jure Hæreticorum & Vedelii. Respondeo uno verbo: Sequi id quod dixi ex doctrinâ istorum hominum, h.e. Hæreticos laudem mereri ac salarium, hoc, inquam, sequi luce clàrius est meridiana. Unde fit ut ipsi Hæreticos summe laudent & inter alia pios, piissimos, sanctissimos homines vocent; & par jus omnium coetuum & sectarum esse doceant. Hoc sufficiat. Addo saltem eos pessimè facere, quod Hæreticos cum Medicis comparant. Etenim non errantes & Hæretici, sed Orthodoxi cum Medicis comparandi sunt, prout à Constantino M. fit in Epistolâ ad Orientales: ubi de errantibus loquens inquit: [illegible, ~40 letters] [illegible, ~40 letters]: At vero si quis medicinam pro se ipso admittere
units.tr: 26. Another doctrine is this: if the commonwealth is disturbed by heretics, this is not to be imputed to them as a crime. This too they do not deny but admit, and they throw the blame for all the disturbances upon the orthodox who oppose themselves to the heretics. And they weave many trifles, pp. 105–106, against the consequence I had drawn from it, namely that the Arminians say: heretics are not to be charged with a crime for disturbing the commonwealth, because they do this for the good and advantage of those whom they wish to convert, no differently than physicians when they disturb the body of the sick. From this I inferred: if this is true, it follows that heretics, as physicians of souls, are not only not to be hindered by any coercion, or rather by any resistance, but also deserve praise and salaries. Here those scoffers sophistry contemptuously and insultingly against that consequence of mine, which they deny, and against my person, and they turn the whole thing against Vedelius, as if he were in Rome or Milan and were to be burned alive, and at last they return to their chatter about the equal right of heretics and Vedelius. I reply in one word: that what I said follows from the doctrine of these men, that is, that heretics deserve praise and salary, this, I say, follows more clearly than the midday light. Hence it comes about that they highly praise the heretics themselves and call them, among other things, pious, most pious, most holy men, and teach that all assemblies and sects have an equal right. Let this suffice. I add at least that they act very badly in comparing heretics with physicians. For it is not the erring and the heretics but the orthodox who are to be compared with physicians, as Constantine the Great does in his Epistle to the Easterners, where, speaking of the erring, he says: [illegible] [illegible]: But if anyone is unwilling to admit the medicine for himself and to be healed, let him not impute it to another. For the medicine is set in the open and exposed to all…

units.la: Greek passage of the Epistle (Constantinus M., ad Orientales) is printed in Greek type; the lines above could not be read reliably. admittere & sanari non vult: illud alteri non imputet. Etenim medicina in aperto posita est & omnibus exposita &c. Eusebvit. Constant. l.2.c.58. Et in oratione ad Patres Nicénos discessuros, ostendens quomodo Orthodoxi se debeant gerere erga errantes, Episcopus ait: διὸ πρὸς πάντας ἁρμόττεσθαι δεῖ ἰατρὸν δίκην ἐκαίσῳ τὰ ἀνοπτικὰ πρὸς σωτηρίαν μεριζομένους: itaque decet omnium infirmitatis se adaptare & medici instar unicuique ea quae utilia sunt ad salutem suggerere. ibid. lib. 3. c. 20. Ita Constant. M. Orthodoxos Medicis comparat secundùm sacram Scripturam, ut passim videre est.
units.tr: The Greek passage of the Epistle (Constantine the Great, to the Eastern bishops) is printed in Greek type; the lines above could not be read reliably. But if anyone refuses to admit the remedy and will not be healed, let him not impute it to another. For the medicine is set out in the open and exposed to all, etc. Eusebius, Constant. l. 2. c. 58. And in his address to the Fathers of Nicaea on their departure, showing how the orthodox ought to behave toward those who err, the bishop says: διὸ πρὸς πάντας ἁρμόττεσθαι δεῖ ἰατρὸν δίκην ἐκαίσῳ τὰ ἀνοπτικὰ πρὸς σωτηρίαν μεριζομένους [therefore one must adapt oneself to all, like a physician, dispensing to each what is useful for salvation]: "so one must adapt oneself to everyone's infirmity and, like a physician, offer to each what is useful for salvation." Ibid., lib. 3, c. 20. Thus Constantine the Great compares the orthodox to physicians, in accordance with Holy Scripture, as may be seen everywhere.

units.la: Quod etiam Arminiani Haereticos ideò crimine liberant, quia intentio eorum sit ut convertant homines & ad suam fidem, quam veram & salvificam putant, adducant: id si locum habet, tùm etiam persecutores rectè faciunt & merito utuntur Tyrannide suâ adversum Orthodoxos. Hi enim ideò persequuntur Orthodoxos, ut eos in viam scilicet reducant, & ab aeterna perditione secum praestent immunes, paratiqravissima quaeque perferre & potius jacturam fortunarum & vita simul facere, quam à proposito isto desistere, ne Deo ac Domino suo displiceant, quae verba Arminianorum sunt de Haereticis loquentium, & quae adaptari merito persequutoribus Orthodoxorum experientia testatur non moderna solùm sed & vetus. Ita enim Valens Imperator ideò persequebatur Orthodoxos, quia omnes volebat traducere ad fidem suam seu doctrinam Arianam, ut Socrates de eo loquitur lib. 4. c. 6. Si excipiant Arminiani, persequi per se malum esse, quod intentione bonâ bonum fieri non possit: idem ego de Haeresi merito regeram.
units.tr: The Arminians also excuse heretics from crime on this ground: that their intention is to convert men and bring them to their own faith, which they think true and saving. If that held good, then persecutors too would be acting rightly and would be justified in using their tyranny against the orthodox. For these men persecute the orthodox in order, of course, to bring them back to the right way, and to keep themselves free from eternal perdition, being prepared to endure the most severe things and rather to suffer the loss of their goods and their lives at the same time, than to desist from that purpose, lest they displease God and their Lord. These are the words of the Arminians speaking of heretics, and experience testifies that they fit the persecutors of the orthodox deservedly, not only today but also in former times. For thus the emperor Valens persecuted the orthodox because he wished to bring all men over to his faith, that is, the Arian doctrine, as Socrates says of him, book 4, chapter 6. If the Arminians object that to persecute is in itself evil, which cannot become good by a good intention, I would deservedly return the same against heresy.

units.la: 27. Ultimum dogma hujus generis est: Haereticos veniam errorum suorum mereri apud Deum pietate suâ & quidem solâ: Item, Deum ob eam solam causam ipsis veniam datúrum: Denique eos aeternùm salvos fieri. Non negant etiam ista sed fatentur cum calumniis adversus doctrinam Orthodoxam de Praedestinatione & aliis nugis, ac speciatim commendatione affectus sui erga Haereticos & contra detestatione doctrinae nostrae quâ Haereticos detestamur ac aversamur. Quibus ego uno verbo regero, id quod Cassiodorus dicit lib. de amicitiâ p. 1257. Si male amaveris odisti, si bene oderis tunc amâsti.
units.tr: 27. The last dogma of this kind is: that heretics deserve forgiveness of their errors before God by their piety alone; likewise, that God will grant them forgiveness for that reason alone; and finally, that they will be saved eternally. They do not deny these things either, but they admit them, along with calumnies against the orthodox doctrine of predestination and other trifles, and especially with praise of their affection toward heretics and with detestation of our doctrine, by which we detest and turn away from heretics. To these things I answer in one word what Cassiodorus says in his book on friendship, p. 1257: If you have loved badly, you have hated; if you have hated well, then you have loved.

units.la: CAP. V.
units.tr: CAP. V.

units.la: Examen Capitis V. Vindic. lib. 2.
units.tr: Examination of Chapter V. Vindication, Book 2.

units.la: I. Responsio Arminianorum generatim considerata. Eam sufficientem esse ad detestationem sectæ Arminianæ perspicuè & solidè ostenditur. 2. Quæstio an Reformati an verò Arminiani fuerint causa Schismatis Belgici, uno verbo decisa? 3. Quæstio decisa an ne ex Reformatorum Theologorum sententiâ de tolerantiâ mutuâ inter Lutheranos & Reformatos sanciendâ, sequatur Synodum Dordracenam injustè tolerantiâ exclusisse Arminianos? Quæstio decisa an ne tolerantiam mutuam inire velle cum omnibus dissentientibus in non necessariis, sit Schismaticum & omnis pacis ac moderationis oiorem esse? Arminiani non negant insignem contumeliam verbo Dei à se factam. 4. Arminiani contra conscientiam suam negant, se tolerantiâ mutuâ comprehendere in Apologiâ & Confessione omnis generis Hæreticos & Sectarios. Vindicantur argumenta quatuor priora auctoris, quibus id ab eo ostensum; & probatur Arminianos contra propriam suam conscientiam ea eludere conari. 5. Quintum argumentum vindicatur ab effugiis frivolis eorum. 6. Sextum argumentum vindicatur. 7. Septimum argumentum vindicatur à protervia quâ generatim ei occurrunt. Arminiani fatentur, doctrinam Socinianorum & Anabaptistarum quâ jus gladii adimunt Magistratui non obstare quò minus communionem cum iis colant. Arminiani negant doctrinam eam, quâ tamen ipsi fatentur auctoritatem Magistratuum & totam societatem humanam everti posse, impiam esse. 8. Arminiani contra conscientiam negant se in Apologiâ docere, ex doctrinâ Evangelicorum de S. Cænâ per se fluere idololatriam. Fatentur se communionem colere velle cum iis cœtibus, ex quorum doctrinâ idololatria per se fluit. 9. Fatentur se communionem colere velle cum iis cœtibus, cum quorum doctrinâ impietas per se cohæret. Non respondent ad argumentum invictum, quo Auctor ostenderat Arminianos in Ecclesiam velle velle Hæreticos introducere. 10. Arminiani contra conscientiam suam negant, se in Apologia docere, quod communionem cum Pontificiis colere velint. Singularis protervia eorum in hac re. 11. Hypotheses aliæ octo Arminianorum, quibus stantibus non possunt Pontificios excludere communione spirituali. 12. Arminiani pro arbitrio suo metiuntur necessaria & non necessaria dogmata, prout iis usu venit. Ipsorum ambulatoria & instabilis Theologia. 13. Non diffitentur contumeliam gravissimam illatam omnibus cœtibus Christianis, adeoque etiam verœ Ecclesiæ. 14. Non negant se communionem colere cum Anabaptistis. Non negant se omnes Ecclesias quæ Pædobaptismum necessarium statuunt aut necessitate medii aut præcepti, intolerabilis Tyrannidis accusasse. 15. Arminiani non negant se communionem colere cum Antitrinitariis & eos habere pro verâ Ecclesiâ. Tribuunt Socinianis quod soli verœ Ecclesiæ competit. Iustini Martyris testimonium in eam rem. 16. Eos ratione doctrinæ omnes Hæreticos & Sectarios tolerantiâ suâ comprehendere asseritur. Eos id contra propriam conscientiam negare ostenditur. 17. Non negant se Pontificios, Lutheranos, Reformatos excludere pace Ecclesiæ & tolerantiâ suâ; quia illi omnes cœtus nolunt tolerare Hæreticos & quos pro Hæreticis habent. Non negant se illudere Orbi Christiano doctrinâ suâ de tolerantiâ: sed tantùm per contemtum id transeunt, ut & præcedens, nec ad probationes vel verbulo respondent. Non negant, se quando ad pacem Ecclesiæ requirunt animos veritatis studiosos, per veritatem intelligere etiam dogmata Hæreticis propria; speciatim Arii, Serveti, Socini, Pelagii. Causæ aperiuntur, ob quas Arminiani omnes sectas & Hæreticos ratione doctrinæ introducunt in Ecclesiam; & tamen Reformatos, Lutheranos, Pontificios eâ excludunt ob praxin eorum.
units.tr: I. The Arminians' reply considered in general. It is clearly and solidly shown that it is sufficient to detest the Arminian sect. 2. Question, whether the Reformed or rather the Arminians were the cause of the Belgic schism, settled in one word? 3. Question settled: whether, according to the opinion of the Reformed theologians on mutual toleration to be sanctioned between Lutherans and Reformed, it follows that the Synod of Dort unjustly excluded the Arminians from toleration? Question settled: whether it is schismatic, and utterly opposed to all peace and moderation, to wish to enter into mutual toleration with all who dissent in non-necessary matters? The Arminians do not deny the notable insult they have offered to the Word of God. 4. The Arminians deny, against their own conscience, that in their Apology and Confession they include every kind of heretic and sectary in their toleration. The first four arguments of the author, by which he showed this, are vindicated; and it is proved that the Arminians, against their own conscience, try to evade them. 5. The fifth argument is vindicated against their frivolous evasions. 6. The sixth argument is vindicated. 7. The seventh argument is vindicated against the shamelessness with which they generally meet it. The Arminians admit that the doctrine of the Socinians and Anabaptists, which takes from the magistrate the right of the sword, does not stand in the way of their cultivating communion with them. The Arminians deny that this doctrine, by which they themselves admit that the authority of magistrates and the whole human society can be overthrown, is impious. 8. The Arminians deny against their conscience that in their Apology they teach that idolatry flows per se from the doctrine of the Evangelicals concerning the Lord's Supper. They admit that they wish to cultivate communion with those congregations from whose doctrine idolatry flows per se. 9. They admit that they wish to cultivate communion with those congregations with whose doctrine impiety coheres per se. They do not answer the unanswerable argument by which the author had shown that the Arminians wish to introduce heretics into the Church. 10. The Arminians deny against their own conscience that in the Apology they teach that they wish to cultivate communion with the Papists. Their singular shamelessness in this matter. 11. Eight other hypotheses of the Arminians, on the assumption of which they cannot exclude the Papists from spiritual communion. 12. The Arminians measure necessary and non-necessary doctrines by their own judgment, as it suits them. Their shifting and unstable theology. 13. They do not deny the most grievous insult offered to all Christian congregations, and so also to the true Church. 14. They do not deny that they cultivate communion with the Anabaptists. They do not deny that they have accused of intolerable tyranny all Churches which hold infant baptism necessary, either by necessity of means or by precept. 15. The Arminians do not deny that they cultivate communion with the Antitrinitarians and regard them as a true Church. They attribute to the Socinians what belongs only to the true Church. Justin Martyr's testimony on this point. 16. It is asserted that by reason of doctrine they include all heretics and sectaries in their toleration. It is shown that they deny this against their own conscience. 17. They do not deny that they exclude the Papists, Lutherans and Reformed from the peace of the Church and from their toleration, because all those congregations are unwilling to tolerate heretics, and those whom they hold to be heretics. They do not deny that they mock the Christian world with their doctrine of toleration; they merely pass this over with contempt, as they did the previous point, and do not answer the proofs even with a word. They do not deny that when they require for the peace of the Church minds eager for the truth, by truth they mean even the doctrines proper to heretics, especially those of Arius, Servetus, Socinus and Pelagius. The causes are laid open for which the Arminians introduce all sects and heretics into the Church by reason of doctrine, and yet exclude the Reformed, the Lutherans and the Papists by reason of their practice.

units.la: 1. Quæ capite quinto lib 2. objeceram Arminianis, ad hæc tria capita redeunt: Primò, Tolerantiam mutuam quam inde ab initio usque ad hoc tempus urserunt & urgent Arminiani esse nihil aliud, quàm communionē spiritualē & fraternitatem, seu introductionem & admissionem sionem in Ecclesiam Dei omnis generis Hæreticorum & sectariorum, modò illi vicissim velint tolerare Arminianos & alias quascunque sectas; speciatim esse communionem cum Anabaptistis. Secundo loco, Arminianos urgere communionem spiritualem præcipuè cum Antitrinitariis, & eos communionem spiritualem cum iis colere. Tertiò : Arminianos excludere ex tolerantia illa mutua sua quam hactenus tantopere vendiârint, Pontificios, Lutheranos, Reformatos, idque ideò quia hi cœtus nolunt communionem colere cum omnis generis Hæreticis & sectariis. Unde ostendi Arminianos toti orbi illudere tolerantia illa sua. Hic quomodo respondent boni illi viri ad has tres gravissimas accusationes? Diffundunt saltem se copiosissima & nugacissima responsione ad primum, quà quatuordecim paginas implent; & negant se docere tolerantiam talem quæ sit communio cum sectariis & Hæreticis omnis generis. Secundum non negant, nec etiam tertium. Hæc duo posteriora sufficientem causam præbent, propter quam unusquisque pius, sapiens, & honestus vir detestari debet Theologos Arminianos, utpote qui, quemadmodum manifestè docent in Apologia sua, se communionem colere cum Antitrinitariorum execranda secta adeoque participare ipsorum blasphemiis, ita illud sibi à me objectum & luculentissimè probatum negare non audent: rursus, cum hactenus inde ab initio in hunc usque diem indesinenter crepuerint coram Illustrissimis Ordinibus & toto mundo tolerantiam mutuam ac restitutionem pacis Ecclesiæ, ac sublationem dissidiorum & Schismatum totius Orbis; tamen excludunt ab eâ non solùm Pontificios, non solùm Reformatos, sed etiam Lutheranos (quibus hactenus turpiter illuserunt) ideò quòd cum omnis generis sectariis & Hæreticis, speciatim cum Antitrinitariis, communionem spiritualem colere nolint: & sic ex tolerantia illa & pace Ecclesiæ excludunt totum Orbem Christianum (nam nec Græci volunt colere communionem cum omnis generis sectariis & Hæreticis) qui Deum in tribus personis adorat, includunt autem tantùm blasphematores Antitrinitarios, & illos qui ex Anabaptistis voluerint. Ob hanc causam non valdè opus esset, ut ulterius laborarem in Examine istius capitis, & probatione primi membri, quod contra conscientiam suam eos negare jam jam patebit: sufficiunt enim ad detestandam omni jure sectam istam duo posteriora quæ negare non audent, imò contra quæ ne hiscere quidem possunt. Tamen, ne Arminiani ansam arripiant cavillandi, præcipuè autem in gratiam pii Lectoris qui forte etiam in eâ parte sibi distinctè satissatisfactum volet, breviter ex instituti ratione ea quoq; examinabimus.
units.tr: 1. The objections which I raised against the Arminians in the fifth chapter of the second book come down to these three heads. First, that the mutual toleration which the Arminians have pressed from the beginning until now, and still press, is nothing other than spiritual communion and fraternity, or the introduction and admission into the Church of God of every kind of heretic and sectary, provided they in turn are willing to tolerate the Arminians and any other sects whatever; and in particular that it is communion with the Anabaptists. Second, that the Arminians press spiritual communion chiefly with the Antitrinitarians, and that they cultivate spiritual communion with them. Third, that the Arminians, by their mutual toleration, which they have so greatly vaunted until now, exclude the Papists, Lutherans and Reformed, and this because these congregations are unwilling to cultivate communion with every kind of heretic and sectary. Hence I showed that the Arminians mock the whole world with their toleration. How do those good men respond to these three very grave accusations? They at least pour out a most copious and most trifling answer to the first, with which they fill fourteen pages; and they deny that they teach a toleration which is communion with sectaries and heretics of every kind. The second they do not deny, nor the third either. These two latter points provide a sufficient cause why every pious, wise and honest man ought to detest the Arminian theologians, since, as they plainly teach in their Apology, they cultivate communion with the execrable sect of the Antitrinitarians, and so share in their blasphemies. Nor do they dare to deny that this was objected to them by me and most clearly proved. Again, although from the beginning until this day they have unceasingly clamoured before the Illustrious Orders and the whole world about mutual toleration, the restoration of the peace of the Church, and the removal of the quarrels and schisms of the whole world, yet they exclude from it not only the Papists and the Reformed, but also the Lutherans (with whom they have hitherto shamefully trifled), for the reason that they are unwilling to cultivate spiritual communion with every kind of sectary and heretic, especially with the Antitrinitarians. And so from that toleration and peace of the Church they exclude the whole Christian world (for not even the Greeks wish to cultivate communion with every kind of sectary and heretic), who worship God in three persons, and they include only the blaspheming Antitrinitarians and those who have come out of the Anabaptists. For this reason there would be little need for me to labour further in the examination of this chapter and in proving the first point, which they will soon be seen to deny against their own conscience. For the two latter points, which they do not dare to deny, or rather against which they cannot even open their mouths, suffice to detest this sect by every right. Nevertheless, lest the Arminians seize an occasion for quibbling, and especially for the sake of the pious reader who perhaps also wishes to be fully satisfied on that part, I will briefly examine these points too, in keeping with the plan of this work.

units.la: 2. Antequam ad rem, seu negationem dogmatis primi veniant, multas nænias, sophismata, mendacia, contexunt. Initio p. 108. inquiunt: In hoc capite Vedelius se declarat hostem mutuæ tolerantiæ, & imprudentissimo dicam an impudentissimo suorum schismati, unde tot mala, proh dolor, enata vidit Belgium nostrum atque ingenuit, patrocinium suum commodat, moderationis ac pacis omnis osor. Postea, cum convitiis in me conjectis, negant se auctores esse schismatis in Belgio nati. Uno verbo respondeo; quòd Arminiani me hostem vocant mutuæ tolerantiæ, & moderationis ac pacis omnis osorem; faciunt contra propriam suam conscientiam. Nam mox p. 109. & sæpius in hoc libro fatentur me cupere & optare tolerantiam mutuam cum Lutheranis & à Lutheranis incundam: Etsi profitear me juxta cum omnibus non solùm personis sed & cœtibus qui Deum in tribus personis adorant, esse hostem tolerantiæ mutuæ, & osorum pacis ac moderationis qualem Arminiani docent. Illâ enim non solùm impietatem suam palàm faciunt, sed etiam ostendunt se toti orbi præcipuè autem Illustrissimis Ordinibus & Proceribus Reip. illusisse. Quorum utrumque ex animo cum omnibus bonis qui Deum in tribus personis adorant, detestor; & quod infuturum posteritas omnis quæ Antitrinitariorum blasphemiis adversatur, detestabitur, quamdiu memoria erit sectæ Arminianæ.
units.tr: 2. Before they come to the matter itself, or to the denial of the first point, they weave together many trifles, sophistries and lies. At the beginning, on page 108, they say: In this chapter Vedelius declares himself an enemy of mutual toleration, and, I may say most imprudently, or most shamelessly, he lends his patronage to the schism of his own people, from which, alas, so many evils have sprung up and grown in our Belgium, a hater of all moderation and peace. Afterwards, with insults thrown at me, they deny that they are the authors of the schism that arose in Belgium. I answer in one word: that the Arminians call me an enemy of mutual toleration and a hater of all moderation and peace, they do against their own conscience. For soon afterwards, on page 109, and often in this book, they admit that I desire and wish for mutual toleration with the Lutherans, and that it be entered into by the Lutherans; although I profess that, together with all who worship God in three persons, I am an enemy of mutual toleration not only of persons but also of congregations, and a hater of peace and moderation such as the Arminians teach. For by that they not only openly show their impiety, but also show that they have mocked the whole world, and especially the Illustrious Orders and the Nobles of the Republic. I detest both of these from my heart, together with all good men who worship God in three persons; and this every posterity that opposes the blasphemies of the Antitrinitarians will detest in future, as long as the memory of the Arminian sect endures.

units.la: Quòd causam schismatis quod in Belgio antehac fuit à se in Reformatos cū convitiò impudentiâ rejiciunt; næ faciunt pro solitâ suâ impudentiâ. Quid enim impudentius, quid injustius, quid insolentius, quàm quòd hi homines conqueri audent Reformatos Belgas schismatis auctores esse eo quòd cū illi dogmata nostris Ecclesiis incognita & inusitata spargerent, se nostris Ecclesiis invitis obtruderent, & à fautoribus suis obtruderētur, populi eos audire noluerint sed in horreis, navibus, hortis convenire, aut in longe dissita loca excurrere, ut solitâ sibi doctrinâ pascerentur, maluerint (hic enim prætextus est quo nixi schismatis accusant Reformatos Belgas) quàm ab istis hominibus doceri qui quales sint totus Orbis jam videt nimirùm Socinianos Hæreticos, qui prætextu quinque articulorum blasphemias illas Turcicas adversus filium Dei & totam S. Trinitate introducere conantur. Quâ in re quàm rectè, piè, sanctè fecerint Belgæ nostri, res ipsa jâ docet. Quo enim in loco forent Ecclesiæ Belgicæ hodie, si isti homines suscepti à populis fuissent? Certè omnia jam perstreperent impunè blasphemiis illis, & Socinianismus omnia repleret. Alia jam non allego, quæ manifestissimum faciant, initium turbarum, & malorum omnium seriem ab his simulatoribus Antitrinitariis profectam esse. Melius novi improbitatem ipsorum, quàm ipsi, cum contemtu mei, petulantissimè hoc loco p. 108. dicunt.
units.tr: That they reject the cause of the schism which existed in Belgium some time ago, and lay it with abuse upon the Reformed, is shameless of them, and in keeping with their usual shamelessness. For what could be more shameless, more unjust, or more insolent than that these men dare to complain that the Belgian Reformed are the authors of the schism, because when those men spread doctrines unknown and unusual in our Churches, and pressed them upon our Churches against their will, and when their supporters pressed them upon the people, the people refused to hear them and preferred to gather in barns, ships and gardens, or to make their way to places far off, so that they might be fed on the teaching to which they were accustomed? (For this is the pretext on which the accusers of the Belgian Reformed of schism rest their case.) Rather than be taught by such men, whom the whole world now sees for what they are, namely Socinian heretics, who under the pretext of the five articles try to introduce those Turkish blasphemies against the Son of God and the whole Holy Trinity. How rightly, piously and holily our Belgians acted in this matter, the event itself now shows. For where would the Belgian Churches be today, if those men had been received by the peoples? Certainly everything would by now be resounding with those blasphemies with impunity, and Socinianism would fill everything. I do not now cite other things which make plain that the beginning of the troubles, and the whole chain of evils, came from these pretended Antitrinitarians. I know their wickedness better than they do, though they, with contempt for me, say so most impudently in this place on p. 108.

units.la: Dico autem Schisma hoc antehac fuisse. Nam jam in Belgio quæstio de Schismate penitus est sublata; ac nullum amplius Schisma in Ecclesiis Belgicis est. Quæstio quippe nunc est, an'ne tolerandi sint Hæretici Antitrinitarii, qui se Remonstrantium nomine tegunt, & Orthodoxam doctrinam de Trinitate simulant, nec non Libertinismum eum qui in doctrinâ est palàm profitentur, in eum præcipuè finem ut aperte blasphemias Antitrinitariorum, quas profiteri nondum audent introducant, atque liberè docere possint? quemadmodum luce clarius meridianâ ostendi Par. II. Arcanorum.
units.tr: I say, however, that this schism existed some time ago. For now in Belgium the question of schism has been entirely removed, and there is no longer any schism in the Belgian Churches. The question now is whether heretical Antitrinitarians should be tolerated, who hide behind the name of Remonstrants and pretend to the orthodox doctrine of the Trinity, and openly profess that Libertinism which is in their teaching, chiefly with the aim that they may introduce the blasphemies of the Antitrinitarians, which they do not yet dare to profess openly, and be able to teach freely? This I have shown, clearer than the midday light, in Part II of the Arcana.

units.la: 3. Porrò ostenderam p. 149. unam eandemq; mentem ac sententiam Arminianorum ministrorum de tolerantiâ mutuâ semper & inde ab initio in hunc usque diem fuisse. Hoc illi non negant, sed fatentur p. 108. & addunt se in hac mente & sententiâ etiamnum persistere, & laetos & alacres esse, quod ea de causa tot gravia ac dura perpessi sunt. Quæ verba diligenter observentur ob usum quem habent, utpote exquibus apparet veracausa, propter quam ipsi Arminiani fatentur se Ecclesias Reformatas & Proceres Reip. sibi tantopere adversarios habuisse & habere, exilium, carceres, privationem officiorum subierint. Fatentur enim hic expresse factum istud ob doctrinam eorum de mutuâ tolerantiâ, quâ tolerantiâ Antitrinitarios præcipuè complectuntur, & in Ecclesiam introducere volunt. Id quod clarius etiam fatentur in Præfat. Apol. f. u. 1. b. & ü. 2. a. quemadmodum ostendi Par. III. lib. 2. c. 5.
units.tr: 3. Furthermore, I had shown on p. 149 that the one and the same mind and opinion of the Arminian ministers concerning mutual toleration has always existed, and from the beginning until this day. They do not deny this, but confess it on p. 108, and add that they still persist in this mind and opinion, and are glad and eager, because for this reason they have suffered so many grievous and hard things. These words should be carefully noted for the use they have, since from them it appears what the true cause is, for which the Arminians themselves confess that they have had, and still have, the Reformed Churches and the civil magistrates as such great adversaries, and that they have undergone exile, prison, and deprivation of office. For here they expressly confess that this happened because of their doctrine of mutual toleration, by which toleration they chiefly embrace the Antitrinitarians and wish to introduce them into the Church. They confess this even more clearly in the Preface to the Apology, ff. u. 1 b and ü. 2 a, as I have shown in Part III, book 2, chapter 5.

units.la: Speciatim autem fatentur, quod ipsis objeceram, se intelligere voce Tolerantiæ non nudam aut solam tolerantiam externam, quâ, pacis civilis & societatis humanæ conservandæ causâ, Hæreses & sectæ diversæ in Rep. seu Politiâ feruntur, prout hic in Belgio fit; sed tolerantiam illam, & communionem seu unionem Ecclesiasticam, fraternitatem ac concordiam spiritualem: p. 110. Remonstrantes, inquiunt, per mutuam tolerantiam intelligere non tantum civilem seu externam quandam tolerantiam, sed Ecclesiasticam & fraternam amorem & unionem certissimum est. Hoc fatentur, quod etiam observandum. Negant autem se per eam intelligere communionem talem quâ Hæretici ipsius Ecclesiæ membra fiunt. Quod ultimum antequam examinemus, quædam mendacia & sophismata eorum quæ p. 109. 110. afferunt runt indicanda & diluenda paucis sunt. Primò ajunt, me ubivis non obscurè cupere exterminatam è Belgio tolerantiam civilem & externam sectarum quarundam; item ajunt Genevensem Ecclesiam & Clarissimum Bogermannum ita sentire.p. 109. Sed hæc mera calumnia est. Nam Genevensis Ecclesiæ, & mea,& omnium Orthodoxorum Theologorum sententia est, quam Par. I. Arcan. non semel, speciatim lib. 2. c. 4. p. 143. exposui, nimirùm ubi constitutionibus fundamentalibus Reip. alicuius Haretici ipsi nedum ii errantes qui Haretici non sunt, in eâ tolerantur; fidem datam omninò servandam esse: Credidit hactenus, dicebam, Ecclesia ex verbo Dei, per Sapientiam æternam & sic veritatem Dei ac sinceram pietatem regnare Reges, & per observationem constitutionum fundamentalium, quæ etiam quandoque seu in certis Regnis & Rebuspublicis jubent certas aliquando sectas tolerari, & iis fidem datam servari. Melius didicimus tùm ex verbo Dei tùm ex experientiâ & Praxi veteris Ecclesiæ quousque Hæreticorum coercitio sese extendat, quàm hi homines, qui ægrè ferunt quod Antitrinitarii non tolerantur in his Provinciis nos docere possunt. Sed de eâ re h. e. tolerantiâ externâ Hæreticorum & aliorum errantium ex professo volente Deo agemus in Parte Tertiâ operis nostri de prudenti à Veteris Ecclesiæ.
units.tr: In particular, they confess what I had charged them with: that by the word toleration they understand not a bare or merely external toleration, by which for the sake of keeping civil peace and human society, diverse heresies and sects are borne in the commonwealth or polity, as happens here in Belgium; but that toleration and ecclesiastical communion or union, spiritual brotherhood and concord (p. 110). The Remonstrants, they say, understand by mutual toleration not merely a certain civil or external toleration, but ecclesiastical and brotherly love and union. This they confess, which is also to be noted. But they deny that by it they understand such communion by which heretics become members of the Church itself. Before we examine this last point, some of their lies and sophisms which they bring forward on pp. 109 and 110 must be pointed out and briefly refuted. First, they say that I everywhere openly desire the civil and external toleration of certain sects to be banished from Belgium; they also say that the Genevan Church and the most distinguished Bogerman think so (p. 109). But this is pure calumny. For it is the opinion of the Genevan Church, and of me, and of all orthodox theologians, which I set out in Part I of the Arcana more than once, especially in book 2, chapter 4, p. 143, namely: where, by the fundamental constitutions of some commonwealth, heretics, and not only those who err but are not heretics, are tolerated in it, faith given must in every way be kept.
