I said: Until now the Church has believed, from the Word of God, through eternal Wisdom, and thus through the truth of God and sincere piety, that kings reign; and through the observance of fundamental constitutions, which also sometimes, in certain kingdoms and commonwealths, command that certain sects be tolerated at times, and that faith be kept with them. We have learned better, both from the Word of God and from the experience and practice of the ancient Church, how far the restraint of heretics extends, than these men, who take it ill that Antitrinitarians are not tolerated in these provinces, can teach us. But concerning this matter, that is, the external toleration of heretics and other erring persons, we shall treat professedly, God willing, in the Third Part of our work, on the prudent practice of the Ancient Church.

units.la: Deinde, quia dixeram Arminianos non intelligere tolerantiam talem qualem Reformati Theologi docent instituendam esse inter Reformatos & Lutheranos, qui cum in fundamentalibus dogmatis & necessariis etiam Controversiis conveniant, in aliis tamen dissident: id exagitant Arminiani, & dicunt me mihi contradicere, hanc enim esse tertiam illam tolerantiam quam damnem & respuam. Sed hoc falsum est; nam tertia illa tolerantia quam damno & rejicio est tolerantia Hæreticorum, & communio spiritualis cum iis. At tolerantia mutua Reformatorum & Lutheranorum est tolerantia non Hæreticorum, sed pax & tolerantia veræ Ecclesiæ, cujus cœtus in fundamentalibus dogmatibus conveniunt, etsi in aliis dissideant, adeóque fraternitas & communio Spiritualis omnium membrorum interse. ô utinam nobis illam pacem tandem post dissidium illud tàm cruentum videre liceat ἐν ἀγάπῃ καὶ ἀληθείᾳ in dilectione & veritate! absque quâ tolerantiâ & pace sit, actum est denuò de Evangelio in Germaniâ. Neque enim Deus semper nobis Regem ex ultimo Septentrione evocabit, & illius (sed quanti Herois!) inæstimabili sanguine discordiam nostram corriget.
units.tr: Next, because I had said that the Arminians do not understand such toleration as the Reformed theologians teach should be established between the Reformed and the Lutherans, who, though they agree in the fundamental doctrines and in the necessary controversies, nevertheless differ in other matters, the Arminians attack this and say that I contradict myself, for this is that third toleration which I condemn and reject. But this is false; for that third toleration which I condemn and reject is toleration of heretics and spiritual communion with them. But the mutual toleration of the Reformed and the Lutherans is not toleration of heretics, but the peace and toleration of the true Church, whose assemblies agree in the fundamental doctrines, although they differ in other things, and so there is brotherhood and spiritual communion of all the members among themselves. Oh, that we might at last be allowed to see that peace after that schism which was so bloody, in love and truth [ἐν ἀγάπῃ καὶ ἀληθείᾳ]! Without that toleration and peace, the Gospel in Germany is undone once more. For God will not always summon for us a king from the far North, who with his (but how great a hero!) priceless blood will correct our discord.

units.la: Tertiò, ex eo quod de tolerantiâ mutuâ Reformatorum & Lutheranorum dixi, volunt inferre, sequi exinde Synodum Dordracenam damnandam esse, quæ Remonstrantes tolerare recusavit, eos functionibus suis privavit ob nullam allam causam, inquit p. 110. quàm quòd ab eâ dissen-tirent in dogmate de praedestinatione aut quinque articulano, in quo Lutherani non minus quam Remonstrantes à vobis dissident, quodque inter non fundamentalia tu hîc aperte collocas. Respondeo, hoc nequaquam sequi. Primò enim, posito sed non concessō, Arminianis ob solam doctrinam suam de Quinque articulis negatam esse tolerantiam; tamen non sequitur Synodum injustè fecisse. Nam, ut jam non dicam ipsum Lutherum non cum Arminianis sed nobiscum sentire, fatentibus Arminianis lib. 2. Vindic. c. 2. p. 78. ubi dicunt Anabaptistas quosdam (Calvini de Praedestinatione & Lutheri de Servo arbitrio doctrinā addictos; item, non omnes Lutheranos cum Arminianis sentire de Quinque articulis illis, denique, longè graviores errores in istis controversiis ab Arminianis admitti quos Lutherani nequaquā habent; praeter haec, inquam omnia, alia ratio est propter quam, si maximè in fundamento non errarent Arminiani quoad articulos illos, sed per omnia convenirent in iis cum Lutheranis, tolerantia mutua merito ipsis à Synodo Dordracenâ negata est. Etenim verbum Dei praescribit, ut tolerentur non omnes errantes, etiam in non fundamentalibus, sed errantes tantùm infirmi Rom. 14. capite per totum & cap. 15. 1. 2. 3. 5. 6. 7. Infirmi autem errantes sunt qui ex Ecclesiâ falsâ aut coetu alio infidelium, ut Ethnicorum prodierunt, & ex gravissimo morbo prodeuntes, ex densissimis errorum & ignorantiae tenebris emergentes, adhuc aliquid erroris reliquum habent, non secus ac qui ex longo & gravissimo morbo convaluerunt, diu adhuc mali reliquias aliquas, ac speciatim languorem circumferunt. Verum hoc esse patet, tùm ex eo quòd Apostolus non errorum sed infirmitatis voce utitur, tùm ex eo quòd infirmos eos vocat qui ex Iudaeis seu falsâ Ecclesiâ ad Christum conversi, ciborum & dierum distinctionem Iudaeis observatam adhuc retinendam putabant. Tales infirmi sunt Lutherani, utpote qui ex Papatu prodierunt; tales etiam nos Reformati (loquor ex hypothesi Lutheranorum qui nos pro errantibus habent) censeri debemus à Lutheranis. Etenim Reformatae Ecclesiae speciatim Genevensis ut & Ecclesiae Helveticae ex Papatu diu satis ante Calvinum prodierunt. Alia autem ratio est Arminianorum; hi enim non sunt infirmi errantes; utpote qui non prodierunt ex Ecclesiâ falsâ, sed ex Ecclesiâ quam ipsi, cùm doctrinae mutationem suscipe-rent, pro verâ habuerunt; atque etiamnum interdum, ubi id causae suae expedire putant, pro verâ habent; prout in his ipsis Vindiciis faciunt in quibus, quemadmodum coetus nostros pro Haereticis habent quando ip-sis lufis lubet, ita interdum, ubi necessitatem causæ suæ id postulare putant, eam pro verâ habent, dum dicunt eam veros Martyres produxisse, qui à Pontificiis è medio sublati sunt. Veri autem Martyres non nisi in verâ Ecclesiâ esse possunt. Hinc eo nomine notantur à Synodo in sententiâ contra ipsos latâ p. 276. At verò quia nonnulli è nobis egressi sub Remonstan-tium titulo &c. Non igitur sunt errantes infirmi : idque eò minus quia his hominibus nihil insolentius, nihil superbius est, ut vel ex eò patet, quòd ipsius veteris & totius Ecclesiæ Christianæ antiquæ & modernæ suffragium ac judicium contra Antitrinitarios latum floccifaciunt; & qui tantâ opinione sui inflati sunt, ut se solos & Socinianos apertos peritos & accuratos rerum æstimatores habeant; omnes eos qui se ipsis oppo-nunt pro indoctissimis, stupidissimis, ineptissimis hominibus traducant, qui denique in omnibus cœtibus & sectis inveniunt articulum aliquem fundamentalem negari ab iis cœtibus, exceptis sectis Antitrinitariorum. In summâ, his suis execrandis dogmatis, quæ tùm à Cll. D. D. Proff. Leydd. aliisque ante hac, tùm in Arcanis exhibita sunt, palàm faciunt, se nec infirmos esse, nec unquam fuisse. Atque hanc distinctionem eò minus rejicere possunt Arminiani, quia ipsi eâ ratione distinguunt inter errantes & quidem (quod magis est) in fundamento; dum cum illis qui in tenebris nati & educati sunt mitius agendum, & moderatione summâ erga eos utendum in disciplinâ Ecclesiastica contendunt quàm cum illis qui in medià luce veritatis nati & educati sunt, ut videre est Vindic.lib.2. c. 8. p. 156. Hoc unum est.
units.tr: Thirdly, from what I said about the mutual toleration of the Reformed and the Lutherans, they want to infer that the Synod of Dort must be condemned, since it refused to tolerate the Remonstrants and deprived them of their functions for no other cause, as he says on p. 110, than that they dissented from it on the doctrine of predestination or the five articles, in which the Lutherans no less than the Remonstrants dissent from you, and which you here openly place among the non-fundamentals. I answer that this by no means follows. First, granting for argument's sake (but not conceding) that toleration was denied the Arminians solely because of their doctrine of the Five Articles, it still does not follow that the Synod acted unjustly. For, to say nothing of Luther himself agreeing not with the Arminians but with us, as the Arminians admit in Vindiciae, book 2, ch. 2, p. 78, where they say that certain Anabaptists were addicted to Calvin's doctrine of predestination and Luther's doctrine of the bondage of the will; likewise that not all Lutherans agree with the Arminians on those five articles; and finally that the Arminians admit far graver errors in those controversies which the Lutherans by no means hold. Besides all these things, I say, there is another reason why mutual toleration was rightly denied them by the Synod of Dort, even if the Arminians did not err in the fundamentals concerning those articles but agreed with the Lutherans in every respect. For the Word of God prescribes that not all who err are to be tolerated, even in non-fundamentals, but only the weak who err: Rom. 14 throughout, and ch. 15 vv. 1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 7. The weak who err are those who have come out of a false Church or some other assembly of unbelievers, such as the Gentiles, and who, emerging from a grave sickness and from the thickest darkness of error and ignorance, still have some remnant of error, just as those who have recovered from a long and serious illness still carry some traces of the disease and above all a lingering weakness. That this is so is clear both from the fact that the Apostle uses the word not of errors but of weakness, and from the fact that he calls weak those who, converted to Christ from the Jews or from a false Church, still thought the distinction of foods and days observed by the Jews ought to be retained. Such weak people are the Lutherans, since they came out of Papacy; and such we Reformed must be considered by the Lutherans (I speak on the hypothesis of the Lutherans, who regard us as erring). For the Reformed Churches, especially the Genevan and also the Helvetic, came out of Papacy quite a long time before Calvin. The case of the Arminians is different. For these are not weak errants, since they did not come out of a false Church but out of a Church which they, when they took up the change of doctrine, held to be true; and even now, where they think it serves their cause, they sometimes still hold it to be true. They do so in these very Vindiciae, in which, just as they regard our assemblies as heretical whenever it pleases them, so sometimes, where they think the necessity of their cause demands it, they hold them to be true, saying that they produced true Martyrs who were removed from the midst by the Papists. True martyrs, however, can exist only in a true Church. Hence they are marked on this account by the Synod in the sentence pronounced against them, p. 276: But since some of us have gone out under the title of Remonstrants, etc. They are therefore not weak errants; and this all the less because nothing is more insolent or proud than these men. This is clear even from the fact that they make light of the vote and judgment of the whole Christian Church, ancient and modern, against the Antitrinitarians; and they are so puffed up with their own opinion that they consider themselves alone, and the open Socinians, to be the skilled and accurate judges of things, and they malign all who oppose them as the most unlearned, most stupid and most inept of men. Finally, they find in every assembly and sect that some fundamental article is denied by those assemblies, except the sects of the Antitrinitarians. In sum, by their execrable dogmas, which have been set forth both by the distinguished Professors of Leiden and others before now, and in the Arcana, they make it plain that they are neither weak nor have ever been. The Arminians can the less reject this distinction because they themselves distinguish in this way between errants, and indeed (what is more) in fundamentals. While they contend that one must act more gently towards those who were born and brought up in darkness, and use the greatest moderation towards them in church discipline, than towards those who were born and brought up in the middle light of the truth, as may be seen in Vindiciae, book 2, ch. 8, p. 156. This is the one point.

units.la: Secundò, falsum est, Arminianos tantùm ob ea dogmata tolerantiâ indignos judicatos. Nam primò ipsi, ut paulò antè diximus, fatentur se tot gravia passos propter doctrinam suam de mutuâ tolerātiâ, ac speciatim ob communionem cum Antitrinitariis. Deinde expressè Synodus eos ideò notat, & tolerantiâ excludit in sententiâ contrâ ipsos latâ, quòd non solùm errores noxios & veteres revocarunt, sed etiam NOVOS PROCUDERUNT, publicè & privatim, voce ac scriptis in vulgus sparse-runt, & acerrimè propugnârunt.
units.tr: Secondly, it is false that the Arminians were judged unworthy of toleration only on account of those doctrines. For, first, they themselves, as we said a little above, confess that they have suffered so many grave things on account of their doctrine of mutual toleration, and especially on account of their communion with the Antitrinitarians. Then the Synod expressly marks them for this and excludes them from toleration in the sentence pronounced against them, because they not only revived old and harmful errors but brought forth NEW ONES, spread them abroad among the people publicly and privately, by voice and by writings, and defended them most fiercely.

units.la: Tertiò, tolerantiâ exclusit Synodus p. 279. 280. 281. 282. 283. eos qui Geysteranorum fratrum dogmata probant de Trinitate, de attributis Dei, de animæ statu post hanc vitam, de Resurrectione, de officio Magistratus, de veteri Testamento, de Iustificatione, de perfectione hominis in hac vitâ, de Baptismo infantium, de Peccato Originali : quæ quidem dogmata Arminiani se fovisse initio turbarum illarum manife-stum stum fecerunt in Confessione, Apologiâ, Responsione ad Excerpta, & Vindiciis suis. Denique, non tantum propter doctrinam, sed etiam propter actiones improbas & turbulentas à Synodo condemnati sunt, his verbis: At quia nonnulli è nobis egressi sub titulo Remonstrantium studiis & consiliis privatis, modis illegitimis, disciplinâ & ordine Ecclesiæ violato, atque fratrum suorum monitionibus & iudiciis contemtis. Belgicas Ecclesias antea florentissimas, in fide & charitate coniunctissimas, his doctrinâ capitibus graviter & periculosè admodum turbârunt &c. doctrinam hactenus in Ecclesiis receptam, calumniis & contumeliis enormibus insectati, nec modum nec finem fecerunt: scandalis, dissi-diiss, conscientiarum scrupulis & exagitationibus omnia passim compleverunt; quæ certè gravia in fidem, in charitatem, in bonos mores, in Ecclesiæ unitatem & pacem peccata sunt &c. Quas ob causas primò Synodus pradictis citatis omni Ecclesiastico munere interdicit, &c. Ex his omnibus manifestum est, ex tolerantiâ mutuâ inter Lutheranos & Reformatos sanciendâ nequaquam sequi, Synodum Dordracenam injustè fecisse quòd Arminianos Theologos tolerandos non esse judicavit. Et sic concidunt etiam, ut hoc obiter dicam, quæ Arminiani super hac re tùm in aliis scriptis tùm inRespons. ad Excerp. p. 139. 140. 141. nugantur occasione tolerantiæ mutuæ inter Lutheranos & Reformatos sanciendæ,
units.tr: Thirdly, the Synod, on pp. 279 to 283, excluded from toleration those who approve the doctrines of the Geyster brethren concerning the Trinity, the attributes of God, the state of the soul after this life, the Resurrection, the office of the magistrate, the Old Testament, justification, the perfection of man in this life, the baptism of infants, and original sin. The Arminians made it manifest that they had fostered these very doctrines at the beginning of those troubles, in their Confession, their Apology, their Response to the Excerpts and their Vindiciae. Finally, they were condemned by the Synod not only on account of doctrine but also on account of wicked and turbulent actions, in these words: But since some of us have gone out under the title of Remonstrants, by private studies and counsels, by illegitimate methods, with the discipline and order of the Church violated and the admonitions and judgments of their brethren despised, have gravely and most dangerously disturbed the Belgic Churches, formerly most flourishing and most closely joined in faith and charity, with these heads of doctrine, etc.; attacking the doctrine hitherto received in the Churches with enormous calumnies and insults, they have made no measure or end; they have filled everything everywhere with scandals, divisions, scruples of conscience and agitations; which are certainly grave sins against the faith, against charity, against good morals, and against the unity and peace of the Church, etc. For these causes the Synod first forbids the aforesaid persons every ecclesiastical office, etc. From all these things it is manifest that from the establishing of mutual toleration between Lutherans and Reformed it by no means follows that the Synod of Dort acted unjustly in judging that the Arminian theologians were not to be tolerated. And so, to say this in passing, fall also the trifles which the Arminians babble on this matter, both in other writings and in the Response to the Excerpts, pp. 139 to 141, on the occasion of the establishing of mutual toleration between Lutherans and Reformed.

units.la: Quod addunt Arminiani p. 110. Me si negem tolerantiæ locum esse cùm in necessariis omnibus dogmatibus convenit, dignum esse qui Schismaticus vocer in superlativo gradu, & pacis omnis osor atque hostis; ea vero contumelia non in me sed in Scripturam sacram resilit, quæ docet non quosvis errantes sed tantum infirmos tolerandos esse: quales infirmi non sunt omnes qui negant dogmata non necessaria ad salutem; ut ex dictis patet. Cui accedit, si semel hæc porta aperiatur, nimirùm tolerandos esse omnes eos qui errant in non Necessariis dogmatis, innovationum in præjudicium veritatis divinæ nullum finem fore, contrà quàm Deus præcipit, qui non vult ut veritas ipsius etiam in non necessariis ad salutem, ab eo nobis in verbo revelata, oppugnetur. Denique exinde fiet ut homines libidine & pruritu novandi laborantes, ipsa etiam necessaria ad salutem oppugnent, & tolerari se & alios qui ea negant velint; idque prætextu eo, quòd ista dogmata quæ pro necessariis habentur, reverà necessaria non sint. Prout docent nos exemplo suo hi homines, qui, ut apertam professionem blasphemiarum Socinianarum introducant, dogmata de Trinitate opposita Antitrinitariis non habent pro Necessariis, & multis argumentis evincere volunt, ea non esse Necessaria. Præterea etiam prout ipsorum causæ conducere videtur; quidvis necessarium aut non necessarium pro arbitrio faciunt; & quod heri pro non necessario habent, hodie pro Necessario venditant, ac contrà.
units.tr: As for what the Arminians add on p. 110: if I deny that there is room for toleration where there is agreement in all necessary doctrines, I deserve to be called a Schismatic in the superlative degree, and an enemy and hater of all peace. But that insult recoils not on me but on Holy Scripture, which teaches that not just any errants but only the weak are to be tolerated; and those who deny doctrines not necessary to salvation are not all weak, as is clear from what has been said. To which is added this: if once this door is opened, namely that all who err in non-necessary doctrines are to be tolerated, there will be no end to innovations to the prejudice of divine truth, contrary to what God commands, who does not wish his truth, revealed to us by him in the Word, to be attacked even in matters not necessary to salvation. Finally, from this it will come about that men labouring under lust and itch for novelty will attack even the things necessary to salvation, and will want to be tolerated, they and others who deny them, under the pretext that the doctrines held to be necessary are in truth not necessary. These men teach us this by their own example: in order to introduce an open profession of Socinian blasphemies, they do not regard the doctrines of the Trinity opposed by the Antitrinitarians as necessary, and they want to prove by many arguments that they are not necessary. Moreover, as their cause seems to suit them, they make whatever they please necessary or not necessary at will; and what they held yesterday to be not necessary, they peddle today as necessary, and vice versa.

units.la: Observetur etiam me objecisse ipsis, quod unionem & concordiam veram ac perfectam Christianam, quam hactenus tota Ecclesia judicavit consistere in consensione veræ doctrinæ, Philip. 2. 2. & alibi, illi atroci contumelia in verbum Dei vocant carnalem & spuriam pacem. Hanc contumeliam verbo Dei à se factam & judicio totius Ecclesiæ secundùm verbum Dei pronunciato, illi non negant, sed sicco pede transeunt.
units.tr: It should also be noted that I objected to them that they call the true and perfect Christian union and concord, which the whole Church has hitherto judged to consist in agreement in sound doctrine (Philip. 2. 2, and elsewhere), by the outrageous insult of carnal and spurious peace in the Word of God. They do not deny that this insult to the Word of God, and to the judgment of the whole Church pronounced according to the Word of God, was made by them, but they pass over it dry-shod.

units.la: 4. Nunc pergamus & videamus, quomodo ad rem ipsam responde-ant? Negant igitur suam mutuam tolerantiam esse communionem, quà Hæretici ipsius Ecclesiæ membra fiant, seu introductionem omnis generis Hæreticorum & sectariorum in Ecclesiam Dei. Sciebam eos non confessuros, ut etiam maturè monueram Par. I. lib. 1. cap. 1. sed, ut accusare, ita nec negare sufficit. Ad probationes rei attendendum est, quam ego septem argumentis luce clariorem feceram. Ostenderam enim eos comprehendere tolerantiâ suâ mutuâ omnes eos cœtus qui in non Necessariis errant, h.e. in non controversis dogmatis, seu, ut interdum loquuntur, cum quorum opinionibus nulla superstitio, nulla idololatria, nulla impietas, nulla profanitas cohæret. Ubi voces impietatis, superstitionis, idololatriæ, profanitatis monueram, non sumi ab iis, prout voces illæ communiter à Christianâ Ecclesiâ sumuntur, quæ non solùm dogmata impia &c. vocat Iudæorum, Turcarum, Atheorum, sed etiam quædam quæ opponuntur controversis inter Christianos dogmatibus quibusdam veris. v. g. dogmata Antitrinitariorum &c. sed Arminianos voces eas sumere longè aliter, nimirum pro impietate, superstitione, idololatriâ &c. quæ extra omnem controversiam talis est &c. id quod septem argumentis docueram.
units.tr: 4. Let us now proceed and see how they answer the matter itself. They deny, therefore, that their mutual tolerance is a communion by which heretics become members of the Church itself, or an introduction of every kind of heretic and sectarian into the Church of God. I knew they would not confess this, as I had warned early on in Par. I. lib. 1. cap. 1. But as it is enough to accuse, so it is not enough to deny. We must attend to the proofs of the matter, which I had made clearer than light with seven arguments. For I had shown that by their mutual tolerance they embrace all those assemblies which err in non-necessary matters, that is, in non-controverted doctrines, or, as they sometimes put it, with whose opinions no superstition, no idolatry, no impiety, no profanity coheres. Where I had warned that the words impietatis, superstitionis, idololatriae, profanitatis are not taken by them as the Christian Church commonly takes those words, which calls not only the impious doctrines of Jews, Turks and atheists by these names, but also certain doctrines opposed to some true doctrines controverted among Christians, e.g. the doctrines of the Antitrinitarians etc.; but that the Arminians take those words quite differently, namely for impiety, superstition, idolatry etc., which is such outside all controversy etc. This I had shown by seven arguments.

units.la: Respondent illi primò p. 110 in genere falsum esse, ut dixi, se docere tolerantiam talem quæ sit communio spiritualis cum Hæreticis; & adjunt id ex præcedentibus sole clarius liquere; deinde patere id ex meâ Confessione, quia dixerim Reformatos, Lutheranos, Pontificios prout illi se hodie habent, excludi ab ipsis ex illâ tolerantiâ; item quia dixerim Arminianos velle discriminari certâ tesserâ à cæteris omnibus sectis.
units.tr: They reply first, at p. 110, that it is in general false, as I said, that they teach such tolerance as is spiritual communion with heretics. They add that this is clearer than the sun from what precedes; then that it is evident from my Confession, because I said that the Reformed, Lutherans, Papists, as they now stand, are excluded by them from that tolerance; likewise because I said that the Arminians wish to be distinguished by a certain badge from all other sects.

units.la: Verùm enimverò salsissimum est, patere id ex præcedentibus. Ex quibus enim? imò contrarium patet ex præcedente ipsorum doctrinâ, & speciatim, ne Lectoris recordationem fatigem, ex immediatè præcedente doctrinâ eorum de naturâ & laudibus Hæreseos. Reformatos, LutheLutheranos, Pontificios excludunt in Apologia sua ex tolerantia, non ob dogmata, sed ob praxin, ut infra ostendam. Et quamvis certa tesserâ distingui velint à caeteris sectis, tamen ea tessera separari nolunt ab ipsis, sed non obstante ea volút cum iis communionem colere; imò istius ipsius tessera praetextu & commendatione, (quae est dissentientes omnes ferre atque amplecti &c. ut loquuntur Apolog. Exam. Cenf. Praef. f. 19. a. b.) volunt homines allicere omnes tanquam vexillo erecto ut hic p. 113. loquuntur ad quod accurrant caeterae sectae. Haec est generalis eorum responsio.
units.tr: But truly it is most absurd that this is evident from what precedes. From what, pray? Rather the contrary is evident from their immediately preceding doctrine, and especially, not to weary the reader's memory, from their immediately preceding doctrine on the nature and praises of heresy. In their Apology they exclude the Reformed, Lutherans and Papists from tolerance, not on account of doctrines but on account of practice, as I will show below. And although they want to be distinguished from other sects by a certain badge, nevertheless they are unwilling to be separated from them by that badge; notwithstanding it, they wish to cultivate communion with them. Indeed, under the pretext and commendation of this very badge (which is to bear with and embrace all dissenters etc., as they speak in Apolog. Exam. Cens. Praef. f. 19 a. b.) they want to attract all men as to a raised banner, as they speak here at p. 113, to which the other sects may run. This is their general reply.

units.la: Ad argumenta mea septem, quibus ostendi p. 154. 155. 156. 157. 158. 159. 160. 161. eorum tolerantiam mutuam esse introductionem omnis generis Haereticorum & sectariorum in Ecclesiam Dei, quorum prima quatuor p. 155. 156. petita sunt ex doctrina eorum de Necessariis, non necessariis, de dogmatis controversis, & coetibus impuris, cujus doctrinae vi profecto omnis generis Haereticos & sectarios introducut in Ecclesiam, utpote qui errant tantum in controversis, adeoque non necessariis, & sic non sunt Ecclesia falsa sed coetus tantum impuri: Haec omnia quatuor argumenta eludere p. 111. 112. improbitate sua & impudentia inhonestissima illa conantur, qua aliquot alia jam dogmata negarunt, dicendo, se nunquam docuisse, nulla dogmata controversa esse necessaria ad salutem. Verum enim vero eos contra conscientiam propriam, atque omnis timoris Dei & pudoris coram Deo & hominibus oblitos id negare, supra luce clarius meridiana à nobis est ostensum.
units.tr: As for my seven arguments, by which I showed at pp. 154, 155, 156, 157, 158, 159, 160, 161 that their mutual tolerance is the introduction of every kind of heretic and sectarian into the Church of God, the first four of which, at pp. 155 and 156, are drawn from their doctrine of necessary and non-necessary matters, of controverted doctrines and impure assemblies, by the force of which doctrine they certainly introduce every kind of heretic and sectarian into the Church, since they err only in controverted, and hence non-necessary, matters, and so are not a false Church but merely an impure assembly: they try, at pp. 111 and 112, to evade all these four arguments with their dishonest and most shameless impudence, just as they have denied several other doctrines already, by saying that they never taught that no controverted doctrines are necessary to salvation. But that they deny this against their own conscience, and forgetting all fear of God and shame before God and men, has been shown by us clearer than the noonday light.

units.la: 5. Quintum meum argumentum p. 157. est ex eo petitum; quia hanc suam tolerantiam volunt esse gloriam sua secta & tesseram quâ ab omnibus aliis sectis discernitur. Atqui si voces illas acciperent in hac materia ea ratione qua diximus accipi communiter ab Ecclesia Christiana, tum ipsorum tolerantia non posset esse tessera qua ab omnibus aliis sectis discernerentur. Nam hoc omnibus sectis commune est, quae omnes profitentur se nolle communionem colere cum iis sectis quae in controversis dogmatis impietatem, superstitionem, profanitatem, idololatriam sentiunt. Hic, quia nesciunt hi homines (quorum tota Theologia nihil aliud quàm quoad rem impietas, quoad modum agendi impostura sophistica est) quid contra solidissimum etiam hoc argumentum afferre queant; respondent primò me affirmativam eorum sententiam in negativam commutare; non esse suam sententiam hanc negativam: Nolle se communionem colere cum sectis illis quae in controversis dogmatis impietatem, superstitionem, profanitatem, idololatriam sentiunt: sed hanc affirmativam; se velle commucommunionem colere cum omnibus sectis in controversis dogmatis à se dissentientibus quibus impietas, superstitio, profanitas, idololatria (quibus addunt p. 111, 112. etiam Tyrannidem) non adhærent. Sed quis non videt eos quia se constrictos sentiunt, illudere orbi velle hac responsione? Primò enim, mihi perinde est sive affirmativè sive negativè enuncient sententiam suam, modò res maneat. Deinde quis puer nescit hasce enunciationes æquipollere, nimirùm affirmativam hanc: Velle communionem colere cum omnibus sectis cum quarum doctrina impietas &c. non cohæret; Et negativam hanc: Nolle communionem colere cum sectis iis, cum quarum doctrina impietas &c. cohæret? Denique, falsum est, me eorum affirmativam in negativam commutásse. Etenim ipsi Arminiani eam enunciationem negativam formárunt, non minùs quàm affirmativam illam. Ita enim Apol. Exam. Præf. f. 19.a.b. Hæc est gloria societatis eorum, hac tessera discriminari gaudent à cæteris omnibus sectis &c. hic limes, hic terminus eorum est: Neminem pium (quales intelleximus capite præcedente esse Hæreticos) à se excludere, NEC PROFANUM admittere. Item: Neminem sic à se dissentientem aut fugiunt aut fugant, si modo piè in Christo & pacificè cum ipsis vivere velit. Solos impios, profanos, mundanos &c. PROCUL A SE ABESSE JUBENT. Hoc erat prius ipsorum responsum.
units.tr: 5. My fifth argument, at p. 157, is drawn from this: that they want this their tolerance to be the glory of their sect and the badge by which it is distinguished from all other sects. But if they took those words in this matter in the sense in which we said the Christian Church commonly takes them, their tolerance could not be a badge by which they were distinguished from all other sects. For this is common to all sects, all of which profess that they are unwilling to cultivate communion with those sects which they judge to hold impiety, superstition, profanity or idolatry in controverted doctrines. Here, since these men (whose whole theology is nothing but impiety in substance and sophistical trickery in method) do not know what they can bring against even this most solid argument, they answer first that I have changed their affirmative statement into a negative one, and that this negative is not their opinion: They are unwilling to cultivate communion with those sects which judge impiety, superstition, profanity, idolatry in controverted doctrines; but this affirmative: they wish to cultivate communion with all sects dissenting from them in controverted doctrines, to which impiety, superstition, profanity or idolatry (to which they add at pp. 111 and 112 also tyranny) do not cling. But who does not see that, feeling themselves hemmed in, they want to mock the world with this answer? For first, it makes no difference to me whether they state their opinion affirmatively or negatively, provided the matter remains the same. Then what boy does not know that these statements are equivalent, namely this affirmative: to wish to cultivate communion with all sects with whose doctrine impiety etc. does not cohere; and this negative: not to wish to cultivate communion with those sects with whose doctrine impiety etc. does cohere? Finally, it is false that I changed their affirmative into a negative. For the Arminians themselves formulated that negative statement no less than the affirmative. For so in Apol. Exam. Praef. f. 19 a. b.: This is the glory of their society; by this badge they rejoice to be distinguished from all other sects etc.; this is their boundary, this is their limit: not to exclude from themselves any pious person (such as we understood in the preceding chapter to be heretics), NOR TO ADMIT ANY PROFANE PERSON. Likewise: They neither flee from nor put to flight anyone who dissents from them, if only he wishes to live piously in Christ and peacefully with them. They ORDER only the impious, profane, worldly etc. to KEEP FAR FROM THEMSELVES. This was their first answer.

units.la: Secundò respondent: Nullum sectam esse, quæ hanc mutuam tolerantiam tesseram suam faciat; & dicunt hoc ex experientiâ constare. Respondeo uno verbo: Agnosco nullam sectam esse quæ hanc tesseram suam faciat eo sensu quo Arminiani eam tolerantiam faciunt tesseram suam, ac voces impietatis, profanitatis, idololatriæ accipiunt: interim constat Reformatos, Lutheranos, Pontificios, Socinianos, omnes denique sectas Christiani nominis perpetuò declarare se communionem velle colere cum omnibus Christianis qui non habent doctrinam, impiam, idololatricam. Quòd autem communionem cum aliis sectis non colunt, id ex eo proficiscitur, quia, quando ad hypothesin venitur, vel in aliis sectis impietatem, idololatriam deprehendunt, quæ causa est propter quam Lutherani & Reformati non possunt communione colere cum Antitrinitariis apertis & occultis, item cum Pontificiis; vel ab aliquo cœtu ad tolerantiam non admittuntur, illius cœtus non, autem suâ culpâ; quæ quidem causa est propter quam Lutherani hactenus à Reformatis oblatam sibi tolerantiam mutuam rejecerint.
units.tr: Secondly they answer that there is no sect which makes this mutual tolerance its badge, and they say this is established by experience. I answer in one word: I acknowledge that no sect makes this its badge in the sense in which the Arminians make their tolerance their badge and take the words impiety, profanity and idolatry. Meanwhile it is established that the Reformed, Lutherans, Papists, Socinians, indeed all sects of the Christian name, constantly declare that they wish to cultivate communion with all Christians who do not hold an impious or idolatrous doctrine. But that they do not cultivate communion with other sects arises from this: when it comes to the case, they either detect impiety or idolatry in the other sects, which is the reason why Lutherans and Reformed cannot cultivate communion with open and secret Antitrinitarians, and likewise with Papists; or they are not admitted to tolerance by some assembly, the fault being that assembly's and not their own. And this indeed is the reason why the Lutherans have hitherto rejected the mutual tolerance offered to them by the Reformed.

units.la: 6. Sextum meum argumentum est: Quia Arminiani profitentur se totius Ecclesiæ & orbis Christiani Schismata curare velle, & pacem inter omnes seElas Christiani nominis erigere, ut à nobis Parte I. ostensum. Hoc autem de se polliceri nequaquam possunt, si voces illas in hac materia acciperent, cum Ecclesiâ Christianâ; & omnes sectas tolerantiâ suâ non comprehenderent. Nam nullus coetus Christianus est, in quo non, aut secundùm esse aut secundùm dici sive accusationem & opinionem aliorum coetuum, sit vel impietas, vel profanitas, vel idololatria, vel superstitio, sub quibus Arminiani etiam Tyrannidem se comprehendere dicunt. Et ipsi Arminiani, dicebam, omnes alios coetus in quibusdam articulis impietatis accusant. Respondent illi ita, ut veteratorie ac fraudulenter omittant, ac non exprimant in propositione argumenti mei illud in quo vis argumenti mei praecipuè consistit; nimirum Arminianos profiteri se velle curare totius orbis Christiani dissidia. Quod si verum est, certè non possunt non tolerantiâ suâ comprehendere omnes sectas Christiani nominis, & aliter vocem impietatis &c. sumere, quàm communis Ecclesiæ usus obtinet.
units.tr: 6. My sixth argument is this: the Arminians profess that they wish to take care of the schisms of the whole Church and of the Christian world, and to establish peace among all the sects of the Christian name, as was shown by us in Part I. But they cannot make this promise about themselves if they understand those words in this matter as referring to the Christian Church, and if their toleration does not embrace all sects. For there is no Christian congregation in which there is not, either in fact or in the accusation and opinion of other congregations, impiety, profanity, idolatry or superstition, and the Arminians say that tyranny is also included under these. The Arminians themselves, as I said, accuse all other congregations of impiety in certain articles. They answer in a crafty and fraudulent way, omitting and not stating in the wording of my argument the very point on which its main force rests: namely, that the Arminians profess they wish to take care of the discords of the whole Christian world. But if that is true, they certainly cannot avoid including all sects of the Christian name within their toleration, and they must take the word impiety and so on in a sense other than that which common usage in the Church gives it.

units.la: Dicunt autem primò se non omnibus sectis tribuere impietatem; esse enim coetus quosdam & publicos quidem in foederato Belgio & reliquo orbe Christiano, in quorum doctrin a nullum ipsorum vitiorum locum habet, & quibus cum communio posset colisi per ipsos liceret. Deinde dicunt me mihi contradicere, dum dico, nullum esse coetum Christiani nominis in quo non, aut secundùm esse aut secundùm dici seu opinionem aliorum coetuum, sit vel impietas vel profanitas &c. & tamen dico, Reformatos profiteri se communionem nolle colere cum iis coetibus, in quibus impietas &c. non est. hoc enim esse tantundem dicere ac communionem velle colere cum omnibus simul ac nullis coetibus. p. 114.
units.tr: First, they say that they do not attribute impiety to all sects. For there are certain public congregations in the united Netherlands and the rest of the Christian world in whose doctrine none of these vices has any place, and with which they would be allowed to hold communion, if this were permitted. Next, they say that I contradict myself, since I say there is no congregation of the Christian name in which there is not, either in fact or in the opinion of other congregations, impiety, profanity and so on, and yet I say that the Reformed profess they are unwilling to hold communion with those congregations in which there is no impiety and so on. For to say this is just the same as saying that they wish to hold communion with all congregations and with none at once. p. 114.

units.la: Respondeo ad prius: quos coetus publicos in Belgio & alibi intelligant, quibus cum communionem colere velint si modò per ipsos liceat, facilè est intelligere: nimirùm Anabaptistas qui sine impedimento Magistratus conventicula sua habent, nec non Lutheranos coetus qui exercitium publicum in Belgio habent. Quod si ita est, certè falsum dicunt, dum ajunt se in Lutheranis coetibus nullum istorum vitiorum reperire. Nam accusant ipsos non minus ac Reformatos & Pontificios Tyrannidis ob doctrinam eorum de coercitione Haereticorum, speciatim Antitrinitariorum. Accusant etiam eos per consequens impietatis: nam doctrinam de coercendis Haereticis impietatem vocant: Remonstrantes non dubitant palàm profiteri se Eeclesias istas OMNES, qua innoxiè errantium (quales ipsis sunt Antitrinitarii) hominum sive Haereticorum quos vocant PERSECUTIONES (ita vocant in Apologiâ qualemcunque coercitionem nem corporalem Hæreticorum) & eadem aut probant aut non improbant, inter eas censere quæ IMPIETATEM propagare dici possunt, neque Christiano homini licitum esse cum ipsis communionem colere. Animus Christianus purus esse debet à piorum & errantium hominum persecutione, cæde ac sanguine. Nec sufficit ut purus sit animus. Contradicendum est tàm malo ac noxio dogmati. Qui non contradicit, qui non reclamat, qui tacet, qui dissimulat, reus est innoxii sanguinis, & affinis eidem culpæ. Respond. ad Excerp. p. 26. Et quod magis est, vocant illud opus Diabolicum: Addunt enim: Quare quàm diu Doctores hi non aperte hoc Diabolicum opus damnabunt, censebuntur à Remonstrantibus impietatem propagare. Ob hanc causam etiam ut Par.I lib. 2. cap. 5. ostendi, profitentur se tolerantiâ suâ non comprehendere Lutheranos; sed eos, cum omnibus illis qui Hæreticorum, speciatim Antitrinitariorum coërcitionem urgent, damnant & execrantur. Tertiò tribuunt etiam Lutheranis, quod cùm eorum doctrinâ cohæreat idololatria, & denique quarto loco superstitio, ut vidimus libro præcedente cap. 4. eos judicare de Evangelicorum omnium doctrinâ circa communionem corporis & sanguinis Christi, & jam jam ulterius videbimus. Hæc quatuor vitia reperiunt Arminiani in Lutheranorum cœtibus. Quâ conscientiâ igitur dicunt, se nullum eorum vitiorum in iis Ecclesiis reperire, item se velle communionem cum iis colere? Unde jam facile videre est, quid sibi velint, quando hîc ajunt se paratos esse cum Lutheranis communionem colere, modò per ipsos liceat: nimirùm inter alia, si Lutherani renuncient dogmati suo de coërcitione Hæreticorum, speciatim Antitrinitariorum, & hos tolerare velint, atque cum istis Hæreticis communionem colere; ut ex dictis patet, & iis quæ amplè expositimus circa finem allegati capitis 5. Par. I. lib. 2. Falsum autem est, quod dicunt stare saltem per Lutheranos, quod communionem non colant cum ipsis. Nam præcipuè stat apud ipsos Arminianos, quorum secta tot impiis & execrandis dogmatis plena est, ut Lutherani (quibus quidem ea dogmata cognita sunt) in æternum non sint cum ipsis communionem & tolerantiam mutuam inituri. Et profectò, si Reges & Principes qui ante hac ipsos in ditiones suas invitârant, maturè perspectam habuissent fidem & Religionem hujus sectæ; certè nunquam eos invitaturi fuissent in suas terras. De Anabaptistis jam jam videbimus.
units.tr: As to the first point: it is easy to understand which public congregations in Belgium and elsewhere they mean, congregations with which they wish to hold communion if only this were permitted: namely the Anabaptists, who have their conventicles without hindrance from the magistrate, and also the Lutheran congregations which have public worship in Belgium. If that is so, they certainly speak falsely when they say that they find none of these vices in the Lutheran congregations. For they accuse the Lutherans no less than the Reformed and the Papists of tyranny, on account of their doctrine about the coercion of heretics, especially Antitrinitarians. They also accuse them, consequently, of impiety, for they call the doctrine of coercing heretics impiety. The Remonstrants do not hesitate to profess openly that they regard ALL these Churches, which either approve or do not disapprove of the PERSECUTIONS of harmlessly erring men (such as the Antitrinitarians are to them), or of heretics, as they call them (in their Apology they call by this name any sort of bodily coercion of heretics), as among those things which can be said to propagate IMPIETY, and that it is not lawful for a Christian man to hold communion with them. The Christian mind ought to be pure from the persecution, slaughter and blood of pious and erring men. Nor is it enough that the mind be pure: one must contradict so evil and hurtful a dogma. Whoever does not contradict it, does not protest, keeps silent or dissembles, is guilty of innocent blood and an accomplice in the same fault. Respond. ad Excerp. p. 26. And what is more, they call it a DIABOLICAL WORK, for they add: "Wherefore, as long as these teachers do not openly condemn this diabolical work, they will be judged by the Remonstrants to propagate impiety." For this reason also, as I showed in Part I, book 2, chapter 5, they profess that they do not include the Lutherans in their toleration, but condemn and execrate them along with all who insist on the coercion of heretics, especially Antitrinitarians. Thirdly, they also attribute to the Lutherans that idolatry coheres with their doctrine, and lastly, in the fourth place, superstition, as we saw in the preceding book, chapter 4, namely that they judge the doctrine of all Evangelicals concerning communion in the body and blood of Christ; and we shall see this further, presently. The Arminians find these four vices in the Lutheran congregations. With what conscience, then, do they say that they find none of those vices in those Churches, and likewise that they wish to hold communion with them? Hence it is now easy to see what they mean when they here say that they are ready to hold communion with the Lutherans, provided it is permitted: namely, among other things, if the Lutherans renounce their dogma about the coercion of heretics, especially Antitrinitarians, and are willing to tolerate them and hold communion with those heretics, as is plain from what has been said, and from what we have set out at length near the end of the cited chapter 5, Part I, book 2. But it is false that they say it is the Lutherans' fault that they do not hold communion with them. For the chief fault lies with the Arminians themselves, whose sect is so full of impious and execrable dogmas that the Lutherans (to whom those dogmas are indeed known) will never in eternity enter into communion and mutual toleration with them. And truly, if the kings and princes who formerly invited them into their dominions had thoroughly known the faith and religion of this sect, they would certainly never have invited them into their lands. We shall see about the Anabaptists presently.

units.la: Ad posterius, nimirum contradictionem quod attinet, quam mihi impingere volunt, sophisticè ludunt: tum enim foret contradictio, si dixissem Reformatos absolutè & simpliciter paratos esse communionem colere cum omnibus sectis & coetibus, sive impietatem &c. doceant aut non doceant. item si dixissem, impietatem &c. reperiri in omnibus coetibus vel secundum esse, vel secundum dici omnium aliorum coetuum, vel Reformatorum coetuum.
units.tr: As to the second point, namely the contradiction which they wish to fasten on me, they play sophistically. For there would be a contradiction if I had said that the Reformed are absolutely and simply ready to hold communion with all sects and congregations, whether they teach impiety and so on or not; or if I had said that impiety and so on is found in all congregations, either in fact or in the opinion of all other congregations, or of the Reformed congregations.

units.la: 7. Septimum argumentum meum ex inductione petitum est, & tale: quia Arminiani expresse profitentur se communionem colere libenter velle cum ejusmodi sectis, cum quarum doctrina impietatem, idololatriam, superstitionem cohaerere dicunt; nimirum cum Anabaptistis & Socinianis, cum Lutheranis ac Reformatis, denique cum Pontificiis; quibus coetibus, doctrinae respectu, impietatem, superstitionem, idololatriam tribuunt: id quod sigillatim probavi ex propria eorum confessione.
units.tr: 7. My seventh argument is drawn from induction, and is this: the Arminians expressly profess that they are gladly willing to hold communion with sects of such a kind, with whose doctrine they say impiety, idolatry and superstition cohere: namely with the Anabaptists and Socinians, with the Lutherans and the Reformed, and finally with the Papists. To these congregations, with respect to doctrine, they attribute impiety, superstition and idolatry, which I have proved particularly from their own confession.

units.la: Respondent illi primo in genere, id falsum esse: hoc enim esse ex eodem ore calidum simul & frigidum efflare. Contrarium, inquiunt p. 114. tribusti paulo ante Remonstrantibus, & recte. Nam verba eorum cutasti, quibus aperte profitentur, se communionem colere non posse cum iis, quorum doctrina superstitio, idololatria, aut impietas adhaeret. Qua fronte itaque hic asseris directe contrarium? Quid protervius his hominibus esse potest, qui audent mihi contradictionem in ea re objicere, cum in conscientia sua norint, me, quod hoc loco dico Arminianos profiteri se communionem colere velle cum iis quorum doctrinae impietas &c. non adhaeret, ideo dicere, ut ostenda eos aliter sumere voces impietatis superstitionis &c. quam communiter ab Ecclesia usurpantur? & id quidem probare ex eo, quia alioquin profitentur se communionem velle colere cum iis sectis cum quarum doctrina impietas &c. cohaeret. Argumentum enim a me allatum ita procedit: Qui profitentur se communionem colere nolle cum sectis quarum doctrina impia &c. est; & tamen ex altera parte profitentur se velle communionem colere cum sectis, quarum doctrina impia est &c. illi, nisi sibi ipsis contradicant, aliter atque aliter sumunt voces impietatis &c. quam ea ab Ecclesia communiter usurpantur. At Arminiani. Ergo &c. Potestne optime Lector, aliquid fraudulentius esse his hominibus, quibus sufficit ut quidvis dicant, modo simplicioribus & imperitioribus imponere possint & fucum facere? Si hi homines vere crederent Deum in coelis esse qui videt omnes actiones hominum & corda eorum scrutatur, certe non ita in negocio Religionis versarentur.
units.tr: They answer first, in general, that this is false: "For this is to blow hot and cold out of the same mouth. The contrary," they say, p. 114, "you attributed a little earlier to the Remonstrants, and rightly. For you have cut off their words, by which they openly profess that they cannot hold communion with those whose doctrine adheres to superstition, idolatry or impiety." With what brazenness, then, do you here assert the direct contrary? What can be more shameless than these men, who dare to object a contradiction to me in this matter, when they know in their own conscience that I, when I say here that the Arminians profess they wish to hold communion with those whose doctrine does not adhere to impiety and so on, therefore say, as I have shown, that they take the words impiety, superstition and so on otherwise than they are commonly used by the Church? And I proved this from the fact that otherwise they profess they wish to hold communion with sects to whose doctrine impiety and so on cohere. For my argument proceeds thus: those who profess that they are unwilling to hold communion with sects whose doctrine is impious and so on, and yet on the other side profess that they wish to hold communion with sects whose doctrine is impious and so on, unless they contradict themselves, take the words impiety and so on otherwise than the Church commonly uses them. But the Arminians do this. Therefore and so on. Can anything, best reader, be more fraudulent than these men, for whom it is enough to say whatever they like, provided they can impose upon the simpler and less experienced and deceive them? If these men truly believed that God is in heaven, who sees all the actions of men and searches their hearts, they would certainly not behave in this way in a matter of religion.

units.la: Post hanc impudentiam, in specie respondent ad inductionem a me allatam. Dixeram: Anabaptistarum & Socinianorum doctrina de jure gladii, qua statuunt non licere Magistratui capitali poena seu sanguinis guinis effusione uti, impia est; utpote quæ auctoritatem Magistratus in nihilum redigit, & apta est toti societati humanæ adeoque ipsi Ecclesiæ evertendæ, quod ipsi Arminiani negare non possunt. Etenim dicunt ipsi de istâ doctrinâ: Actum est de auctoritate publicâ, de salute subditorum, ubi jus necis eripitur Magistratibus. Pauci scurra evertenda toti humana societati sufficerent. Atque hoc, etsi ficfe habere credant Remonftrantes &c. tamen eos libenter tolerare parati sunt, dummodo secus sentientes non damnent ut intolerabiles. Apol. c. 12. f. 141. a.
units.tr: After this impudence, they respond in particular to the instance I had cited. I had said: the doctrine of the Anabaptists and Socinians on the right of the sword, by which they hold that the magistrate may not use capital punishment or the shedding of blood, is impious, since it reduces the authority of the magistrate to nothing and is apt to overturn all human society and therefore the Church itself, which the Arminians themselves cannot deny. For they themselves say of this doctrine: Public authority is at an end, and the safety of subjects, where the right of life and death is taken from the magistrates. A few scoundrels would suffice to overturn the whole human society. And although the Remonstrants believe this to be false &c., they are nevertheless ready to tolerate those holding it, provided they do not condemn those who think otherwise as intolerable. Apology, ch. 12, p. 141a.

units.la: Respondent Arminiani ita ut fateantur fe dixisse fe communionem colere cum iis sectis paratos esse; negant tamen tùm minorem, tum consequentiam majoris. Quoad minorem: negant doctrinam illam Socinianorum & Anabaptistarum impiam esse. Observet pius Lector, me ita æquum erga Arminianos fuisse, ut antehac dixerim cap. allegato Arcan. p. 157. eos non solum alias sectas sed etiam Socinianos alicubi impietatis accusare. Quâ in re quod ad Socinianos attinet, respiciebam ad hunc locum Apologiæ, in quo de doctrinâ Socinianorum circa jus gladii, ita ut vidimus, judicant. Putabam enim eos non ita bene sentire de Socinianis, nec tantopere ipsorum labe infectos esse: Verùm jam eâ opinione me liberârunt Vinindiciis suis, absque quibus foret, orbis eos nequaquam itâ bene noffet. Nam, ut videas quantus fit affectus eorum erga Socinianos, quantus cum iis nexus, quàm arcta conjunctio, jam etiam in istâ parte eos crimine impietatis eximere cupiunt. Negat enim illâ doctrinam impiâ esse: Falsa & noxia doctrina, inquiunt p. 114. nö statim impia est &c. Bone Deus! Eamne doctrinam Arminianos non habere pro impiâ, quam non solùm ipsi fatentur verbo & mandato Dei contrariam esse, sed etiam ita noxiam ut actum fit de auctoritate Magistratus, de salute subditorum, nec non ut pauci scurra evertenda toti societati humana (adeòque toti Ecclesiæ Dei) sufficerent, quæ propria ipsorum verba sunt quibus hanc doctrinam commendant? In summâ, eamne doctrinam impiam non esse, quæ totam tabulam fecundam Decalogi tollit: ex qua denique scelerum licentia, ut hic loquuntur, & impietatis diluvium sequitur?
units.tr: The Arminians reply in such a way as to confess that they said they were ready to maintain communion with those sects; yet they deny both the minor premise and the consequence of the major. As to the minor, they deny that the doctrine of the Socinians and Anabaptists is impious. Let the pious reader observe that I was so fair to the Arminians that I said earlier, in the chapter cited from the Arcana, p. 157, that they accuse not only other sects but even the Socinians at some points of impiety. In this matter, as far as the Socinians are concerned, I had regard to this passage of the Apology, in which they judge about the doctrine of the Socinians concerning the right of the sword, as we have seen. For I thought they did not think so well of the Socinians, nor were they so deeply stained by their taint. But now, by their Vindiciae, they have freed me from that opinion; without them the world would by no means know them so well. For, that you may see how great their affection towards the Socinians is, how close their bond with them, how tight their union, they now seek to exempt them from the charge of impiety even in this part. For they deny that this doctrine is impious: A false and harmful doctrine, they say on p. 114, is not at once impious &c. Good God! Are the Arminians not to regard as impious that doctrine which they themselves not only confess to be contrary to the word and command of God, but also so harmful that the authority of the magistrate is at an end, the safety of subjects, and a few scoundrels would suffice to overturn the whole human society (and therefore the whole Church of God)? These are their own words by which they commend this doctrine. In short, is that doctrine not impious which removes the whole second table of the Decalogue, and from which at last follows the license of crimes, as they here put it, and a deluge of impiety?

units.la: Sed dicunt Arminani p. 115. ea mala fluere ex doctrinâ illâ per accidens, non per fe, quia flagitiosi abuti illa possint. Verùm enimverò illud salsissimum est. Primò enim contradicunt sibi ipsis; dixerant quippe loco allegato Apologiæ: Actum est de auctoritate publicâ, de salute fubduorum, ubi jus necis eripitur Magistratibus. Vides eos ipsi doctrinæ mala ista attribuere: adeòque non per accidens, sed per fe fluere illa ex doctrinâ istâ. Deinde, tunc fluèret flueret diluvium scelerum per accidens & non per se ex doctrinâ istâ, siquidem illa doctrina vera esset, adeòque mali homines illius veritate abuti possent. Atqui ista doctrina salsissima est, & verbo Dei plane contraria: unde etiam istius doctrinæ veritate ( quæ nulla est ) homines flagitiosi non abuti, sed falsitate illius uti possunt, quaⁱse ad scelera magis ac magis incitent. Cùm igitur doctrina ista falsa sit, fatentibus ipsis Arminianis, & ex ea impietas sequatur; manifestum est hanc ex illâ non per accidens sed per se fluere. Ut enim ex veritate doctrinæ bonum per se, malum autem per accidens fluit; ita ex falsâ doctrinâ malum per se fluit, bonum autem non nisi per accidens fluere potest. Argumenta quæ afferunt p. 114. 115. 116. non digna sunt quæ refutentur, ob singularem & notoriam pofanitatem atque impietatem quam continent, prout ex Parte III. lib. 2. cap. 5. videre est. Recitasse ea est refutasse.
units.tr: But the Arminians say on p. 115 that those evils flow from that doctrine by accident, not in itself, because wicked men can abuse it. But that is most absurd. For, first, they contradict themselves; for they said in the passage of the Apology cited: Public authority is at an end, and the safety of subjects, where the right of life and death is taken from the magistrates. You see that they themselves attribute those evils to the doctrine: therefore they flow from this doctrine not by accident but in itself. Next, the deluge of crimes would flow by accident and not in itself from this doctrine, if that doctrine were true, and wicked men could therefore abuse its truth. But this doctrine is most absurd and plainly contrary to the word of God; hence wicked men cannot abuse the truth of this doctrine (for there is none), but can use its falsehood, which incites them more and more to crimes. Since, then, this doctrine is false, as the Arminians themselves confess, and impiety follows from it, it is manifest that this impiety flows from it not by accident but in itself. For just as good flows from the truth of a doctrine in itself and evil by accident, so from a false doctrine evil flows in itself, while good can flow only by accident. The arguments which they bring forward on pp. 114, 115, 116 are not worth refuting, on account of the singular and notorious profanity and impiety they contain, as may be seen from Part III, book 2, chapter 5. To recite them is to refute them.

units.la: Dixi præterea, eos negare secundo loco consequentiam argumenti hujus septimi. Id quod faciunt hoc prætextu, quòd, quando dicunt se libenter velle communionem colere cum iis sectis omnibus, mens eorum non hæc sit; se velle communionem colere cum iis sectis, ex quarum doctrina NULLO PRORSUS MODO impietas sequitur; sed ex quarum doctrina vi ac genio adeòque per se impietas ita non sequitur, ut ipsi doctrinæ impietas adhæreat p. 116. Talem autem non esse istam doctrinam Socinianorum & Anabaptistarum de jure gladii: utpote ex quâ non per se sed per accidens, nimirum ex abusu illius seu vitio eorum qui illâ abutuntur fluat impietas. Respondeo: Hæ meræ nugæ sunt, quæ adversùm me non faciunt, qui dixi eos communionem colere velle cum sectis iis ex quarum doctrinâ per se fluit impietas, idololatria &c. Et ostenderam hoc inductione, ut v.g. communionis eorum cum Socinianis & Anabaptistis cum, quorum doctrinâ impietas non per accidens sed per se cohæret, ut ostensum. Secundò, contradicunt ei quod mox p. 117. dicunt, ubi profitentur se velle communionem colere cum iis sectis ex quarum doctrinæ vi & genio apta nata est fluere impietas & idololatria, modò ab actu impietatis & idololatriæ abstineant illi qui eam doctrinam profitentur. Denique, fatentur hoc loco p. 116 se dixisse istud dogma Socinianorum & Anabaptistarum non obstare, quòminus communionem colant cum iis sectis, his verbis. Atque hæc causa est, cur Remonstrantes cum iis communionem se colere & bonâ conscientiâ posse & libenter velle, quantum ad hoc dogma attinet, professi sint, inprimis cum videat esse non paucanec leviaScripturarum loca, quæ eos imprudenter in errorem rem istum faciunt incidere. Hoc sufficit nobis: nimirùm quòd communionem volunt colere cum iis sectis, quarum doctrinam, quâ jus necis Magistratui eripiunt, ita falsam & noxiam esse fatentur, ut actum sit de auctoritate publicâ, salute subditorum, & totâ societate humanâ. Hoc inquam sufficit nobis; & crimine eos non liberat, etiamsi tàm perniciosam & impiam doctrinam pro impiâ habere nolint.
units.tr: I have further said that they deny, in the second place, the consequence of this seventh argument. They do so under this pretext: that when they say they are willing to maintain communion with all those sects, their mind is not this: that they are willing to maintain communion with those sects, from whose doctrine by NO MEANS WHATSOEVER impiety follows; but from whose doctrine, by its force and tendency, and therefore in itself, impiety does not follow in such a way that impiety clings to the doctrine itself, p. 116. Such, however, this doctrine of the Socinians and Anabaptists concerning the right of the sword is not: since impiety flows from it not in itself but by accident, namely from the abuse or fault of those who abuse it. I answer: these are mere trifles, which do not tell against me, who said that they were willing to maintain communion with those sects from whose doctrine impiety, idolatry etc. flows in itself. And I had shown this by an instance, namely their communion with the Socinians and Anabaptists, with whose doctrine impiety clings not by accident but in itself, as has been shown. Secondly, they contradict what they say a little later on p. 117, where they profess that they are willing to maintain communion with those sects from whose doctrine's force and tendency impiety and idolatry is fitted and apt to arise, provided that those who profess that doctrine abstain from the act of impiety and idolatry. Finally, in this place on p. 116 they confess that this dogma of the Socinians and Anabaptists does not stand in the way of their maintaining communion with those sects, in these words: And this is the reason why the Remonstrants have professed that, as far as this dogma is concerned, they can with a good conscience and are willing to maintain communion with them, especially since they see that there are not a few and not light passages of Scripture which lead them, in their imprudence, into this error. This is enough for us: namely that they wish to maintain communion with those sects, whose doctrine by which they take the right of life and death from the magistrate they confess to be so false and harmful that public authority, the safety of subjects, and the whole human society are at an end. This, I say, is enough for us; and it does not free them from the charge, even if they are unwilling to regard so pernicious and impious a doctrine as impious.

units.la: 8. Secundum exemplum est, quòd profitentur se libenter velle communionem colere cum Lutheranis & Reformatis, etiamsi ex eorum doctrinâ de reali communione corporis & sanguinis Christi nasci ac fluere contendant, etiamnum hodie, ingente idololatriam quâ major concipi vix possit, eamque doctrinam vel ex curiositate vel ex superstitione enatam. Apol.c.23.f.250.b.& 251.a. Unde sequitur eos profiteri se communione colere velle cum iis sectis, cum quarum doctrinâ impietas, idololatria & superstitio cohæreat. Respondent per negationem consequentiæ.Nam
units.tr: 8. The second example is that they profess they are willing to maintain communion with the Lutherans and the Reformed, even though they contend that from their doctrine of the real communion of the body and blood of Christ there arises and flows, even today, an enormous idolatry, than which one can hardly conceive a greater, and that this doctrine has sprung up either from curiosity or from superstition. Apology, ch. 23, p. 250b and 251a. From this it follows that they profess they wish to maintain communion with those sects, with whose doctrine impiety, idolatry and superstition cohere. They reply by denying the consequence. For

units.la: 1. Idololatriam non nasci per se sed per accidens ex illâ doctrinâ, nimirum ex accidente nimiâ superstitione aut curiositate, ut verba Remonstrantium, inquiunt, disserte habent. Curiositas autem & superstitio vitia hominum sunt, non autem doctrina: Per accidens itaque idololatriam ex eâ nasci certissimum est. Secundò respondent p. 117. se paratos esse communionem colere cum iis, etsi ex doctrinę istius genio fluat idololatria: Secundò respondeo, inquiunt, aliud esse ex doctrina alicujus genio idololatriam fluere, id est, doctrinam aliquam adactus idololatricos gignendum in animis hominum, aptam atq; idoneam esse. Aliud, ipsum idololatriæ actu isti doctrinæ cohærere atque adjunctum esse. Remonstrantes existimant communionem coli posse etiam cum cœtu aliquo, qui doctrinam docet ex quâ apta nata est existere idololatria, si modo actus ipse idololatriæ isti doctrinæ non cohæreat &c. Item: Magnum enim idololatriæ odium esse oportet, quod non exstinguitur à doctrinâ, quæ incitamentum ad idololatriam in se habet. Verùm enim verò, optime Lector, quis non videt ex duplice hac responsione, me non falsum sed verum dixisse; Arminianos autem convictos esse falsitatis, & ad incitas redactos, adeòque etiam in hac parte causam nostram superiorem esse? Nam primò, istæ duæ responsiones sibi invicem contradicunt manifestissimè. Etenim in priore dicunt, ex doctrinæ istius genio seu per se non fluere idololatriam; in alterâ autem dicunt fluere idololatriam ex genio istius doctrinæ, eam ad actus idololatricos gignendum in animis hominum aptam atq; idoneam esse, eam incitamentum ad idololatriam in se habere. Deinde quòd in priore ajunt, se dixisse idololatriâ non fluere ex istâ doctrina per se, sed per accidens, scilicet ex accedente nimia
units.tr: 1. Idolatry does not arise from that doctrine in itself but by accident, namely from the accident of excessive superstition or curiosity, as the words of the Remonstrants, they say, expressly state. But curiosity and superstition are faults of men, not of the doctrine: therefore it is most certain that idolatry arises from it by accident. Secondly, they reply on p. 117 that they are ready to maintain communion with those, even though idolatry flows from the tendency of that doctrine: Secondly, I reply, they say, that it is one thing for idolatry to flow from the tendency of a doctrine, that is, for a doctrine to be fitted and suited to beget idolatrous acts in the minds of men; another thing for the very act of idolatry to cohere with and be joined to that doctrine. The Remonstrants think communion can be maintained even with a body which teaches a doctrine from which idolatry is apt and fitted to arise, provided only that the act of idolatry itself does not cohere with that doctrine &c. Likewise: For there must be a great hatred of idolatry, which is not extinguished by a doctrine that has in itself an incitement to idolatry. But truly, best of readers, who does not see from this double reply that I have said not what is false but what is true, and that the Arminians are convicted of falsehood and reduced to straits, and therefore in this part too our cause is the stronger? For first, these two replies contradict each other most plainly. For in the former they say that idolatry does not flow from the tendency of that doctrine, that is, in itself; but in the latter they say that idolatry flows from the tendency of that doctrine, that it is fitted and suited to beget idolatrous acts in the minds of men, that it has in itself an incitement to idolatry. Next, when in the former they say that they had said idolatry flows from this doctrine not in itself but by accident, namely from the accession of excessive

units.la: Y nimia curiositate aut superstitione: in eo contra conscientiam suam loquuntur. Nam expresse dicunt loco allegato Apologiæ, ex ipso mysterio quod attribuunt Lutherani & Reformati S. Cœnæ fluxisse & fluere horrendam idololatriam, item superstitiosam vanitatem. Me verum dicere patet ex verbis eorum, quæ allegata invenire est libro præcedente hujus partis Quartæ Arcan. cap. 4. quo Lector haud gravatim recurret. Ita igitur contra conscientiam suam ajunt se dixisse, idololatriam fluere ex eâ doctrinâ non per se sed per accidens. Deinde etiam contra conscientiam suam loquuntur, quando ajunt se dixisse, istam idololatriam fluere ex curiositate accedente, seu superstitione. Nam faciunt quidem verbis modo allegatis mentionem superstitionis & curiositatis; sed non dicunt idololatriam fluxisse ex superstitione aut curiositate accedente isti doctrinæ; sed ipsam doctrinam Evangelicorum dicunt fluxisse ex antecedente superstitione aut curiositate; item superstitiosam vanitatem rursus ex eâ doctrinâ manâsse: Et incomprehensibilia, inquiunt, ineffabilia ista mysteria, quæ humana seu curiositas, seu superstitio &c. finxit potius quàm reperit. Item: Nimis magnorum mysteriorum quæ huic ritui subesse creduntur apprehensio peperit admirationem, quam adoratio è vestigio sequuta est &c. & in cæteris Ecclesiis tanta tamque superstitiosa vanitas.
units.tr: and with excessive curiosity or superstition: in saying this they speak against their own conscience. For they expressly say, in the passage of the Apology cited, that the horrible idolatry, and likewise the superstitious vanity, has flowed and still flows from the very mystery which the Lutherans and the Reformed attribute to the Lord's Supper. That I speak the truth is clear from their own words, which may be found quoted in the preceding book of this Fourth Part of the Arcana, chapter 4, to which the reader may return without difficulty. So they say against their own conscience that they said the idolatry flows from this doctrine not in itself but by accident. Again, they speak against their own conscience when they say that they said this idolatry flows from an accompanying curiosity or superstition. For they do indeed mention superstition and curiosity in the words just cited, but they do not say that the idolatry flowed from a superstition or curiosity added to that doctrine. Rather, they say that the doctrine of the Evangelicals itself flowed from a prior superstition or curiosity; and again, that the superstitious vanity flowed from that doctrine: "And these mysteries, they say, are incomprehensible and ineffable, which human curiosity or superstition, etc., has invented rather than discovered." Also: "The grasping of the great mysteries which are believed to lie beneath this rite has produced an admiration, which adoration immediately followed, etc., and in the other Churches there is such a great and so superstitious vanity."

units.la: 9. Tertium exemplum est speciatim Reformatorum, quos ipsi Calvinianos vocant. Non semel enim profitentur se communionem colere velle cum iis non obstante doctrinâ ipsorum de Quinque articulis, quam tamen impiissimam esse dicunt, ac in specie (ut negare non possint Arminiani se Hæreticos in Ecclesiam Dei introducere velle) sententiam Calvini Hæreticam vocant, item cum quâ forte nulla hæresis comparari mereatur. Hæc dixeram ego p. 160. cap. alleg. Fatentur se ita dixisse & persistunt in eo: Remonstrantes existimant, inquiunt p. 117. se communionem colere posse cum Calvinistis, non obstante articulo de Prædestinatione, ex quo, imò ex cujus vi ac genio ad impietatem & profanitatem calcar ac stimulum non levem oriri persuasissimum habent &c. Observetur igitur, eos fateri, quod dixi docere illos, se communionem posse colere cum iis sectis cum quarum doctrinâ impietas per se cohæret. Interim hoc etiam notetur, quòd cùm ostenderim verbis allatis meis, eos negare non posse, se Hæreticos in Ecclesiam introducere velle, quia dicunt sententiam Calvini Hæreticam esse, imò nullam forte hæresin cum eâ comparari posse; notetur, inquam, eos ne verbum quidem ad hoc respondere, sed tacito pede argumentum solidissimum & invictum præterire, quo ostenderam eos Hæreticos in Ecclesiam velle introducere, quia nobiscum cum, quos habent pro Hæretecis gravissimis, communionem se colere velle profitentur. Unde quis non videt hos homines in conscientiâ suâ convictos malæ suæ causæ esse?
units.tr: 9. The third example concerns especially the Reformed, whom they themselves call Calvinists. For they profess more than once that they wish to keep communion with them, notwithstanding their doctrine of the Five Articles, which yet they call most impious, and in particular (since the Arminians cannot deny that they wish to introduce heretics into the Church of God) they call the opinion of Calvin heretical, and say that perhaps no heresy deserves to be compared with it. I had said this at p. 160 of the chapter cited. They confess that they have said so and persist in it: "The Remonstrants think, they say at p. 117, that they can keep communion with the Calvinists, notwithstanding the article on predestination, from which, indeed, from whose force and spirit they are most firmly persuaded that a not slight goad and spur to impiety and profanity arises, etc." Let it be observed, then, that they admit what I said, that they teach that they can keep communion with those sects with whose doctrine impiety is inherently bound up. Meanwhile let this also be noted: when I showed by the words I quoted that they cannot deny that they wish to introduce heretics into the Church, because they say that the opinion of Calvin is heretical, and perhaps no heresy can be compared with it, let it be noted, I say, that they do not answer a single word to this, but slip silently past the most solid and unanswerable argument, by which I had shown that they wish to introduce heretics into the Church, because they profess that they wish to keep communion with those whom they hold to be most grievous heretics. Whence who does not see that these men are convicted by their own conscience that their cause is bad?

units.la: 10. Quartum membrum inductionis concernit Pontificios. Hos enim, vi suarum hypothesum, quas capite quinto Par. I. Arc. lib. 2. primis sex argumentis expositimus, præcipue autem vi doctrinæ suæ de Necessariis &non necessariis, excludere non possunt ex istâ tolerantiâ. Et addideram p, 161. eos etiam post editam Apolog. in Resp. Belgicâ ad Excerpta Cl. V. D. Festi Hommii manifeste declarare se tolerare velle omnes errantes, modo in controversiâ tes sit posita(Wanneer tsluck eenigsins disputabel is) aut alioquin valde difficilis sit comprehensu f. g. 3. a. Remonstrantes, inquiunt, etiamnum libenter profitentur, & in eo persistunt, quod in rebus quae aeternam salutem aut condemnationem concernunt, malint judicare in partem mitiorem quam duriorem, modo res illa aliquomodo disputabilis sit, aut alioquin valde difficilis intellectu. Atqui de illis erroribus Pontificiorum controvertitur. Ergo nec illi excluduntur ab Arminianis ob superstitionem aut idololatriam. Ita dixeram loco allegato.
units.tr: 10. The fourth member of my induction concerns the Papists. For by virtue of their hypotheses, which we set out in the first six arguments of chapter five of Part I, Book 2 of the Arcana, and especially by virtue of their doctrine of necessary and unnecessary matters, they cannot exclude them from this tolerance. And I had added at p. 161 that they also, after the publication of the Apology, in their Belgic Response to the Excerpts of the very learned Festus Hommius, clearly declare that they wish to tolerate all who err, provided the matter in controversy is somewhat disputable (Wanneer tsluck eenigsins disputabel is), or otherwise very difficult to comprehend, f. g. 3. a. "The Remonstrants, they say, still willingly profess, and persist in this, that in matters which concern eternal salvation or condemnation, they prefer to judge in the milder rather than the harsher direction, provided the matter is in some way disputable, or otherwise very difficult to understand." But the controversy is about those errors of the Papists. Therefore they too are not excluded by the Arminians on account of superstition or idolatry. Thus I had written in the passage cited.

units.la: Respondent illi, se non posse communionem colere cum Pontificiis, & rursus negant se docuisse: Nulla dogmata controversa esse necessaria ad salutem, & addunt: Hoc ipsum enim quod hic controversum esse dicit Vedelius, existimant Remonstrantes idcirco controversum non debere videri, quia non tantum κατὰ τὴν διάνοιαν sed κατὰ τὸ ῥητὸν in scriptura est, idololatriam esse id quod non nisi muta inanimis & bruta res est, divino cultu adorare &c. Respondeo: Ex hoc non sequitur me falsò ipsis objecisse tolerantiam & communionem cum Pontificiis; sed quia, ut suprà ostendimus, revera ita docent de controversis & non necessariis dogmatis, item de Necessariis, hic autem jam negant, sequitur eos αὐτοκατάκριτος esse, ac in conscientiâ suâ convictos malæ suæ causæ, & tamen contra eam negare se docuisse quod revera docuerunt, ut patet ex cap. 8. libri primi. Quod dicunt dogma hoc ideò non debere videri controversum, quia κατὰ τὸ ῥητὸν in scriptura est &c. profectò singularis est protervia, quâ volunt oculos eruere hominibus & ipsis persuadere ut non amplius pro controverso dogmate habeant de quo controversia seu lis est. Hactenus enim totus mundus credidit; & Grammatices, Logices, Theologiæ & omnium disciplinarum ac facultatum usus docuit controversum esse id, de quo controvertitur seu de quo lis est: sive jure sive injuriâ id fiat; id ad rem non facit. Iam quia id ex usu est causæ Arminianorum, & nihil habent solidi quod respondere possint; & tamen (utpote homines qui non veritatis sed suam victoria quaerunt) ... victoriam quaerunt) victores cupiunt videri ; sine ullâ fronte dicunt jam non id habendum esse pro controverso de quo lis est seu de quo actu controvertitur; sed id tantum quod nec πνῃτῶς nec κατὰ διάνοιαν in scriptura est.
