I, book 1, chapter 3, and from the preceding book of this Fourth Part; and indeed, among other things, from the fact that they say: The Spirit, that is, the interpretations which anyone believes he has by the suggestion of the Spirit of God, the Apostle certainly wishes to be entirely free in the Church. Apology, chapter 4, f. 275 b. It is also clear from the doctrine of the Apology on Toleration, which we set out in Par. I, book 2, chapter 5, and book 2, chapter 5 of this part. What they mean by force is manifest: namely every corporeal resistance, however it may be, by which the attempts of heretics are opposed, especially the prohibition of private conventicles. I leave insults and calumnies to God, and the outcry in its place. As to what they say among other things on page 144: Let Vedelius see that he may one day feel the same blow struck on his own head, to his own loss and harm, the wise, to whom the actions and deeds of these men are known, know what they mean by these words, and those who remember what they said above in Vindication book 2, chapter 6, pages 130 and 131: namely that I deserve to experience the tyranny not only of Papists, Lutherans, and Anabaptists, but of any other sect whatever, whenever I shall have to appear before it at some Synod. This is enough for me; for they have spoken to one who understands. But God will preserve me and other faithful servants of his from a Synod of the Arminians, that is, of pretended Socinians. As to their referring the reader to chapter 3 of book 2 of the Vindication, it is well, and in accordance with my own opinion; for there the reader both has seen and will see the baseness of this sect.

units.la: 4. Tertium medium est, quod ad ministerium verbi admittendos docent Anabaptistas. Probavi ex eo, quia admittendos dicunt ad ministerium qui docent Pædobaptismum non esse necessarium, nec necessitate medii nec necessitate praecepti, h. e. ut ipsi se explicant in Apologia & Resp. ad Excerp. Cll. DD. Proff. Leydd. non esse praeceptum a Deo. Hic non negant, sed fatentur, se docere admittendos esse tales ad ministerium: sed 1. negant exinde sequi Ergo Remonstrantes Anabaptistarum omnia probant. Quāin re eos sophistas agere est manifestum: nec enim illa est illatio seu conclusio mea, ut unusquisque videt. Deinde dicunt, non sequi illam conclusionem ex eo quod Remonstrantes propter istud unum sive istum solum articulum in quo conveniunt isti fratres sui cum Anabaptistis, non putant eos damnandos aut ex coetu suo excludendos esse. Verum falsum est, eos fratres ipsorum aut se in illo uno & solo articulo convenire cum Anabaptistis, & propter illum solum statuere tolerandos esse in Ecclesia; Nam ex Par. I. Arc. lib. 1. cap. 9. & lib. 2. c. 5. patet Arminianos revocare in dubium & convellere argumentis suis, non pauca dogmata orthodoxa quae ab Anabaptistis negantur & oppugnantur: quod an sit sentire cum Ecclesia Evangelica an cum Anabaptistis unicuique dijudicandum relinquo.
units.tr: 4. The third point is that the Arminians admit to the ministry of the Word those who teach the Anabaptists' view. I proved this from the fact that they say those are to be admitted to the ministry who teach that infant baptism is not necessary, neither by necessity of means nor by necessity of precept; that is, as they explain themselves in their Apology and in the Response to the Excerpts of the Professors of Leiden, it is not a precept of God. Here they do not deny but confess that they teach such persons are to be admitted to the ministry. But first, they deny that it follows from this, "Therefore the Remonstrants approve all the things of the Anabaptists." In this they plainly act the sophists: for that is not my inference or conclusion, as anyone can see. Next, they say the conclusion does not follow from the fact that "the Remonstrants, because of that one article, or that single article in which their brethren agree with the Anabaptists, do not think them to be condemned or excluded from their assembly." But this is false: that their brethren agree with the Anabaptists in that one and only article, and that for that alone they resolve they are to be tolerated in the Church. For from Part I, Arcana, book 1, chapter 9, and book 2, chapter 5, it is evident that the Arminians call into question, and overthrow with their arguments, not a few orthodox doctrines which the Anabaptists deny and attack. Whether this is to think with the Evangelical Church or with the Anabaptists, I leave for each to judge.

units.la: Pergunt, ac litigant de appellatione Anabaptistarum, & dicunt me debuisse potius inferre Remonstrantes non docere Anabaptistas admittendos esse ad ministerium verbi quia Anabaptista non tantum credunt Pædobaptismum non esse necessarium, sed etiam illicitum ac non tolerandum in Ecclesia, & addunt me nescire quid Anabaptista sit, utpote qui habeam pro Anabaptistis omnes eos qui solum Pædobaptismi necessitatem non probant. Sed haec merae nugae sunt, quibus persuadere volunt, Anabaptistas non esse eos qui nolunt usurpare Pædobaptismum, & negant eum praeceptum esse a Christo. Atqui hoc proprie loquendo est Anabaptistam esse seu Catabaptistam vi vocis ipsius. Et Anabaptistica secta inde tanquam a notiori nomen accepit, quamvis multos alios tetriores errores habeat. Dicunt autem expresse, se nullam causam videre, cur pastores qui pædobaptismum per conscientiam usurpare NON AU-DENT & interim alios, seu ex conscientia, seu ex traditione, seu ex consuetudine vel recepto more usurpantes tolerare parati sunt, pro veris ac legitimis Christi pastoribus habendi non sint. Apol. c. 23. f. 248. 2. b. Certè, ut tales Arminiani, qui nolunt usurpare pædobaptismum, non vocentur Anabaptistae sive Catabaptistæ, adeoque nomine quod ipsis proprie competit, in æternum non persuadebunt Ecclesiæ: maximè quia ut dictum non in solâ doctrinâ de pædobaptismo, sed etiam in aliis orthodoxis dogmatis, quæ ab Anabaptistis oppugnantur, dissentiunt ab Ecclesiâ. Interim quocunque nomine illos tales vocare velint, nobis perinde est; quibus sufficit, quòd fatentur se ad ministerium verbi admittere tales qui cum Anabaptistis pædobaptismum negant, & usurpare nolunt; quales quàm idonei ministri verbi in Ecclesiâ Dei sint, unusquisque facilè judicare poterit. Convitium de ignorantiâ meâ transeat, cum reliquâ ipsorum maledicentiâ, quam à Patre mendacii didicerunt.
units.tr: They go on, and quarrel about the name "Anabaptists," and say that I ought rather to have inferred that the Remonstrants do not teach that Anabaptists are to be admitted to the ministry of the Word, because Anabaptists not only believe infant baptism to be unnecessary but also unlawful and not to be tolerated in the Church; and they add that I do not know what an Anabaptist is, since I count as Anabaptists all those who merely do not prove the necessity of infant baptism. But these are mere trifles, by which they want to persuade that Anabaptists are not those who are unwilling to use infant baptism and deny that Christ commanded it. Yet properly speaking, by the force of the word itself, this is to be an Anabaptist or Catabaptist. And the Anabaptist sect took its name from this, as from the better-known feature, although it has many other, more foul errors. They say expressly that "they see no cause why ministers who, through conscience, DARE NOT use infant baptism, while they are ready to tolerate others who use it, whether from conscience, tradition, custom or accepted practice, should not be held to be true and lawful ministers of Christ." Apology, ch. 23, p. 248, col. 2, b. Certainly, the Arminians who are unwilling to use infant baptism will not, by being called not Anabaptists or Catabaptists, and so by avoiding the name properly belonging to them, persuade the Church for ever; especially because, as has been said, they dissent from the Church not only in the doctrine of infant baptism but also in other orthodox doctrines which the Anabaptists attack. Meanwhile, by whatever name they wish to call such people, it is all the same to us; it is enough for us that they confess that they admit to the ministry of the Word such persons as deny infant baptism with the Anabaptists and are unwilling to use it. How fit such ministers of the Word are in the Church of God anyone can easily judge. Let the reproach concerning my ignorance pass, together with the rest of their slander, which they learned from the Father of lies.

units.la: Addideram & probaveram eos falsò dicere: Fr. Junium (Theologum de Ecclesiâ Dei optimè meritum) ejusdem sententiæ in hac re secum esse; ad quod illi nihil replicant, & sic non negant se falso testimonio orbi illudere.
units.tr: I had also added and proved that they say falsely that Francis Junius (a theologian who deserved very well of the Church of God) is of the same opinion as they are on this matter. To this they make no reply, and so they do not deny that they are mocking the world with false testimony.

units.la: 5. Quartum dogma est: Ministerium verbi non esse simpliciter necessarium necessitate præcepti, seu Deum id non simpliciter sive absolutè præcepisse. Cujus sententiæ falsitatem argumento ostenderam, quod ex eo desumtum est: quòd, si hoc verum sit, non peccent illi, qui prohibent exercitium ministerii seu prædicationem Evangelii &c. Fatentur se ita docere, & ideò me insciliæ arguunt, ac dicunt ministerium non esse necessarium necessitate præcepti ad semper, seu pro semper. ut e. g. necessaria est fides & sanctimonia &c. idque ob eam causam, quia incidere possunt tempora, ut Pastores nulli sint, ob persecutionem aut aliam causam &c. p. 145. Et dicunt se diversis verbis asserere, ministerium esse necessarium & quidem necessitate perpetuâ, sed non eâ necessitate, quæ barbarè sed emphaticè dicitur Necessitas ad semper & pro semper. Respondeo primò: Ista distinctio tùm impertinens, tùm falsa est. Impertinens: nam quæstio est de necessitate præcepti contradistinctâ necessitati absolutæ medii. Atqui necessitas illa quam ad semper & pro semper illi vocant, est necessitas absoluta medii ut patet ex exemplis quæ afferunt, fidei, sanctimoniæ. Falsa etiam est, ut ostendi argumento modò memorato, ad quod illi ne verbo quidem respondent. Secundò falsum etiam est, eos tantùm propter istam causam negare ministerium esse absolutè necessarium. Est enim alia etiam eaque primaria causa, quæ ipsis cum aliis fanaticis communis est: Nam M. Episcopius expressè dicit in thesibus privatis de Notis Ecclesiæ: prædicationem Euangelii non tàm necessariam esse POST QUAM scriptura omnibus & singulis legenda data est. Hoc M. Episcopii dogma Arminiani Apol. c. 22. f. 233. a. suum faciunt, cùm dicunt: Et hoc est illud quod in thesibus suis suis optimè dixit (clarissimus Vir (hoc enim elogio se ipsum insignire & nominare solet Episcopius, pro suâ modestiâ, prout etiam facit Vindic. lib. 1. in præfatione suâ petulante & histrionicâ p. 5. quâre profectò nihil vanius & superbius fieri potest :) Episcopius. Et f. 242. b. vocant istud dogma M. Episcopii manifestissimam veritatem. Atque hoc objeceram ipsis loco allegato Arcanorum, ut pateret vera & ipsissima causa, propter quam Arminiani negant ministerium simpliciter à Deo præceptum esse. Sed ad hæc illi ne verbum quidem respondent; saltem ut dixi fucum volunt Lectori facere, allegando aliam causam nimirum persecutionem &c. Quod dicunt se disertis verbis asserere ministerium esse necessarium necessitate præcepti, & quidem perpetuâ; lectorem in eo etiam ludibrio habent. Nam dicunt quidem Deum id perpetuò exerceri voluisse, sed illam perpetuitatem limitant, hoc modo: quando impossibile non est ut exerceatur; item cum obtineri potest, ut expressè & conceptis verbis dicunt loco à me allegato Par. I. lib. 2. c. 7. p. 209. 210. ex Apologiæ c. 22. f. 233. a.
units.tr: 5. The fourth doctrine is this: "The ministry of the Word is not simply necessary by necessity of precept, or God has not simply or absolutely commanded it." I had shown the falsity of this opinion by an argument drawn from this: "that, if this is true, those who forbid the exercise of the ministry, or the preaching of the Gospel, etc., do not sin." They confess that they teach this, and therefore they accuse me of folly, and say that "the ministry is not necessary by necessity of precept always, or for always, as, for example, faith and holiness are necessary, etc.; and this for the reason that times may come when there are no ministers, through persecution or some other cause, etc." p. 145. And they say they assert in different words that "the ministry is necessary, and indeed by a perpetual necessity, but not by that necessity which is barbarously yet emphatically called necessity for always and for ever." I reply first: this distinction is both irrelevant and false. Irrelevant: for the question is about necessity of precept, distinguished from the absolute necessity of means. But that necessity which they call "for always and for ever" is the absolute necessity of means, as is clear from the examples they bring: faith, holiness. It is also false, as I have shown by the argument just mentioned, to which they do not so much as reply with a word. Secondly, it is also false that they deny the ministry is absolutely necessary only for that reason. There is another cause, and that the primary one, which they share with other fanatics: for M. Episcopius expressly says, in his private theses on the Marks of the Church, that "the preaching of the Gospel is not so necessary AFTER THE TIME that Scripture has been given to all and each to be read." The Arminians make this doctrine of M. Episcopius their own, in their Apology, ch. 22, p. 233, col. 1, a, when they say: "And this is that which the most distinguished man (for Episcopius is accustomed to adorn himself with this title and to name himself so, out of his modesty, as he also does in his petulant and theatrical preface to the Vindication, book 1, p. 5, whence nothing could truly be more vain and proud) excellently said in his theses: Episcopius." And on p. 242, col. 2, b, they call this doctrine of M. Episcopius "a most manifest truth." And I had objected this to them at the cited place of the Arcana, so that the true and very cause might be plain, for which the Arminians deny that the ministry was simply commanded by God. But to these things they do not reply a single word; at least, as I said, they wish to dupe the reader by alleging another cause, namely "persecution," etc. As for their saying that they assert in express words that the ministry is necessary by necessity of precept, and indeed perpetually, they mock the reader in this too. For they do indeed say that God willed it to be exercised perpetually, but they limit that perpetuity in this way: "when it is not impossible that it be exercised," and likewise "when it can be obtained," as they say expressly and in so many words in the place I cited, Part I, book 2, ch. 7, pp. 209–210, from Apology ch. 22, p. 233, col. 1, a.

units.la: 6. Quintò denique, ostendi eos ministerium verbi evertere doctrinâ suâ de non necessariis seu controversis, dum dicunt ea non esse firmiter constanterque credenda; in iis Religionem non esse positam; licere contradicere iis; fidem annuam, menstruam, horariam in iis habere licere &c. Quâ ratione quis non videt hominibus occasionem aperiri dubitando de eorum veritate, dicebam, aut saltem indifferenter habendi ea quæ à Pastore de dogmatis fidei, quæ fere omnia controversa sunt, è verbo Dei proponuntur? Unde tandem contagium paulatim etiā ad necessaria seu quæ extra controversiam sunt, serpit. Conquestus etiam fui, istud dogma de controversiis ex animis parentum eximere curam instituendi liberos in veritate divinâ seu verâ Religione. Respondent his ipsis nec pluribus nec paucioribus verbis p. 145: Quintum, vetus cantilena est, ad quam jam aures tinniunt: profectò molesta est iterum atque iterum Pythum versus via. Et his verbis caput septimum claudunt. Estne hoc respondere, an Lectori illudere? Si negare volunt à se hoc fieri, cur rationem non reddunt & bonâ fide respondent? Sed negare illud non possunt: res enim evidentissima est. Et Lector me verum etiam in hac parte dixisse evidentissimè intelliget ex iis quæ lib. 1. cap. 8. Vindic. respondent ad dogmata illa sibi objecta, collatis cum lib. 1. c. 8. Partis hujus Quartæ. Quibus dogmatis positis; certè ministerium verbi ludibrio exponitur. Patet igitur me in hoc etiam capite, nihil per calumniam ipsis imputâsse.
units.tr: 6. Fifthly and finally, I showed that they overturn the ministry of the Word by their doctrine concerning things not necessary or controverted, while they say "these are not to be believed firmly and constantly; religion does not rest on them; it is lawful to contradict them; it is lawful to hold annual, monthly or hourly faith concerning them," etc. By what reasoning, I said, does no one see that an opening is given to men to doubt their truth, or at least to hold indifferently those things which the minister sets forth from the Word of God concerning the doctrines of faith, which are almost all controverted? Whence at last the contagion gradually creeps even to the necessary things, or to those that are beyond controversy. I also complained that this doctrine about controversies takes from the minds of parents the care of instructing their children in divine truth, or the true religion. They reply to these things in words neither more nor fewer, p. 145: "Fifthly, it is an old song, to which our ears already tingle: truly it is troublesome again and again, the road to Pytho." And with these words they close the seventh chapter. Is this to reply, or to mock the reader? If they wish to deny that they do this, why do they not give a reason and reply in good faith? But they cannot deny it: the matter is most evident. And the reader will most clearly understand that I have spoken the truth in this part also, from what they reply in book 1, ch. 8, of the Vindication to the doctrines objected to them, compared with book 1, ch. 8, of this Fourth Part. With these doctrines laid down, the ministry of the Word is certainly exposed to mockery. It is therefore plain that in this chapter also I have imputed nothing to them by calumny.

units.la: CAP. VIII.
units.tr: CHAPTER VIII.

units.la: Examen Capitis VIII. lib. 2. Vindiciarum.
units.tr: Examination of Chapter VIII of Book 2 of the Vindiciae.

units.la: 1. Arminianorum protervia, totam veterem & modernam Ecclesiam oscitantia & stupiditatis accusantium, ex antiquitate Ecclesiastica arguitur. 2. Fatentur quod docent: Disciplinam Ecclesiasticam exercendam esse sine noxa Haereticorum. 3. Ad argumentum quo constricti tenentur & convincuntur toti orbi illudere doctrina sua de Tolerantia ne verbum quidem respondent. Ad accusationem qua evidentissime ostenditur eos veritatis divinae curam in doctrina de disciplina Ecclesiastica non habere, etiam nihil respondent. 4. Mala fide negant se docere: quod Haereticis liceat excommunicare veram Ecclesiam. Varia impostura eorum circa hanc rem redarguuntur. 5. Fatentur se docere, praestare fortassis non separare Haereticum a communione Ecclesiae quam eum ab illa separare. 6. Fatentur se docere, Excommunicationem esse voluntariam tantummodo secessionem ab aliquo. Item sufficere ad excommunicationem, ut Ecclesia significet excommunicando, sibi non licere amplius sponte sua atque ultro cum illo tanquam cum Christiano sacra facere. Item, si excommunicatus obtemperare nolit, cogi Ecclesiam eum admittere ad sacra. Non respondent argumento, quo ostensa erat falsitas istius dogmatis. 7. Fatentur quod docent: non licere Ecclesiae Magistratum monere ut Haereticos coerceat. Multiplex falsitas eorum & imperitia antiquitatis Ecclesiasticae, quam hic praetexunt, redarguitur. Anne Haereticorum coercitio Legi naturae contraria sit, ut Arminiani volunt? 8. Fatentur se docere, Haereticis, speciatim Antitrinitariis, anathema dicendum non esse. Arminianos tamen proterve anathema dicere omnibus coetibus qui Deum in tribus personis adorant ostenditur. 9. Fatentur, Haereticis silentium imponendum non esse. Ad aliud argumentum, ex quo patet eos falsitatis convictos esse, nihil respondent. 10. Fatentur; se docere non esse exercendam disciplinam Ecclesiasticam adversum eos qui errant in fundamento, nisi to nisi constet eos voluntarià culpà errare, h. e. adversum Hæreticos quos tota Ecclesia quæ Deum in tribus personis adorat sic vocat. II. Fatentur se docere, mandatum à Deo non esse ut separentur errantes ab Ecclesiâ, aut ut quis se ab illis segreget. 12. Ad decimum quod objectum erat, quid respondeant?
units.tr: 1. The Arminians' insolence, accusing the whole old and modern Church of drowsiness and stupidity, is refuted from ecclesiastical antiquity. 2. They confess what they teach: that ecclesiastical discipline must be exercised without harm to heretics. 3. To the argument by which they are bound and convicted, namely that their doctrine of toleration mocks the whole world, they do not reply even a word. To the charge by which it is most evidently shown that they have no care for divine truth in their doctrine of ecclesiastical discipline, they likewise reply nothing. 4. They deny in bad faith that they teach that heretics may excommunicate the true Church. Their various deceptions on this point are refuted. 5. They confess that they teach that it is perhaps better not to separate a heretic from the communion of the Church than to separate him from it. 6. They confess that they teach that excommunication is merely a voluntary withdrawal from someone. Likewise, that it is enough for excommunication that the Church signify by excommunicating that it is no longer lawful for it to perform sacred acts with him of its own accord and gladly, as with a Christian. Likewise, that if the excommunicated person is unwilling to submit, the Church is compelled to admit him to the sacred rites. They do not reply to the argument by which the falsity of this doctrine was shown. 7. They confess that they teach that it is not lawful for the Church to urge the magistrate to restrain heretics. Their manifold falsehood and their ignorance of ecclesiastical antiquity, which they put forward here, are refuted. Is the restraint of heretics contrary to the law of nature, as the Arminians maintain? 8. They confess that they teach that anathema is not to be pronounced on heretics, especially Antitrinitarians. Yet it is shown that the Arminians insolently pronounce anathema on all assemblies that worship God in three persons. 9. They confess that silence is not to be imposed on heretics. To another argument, from which it is clear that they have been convicted of falsehood, they reply nothing. 10. They confess that they teach that ecclesiastical discipline is not to be exercised against those who err in the foundation, unless it is established that they err through voluntary fault, that is, against those heretics whom the whole Church that worships God in three persons so calls. 11. They confess that they teach that God has not commanded that those who err be separated from the Church, or that anyone separate himself from them. 12. To the tenth objection, what do they answer?

units.la: CApite octavo, antequam Arminiani ad dogmata sibi à me objectæ respondeant, protestantur prius, sibi valdè curæ esse disciplinam Ecclesiasticam circa peccatores coërcendos; id quod ad rem non facit. Nam quæstio est de disciplinâ Ecclesiasticâ exercendâ adversum Hæreticos, quam penitus evertunt. ut Parte I. lib. 2. c. 8. ostendi, & jam ex hoc capite porrò patebit. Invehuntur etiam in eos qui totius disciplinæ Ecclesiasticæ exercitium in solos Hæreticos dirigunt, & me inter eos salsissimè referunt. Nam quod cap. 8. illo de disciplinâ adversus peccatores non egi, id instituti mei ratio non ferebat, ut unusquisque videt. Postea ad coccysmum suum de Vedelio redeunt, si coram Pontificio tribunali hæreseos reus staret. Invehuntur etiam in me, quòd, ut disciplinam Ecclesiasticam adversus Hæreticos exercendam etiam cum anathemate probarem, allegârim Epistolam Pauli Gal. 1. 8. & 1. Cor. 16. 22. Pudeat Vedelium, inquiunt p. 146. non tam supina oscitantia quam stupiditatis sua, cum Scriptura auctoritatem tam perfunctorie adeoque tam perverse allegat, ad rei tam ingentis probationem; & ut illa loca ad rem non facere probent, pandunt nobis novum arcanum quoddam, de quo egimus Par.III. lib.2. c. 8. §. 1. cum solita laude quâ Hæreticos commendant ob pietatem & amorem Jesu Christi, nec non rursus cum coccysmo contra Vedelium stantem coram tribunali Pontificio.
units.tr: In chapter eight, before the Arminians reply to the doctrines I objected to them, they first protest that they are very concerned about ecclesiastical discipline for restraining sinners. This has nothing to do with the matter. For the question is about exercising ecclesiastical discipline against heretics, which they utterly overturn, as I showed in Part I, book 2, chapter 8, and as will now become clearer from this chapter. They also rail against those who direct the whole exercise of ecclesiastical discipline only against heretics, and they very wittily count me among them. For that in chapter 8 I did not treat of that discipline against sinners, the purpose of my undertaking did not require it, as everyone sees. Afterwards they return to their sneering at Vedelius, as if he were standing as a defendant before a Papist tribunal for heresy. They also rail against me because, in order to prove that ecclesiastical discipline must be exercised against heretics even with anathema, I cited Paul's Epistle to the Galatians 1:8 and 1 Corinthians 16:22. Vedelius should be ashamed, they say, p. 146, not so much of his listless drowsiness as of his stupidity, since he cites Scripture so carelessly, and so perversely, to prove a matter of such weight; and to show that those passages do not bear on the matter, they bring out for us some new secret, which we discussed in Part III, book 2, chapter 8, §1, with their usual praise by which they commend heretics for piety and love of Jesus Christ, and again with their sneering against Vedelius standing before the Papist tribunal.

units.la: Sed isthæc convitia supinæ oscitantiæ & stupiditatis non in me tantum redundant, verùm in totam Ecclesiam veterem & recentem, quæ eorum locorum & similium argumento Hæreticis anathema dicendum esse recte credidit. Ita enim, ut unum saltem atque alterum exemplum allegem, Alexander Alexandrinus Episcopus, Vir non minoris sanctitatis quàm zeli ad defendendam orthodoxam doctrinam contra Arium, in Epistolâ ad Alexandrum Constantinopolitanum ait, quòd Arius, Achillas & reliqui eorum complices ἀποσυνάγωγοι τῆς ἐκκλησίας, ἀλόγειοι γεγόμενοι τῆς ἐυσεβοῦς ἡμῶν διδασκαλίας, κατὰ τὸν μακάριον παῦλον λέγοντα: εἴτις ὑμᾶς εὐαγγελίζεται παρ' ὃ παρελάβετε ἀνάθεμα ἔστω. quia defecerunt à pia nostra doctrina, ab Ecclesia communione separati sunt juxta S. Paulum dicentem: Si quis vobis Evanbis Evangelizaverit, praeter id quod accepistis anathema esto. Theodor. lib. 1. cap. 4. Et ut magis videas quâ temeritate hi homines me accusent stupiditatis atque inscitiæ, scito, optime Lector, hos homines per meum latus convitio stupiditatis & inscitiæ proscindere Episcopos ducentos & quinquaginta Romae, Hispaniae, Galliae, Italiae, Campaniae, Calabriae, Africae, Sardiniae, Pannoniae, Mysiae, Daciae, Dardaneae, Daciae inferioris, Macedoniae, Thessaliae, Achaiae, Epiri, Thraciae, Rhodopae, Asiae, Cariae, Bithyniae, Hellespontii, Phrygiae, Pisidiae, Cappadociae, Ponti, Phrygiae minoris, Ciliciae, Pamphiliae, Lydiae, insularum Cycladum, Aegypti, (inter quos fuit etiam magnus ille Athanasius) Thebaidis, Libyae, Galatiae, Palaestinae, Arabiae. Hi enim in Epistolâ suâ Synodicâ Sardicae scriptâ, (cujus initium est: Sanctum Concilium ab Episcopis Romae, Hispaniae, Galliae &c.) Arianis Episcopis anathema dicunt argumento loci eiusdem ad Galatas: ερωτον Sunto igitur vobis & omnibus anathema, quia verbum veritatis cauponati sunt; Est enim praeceptum Apostolicum, si quis vobis Evangelizaverit praeterquam quod accepistis, anathema esto. Ubi etiam Orthodoxi Episcopi exhortantur fideles ne communicent cum Haereticis, & huc referunt illud Apostoli 2. Cor. 6. 14. Quid communio luci cum tenebris, Beliali cum Christo? Theodor. lib. 2. c. 8. Haec non allego ob alium finem, quàm ut Lector judicet quâ fronte imò quàm superbè & leviter hi homines subinde, speciatim in re praesente stupiditatis, inscitiæ, ofcitantiæ me arguant; & ut intelligat quid solidae eruditionis habeant petulantes hi homines h. e. M. Episcopius & pauci aliquot pseudoministelli contra Edicta Illustrissimorum Ordinum venena sua spargentes per pagos & urbes, qui me hic audent supinae ofcitantiae & stupiditatis arguere, nescii ob summam imperitiam antiquitatis Ecclesiasticae se ea convitia dicere S. Athanasio & fere omnibus tunc temporis Episcopis Europae, Asiae, Africae, seu totius Christianitatis. Pudeat in aeternum hos homines!
units.tr: But these reproaches of listless drowsiness and stupidity fall not only on me but on the whole old and recent Church, which rightly believed, on the strength of those passages and similar ones, that anathema is to be pronounced on heretics. For example, to cite at least one or two instances, Alexander, Bishop of Alexandria, a man of no less holiness than zeal in defending orthodox doctrine against Arius, says in his Letter to Alexander of Constantinople that Arius, Achillas and their other accomplices, having been cast out of the synagogue of the Church and having become estranged from our pious teaching, are, according to the blessed Paul who says: "If anyone preaches to you a gospel other than what you have received, let him be anathema" [ἀποσυνάγωγοι τῆς ἐκκλησίας, ἀλόγειοι γεγόμενοι τῆς ἐυσεβοῦς ἡμῶν διδασκαλίας, κατὰ τὸν μακάριον παῦλον λέγοντα: εἴτις ὑμᾶς εὐαγγελίζεται παρ' ὃ παρελάβετε ἀνάθεμα ἔστω], because they have fallen away from our pious doctrine, they are separated from the communion of the Church, according to St. Paul saying: If anyone preaches a gospel to you other than what you have received, let him be anathema. Theodoret, book 1, chapter 4. And so that you may see with what rashness these men accuse me of stupidity and ignorance, know, best Reader, that these men, through my side, tear apart with the charge of stupidity and ignorance two hundred and fifty bishops of Rome, Spain, Gaul, Italy, Campania, Calabria, Africa, Sardinia, Pannonia, Moesia, Dacia, Dardania, Lower Dacia, Macedonia, Thessaly, Achaia, Epirus, Thrace, Rhodope, Asia, Caria, Bithynia, the Hellespont, Phrygia, Pisidia, Cappadocia, Pontus, Lesser Phrygia, Cilicia, Pamphylia, Lydia, the Cyclades, Egypt (among whom was also the great Athanasius), the Thebaid, Libya, Galatia, Palestine, Arabia. For these bishops, in their Synodal Letter written at Sardica (whose opening is: The holy council of bishops from Rome, Spain, Gaul, etc.), pronounce anathema on the Arian bishops, citing the same passage in Galatians: "Let them therefore be anathema to you and to all, because they have corrupted the word of truth; for it is the apostolic command: If anyone preaches to you other than what you have received, let him be anathema." Here the orthodox bishops also urge the faithful not to communicate with heretics, and they refer to that saying of the Apostle, 2 Corinthians 6:14: What fellowship has light with darkness, Belial with Christ? Theodoret, book 2, chapter 8. I cite these things for no other purpose than that the Reader may judge with what brazenness, indeed how proudly and lightly, these men keep accusing me of stupidity, ignorance and listlessness, especially in the present matter; and that he may understand what solid learning these impudent men have, namely M. Episcopius and a few pseudo-ministers who scatter their poison through villages and towns against the Edicts of the Most Illustrious Orders, who here dare to accuse me of listless drowsiness and stupidity, unaware that, through their great ignorance of ecclesiastical antiquity, they speak these reproaches against St. Athanasius and almost all the bishops of that time in Europe, Asia, Africa, that is, of the whole of Christendom. Let these men be ashamed forever!

units.la: 2. Postquam tandem p. 147. propositissent seu potius involvissent sententiam suam de Haeresi coercendâ, quae manifestius patebit ex sequentibus, veniunt ad dogmata sibi objecta. Primum est, quod in genere requirunt ut disciplina exerceatur citra noxam Haereticorum. Fatentur p. 148. & dicunt se loqui de noxâ corporali. Verum non tantum de noxâ corporali loquuntur, sed etiam nolunt permittere ut repellatur excommunicatus, si ritibus sacris ante reconciliationem sese immisceat; ne anathema nathema iis denuncietur, ne denique iis silentium imponatur, ut partim ex supra dictis patet, partim ex subsequentibus patebit.
units.tr: 2. After they had at last, on p. 147, put forward, or rather entangled, their opinion on restraining heresy, which will be more clearly seen from what follows, they come to the doctrines objected to them. The first is that they generally require that discipline be exercised without harm to heretics. They confess this on p. 148 and say that they speak of bodily harm. But they do not speak only of bodily harm; they also refuse to allow an excommunicated person to be repelled if, before reconciliation, he mingles in sacred rites, so that anathema is not pronounced on them, and so that silence is not finally imposed on them, as partly appears from what was said above and partly will appear from what follows.

units.la: 3. Porro objeceram ipsis, quod permittunt sectae cuilibet exercendam disciplinam Ecclesiasticam contra dissentientes reciproce & ex lege talionis, & ostenderam, exinde manifestum esse Arminianos illudere orbi doctrina sua de mutua tolerantia: Si enim ita reciproce licet exercere disciplinam Ecclesiasticam omnibus sectis adversus dissentientes, quomodo, dicebam, mutua tolerantia ipsorum seu communio spiritualis & pax illa Ecclesiae, quam pollicentur subsistere poterit? annon igitur ista pax illusoria est? Ad hoc argumentum ex quo manifestissime apparet impostura ipsorum qua hactenus illuserent toti orbi, illi ne verbum quidem respondent sed sicco pede illud transeunt. Ostenderam etiam, eos perperam facere, dum Ecclesiasticam disciplinam permittunt exercendam, saltem sub hac conditione duplici, salvo studio pietatis & obsequii debiti Magistratui. Et dixeram, eos ante omnia debuisse dicere salvo veritatis studio, absque qua nec vera pietas esse nec verum & Christiano homine dignum ac Deo gratum obsequium erga Magistratum praestari potest. Quia autem veritatis conditionem non addant, ostendi sequi exinde eos omnis generis Haereticos, pestes veritatis divinae, in Ecclesiam introducere velle. Ad hoc etiam nihil respondent, sed id tacito pede transeunt.
units.tr: 3. Further, I had objected to them that they permit every sect to exercise ecclesiastical discipline against dissenters in turn and by the law of retaliation, and I had shown that from this it is evident that the Arminians mock the world with their doctrine of mutual toleration: For if it is thus lawful for all sects to exercise ecclesiastical discipline reciprocally against dissenters, how, I said, can their mutual toleration, or that spiritual communion and that peace of the Church which they promise, subsist? Is not that peace therefore illusory? To this argument, by which their imposture, with which they have hitherto mocked the whole world, is most manifestly exposed, they do not reply even a word, but pass it over with dry feet. I had also shown that they act wrongly in permitting ecclesiastical discipline to be exercised, at least under this twofold condition, saving the zeal for piety and the due obedience owed to the magistrate. And I had said that they ought above all to have said saving the zeal for truth, without which neither true piety nor the obedience that is worthy of a Christian man and pleasing to God toward the magistrate can be rendered. But since they do not add the condition of truth, I showed that it follows from this that they wish to introduce into the Church every kind of heretic, the pests of divine truth. To this too they reply nothing, but pass it over with silent feet.

units.la: 4. Secundum dogma est: Licere Haereticis excommunicare veram Ecclesiam. Negant hoc, & dicunt se dixisse licere Haeretico Vedelium Haereticum & infidelem excommunicare. Et ad coccysmum suum de Vedelio, de judicio ipsius, & pari jure Haereticorum & meo redeunt, atque inter alia calumniantur me docere verbum Dei obligare hominum conscientias ita ut ne quidem judicium cujusque suum intervenire velim. Et addunt se vocem Licere sumere non pro jure sed pro licentia, qua nulla vi aut auctoritate coercenda est quale tu cum tuis usurpas & usurpare tibi licere vis inter omnes alias sectas quae te Haereticum censent p. 148. item p. 149. Cum licere aliis in Vedelianam sectam idem dicunt Remonstrantes quod secta Vedeliana in alios sibi licere credit; verbum impersonale LICET usurpant eodem sensu quo illud usurpat Vedelius, quando libertatem conscientiae in eo positam esse dicit, quod cuique privatim sentire liceat apud se quod libet &c. & quo licere dicimus alicui bona sua dilapidare, jurgari, litigare, aliaque similia peccata committere contra quae publica poena constituta non est. Haec omnia ne verbulum quidem veritatis habent. Nam in Apologia quando dicunt: Id quod nobis in alios, idem aliis licet in nos no loquuntur de Vedelio, de quo tunc ne cogitarant quidem cum ista scribescriberent; nec etiam de Reformatis tantum : sed loquuntur generatim de omnibus coetibus Christiani nominis, inter quos profecto est aliqua Ecclesia vera, quaecunque tandem illa sit (nam de hac re nunc non est contendendi locus) imo de se ipsis loquuntur. Verba eorum sunt Apol. c. 24. f. 277. a. Quilibet secta eam (disciplinam Ecclesiasticam) exercere poterit pro dicta nine conscientiae suae, & quod NOBIS in alios, idem aliis licebit in NOS. Aut suntne & ipsi Haretici & infidelis Vedelius, aut de secta Vedeliana? ut hic maledice & scurriliter loquuntur. Quare falsum est, quod aiunt se dixisse in Apologia Licere aliis in Vedelianam sectam idem quod Vedeliana secta in alios sibi licere credit. Quod dicunt me statuere verbo Dei simpliciter obligari conscientias, ita ut ne judicium cujuscunq; suum intervenire velim, profecto contra propriam conscientiam dicunt. Nam ipsi cap. 6. p. 135. allegant verba mea quibus contrarium expresse profiteor, & dicunt hanc esse meam doctrinam, nimirum judicium requiri in ea re. Nam haec ipsa, inquiunt, doctrina, est tua doctrina quam hoc ipso in loco profiteris; & subdunt verba mea: Verum quidem est firmam persuasionem, judicium ac notitiam requiri ad fidem generandam in homine. En honestatem ac candorem horum hominum!
units.tr: 4. The second dogma is: It is lawful for heretics to excommunicate the true Church. They deny this and say that what they said was: it is lawful for a heretic to excommunicate Vedelius, a heretic and an unbeliever. In their noisy complaint about Vedelius, about his judgment, and about the equal right of heretics and of me, they go on to slander me, saying that I teach that the Word of God binds men's consciences so firmly that I do not even want anyone's own judgment to intervene. They add that they take the word Licere not in the sense of a right but in the sense of a licence, which needs no force or authority to restrain it, "such as you and yours usurp, and such as you want to be allowed to usurp over all the other sects that consider you a heretic" (p. 148). Likewise, on p. 149: "The Remonstrants use the words 'it is lawful for others against the Vedelian sect' in the same sense in which the Vedelian sect believes it is lawful for itself against others. They use the impersonal verb LICET in the same sense in which Vedelius uses it when he says that liberty of conscience consists in this, that each person may privately think whatever he likes to himself, and in which we say that it is lawful for someone to squander his goods, to quarrel, to litigate, and to commit other similar sins for which no public penalty has been established." None of this has even a grain of truth. For in the Apology, when they say: What we are allowed to do against others, others are equally allowed to do against us, they are not speaking of Vedelius, whom they were not even thinking of when they wrote those words, nor only of the Reformed, but they are speaking generally of all the assemblies of the Christian name, among which there is certainly some true Church, whatever it may be (for this is not the place to argue about that now), and indeed they are speaking of themselves. Their words are in Apology ch. 24, p. 277a: Any sect may exercise that ecclesiastical discipline according to its conscience, and what is allowed to US against others, the same will be allowed to others against US. Or are they themselves heretics and an unbeliever, like Vedelius, or of the Vedelian sect? as they speak here, maliciously and scurrilously. Therefore it is false that they said in the Apology: it is lawful for others against the Vedelian sect in the same way as the Vedelian sect believes it is lawful for itself against others. When they say that I maintain that consciences are simply bound by the Word of God, so that I do not want anyone's own judgment to intervene, they certainly speak against their own conscience. For in ch. 6, p. 135, they quote my own words, in which I expressly profess the opposite, and they say that this is my doctrine, namely that judgment is required in this matter. "For this very doctrine," they say, "is your doctrine, which you profess in this very place; and they add my words: It is indeed true that a firm persuasion, judgment and knowledge are required to generate faith in a man." See the honesty and candour of these men!

units.la: Quod dicunt se vocem LICET sumere non pro jure sed tantum pro licentia, speciatim mea; in eo rursus contra conscientiam suam loquuntur, ut patet primo ex dictis. Etenim loquuntur generatim, ut dixi, de omnibus coetibus Christianis, inter quos profecto est aliqua Ecclesia vera, quae certe quando eos qui vere Haeretici sunt excommunicat, facit illud non ex licentia usurpata, sed ex jure sibi tradito a Christo. Deinde loquuntur ut vidimus etiam de se ipsis. Igitur quando me hic Haereticum & infidelem vocant adeoque communione Ecclesiae indignum judicant, judicium illud proficiscitur aut ex usurpata saltem licentia, aut ex jure; Si ex jure: Ergo falsum est, quod dicunt se loqui saltem de licentia, qualis est male agentium & peccantium. Si autem ex licentia; Ergo sunt αὐτοκατάκριτοι & a propria conscientia convicti & condemnati in eo, quod me Haereticum & infidelem vocant, adeoque indignum communione Ecclesiae judicant; utpote qui illud jure non faciunt, sed saltem ex licentia, quam insolenter & petulanter sibi sumunt. Tertio expresse illud hic jus appellant: At illi Haeretici sunt, inquies. At cur tu non es Haereticus quaero ego? Cur tibi licet illos Haereticos censere, & non illis te? Judicium tuum Jus tibi non dat majus aut amplius in illos, quam illis judicium suum in te. Et in Responf. ad Excerp. CII. DD. Proff. Leydd. dicunt: Par omnium sectarum sectarum est ratio. Nullum secta ulla privilegium habet p. 126. Obiter observetur quod hic dicunt p. 148. Etiamsi verum sit judicium quo Haresreos aliquis reus peragitur; tamen par jus esse Hareticorum & recte sentientium, seu idem licere illis in recte sentientes, quod recte sentientibus in illos. Hic verum quidem est: Haereticos id sibi arrogare. Nam ut homo injustus abominationi est justis: ita justus abominationi est impio Proverb. 29. 27. Sed ut Par. I. lib. 2. c. 8. monui, falsum est Haereticis id jus competere.
units.tr: As to their saying that they take the word LICET not as a right but only as a licence, and especially my use of it, they again speak against their own conscience, as is clear, first, from what has been said. For they speak generally, as I said, of all Christian assemblies, among which there certainly is some true Church, which surely, when it excommunicates those who are truly heretics, does so not by a licence it has usurped but by a right handed to it by Christ. Second, as we have seen, they also speak of themselves. Therefore, when they here call me a heretic and an unbeliever, and so judge me unworthy of communion with the Church, that judgment proceeds either from a licence at least usurped or from a right. If from a right, then it is false that they say they speak only of a licence, such as belongs to those who behave badly and sin. If from a licence, then they are self-condemned (αὐτοκατάκριτοι) and convicted and condemned by their own conscience in calling me a heretic and an unbeliever, and so judging me unworthy of communion with the Church; since they do not do this by right, but only by the licence which they take insolently and wantonly. Third, they expressly call this a right: "But they are heretics, you will say. But why are you not a heretic, I ask? Why is it allowed to you to judge them heretics, and not to them to judge you? Your judgment gives you no greater or wider right over them than their judgment gives them over you." And in their Response to Excerpt CII of the Professors of Leiden they say: The reason is the same for all sects. No sect has any privilege (p. 126). It may be noted in passing that they say here, p. 148: Even if the judgment by which someone is brought to trial as a heretic were true, nevertheless the right of heretics and of those who think rightly is equal, or it is equally lawful for them against those who think rightly as it is for those who think rightly against them. Here it is indeed true that heretics claim this for themselves. For an unjust man is an abomination to the just, and the just is an abomination to the wicked (Prov. 29. 27). But, as I warned in Par. I, lib. 2, ch. 8, it is false that this right belongs to heretics.

units.la: Falsum denique est, quòd dicunt me Libertatem conscientiae in eo ponere, quòd cuique privatim sentire liceat apud se quod libet. Dixi quidem Par. I. lib. 1. c. 3. ad quem locum hi homines forte respiciunt, Haereticis non fieri injuriam, nec vim fieri conscientiae eorum quando actus externi eorum impediuntur: Sed libertatem conscientiae in eo positam esse quod illi dicunt, nullibi dixi; nec etiam id ex iis quae loco allegato extant, sequitur. Nisi forte existiment Arminiani nullam libertatem conscientiarum esse quàm quae Haereticis competit; qui manifestum in omnibus suis scriptis (de Arminianis loquor) faciunt, se non intelligere quid sit Libertas conscientiarum, nec scire discrimen inter libertatem conscientiarum quae praecepti & inter eam quae permissionis est. De qua materia aliquando, ubi Deus voluerit, ex professo acturi sumus.
units.tr: Finally, it is false that they say I place liberty of conscience in this, that each person may privately think whatever he likes to himself. I did indeed say in Par. I, lib. 1, ch. 3, which is perhaps the passage these men have in mind: No injury is done to heretics, nor is any force done to their conscience, when their external acts are hindered. But I nowhere said that liberty of conscience consists in what they say, nor does this follow from what stands in the passage cited. Unless perhaps the Arminians think there is no liberty of conscience except that which belongs to heretics; and in all their writings (I am speaking of the Arminians) they make it plain that they do not understand what liberty of conscience is, nor know the difference between that liberty of conscience which is a matter of command and that which is a matter of permission. We shall, God willing, some time treat this subject expressly.

units.la: 5. Tertium dogma est: praestare fortassis non separare Haereticum a communione Ecclesiae, quàm eum unquam separare ab illa. Fatentur: sed dicunt, se non loqui de Haeretico eo qui verè Haereticus est, sed de errante, quatenus a peccatore distinguitur, & quidem errante probo pioque & pacem cum Christianis ambiente ac volente. Hoc est uno verbo; dicunt se loqui de Haeretico prout ea vox sumitur ab Ecclesiâ quae Deum in tribus personis adorat, qualis est Antitrinitarius, speciatim Socinianus Haereticus. Tales enim non habent pro Haereticis sed pro hominibus piis, piissimis, sanctissimis, & pro verâ Ecclesiâ Dei. Hoc nobis sufficit: nec enim aliud volui. Quod attinet ad ea, quibus in me invehuntur: Vedelius savus & crudelis medicus est. Ad ferrum statim & ad ignem recurrit. Urendum, secandum est, in quosvis saviendum extremis remediis &c. illae merae calumniae sunt. Ego enim, ut suprà etiam monui, sententiam meam nondum dixi, de modo quo Haeretici coercendi sunt; quam si illi nôssent (nôsse autem eam nondum possunt, utpote qui ex verbo Dei & experientiâ veteris Ecclesiae nondum didicerunt quomodo coercendi sint Haeretici) forte moderatiorem & mitiorē me dicerent, quàm ipsi putant. Nec enim verbum Dei crudelitatē & saevitiem, sed justitiam & prudentiam in Haereticis coercendis requirit.
units.tr: 5. The third dogma is: It is perhaps better not to separate a heretic from communion with the Church than ever to separate him from it. They admit this, but they say that they are not speaking of a heretic who is truly a heretic, but of an erring person, as distinguished from a sinner, and indeed of an erring person who is upright and pious and who seeks and wants peace with Christians. In a word, they say they are speaking of a heretic in the sense in which that word is taken by the Church which worships God in three persons, such as an Antitrinitarian, especially a Socinian heretic. For such men they do not regard as heretics but as pious, most pious, most holy men and as the true Church of God. This is enough for us; for I wanted nothing else. As for what they rail against me: Vedelius is a savage and cruel doctor. He runs at once to the sword and to the fire. He must burn, he must cut, he must rage against anyone with extreme remedies, and so on, these are pure calumnies. For I, as I have also said above, have not yet given my opinion on the manner in which heretics are to be restrained; if they knew it (and they cannot yet know it, since they have not learned from the Word of God and from the experience of the ancient Church how heretics are to be restrained), perhaps they would call me more moderate and gentle than they think. For the Word of God requires in restraining heretics not cruelty and savagery, but justice and prudence.

units.la: Similis farinæ est, quod dicunt constare quàm leviter conniveam ad mulio‑rum carnalia opera &c. Quod si autem Ecclesiæ aliquæ Reformatæ erga homines impios, comessatores, compotatores, prodigos, rixosos &c: non utuntur disciplinâ Ecclesiasticâ, id ad me non pertinet. Certè Genevensis Ecclesia, ob quam sæpè mihi convitiantur, quia in eâ docui, ta‑libus hominibus non parcit, sed actiones vitiosas de quibus constat & scandala severâ disciplinâ castigat; quam utrum hi homines (qui tantopere hîc zelum disciplinæ Ecclesiasticæ erga peccatores venditant) ἀνυ‑πόρατοι ferre possent si Genevæ essent, an verò potius omnia ibi turbaturi essent, & conaturi sursum deorsum cuncta vertere non secus ac in Belgio, unicuique dijudicandum relinquo.
units.tr: They are of the same kind when they say that it is well known how lightly I connive at the carnal works of women, and so on. But if some Reformed Churches do not use church discipline against impious men, drunkards, revellers, spendthrifts, brawlers and the like, that is no concern of mine. The Genevan Church, for which they often revile me because I taught in it, certainly does not spare such men. It punishes with severe discipline the vicious actions and scandals that are proven. Whether these men, who here so loudly flaunt their zeal for church discipline toward sinners, could endure this if they were at Geneva, or would rather be stirring up everything there and trying to turn all things upside down, as they do in Belgium, I leave for each reader to judge. It is intolerable [ἀνυπόρατοι].

units.la: 6. Quartum dogma est : Excommunicationem esse voluntariam tantum‑modo secessionem ab aliquo : item, sufficere ad excommunicationem, ut Ecclesia significet excommunicando, sibi non licere amplius sponte suâ atque ultrò cum illo tanquam cum Christiano sacra facere : item, si excommunicatus obtemperare nolit, cogi Ecclesiam eum admittere ad sacra. Fatentur totum hoc; postquam sophisticè & veteratorie pro more suo, ut Lectori imponerent, divul‑sissent objectionis sibi à me factæ partes, & illius partem saltem arripuissent, ut inde evincerent me mihi contradicere ibi ubi nulla ne species quidem contradictionis est, si tota sententia exhibeatur; quod ipsi coguntur fateri, solventes contradictionem quam finxerant: At dices inquit Vedelius, Ecclesiam significare sibi non licere &c. Ita igitur fatentur dogma illud. Negant saltem illud malum illusorium & noxium esse. Objeceram enim ipsis, eos illudere istâ ratione disciplinæ Ecclesiasticæ, & Hæreticos aliosque impios introducere in Ecclesiam, præsertim dum dicunt, Ecclesiam teneri excommunicato significare, sibi non licere sponte suâ atque ultrò cum eo tanquam cum Christiano sacra facere, quòd si excommunicatus obtemperare nolit, teneri Ecclesiam eum admittere. Hic respondent; hoc non esse illudere disciplinæ Ecclesiasticæ, quia scilicet Ecclesia tunc nom communicet cum eo tanquam cum Christiano, sed cum violento invasore. Rationem addunt: Quid enim faciet Ecclesia, inquiunt, inprimis si exigua, si authoritate destituta & sub cruce cogatur vivere? Aut vis inferenda est, aut ferenda vis, aut abrumpenda sacra &c. & concludunt licitam esse hanc Ecclesiæ communionem, quia non licet Ecclesiæ sine illis eam facere nisi vis illicita adhibeatur. Ita'ne Arminiani? Quasi verò præter hos modos alius licitus ac legitimus non detur! nimirùm resistentia quâ fit, ut ordine ac modo conveniente per personam aut, si una non sufficiat per personas Ecclesiasticas, sive Ecclesiæ & sacro ritui inservientes vis, quam invasor inferre vult prudenter præveniatur. Inquiet M. Episcopius, hâc enim redeunt quæ hoc loco dicit: at si vis præventa prudenter non fit, sed invasor involet in locum conventus qui sub cruce peragitur: quid tunc faciendum? Respondeo primò: an'non igitur hi homines orbi illudunt, qui ex casu extraordinario, qui (ut liberaliter dem ipsis eum aliquando contigisse) non nisi rarissime contingere potest, nobis excommunicationis novam naturam formant ac fingunt? Deinde posito hoc casu: an'non præstat illatam vim ab invasore tali repellere ejectione ex loco conventus per eos quibus ordinis in Ecclesiâ conservatio commissa est; quod non magis est vim illegitimam inferre invasori Ecclesiæ, quàm vis illegitima infertur ab illis qui accurrunt ad clamorem virginis cui vim inferre vult nebulo aliquis, & eum repellunt ac virginem manibus ejus eripiunt: an'non, inquam, hoc præstat, quàm generalem maximam formare, quâ contra expressum verbum Dei statuitur, Ecclesiam teneri admittere excommunicatum non resipiscentem, sed adeò perseverantem in malo ut veteri crimini novum addat, & profanare Sacramentum velit? Aut, si Arminianis etiam ista legitima resistentia & ejectio è loco conventus displiceat, vel impossibilis videatur ob multitudinem quam p. 151. fingunt plurium excommunicatorum qui invasores esse velint: quis impediat ministrum quò minus manum suam abstineat, eam non extendat & ea sacramentum non administret istis invasoribus? Hoc enim in æternum non licet ministro Ecclesiæ, ob prohibitionem Dominicam, quæ non permittit, ut porrigat Sacramentum excommunicato non resipiscenti sed augenti malitiam & impietatem suam. Sed quis non videt hæc, quæ Arminiani dicunt, nihil aliud esse quàm merum prætextum quo palliare volunt doctrinam suam impiam & detestandam?
units.tr: 6. The fourth dogma is this: that excommunication is merely a voluntary secession from someone; likewise, that it is enough for excommunication that the Church signify by excommunicating that it is no longer lawful for it to perform sacred acts with him of its own accord and freely, as with a Christian; likewise, if the excommunicated person is unwilling to obey, the Church must be compelled to admit him to the sacred rites. They confess all of this. But after they had, in their usual sophistical and crafty way, in order to deceive the reader, torn apart the parts of my objection and seized only a part of it, so that from that they might prove that I contradict myself where there is not even the appearance of a contradiction if the whole statement is set out, they are forced to admit this, resolving the contradiction they had invented: But you will say, says Vedelius, that the Church signifies that it is not lawful for it, etc. So they do admit that dogma. They deny only that this evil is illusory and harmful. For I had charged them with mocking church discipline in this way and introducing heretics and other impious persons into the Church, especially when they say: the Church is bound to signify to the excommunicated person that it is no longer lawful for it of its own accord and freely to perform sacred acts with him as with a Christian; but if the excommunicated person is unwilling to obey, the Church is bound to admit him. Here they reply that this is not mocking church discipline, because, clearly, the Church then does not communicate with him as with a Christian, but with a violent invader. They add a reason: For what will the Church do, they say, first of all, if it is small, destitute of authority, and forced to live under the cross? Either force must be applied, or force must be endured, or the sacred rites must be broken off, etc. And they conclude that this communion of the Church is lawful, because the Church may not practise it without them unless unlawful force is used. Is that so, Arminians? As if, apart from these ways, no other lawful and proper way were available! Namely, resistance, by which force that the invader wishes to apply is prudently forestalled, in an orderly and fitting manner, through a person, or, if one person is not enough, through ecclesiastical persons, that is, those who serve the Church and the sacred rite. M. Episcopius will object, for these are the things he says at this point: but if the force is not prudently forestalled, and the invader rushes into the place of the assembly that is conducted under the cross, what then is to be done? I answer, first: do not these men mock the world, who from an extraordinary case, which (even if I grant them that it has ever happened to them) can happen only very rarely, form and fashion for us a new nature of excommunication? Next, given this case: is it not better to repel the force applied by such an invader by ejecting him from the place of assembly through those to whom the preservation of order in the Church has been entrusted? This is no more an unlawful use of force against an invader of the Church than the unlawful force used by those who run to the cry of a maiden whom some scoundrel wishes to assault, and who drive him off and snatch the maiden from his hands. Is it not, I say, better to do this than to frame a general maxim by which, against the express word of God, it is laid down that the Church is bound to admit an excommunicated person who does not repent, but persists so obstinately in evil that he adds a new crime to an old one and wishes to profane the Sacrament? Or, if even this lawful resistance and ejection from the place of assembly displease the Arminians, or seem impossible because of the multitude of several excommunicated persons, whom they imagine wishing to be invaders (p. 151), who would prevent the minister from keeping his hand back, from not extending it, and from not administering the sacrament to those invaders? For the minister of the Church may never do this, on account of the Lord's prohibition, which does not permit him to give the Sacrament to an excommunicated person who does not repent, but increases his malice and impiety. But who does not see that these things the Arminians say are nothing but a mere pretext by which they wish to cover their impious and detestable doctrine?

units.la: Porrò, quia dixeram: Ita'ne Ecclesia (si scilicet tali excommunicationis modo, qualem Arminiani hic præscribunt, utatur) excusabitur coràm Deo? Ita'ne castitatem suam ab adulteris h. e. Hæreticis & profanis &c. sartam tectam conservabit? Non magis profecto, quam si sponsa sive uxor ab adultero sollicitata dicat sibi non licere sponte sua atque ultrò se cum ipso tanquam cum marito miscere &c. Hic respondent hi homines innocentissimi scilicet: Quid est obsecro calumniari OPTIME DICTA si hoc non est? Et dicunt Ecclesiam excusari ideo coràm Deo quia vi extorta est communio. Imò inquam ego, quid est hypocritam agere & orbi imponere velle; si ita respondere hypocriticum & illusorium non est? Iudica enim tu, pie Lector, an istud dogma Arminianum ex optime dictis fit, quod mandato Christi repugnat ; per consequens an'ne ipsos calumniatus sim ? De communione vi extorta quod dicunt, nihil est. Ecclesiae enim, ut ostendi, communio extorqueri non potest. Praestet enim in omnem eventum mori , quàm Christo non obedire. Hoc est quod Par. I. loco de quo quaestio, est dixeram , neminem Pastores seu totam Ecclesiam ad eam communionem cogere posse. Ob hanc causam hi homines p. 151. cum convitiis & contumelia me inexperientiae accusant & dicunt : nimium multa exempla hujus rei in foederatis Provinciis esse. Sed hoc falsum est : dabo enim ipsis occurrere exempla invasorum, sed nullum exemplum dari potest quo ostendatur cogi posse Ecclesiam ad communicandum cum invasoribus. Si communicat Ecclesia cum iis, volens communicat. Nemo qui cum Haeretico, infideli, idololatra, excommunicato, adeoque Ethnico (pro tali enim habendum esse excommunicatum Christus docet ) communicat, quin volens communicet, nequidem si mortis metu adactus id faciat. Hoc est quod Cyprianus ait sermone de lapsis, h. e. iis qui mortis metu communicârant cum idololatris : Non excusat oppressum necessitas criminis, ubi crimen est voluntatis.
units.tr: Moreover, since I had said: Will the Church be thus excused before God (namely, if it uses that kind of excommunication which the Arminians prescribe here)? Will it thus keep its chastity intact from adulterers, that is, from heretics and profane persons, etc.? Certainly no more than if a bride or wife, solicited by an adulterer, said that it was not lawful for her of her own accord and freely to mingle with him as with her husband, etc. Here these most innocent men reply: What, I beg you, is it to slander the BEST-SAID WORDS if this is not so? And they say that the Church is excused before God for this reason, that communion was extorted by force. But I reply: what is it to play the hypocrite and wish to deceive the world, if to answer thus is not hypocritical and illusory? Judge for yourself, pious reader, whether this Arminian dogma is made out of the best-said words, when it conflicts with the command of Christ; and consequently whether I have not slandered them. What they say about communion extorted by force is nothing. For, as I have shown, the communion of the Church cannot be extorted. It is better in every event to die than not to obey Christ. This is what I said in Part I, in the passage under discussion, that no ministers or whole Church can compel anyone to that communion. For this reason these men (p. 151) accuse me with insults and abuse of inexperience, and say: There are far too many examples of this thing in the United Provinces. But this is false: for I will grant them examples of invaders, but no example can be given by which it is shown that the Church can be compelled to communicate with invaders. If the Church communicates with them, it communicates willingly. No one who communicates with a heretic, an unbeliever, an idolater, an excommunicated person, and so with a heathen (for Christ teaches that an excommunicated person must be held as such), communicates otherwise than willingly, not even if he does so compelled by fear of death. This is what Cyprian says in his sermon on the lapsed, that is, those who from fear of death had communicated with idolaters: The necessity of the crime does not excuse the one who was overcome, where the crime is of the will.

units.la: Caeterum ostenderam p. 216. ex verbo Dei speciatim exemplo Pauli communionem cum excommunicato non resipiscente Ecclesiae simpliciter prohibitam esse ; item excommunicationem non in sola secessione consistere, sed etiam in vi spirituali, nominatim in anathematizatione : ad hoc hi homines ne verbo quidem respondent, sed sicco pede transeunt illud. Ex his omnibus apparet, quàm abominabilis doctrina sit Theologorum istorum, & quàm ipsi detestandi sint, qui, ut Haereticos, speciatim Antitrinitarios in Ecclesiam introducere possint, doctrinam suam detestandam de excommunicatione palliare volunt casu extraordinario & inusitato, (contra quem tamen certissimum remedium est etiamsi non violetur disciplina ) nullâ habita ratione regulae & praecepti à Spiritu S. traditi, cui profecto nihil, nedum casus aliquis extraordinarius, ne dicam fictus, praejudicare potest.
units.tr: Moreover, I had shown at p. 216, from the word of God, and specifically from the example of Paul, that communion with an excommunicated person who does not repent is simply forbidden to the Church; likewise that excommunication does not consist in mere secession, but also in spiritual power, namely in anathematization. These men do not answer even a word to this, but pass over it with dry feet. From all this it appears how abominable the doctrine of these theologians is, and how they themselves are to be detested, who, in order to be able to introduce heretics, especially Antitrinitarians, into the Church, wish to cover their detestable doctrine of excommunication with an extraordinary and unusual case (against which, nevertheless, there is a most certain remedy, even if church discipline is not violated), with no regard for the rule and precept handed down by the Holy Spirit, which assuredly nothing can prejudge, much less some extraordinary case, not to say a fictitious one.

units.la: 7. Quintum dogma est : non licere Ecclesiae ita exercere disciplinam in Haereticos, ut consequenter Magistratum officu sui moneat h. e. ut Haereticos coerceat. Fatentur p. 151. se hoc docere, & mentiuntur me non solùm incarcerationem aut exilium, sed etiam flagellationem, suspendium, decollationem & vivicomburium intelligere. Et addunt : coercitione corporali Haereticorum posita necessario tandem in ultimum supplicium eam desinere. Quod etiam falsum esse docet experientia veteris Ecclesiæ, in quâ etiam coërcuerunt Orthodoxi Imperatores Hæreticos, sed ἀναμαχητί[?], sine sanguinis effusione. Sed hi homines nos metiuntur ex suo genio, & ex proposito quo statuerunt apud animum suum durioribus remediis coërcere Reformatos ut ostendi Par. II. Quæ duriora remedia qualia sint, patet ex eo, quod hoc loco, ut & in Apologiâ dicunt, in coërcitione eorum quibus non permittitur libertas conscientiarum, necessariò tandem ad sanguinem veniendum esse. Talis igitur est coërcitio quam ex propria confessione istorum hominum adversus Reformatos ipsi moliuntur. Cavete vobis Orthodoxi Magistratus, Doctores, populi ab huius sectæ molimínibus, & maturè ea tandem prævenite, ex officii vestri ratione ac præscripto Dei, eâ quâ par est prudentiâ & vigilantiâ: alioquin profectò sententiam quam adversum vos pronunciatam jam videtis ab Arminianis ministris, vos & liberi vestri executioni ab ipsis mandatum iri experiemini. Nî hoc faciatis, memineritis aliquando mei. Agitur non tantùm de Religione vestrâ, sed etiam de vitâ vestrâ, & liberorum vestrorum. Multi sunt qui hæc non considerant. Videant ne nimis serò id expendant. Si antè actorum & gestorum ab iis hominibus in Belgio obliti sunt (quæ docent quàm crudeles, violenti, & sanguinarii isti Theologi sunt) futurum caveant. Id profectò alioquin totum in capita ipsorum recidet, quod Deus clementer avertat.
units.tr: 7. The fifth dogma is: it is not lawful for the Church to exercise discipline against heretics in such a way that it consequently warns the magistrate, that is, that he should restrain heretics. They confess (p. 151) that they teach this, and they falsely say that I understand by it not only imprisonment or exile, but also flogging, hanging, beheading and burning alive. They add that once bodily restraint of heretics is imposed, it necessarily ends at last in capital punishment. Experience of the ancient Church shows this to be false, since orthodox emperors also restrained heretics there, but without any fighting [ἀναμαχητί], that is, without bloodshed. But these men measure us by their own disposition, and by the purpose they have settled in their minds, to restrain the Reformed with harsher remedies, as I showed in Part II. What these harsher remedies are is clear from this: in this place, as also in their Apology, they say that in restraining those to whom liberty of conscience is not granted, one must necessarily come at last to blood. Such, then, is the coercion which these men, by their own confession, are devising against the Reformed. Beware, you orthodox magistrates, teachers and peoples, of the schemes of this sect, and forestall them in time, from the reasoning of your office and the precept of God, with the prudence and vigilance that befits you. Otherwise you will surely find that the sentence, which you already see pronounced against you by the Arminian ministers, will be carried out on you and your children. If you do not do this, you will remember me one day. It is not only your religion that is at stake, but also your life and the lives of your children. Many do not consider these things. Let them see that they do not weigh them too late. If they have forgotten the deeds done by those men in Belgium (which show how cruel, violent and bloodthirsty these theologians are), let them beware of what is to come. Otherwise it will all fall back on their own heads, which God in his mercy avert.

units.la: Pergo: Posthæc igitur Arminiani ad coccysmum suum de Vedelio redeunt, & dicunt Scripturam sacram docere, Magistratum non ab Ecclesiâ de eâ re monendum esse. Proferant tabulas & loca. Allegant etiam antiquitatem priscam, sed salsissimè & pro imperitiâ suâ. Dicunt Arianos primos fuisse, qui auxilium Cæsarum implorârunt contra Orthodoxos. Quod primò ad rem non facit: quæstio enim est de coërcitione non Orthodoxorum, sed Hæreticorum verè sic dictorum. Deinde falsum est; Arianos primos implorâsse auxilium Cæsarum contra dissentientes. Nam verum quidem est Arianos primos post Judæos & Ethnicos sævitiam Cæsarum implorâsse contra Orthodoxos, adeoque inter eos qui Christi nomen præ se ferunt primos usos esse crudelitate adversum illos: sed falsò est, eos inter Christianos auxilium Magistratus primos implorâsse contra dissentientes. Nam antea Ethnici Imperatoris auxilium contra Paulum Samosatenum (qui ex Coryphæis Socinianarum blasphemiarum Doctoribus fuit) implorârant Orthodoxi & obtinuerant, ut videre est apud Eusebium lib. 7. cap. 24. Quod aiunt Arminiani de Episcopis qui lege talionis uti noluerunt contra Arianos, illud ad rem non facit. Nam etsi ea lege usi non sint, & merito, h. e. saevitia & crudelitate illa horrenda qua Ariani per caedes, suspendia, ignes, aquas grassati fuerant in Orthodoxos, tamen coercitionem eorum, ut & aliorum Haereticorum postulârunt a Magistratu, ut patet ex antiquitate, cuius hi homines ignorantissimi sunt, & cuius imperitia multum adjumenti ad generandas haereses confert, prout experientia Nestorii docet, teste Socrate lib. 7. c. 32. Quod de Priscillianistis dicunt, & Bongomili exustione, etiam ad rem & contra nos non facit; cui accedit, quod, cum priscae antiquitatis exemplis pugnare se velle dicant, recentius exemplum proferunt illud Bongomili, quod contigit ante annos tantum quingentos, nimirum sub Henrico Quarto & Alexio Comneno Impp. circa annum 1118.
units.tr: Going on, the Arminians then return to their cackling about Vedelius and say that Holy Scripture teaches that the magistrate is not to be warned about such a matter by the Church. Let them produce their tables and passages. They also allege ancient antiquity, but very foolishly and out of their ignorance. They say that the Arians were the first to implore the help of the emperors against the orthodox. This, first, has no bearing on the matter: the question concerns the restraint not of the orthodox but of heretics properly so called. Second, it is false that the Arians were the first to implore the emperors' help against dissenters. It is true that the Arians, after the Jews and pagans, were the first to implore the emperors' cruelty against the orthodox, and so among those who bear the name of Christ they were the first to use cruelty against them. But it is false that among Christians they were the first to seek the magistrate's help against dissenters. For earlier the orthodox had implored the help of a pagan emperor against Paul of Samosata (one of the leaders of the Socinian blasphemies), and had obtained it, as can be seen in Eusebius, book 7, chapter 24. What the Arminians say about the bishops who would not use the law of retaliation against the Arians does not bear on the matter. For although those bishops did not use that law, and rightly so, given the horrible savagery and cruelty with which the Arians had raged against the orthodox through murders, hangings, fires and drownings, nevertheless they sought the restraint of the Arians, as of other heretics, from the magistrate. This is clear from antiquity, of which these men are very ignorant, and whose ignorance contributes much to the generation of heresies, as the experience of Nestorius teaches, witness Socrates, book 7, chapter 32. What they say about the Priscillianists and the burning of the Bogomils does not bear on the matter either, nor is it against us. Add to this that, although they say they wish to contend with examples of the ancient past, they bring forward a more recent example, that of the Bogomils, which happened only five hundred years ago, namely under the emperors Henry IV and Alexius Comnenus, around the year 1118.

units.la: Addunt: Inter hos ERAT etiam Augustinus. Recte dicunt ERAT. Etenim Haereticos non esse coercendos ulla corporali ratione putarat Augustinus cum in Rogatianorum Haereticorum errore versaretur, ut ipse fatetur Epist. 48. ad Vincentium. Sed cur non addunt Augustinum melius e verbo Dei edoctum (ut ipse testatur & probat ibidem) sententiam suam mutasse, & ex verbo Dei defendisse eadem quae nos contra Arminianos, qui jam Rogatianorum quoque Haeresin ex inferis resuscitant, defendimus? Et sic salsissimum est sententiam suam totius Antiquitatis esse: tota, inquiunt, Antiquitas pura judicavit ita.
units.tr: They add: "Among these WAS also Augustine." They rightly say WAS. For Augustine had thought that heretics were not to be restrained by any bodily means while he was in the error of the Rogatists, as he himself confesses in Epistle 48 to Vincentius. But why do they not add that Augustine, better taught from the Word of God (as he himself testifies and proves in the same place), changed his opinion, and defended from the Word of God the very things we defend against the Arminians, who now raise the heresy of the Rogatists from the dead? And so it is utterly absurd to claim that their opinion is that of all antiquity: "the whole of antiquity, they say, judged so in purity."

units.la: Adferunt etiam legem naturae, & dicunt eam hoc suadere. Intelligunt autem ut patet ex Responsi ad Excerpta Cll. DD. Proff. Leydd. p. 130. hanc legem: Quod tibi fieri non vis, alteri ne feceris. Sed hoc profecto est audacissime abuti ista lege. Nam eadem ratione Magistratui homicida aliquis aut alius sceleratus eripiat potestatem ipsum & alios coercendi. Lex ista limites suos habet, quae ad coercitionem peccantium, quales sunt Haeretici, extendenda non est. Adde, quod ista Lex contra Haereticos facit, qui quia nolunt ut sibi quisquam molestus sit, nemini h. e. Ecclesiae Dei molestiam facescere, & eam in jure suo, pace ac quiete turbare non debent. Quemadmodum igitur si homicida Magistratui objiceret Legem istam naturae, quo supplicium illius praetextu evadere posset, in eum recte lex ista retorqueretur, & vi illius puniretur: ita merito coercentur invasores alieni juris Haeretici, & perturbatores Ecclesiae, secundum dictamen legis illius, quam Arminiani pro Haereticis, sed in propriae simul causae praesidium allegant. Maxime quia constat quae indoles Haereticorum sit, quibus impossibile est, ubi vires nacti sint, ut a persecutione cutione Orthodoxorum sibi temperent, ut alias ostendemus.
units.tr: They also bring forward the law of nature and say that it recommends this. They understand it, as is clear from the Response to the Excerpts of the Leiden professors, p. 130, to be this law: "What you do not want done to you, do not do to another." But this is truly to abuse that law most audaciously. For by the same reasoning some murderer or other criminal could snatch from the magistrate the power of restraining him and others. That law has its limits, and it must not be extended to the restraint of sinners, such as heretics are. Add that this law works against the heretics themselves: since they do not want anyone to trouble them, they ought not to cause trouble to anyone, that is, to the Church of God, nor disturb it in its right, its peace and its quiet. Just as, if a murderer objected that law of nature to the magistrate in order to escape punishment under its pretext, the law would rightly be turned against him and he would be punished by its force, so the invaders of others' rights, the heretics, and the disturbers of the Church are rightly restrained according to the dictate of that law, which the Arminians allege on behalf of heretics but at the same time in defence of their own cause. Especially since it is clear what the nature of heretics is: once they have gained power, they cannot refrain from persecuting the orthodox, as we shall show elsewhere.

units.la: Athanasii dictum, quo in Arianorum crudelitatem contra Orthodoxos invehitur, etiam ad rem non facere quis non videt ? Hæc breviter vaniloquiis horum hominum nullo veritatis sale aut solidæ eruditionis flore aspersis reponere visum fuit, quia talia subinde inculcant, quibus incautis imponere studeant. Cæterum de modo coercendi Hæreticos agemus ubi Deo visum fuerit, in progressa operis nostri de prudentia veteris Ecclesiæ.
units.tr: Who does not see that the saying of Athanasius, in which he attacks the cruelty of the Arians against the orthodox, also has no bearing on the matter? I have thought it fit to answer these babblings of theirs briefly, since they are sprinkled with no salt of truth or flower of solid learning, but because they keep inculcating such things, with which they are eager to impose on the incautious. Moreover, we shall treat of the manner of restraining heretics when God sees fit, in the course of our work on the prudence of the ancient Church.

units.la: 8. Sextum est : Hæreticis anathema dicendum non esse. Id quod docent eo prætextu, quòd Christus eos non damnet expresse, nec per consequentiam omnibus obviam. In specie autem ostendi eos Antitrinitarios nolle dicere anathema. Fatentur p. 153. hæc omnia & persistunt ; atque contrà dicunt Hæreticos esse & forte anathemate dignos, item Tyrannos esse qui aliter sentiunt, ut vidimus Par. III. lib. 2. c. 8. §. 5. Et in eum finem abuntur verbis Buceri & Fr. Junii qui profecto non loquuntur de Hæreticis.
