Nam posito, sed non concesso, illorum dogmata de Quinque articulis vera esse, sunt ea tamen ex ipsorum pro- priis hypothesibus talia, quæ firmiter constanterque credenda non sunt; talia in quibus licet annuam, menstruam, horariam fidem habere; talia quæ non niituntur oraculis divinis, sed rationibus quæ à divinis oraculis differunt; talia quæ in dubi- um vocare licet. Et ex eorundem hypothesibus, dicebam: potestis in nostro coe- tu æque salvari atque in vestro.
units.tr: 2. One further point, and the chief one, must be noted. I had shown (pp. 260, 261, 263), from these theologians' own hypotheses, that first, the peoples of the Remonstrants ought to desert them and return to us and to our doctrine. For granting, though not conceding, that their doctrines on the Five Articles are true, yet by their own hypotheses they are such that they are not to be believed firmly and constantly; such that one may hold them with a yearly, monthly, or hourly faith; such that they do not rest on divine oracles but on reasons which differ from divine oracles; such that it is permitted to call them into doubt. And from the same hypotheses I said: you can be saved in our congregation just as well as in yours.

units.la: Dixi etiam eos ministros dum doƈtrinam nostram de quinque articu- lis ut summè impiam, ut Hæreticam, ut blasphemam, ut Atheismi ma- trem accusant & traducunt, more sibi consueto, fidem non mereri apud populos suos: quia apud eos fidem mereri non debent qui ex doƈtri- nâ Ecclesiæ Christianæ de immensitate & omnipræsenti â Dei dicunt facilem pro- lapsum in Atheismum esse: item qui Reformatos pro Hæreticis & impiis habent, Antitrinitarios autem h. e. Socinianos & similia monstra pro Hæreticis & impiis habere nolunt, sed pro hominibus piis, imò piissimis: item qui docent nulli ho- mini aut Ecclesiæ judicium infallibile de erroribus aliorum delatum esse, & alia quæ in excusationem blasphemiarum Hæreticarum proponunt.
units.tr: I also said that these ministers, while they accuse and traduce our doctrine of the five articles as most impious, heretical, blasphemous, and the mother of Atheism, do so in their customary manner, and that they do not deserve credit with their own peoples. Those do not deserve credit among them who say that the doctrine of the Christian Church concerning the immensity and omnipresence of God leads to an easy lapse into Atheism; likewise those who hold the Reformed to be heretics and impious, but are unwilling to regard the Antitrinitarians, that is, the Socinians and similar monsters, as heretics and impious, but as pious men, indeed most pious; likewise those who teach that no man or Church has been granted an infallible judgment concerning the errors of others, and others of the same kind which they put forward in excuse of heretical blasphemies.

units.la: Denique dixeram p. 262. manifestam esse ex illis dogmatibus injusti- tiam causæ istorum ministrorum. Nam Reformati, dicebam, pugnant cir- ca notorios illos quinque articulos, ut omnes alios, pro iis dogmatis quæ credunt (ita enim in præsens dicere sufficiat) niti oraculis divinis, non autem rationibus quæ à divinis oraculis differunt; & propter honorem quem divinis oraculis deferunt, ea constanter firmiterque credenda censent, ac propter eundem honorem nefas esse ar- bitrantur, ea in dubium vocare vel illis contradicere. At Remonstrantes pugnant pro talibus dogmatis quæ ipsi dicunt non esse firmiter constanterque credenda, utpote quæ nitantur rationibus quæ à divinis oraculis differunt, quæ licet in dubium voca- re,cum Religio vera inter infinitas adeoque horarias,circa controversias, variationes manere possit salva atque illæsa &c. propter talia igitur dogmata, si maximè vera essent, constanter tamen contendere ne per suas quidem hypotheses possunt, quæ non permittunt permittunt ea firmiter constanterque credi. Cum igitur constantia laudem non meretur assertio illorum dogmatum; an non pertinacia est inexcusabilis, si in illis asserendis pergere sustineant, maxime postquam bene norunt praesentissima ruina periculum imminere patriae suae ex ea contentione, quae circa veritatem talem est, quae firmiter constanterque, secundum ipsos, credenda non est? Omnes honestos viros jam interrogo, utra causa justior sit Reformatorum an ne Remonstrantium? Ad haec omnia quid Arminiani? Non negant me vere dixisse, sed sicco pede praetereunt & ne verbum quidem ad ista quae maximi momenti sunt respondent. Manet igitur firmum quod dixeram ibi, hos homines non solum αὐτοκατάκριτοι esse & in sua propria conscientia convictos, sed etiam verissimum esse quod dixi eos nullam fidem apud populos suos speciatim circa doctrinam de Quinque articulis mereri, & omnes honestos viros qui illam ipsorum doctrinam sequuti hactenus sunt, teneri eam deserere. Quibus accedunt tot fraudes & impostura, quibus contra conscientiam suam usi sunt in istis Vindiciis suis, Maxime autem quod ex Partibus his Quatuor Arcanorum luce clarius meridiana jam constat, speciatim ex Parte Secunda, controversiam quam nobis circa quinque articulos moverunt non esse nisi merum praetextum sub quo introducant professionem apertam Turcicarum illarum blasphemiarum Socini contra Filium Dei, quibus se plane immersos esse manifestissimum fecerunt in Vindiciis suis. Nunc judica pie Lector, de causa nostra & Arminianorum. Maxime autem Tu Iudex totius Terrae, cui judicium omne traditum est, Iesu Christe aeterne Fili Dei judica causam tuam. Non enim mea aut cujusquam hominis privata, sed tua est. Tua gloria agitur qui cum Patre & Spiritu S. es unus ille verus Deus Israelis, quem hi homines negant, dum audent hanc blasphemiam evomere, eos colere verum Deum Israelis qui non est Pater Filius & Spiritus S. & eos colere verum Deum qui te non colunt, sed horrendum in modum blasphemant, qui negant esse peccatum oppugnare aeternam Deitatem tuam & sacrosanctam Trinitatem, qui deniqne simulant professionem Orthodoxae doctrinae, ut blasphemiarum & contumeliarum quibus Antitrinitarii te petunt, & quibus isti homines ex animo addicti sunt, professionem publicam in Ecclesiam tuam, salsissimo praetextu Libertatis conscientiarum, introducant. Exurge, Christe Iesu, miserere harum Provinciarum, vindica gloriam tuam. Tibi, qui cum Patre & Spiritu S. es unus ille & solus verus Deus Israelis, sit honos, laus & gloria in secula. Amen.
units.tr: Finally, I had said (p. 262) that the injustice of the cause of these ministers was plain from those dogmas. For the Reformed, I said, struggle over those notorious five articles, as over all others, for the doctrines they believe (for it is enough to say so for the present) to rest on divine oracles, and not on reasons which differ from divine oracles; and out of the honour they render to divine oracles, they judge those doctrines to be firmly and constantly to be believed, and for the same honour they consider it wrong to call them into doubt or to contradict them. But the Remonstrants struggle for such doctrines as they themselves say are not to be firmly and constantly believed, since they rest on reasons which differ from divine oracles, and which may be called into doubt, since the true religion can remain safe and unharmed amid infinite and hourly variations concerning controversies, and so on. Therefore, even by their own hypotheses, they cannot contend constantly for such doctrines, even if they were most true, since their hypotheses do not permit them to be believed firmly and constantly. Since therefore constancy does not earn praise for the assertion of those doctrines, is not obstinacy inexcusable if they persist in asserting them, especially now that they well know the most imminent danger of ruin threatens their country from that contention, which concerns a truth that, on their own account, is not to be believed firmly and constantly? I now ask all honest men: which cause is more just, that of the Reformed or that of the Remonstrants? To all this what do the Arminians reply? They do not deny that I spoke truly, but they pass it by with dry feet, and do not answer a single word to these matters, which are of the greatest moment. What I said there therefore stands firm: these men are not only [self-condemned] (αὐτοκατάκριτοι) and convicted by their own conscience, but it is also most true, as I said, that they deserve no credit with their own peoples, especially concerning the doctrine of the Five Articles, and that all honest men who have hitherto followed their doctrine are bound to desert it. To this are added so many frauds and deceptions, which they have used against their own conscience in their Vindications. Above all, it is now plain, clearer than midday light, from these Four Parts of the Arcana, and especially from Part Two, that the controversy they have raised against us over the five articles is nothing but a mere pretext, under which they may introduce an open profession of those Turkish blasphemies of Socinus against the Son of God, in which they have most manifestly shown in their Vindications that they are wholly immersed. Now, pious reader, judge our cause and that of the Arminians. But above all you, Judge of all the earth, to whom all judgment has been committed, Jesus Christ, eternal Son of God, judge your own cause. For it is not mine or any private man's, but yours. Your glory is at stake, you who with the Father and the Holy Spirit are that one true God of Israel. These men deny this, while they dare to vomit forth this blasphemy: that they worship the true God of Israel who is not the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, and that they worship the true God who does not worship you, but blasphemes you in a dreadful manner, who deny that it is a sin to assail your eternal Deity and the most holy Trinity. Finally, they feign a profession of Orthodox doctrine, so that they may introduce into your Church, under the most salt-seasoned pretext of liberty of conscience, a public profession of those blasphemies and insults with which the Antitrinitarians assail you, and to which these men are wholly devoted. Arise, Christ Jesus, have mercy on these Provinces, vindicate your glory. To you, who with the Father and the Holy Spirit are that one and only true God of Israel, be honour, praise, and glory for ever. Amen.

units.la: FINIS.
units.tr: THE END.
